w.how: Cut a sponge cake into cubes and press into a glass bowl. Make up raspberry jelly, pour over the sponge and chill until set. Layer with sliced mango, 500ml custard and whipped cream. Chill overnight and finish with gold sprinkles just before serving.

d.note: Pomegranate and cranberry punch with soda and lime over ice
d.how: Fill tall glasses with ice. Pour in equal parts pomegranate juice and cranberry juice to about halfway. Top with cold soda water and squeeze in a wedge of lime. Stir once and serve straight away while it is deep red and fizzing.

s.note: Golden crab cakes pan-fried in butter with lemon and tartare
s.how: Mix 400g crab meat with 2 tbsp mayonnaise, an egg, a teaspoon of Dijon, a pinch of paprika and half a cup of breadcrumbs. Shape into 8 small cakes and chill for 30 minutes. Pan-fry in butter until golden on both sides and serve with lemon wedges and tartare.

s.note: Creamy deviled eggs with a kick of hot sauce and smoked paprika
s.how: Boil 8 eggs for 10 minutes, cool in cold water and peel. Halve and whip the yolks with mayonnaise, yellow mustard and a dash of hot sauce until smooth. Pipe back into the whites, dust with smoked paprika and finish with snipped chives.

m.note: Charred rare beef sliced thin on rolls with onion and horseradish
m.how: Rub a 1kg piece of beef topside with salt, cracked pepper, garlic powder and smoked paprika. Grill over high heat, turning, until charred outside and rare inside. Rest, slice paper thin and pile onto bread rolls with raw onion and horseradish sauce.

w.note: Vanilla cupcakes with tall beehive swirls of pastel buttercream
w.how: Beat 125g butter with 150g sugar, then 2 eggs, then fold in 200g self-raising flour and 125ml milk. Bake in cases at 175C for 18 minutes and cool. Beat butter and icing sugar with a drop of colouring and pipe tall beehive swirls on top. Finish with pastel sprinkles.

d.note: Thick vanilla malted milkshakes topped with a cherry
d.how: Blend 4 big scoops of vanilla ice cream with 500ml cold milk and 4 tbsp malted milk powder until thick and smooth. Pour into tall chilled glasses and top each with a maraschino cherry. Add a striped straw and serve straight away.

s.note: Golden sausage rolls with onion and carrot, tomato sauce for dipping
s.how: Mix 500g pork sausage mince with a grated onion and a grated carrot. Lay along the edge of 2 halved puff pastry sheets, roll up and seal. Brush with beaten egg, cut into pieces and bake at 200C for 25 minutes. Serve hot with tomato sauce.

s.note: Charred squid with chilli, garlic and lime
s.how: Score 600g cleaned squid tubes and cut into pieces. Toss with oil, 2 crushed garlic cloves, 1 chopped chilli and salt. Grill on a very hot barbecue for 1 minute a side and finish with lime juice and coriander.

m.note: Snags and rump steaks off the coals with potato salad and bread
m.how: Boil 1kg potatoes until tender, cool and dress with mayonnaise and chives. Grill 8 thick beef sausages and 4 rump steaks over hot coals. Fry 2 sliced onions on the hotplate until golden. Serve it all with a stack of white bread and the potato salad.

w.note: Butter sponge squares dipped in raspberry jelly and rolled in coconut
w.how: Bake a butter sponge in a square tin and cool overnight. Make up raspberry jelly and chill until just starting to set. Cut the sponge into cubes, dip each in the jelly and roll in desiccated coconut. Chill until firm and red and fluffy all over.

d.note: Australian lager stubbies buried in an esky of ice
d.how: Fill an esky with ice and cold water, which chills bottles faster than ice alone. Bury the stubbies right down and leave them for 30 minutes. Hand one out to everyone in a stubby holder and keep the lid on between rounds.

s.note: Crisp bacon in soft white rolls with butter and brown sauce
s.how: Fry 8 thick rashers of bacon until crisp at the edges. Split 4 soft white rolls and butter them generously. Stuff two rashers into each roll with a good squeeze of brown sauce, then wrap tightly in paper so they stay warm until the next drop.

s.note: Mussels steamed in white wine and garlic with crusty bread
s.how: Soften 2 chopped eschalots and crushed garlic in butter in a big pot. Add 1kg cleaned mussels and 200ml white wine, cover and steam for 5 minutes until open. Toss through chopped parsley and a knob of butter and serve with crusty bread to mop up.

m.n: Normandy chicken with cider and cream
m.note: Chicken braised in cider with mushrooms and cream
m.how: Brown 1kg chicken thighs, then soften 2 shallots and 200g mushrooms. Add 375ml apple cider and simmer covered 25 minutes. Stir in 150ml cream and parsley and serve with crusty bread.

w.note: Warm sticky date sponge soaked in butterscotch sauce with custard
w.how: Soak 200g chopped dates in boiling water with a pinch of bicarb. Cream 60g butter with 150g brown sugar, add 2 eggs, the dates and 175g self-raising flour. Bake at 180C for 35 minutes. Pour over hot sauce of butter, brown sugar and cream and serve with custard.

d.note: Strong black tea from a big pot, served in metal mugs
d.how: Warm a big teapot with boiling water and tip it out. Add 6 tea bags and fill with freshly boiled water. Leave it to stew for 5 minutes so it is properly strong. Pour into metal mugs and set milk and raw sugar on the side.

s.note: Golden corn fritters with a sour cream and chive dip
s.how: Mix a drained can of corn kernels with 100g flour, 2 eggs, sliced spring onions and a pinch of paprika. Fry spoonfuls in a little oil until golden on both sides. Stir chopped chives through sour cream for the dip and serve the fritters warm.

s.note: Smoked salmon blinis and prosciutto wrapped melon on silver trays
s.how: Top 16 blinis with a little creme fraiche, a fold of smoked salmon and a sprig of dill. Cut a rockmelon into neat wedges, remove the skin and wrap each in a slice of prosciutto. Arrange both on silver trays and serve chilled to the guests.

m.note: Parmesan pumpkin risotto finished with crisp sage butter
m.how: Roast 1kg diced butternut pumpkin at 200C until soft. Stir 300g arborio rice in butter, then add 1.25L hot stock a ladle at a time for 20 minutes. Mash half the pumpkin through, fold in the rest with grated parmesan and spoon over butter fried with sage leaves.

w.note: Glittering slipper-shaped meringues with whipped cream and strawberries
w.how: Whisk 3 egg whites to stiff peaks, then add 170g caster sugar a spoon at a time until glossy. Pipe into little slipper shapes on lined trays and bake at 100C for an hour. Cool, dust with edible glitter and serve with whipped cream and sliced strawberries.

d.note: Blueberry juice and lemonade with lime and frozen blueberries floating
d.how: Fill a jug with ice and a handful of frozen blueberries. Pour in 1L blueberry juice and 1L cold lemonade, then squeeze in the juice of a lime. Stir gently and pour into glasses before the clock strikes midnight.

s.note: Watermelon, figs, dates and pomegranate with mint, feta and lime
s.how: Cut 1kg watermelon into wedges and lay on a big platter. Add halved fresh figs and torn medjool dates, then scatter with pomegranate seeds, mint leaves and crumbled feta. Squeeze over a little lime just before serving so it is cool and fresh.

s.note: Falafel in mini pita with tahini, pickled turnip and tomato
s.how: Soak 250g dried chickpeas overnight, drain and blitz with parsley, onion, garlic and cumin. Shape into small balls and fry at 180C until dark golden. Tuck into mini pita with tahini, pickled turnip and sliced tomato, then wrap in paper for the flight.

m.note: Charred harissa lamb sliced over couscous with a cool yoghurt sauce
m.how: Butterfly a 1.5kg lamb leg and rub with harissa, crushed garlic and cumin. Marinate for 2 hours, then grill over high heat until charred outside and pink inside. Rest for 15 minutes and slice over fluffy couscous with a garlic yoghurt sauce.

w.note: Pistachio and cardamom baklava soaked in honey syrup
w.how: Layer buttered filo sheets in a tin with chopped pistachios mixed with cardamom between every few layers. Cut into triangles and bake at 180C for 40 minutes until golden. Pour over warm honey syrup with lemon juice and leave for several hours to soak in.

d.note: Chilled hibiscus tea, deep red and tart, Egyptian style.
d.how: Steep 30g dried hibiscus flowers in 1L just-boiled water for 10 minutes, strain and stir in 80g sugar. Chill and serve over ice with a lime wedge in each glass.

s.note: Sticky red wine chorizo, Manchego with quince paste and warm olives
s.how: Slice 2 chorizo and fry until crisp, then add a splash of red wine and cook until sticky. Cut Manchego into triangles and top each with a sliver of quince paste. Warm olives with strips of orange peel and serve everything on small plates.

s.note: Melting cheese and green chilli quesadillas with a Z scored on top
s.how: Fill 4 flour tortillas with grated Monterey Jack and chopped roasted green chilli, then fold in half. Cook in butter over medium heat until golden on both sides and melted inside. Score a sharp Z into the top with a knife and cut into wedges.

m.note: Marinated grilled skirt steak with rice, black beans and fresh salsa
m.how: Marinate 800g skirt steak for 2 hours in lime and orange juice with crushed garlic and cumin. Grill over very high heat for 3 minutes a side, rest and slice thinly against the grain. Serve with long grain rice, warm black beans and a fresh tomato salsa.

w.note: Cinnamon sugar churros with a cup of thick hot chocolate
w.how: Bring 250ml water and 60g butter to the boil, beat in 150g flour, then beat in 2 eggs. Pipe lengths into 180C oil and fry until golden. Roll in cinnamon sugar. Melt 150g dark chocolate into hot milk until thick and serve in small cups for dipping.

d.note: Red wine sangria with brandy, orange and apple, topped with soda
d.how: Slice 2 oranges and an apple into a big jug. Pour in a bottle of red wine, 60ml brandy and 250ml orange juice. Chill for 2 hours so the fruit soaks it up. Top with cold soda water just before pouring into glasses over ice.

s.note: Battered flathead and chips wrapped in paper and eaten on the sand
s.how: Cut 1kg potatoes into thick chips and fry at 140C until soft. Whisk flour with ice-cold lager to a thin batter. Dip 600g flathead in flour, then batter, and fry at 180C for 4 minutes. Fry the chips again until crisp and wrap it all in paper with lemon and tartare.

s.note: Little beef pies sitting in mushy peas with tomato sauce on top
s.how: Braise 800g diced beef chuck in stock for 2.5 hours, thicken and cool. Bake in shortcrust cases with puff lids at 200C for 30 minutes. Cook 500g peas and mash roughly with butter. Spoon peas into bowls, sit a pie on top and finish with tomato sauce.

m.note: Salt and pepper squid tossed with chilli and spring onion, egg fried rice
m.how: Score 500g squid tubes and cut into pieces. Toss in rice flour with ground Sichuan pepper and salt and fry at 190C for 60 seconds. Toss with chilli and sliced spring onion. Fry cold cooked jasmine rice with scrambled egg and spring onion and serve together.

w.note: Crisp pavlova piled with whipped cream and passionfruit
w.how: Whisk 4 egg whites to stiff peaks, then add 220g caster sugar a spoon at a time until glossy. Fold in a teaspoon each of cornflour and white vinegar. Shape into a round, bake at 120C for 90 minutes and cool in the oven. Top with whipped cream and passionfruit.

d.note: Cold Australian lager in chilled schooner glasses
d.how: Chill the schooner glasses in the freezer for 20 minutes. Pour the lager slowly down the side of the tilted glass, straightening up at the end for a neat head. Keep the rest in the fridge and pour a pint for anyone who is game.

s.note: Pork and prawn wontons in ginger broth, more wontons than soup
s.how: Mix 250g pork mince with 150g chopped green prawns, grated ginger and soy. Fill wonton wrappers and fold. Simmer 1.5L chicken stock with ginger slices and soy, add the wontons and cook 4 minutes. Add halved bok choy for the last minute and load up the bowls.

s.note: Bright green avocado and edamame dip with prawn crackers
s.how: Blitz 2 avocados with 200g thawed edamame, the juice of 2 limes, a crushed garlic clove, a handful of coriander and salt until smooth and very green. Spoon into a bowl and serve with prawn crackers and cucumber sticks for dipping.

m.note: Crisp sweet and sour pork with pineapple and egg fried rice
m.how: Cut 600g pork scotch fillet into chunks, coat in cornflour and fry until crisp. Simmer rice vinegar, sugar and tomato sauce, add pineapple pieces and sliced capsicum and toss the pork through. Serve with egg fried rice made from cold long grain rice.

w.note: Crisp folded cookies with a paper fortune tucked inside
w.how: Whisk 2 egg whites with 80g sugar, then mix in 60g flour, 30g melted butter and a drop of vanilla. Spread thin rounds on a lined tray and bake at 180C for 6 minutes. Working fast while hot, lay a paper fortune on each, fold in half and bend over a cup edge.

d.note: Glowing lime soda with crushed ice and fresh lime
d.how: Fill tall glasses with crushed ice. Add a good splash of lime cordial and a squeeze of fresh lime to each. Top up with cold soda water and add a drop or two of green food colouring if you want it properly glowing. Stir and serve.

s.note: Toasts with smashed pea, mint and feta ridged like a crocodile's back
s.how: Slice a baguette and brush with olive oil, then toast until golden. Cook 300g peas, then smash with chopped mint, crumbled feta and a squeeze of lemon. Spread thickly on the toasts and run a fork along the top to make green crocodile ridges.

s.note: Chilled poached prawns on ice with a classic cocktail sauce
s.how: Bring a pot of salted water to the boil with lemon slices. Add 500g green prawns and poach for 2 minutes until pink, then plunge into iced water. Peel, leaving tails on, and serve on ice with a sauce of mayonnaise, tomato sauce, lemon and hot sauce.

m.note: Beef chuck simmered with dark rum, carrots and allspice
m.how: Brown 1kg diced beef chuck in batches. Soften 2 onions and 3 carrots, add the beef back with 125ml dark rum, a teaspoon of allspice and water to cover. Simmer gently for 3 hours until thick and tender. Serve in big bowls with crusty bread.

w.note: Fairy bread triangles with hundreds and thousands and a hint of glitter
w.how: Spread slices of soft white bread with butter right to the edges. Press each buttered side into a plate of hundreds and thousands until well covered. Cut into triangles, dust with a tiny pinch of edible glitter and pile them on a plate.

d.note: Warm honey vanilla milk with nutmeg, served in bedtime mugs
d.how: Heat 1L milk gently until steaming but not boiling. Stir in 2 tbsp honey and a drop of vanilla until dissolved. Pour into mugs and grate a small pinch of nutmeg over the top. Serve at bedtime with the lights turned down low.

s.note: Cheese cubes with chutney tipped out of a wooden cup like dice
s.how: Cut 200g aged cheddar and 200g gouda into neat cubes. Put a small dot of tomato chutney on each. Pile them into a wooden cup, then tip them out onto a board with water crackers like a roll of the dice. Call your bid before you eat.

s.note: Sticky honey, chilli and lime pork and pineapple skewers
s.how: Cut 500g pork scotch fillet and half a pineapple into chunks and thread onto skewers. Warm 3 tbsp honey with a chopped red chilli and lime juice. Grill the skewers over hot coals, brushing with the glaze, until sticky and charred on all sides.

m.note: Prawns, mussels, corn and potatoes tipped onto paper with butter
m.how: Boil 800g baby potatoes in salted water with smoked paprika, garlic and lemon for 15 minutes. Add 4 halved corn cobs for 5 minutes, then 500g green prawns and 1kg mussels for 4 minutes. Drain, tip onto paper and pour over melted garlic butter.

w.note: Inky dark chocolate tart in cocoa pastry with sea salt
w.how: Blind bake a sweet shortcrust case with a spoon of cocoa rubbed into the pastry. Heat 300ml cream and pour over 300g chopped dark chocolate, stirring until glossy. Pour into the case and chill overnight. Sprinkle with sea salt flakes before slicing.

d.note: Hibiscus brewed with ginger, cloves and orange, iced
d.how: Steep 30g dried hibiscus, a knob of sliced ginger, 4 cloves and orange peel in 1.2L boiling water for 30 minutes. Strain, stir in 120g sugar and chill. Serve over ice, with a splash of dark rum for the grown-ups.

s.note: Sticky barbecue, honey and hot sauce wings off the grill
s.how: Leave 1kg chicken wings uncovered in the fridge overnight, then toss with garlic powder and salt. Bake at 220C for 45 minutes until crisp. Warm barbecue sauce with honey and a splash of hot sauce, toss the wings through and serve with plenty of napkins.

s.note: Devilled eggs with mustard, sweet relish and a dash of hot sauce
s.how: Boil 8 eggs for 10 minutes, cool and peel. Halve and mash the yolks with mayonnaise, yellow mustard, a spoon of sweet relish and a dash of hot sauce until smooth. Pipe back into the whites and dust with smoked paprika. Serve chilled on the porch.

m.note: Slow baked pork ribs glazed over hot coals with coleslaw
m.how: Rub 2kg pork ribs with smoked paprika, brown sugar, garlic powder, cayenne and salt. Wrap in foil and bake at 150C for 2.5 hours. Unwrap, brush with barbecue sauce and finish over hot coals until sticky. Serve with a crunchy cabbage coleslaw.

w.note: Spiced sweet potato pie in a crisp pastry case
w.how: Roast 800g sweet potatoes until soft, then mash with 60g butter, 150g brown sugar, 2 eggs, 200ml evaporated milk, cinnamon and nutmeg. Pour into a blind-baked sweet shortcrust case and bake at 170C for 50 minutes until just set. Cool before slicing.

d.note: Red fruit punch of cranberry, pineapple and lemonade from a cooler
d.how: Fill a big drink cooler with ice. Pour in 1L cranberry juice and 1L pineapple juice and stir. Top up with 2L cold lemonade just before everyone arrives so it stays fizzy. Set out plastic cups and let people help themselves all afternoon.

s.note: Hot roasted chestnuts in paper cones.
s.how: Score a cross in 600g chestnuts and roast at 220C for 25 minutes until the shells curl open. Wrap in a tea towel for 5 minutes to steam, then peel while warm and serve in paper cones with a pinch of sea salt flakes.

s.note: Celery sticks with blue cheese cream and crackers with sharp cheddar
s.how: Beat 250g cream cheese with 50g blue cheese and snipped chives until smooth. Cut celery into short sticks and pipe or spoon the filling along each. Serve on a platter beside crackers topped with slices of vintage cheddar, the way a 1940s party did it.

m.note: Beef chuck braised in red wine with vegetables and potatoes
m.how: Sear a 1.5kg piece of beef chuck all over. Add a sliced onion, 3 carrots and 2 celery sticks, then 250ml red wine and enough water to come halfway. Cover and braise at 160C for 3 hours, adding 800g potatoes for the last hour. Slice and serve with the juices.

w.note: Rich brandy-soaked fruit pudding, steamed and flamed with custard
w.how: Soak 500g mixed dried fruit in 100ml brandy overnight. Mix with 125g melted butter, 125g brown sugar, 2 eggs, breadcrumbs, flour and mixed spice. Steam in a greased basin for 4 hours. Warm a little brandy, pour over, light at the table and serve with custard.

d.note: Hot spiced apple juice ladled into mugs
d.how: Pour 2L cloudy apple juice into a pot with 3 cinnamon sticks, 6 cloves and a few strips of orange peel. Simmer gently for 15 minutes so the spices come through. Ladle hot into mugs, leaving the spices behind, and wrap your hands around it.

s.note: White chocolate popcorn clusters with red and green sprinkles
s.how: Pop 100g popping corn and spread on a lined tray. Melt 200g white chocolate and drizzle all over, then scatter with red and green sprinkles and a pinch of sea salt. Leave to set for 30 minutes, then break into clusters for the mission team.

s.note: Little fruit mince pies with pastry stars and icing sugar
s.how: Cut 3 sheets of shortcrust into rounds and press into a patty tin. Fill with fruit mince mixed with orange zest. Top each with a small pastry star, brush with beaten egg and bake at 190C for 18 minutes. Cool a little and dust with icing sugar.

m.note: Turkey breast rolled with bacon stuffing, sprouts and cranberry sauce
m.how: Fry chopped bacon and onion with sage and breadcrumbs for a stuffing. Butterfly a 1.5kg turkey breast, spread with stuffing, roll and tie. Roast at 180C for 90 minutes with 1kg potatoes alongside. Serve sliced with roasted brussels sprouts and cranberry sauce.

w.note: Warm fruit pudding slices with brandy custard and a spoon of cream
w.how: Heat the Christmas pudding following the packet directions until hot right through. Warm 500ml custard gently and stir in 2 tbsp brandy. Cut the pudding into thick slices, pour over the brandy custard and add a spoon of cream on top.

d.note: Chilled creamy eggnog with nutmeg and rum for the adults
d.how: Whisk 4 eggs with 100g sugar in a pot. Stir in 500ml milk and 250ml cream and heat gently, stirring, until slightly thickened, without boiling. Chill well, grate nutmeg on top and add a splash of dark rum to the adult glasses.

s.note: Flaky buttermilk biscuits split warm with butter and honey
s.how: Rub 100g cold butter into 450g self-raising flour with a pinch of salt. Stir in 300ml buttermilk until it just comes together. Pat out, cut into rounds and bake at 220C for 14 minutes until tall and golden. Split while warm and spread with butter and honey.

s.note: Maple roasted pecans, walnuts and pepitas broken into clusters
s.how: Toss 100g pecans, 100g walnuts and 50g pepitas with 4 tbsp maple syrup and a pinch of sea salt. Spread on a lined tray and roast at 170C for 12 minutes, stirring once. Leave to cool completely so they set, then break into rough clusters.

m.note: Chicken, pumpkin, corn and beans simmered thick with cornbread alongside
m.how: Brown 600g diced chicken thighs, then add 500g diced butternut pumpkin, a can of corn, a can of drained kidney beans, a can of crushed tomatoes and a teaspoon of smoked paprika. Simmer 40 minutes until thick. Bake a quick cornbread from cornmeal, flour, egg and milk to serve alongside.

w.note: Warm maple roasted peaches with vanilla ice cream and pecans
w.how: Halve 4 ripe peaches and remove the stones. Sit cut side up in a baking dish, dot with butter and drizzle with maple syrup. Roast at 200C for 15 minutes until soft and syrupy. Serve warm with a scoop of vanilla ice cream and crushed pecans on top.

d.note: Cranberry and sparkling water with blueberries and mint over ice
d.how: Fill tall glasses with ice, a few fresh blueberries and a couple of mint leaves. Pour in cranberry juice to halfway, then top with cold sparkling water. Stir gently so the berries swirl like a river current and serve straight away.

s.note: Smoked salmon blinis and prosciutto melon laid out for the launch crowd
s.how: Top 16 blinis with creme fraiche, a fold of smoked salmon and snipped chives. Cut a rockmelon into neat wedges, remove the skin and wrap each with a thin slice of prosciutto. Lay both out on trays in rows for the book launch crowd.

s.note: Crunchy coconut prawns with sweet chilli sauce for dipping
s.how: Peel 500g green prawns, leaving the tails on. Dip each in beaten egg, then press into a mix of shredded coconut and panko breadcrumbs. Fry at 180C for 2 minutes until golden and crisp. Drain on paper and serve hot with sweet chilli sauce.

m.note: Lime and chilli snapper grilled in banana leaves with coconut rice
m.how: Rub 4 snapper fillets with lime juice, crushed garlic, chopped chilli and salt. Wrap each in a softened banana leaf and grill for 10 minutes. Cook rice in coconut milk with a pinch of salt, and warm a can of black beans. Serve the fish in its leaf.

w.note: Bright mango and lime sorbet scraped smooth with passionfruit on top
w.how: Dissolve 150g sugar in 150ml hot water and cool. Blend the flesh of 3 ripe mangoes with the syrup and the juice of 2 limes until smooth. Freeze in a tray, scraping with a fork every hour for 4 hours. Scoop into glasses and top with passionfruit pulp.

d.note: Coconut water and pineapple with lime and mint over ice
d.how: Fill tall glasses with ice and a few mint leaves. Pour in equal parts coconut water and pineapple juice, then squeeze in a wedge of lime. Stir well and serve cold, the kind of drink you need after hiking out of a jungle.

s.note: Spicy smoked sausages grilled over coals with mustard and jalapenos
s.how: Grill 8 hot smoked sausages slowly over medium coals, turning often, until the skins blister and they are hot right through. Slice thickly on an angle and spear each piece with a toothpick. Serve with a bowl of yellow mustard and pickled jalapenos on the side.

s.note: Steamed beef tamales with hot sauce, Chicago South Side style.
s.how: Brown 400g beef mince with 1 onion, 2 tsp chilli powder and 1 tsp cumin. Beat 300g masa harina with 100g lard, 1 tsp baking powder and 400ml warm stock to a soft dough. Spread on 16 soaked corn husks, add beef, roll up and steam 60 minutes. Serve with hot sauce.

m.note: Slow roasted rib tips glazed with barbecue sauce, with bread and fries
m.how: Rub 1.5kg pork ribs cut into short pieces with smoked paprika, brown sugar, garlic and salt. Cover and roast at 150C for 2.5 hours. Uncover, brush with tangy barbecue sauce and roast hot until sticky. Pile over slices of white bread with oven fries.

w.note: Spiced sweet potato pie baked in a crisp pastry case
w.how: Roast 800g sweet potatoes until soft, then mash with 60g butter, 150g brown sugar, 2 eggs, 200ml evaporated milk, cinnamon and nutmeg. Pour into a blind-baked sweet shortcrust case and bake at 170C for 50 minutes until just set. Cool completely before slicing.

d.note: Ice cold apple juice with a name on it, or apple soda
d.how: Chill a bottle of cloudy apple juice and write a name on it in marker so nobody else touches it. For everyone else, pour apple juice over ice, top with soda water and squeeze in a wedge of lime. Serve in plain glasses at the counter.

s.note: Little ham and cheese and egg sandwiches wrapped with a punched ticket
s.how: Hard boil 4 eggs, mash with mayonnaise and salt, and spread on buttered bread with shredded lettuce. Make more with sliced ham and vintage cheddar. Cut all into triangles, wrap in paper and tuck a punched paper ticket on top of each parcel.

s.note: Butter shortbread cut into tickets and dusted with gold sugar
s.how: Beat 250g butter with 80g icing sugar, then mix in 350g flour to a soft dough. Roll out and cut into ticket rectangles, punching a hole in each with a straw. Bake at 160C for 15 minutes, then sprinkle with caster sugar and gold sprinkles while warm.

m.note: Creamy chicken and vegetable pie under a golden puff lid
m.how: Brown 600g diced chicken thighs, then add a diced onion, 2 carrots and 2 celery sticks and soften. Stir in a spoon of flour, 300ml cream, thyme and a cup of peas and simmer until thick. Pour into a dish, top with puff pastry, egg wash and bake at 200C for 30 minutes.

w.note: Bell-shaped sugar cookies iced white with silver cachous and red ribbon
w.how: Beat 200g butter with 150g caster sugar, then mix in 300g flour. Chill, roll and cut into bell shapes. Bake at 180C for 8 minutes and cool. Ice white with icing sugar and water, press in silver cachous and pipe a red ribbon with tinted icing.

d.note: Thick frothy hot chocolate poured from a height with whipped cream
d.how: Heat 750ml milk and 250ml cream until steaming. Whisk in 100g chopped dark chocolate and 100g milk chocolate until thick and smooth. Pour from a height into mugs so it froths, then top each with a spoon of whipped cream. Thick, rich and hot.

s.note: Hot spinach and artichoke dip with toasted baguette.
s.how: Mix 250g softened cream cheese with 100g sour cream, 250g thawed spinach squeezed dry, 1 jar drained chopped artichoke hearts, 1 crushed garlic clove and 100g grated mozzarella. Bake at 190C for 20 minutes until bubbling and serve with toasted baguette slices.

s.note: Bubbling ham and gruyere toasties with Dijon and bechamel
s.how: Make a quick bechamel with 30g butter, a spoon of flour and 250ml milk. Spread bread with Dijon, fill with ham and grated gruyere, and top with bechamel and more cheese. Grill until bubbling and golden, then cut into small squares to share.

m.note: Penne in a rosy tomato and vodka cream sauce with parmesan
m.how: Soften crushed garlic and a pinch of chilli in olive oil. Add a can of crushed tomatoes and 60ml vodka and simmer 10 minutes. Stir in 200ml cream until rosy. Toss with 500g cooked penne, then finish with grated parmesan and torn basil.

w.note: Fudgy brownies cut into ten squares, each with a different topping
w.how: Melt 200g dark chocolate with 150g butter. Whisk in 250g sugar and 3 eggs, then fold in 100g flour. Bake in a lined tin at 170C for 25 minutes and cool. Cut into ten squares and top each differently with raspberries, nuts, salt flakes or anything you like.

d.note: Iced vanilla coffee over ice, or a hot flat white for Kat
d.how: Brew strong espresso and let it cool. Fill glasses with ice, add 30ml espresso, a spoon of vanilla syrup and top with cold milk. For Kat, steam milk and pour it over a hot shot instead for a proper flat white.

s.note: Toasted tuna, mayo and cheese melts on muffins
s.how: Mix 2 drained 185g tins of tuna with 3 tbsp mayonnaise, a diced celery stick and pepper. Pile onto 4 split English muffins, cover with 120g grated cheddar and grill until bubbling. Cut into quarters.

s.note: Little cheese balls rolled in chopped walnuts with crackers
s.how: Mix 200g grated cheddar, 250g cream cheese and snipped chives until well combined. Roll into small balls, then coat in finely chopped walnuts. Chill for an hour until firm. Serve piled in a bowl with water crackers on the side for scooping.

m.note: Glazed beef meatloaf with buttery mash, diner style
m.how: Mix 800g beef mince with a grated onion, a cup of breadcrumbs, an egg and salt. Press into a loaf tin, spread with tomato sauce and bake at 180C for an hour. Boil 1kg potatoes and mash with butter. Serve thick slices of meatloaf on the mash.

w.note: Lightning bolt shortbread iced white once cool
w.how: Beat 250g butter with 100g caster sugar, then mix in 350g flour to a soft dough. Roll out and cut into lightning bolt shapes. Bake at 160C for 15 minutes until pale golden. Cool on the tray, then ice with white icing made from icing sugar and water.

d.note: Cold chocolate milk shaken with cocoa and ice
d.how: Mix 2 tbsp cocoa with 2 tbsp sugar and a splash of hot water to a smooth paste. Pour into a jar with 1L cold milk and a handful of ice. Put the lid on and shake hard until frothy, then pour into glasses.

s.note: Crisp potato hash brown cakes with sour cream and chives
s.how: Grate 800g potatoes and a small onion, then squeeze out as much liquid as you can. Season well and shape into small flat cakes. Fry in butter over medium heat for 5 minutes a side until deep golden and crisp. Serve hot with sour cream and chives.

s.note: Golden wings glazed with honey, garlic, thyme and butter
s.how: Toss 1kg chicken wings with salt and roast at 220C for 45 minutes until crisp. Melt 50g butter with 4 tbsp honey, crushed garlic and thyme leaves. Toss the hot wings through the glaze until shiny and golden and serve on a big platter fit for a feast.

m.note: Slow-cooked beef ribs with roasted root vegetables and crusty bread
m.how: Rub 2kg beef short ribs with salt and cracked pepper. Roast covered at 140C for 5 hours until tender. For the last hour, add chunks of carrot, parsnip and potato to the tray to roast in the juices. Serve on a big board with crusty bread.

w.note: Fluffy buttermilk pancakes with butter and maple
w.how: Whisk 300g self-raising flour, 2 tbsp sugar, 2 eggs and 400ml buttermilk into a thick batter. Cook ladles in a buttered pan for 2 minutes a side and stack with butter and 200ml maple syrup.

d.note: Strong drip coffee in thick diner mugs, refilled on request
d.how: Brew a big pot of strong drip coffee from freshly ground beans. Pour into thick diner mugs with a splash of milk for anyone who wants it. When a cup is finished, refill it straight away rather than smashing the mug on the floor.

s.note: Mushroom caps stuffed with bacon, garlic and parmesan.
s.how: Remove the stems from 20 button mushrooms and chop the stems. Fry with 2 rashers diced bacon and 1 crushed garlic clove, then mix with 1/2 cup breadcrumbs and 50g grated parmesan. Fill the caps and bake at 200C for 15 minutes.

s.note: Cheddar and chive scones with a pinch of cayenne and butter
s.how: Rub 60g butter into 450g self-raising flour, then stir in 150g grated vintage cheddar, chopped chives and a pinch of cayenne. Mix in 300ml milk to a soft dough. Pat out, cut into rounds and bake at 220C for 12 minutes. Serve warm with butter.

m.note: Beef stew with paprika and hot sauce, finally with proper flavour
m.how: Brown 1kg diced beef chuck, then add 2 onions, crushed garlic, a spoon of smoked paprika and thyme. Pour in stock, a can of tomatoes and a splash of hot sauce. Braise for 3 hours, adding potatoes and carrots for the last hour. Proper flavour this time.

w.note: Buttered bread and sultanas baked in vanilla custard
w.how: Butter 8 slices of white bread, cut into triangles and layer in a dish with 80g sultanas. Whisk 3 eggs, 500ml milk, 100ml cream, 70g sugar and 1 tsp vanilla, pour over and soak 20 minutes. Sprinkle with nutmeg and bake at 170C for 40 minutes until puffed and golden.

d.note: Big pot of English breakfast tea in plain white cups
d.how: Warm a big teapot with boiling water and tip it out. Add 6 English breakfast tea bags and fill with freshly boiled water. Steep for 4 minutes. Pour into plain white cups and set milk and sugar on the table so everyone can fix their own.

s.note: Pumpkin and feta half moons with jack-o'-lantern faces cut in
s.how: Roast 600g diced pumpkin until soft, then mash with crumbled feta, chopped sage and nutmeg. Cut shortcrust into rounds, fill and fold into half moons. Cut a little jack-o'-lantern face into each, brush with egg and bake at 200C for 20 minutes.

s.note: Ghostly meringue teardrops with a glowing red nose
s.how: Whisk 3 egg whites with a pinch of cream of tartar to stiff peaks, then add 170g caster sugar a spoon at a time until glossy. Pipe ghostly teardrops onto lined trays and bake at 100C for 90 minutes. Cool and add a dot of red icing for the nose.

m.note: Pumpkin and carrot soup with a sour cream spiderweb on top
m.how: Roast 1kg pumpkin and 3 carrots with garlic and thyme until soft. Blend with 1L hot chicken stock until smooth. Pour into bowls, then pipe circles of sour cream on top and drag a skewer from the centre outwards to make a spiderweb pattern.

w.note: Chocolate mousse cups with biscuit soil and gummy worms crawling out
w.how: Melt 200g dark chocolate and cool slightly. Whip 300ml cream and whisk 3 egg whites to soft peaks. Stir the yolks into the chocolate, then fold in the cream and whites. Spoon into cups, chill, cover with crushed chocolate biscuits and push in gummy worms.

d.note: Hot spiced apple juice served from a black pot
d.how: Pour 2L cloudy apple juice into a black pot with 3 cinnamon sticks, 2 star anise and a few cloves. Simmer gently for 15 minutes so the spices come through. Ladle into mugs straight from the cauldron, leaving the spices behind.

s.note: Soy, honey and ginger glazed salmon bites on toothpicks
s.how: Cut 600g salmon fillet into bite-sized cubes. Mix 3 tbsp soy sauce, 2 tbsp honey and grated ginger and toss the salmon through. Spread on a lined tray and bake at 200C for 10 minutes until just cooked and sticky. Spear on toothpicks and serve with lime wedges.

s.n: Glen and Annie's grilled cheese soldiers
s.note: Toasted cheese sandwiches cut into dipping fingers.
s.how: Butter 8 slices of bread on the outside and sandwich with 8 slices cheddar. Cook in a pan over medium heat for 3 minutes a side until golden and melted. Cut each sandwich into 4 fingers and serve warm with tomato sauce for dipping.

m.note: Linguine with crab, garlic, chilli and lemon
m.how: Cook 400g linguine. Gently fry 3 garlic cloves and 1 chilli in 80ml olive oil, add 300g crab meat, the zest and juice of 1 lemon and a splash of pasta water. Toss with the pasta and parsley.

w.note: Cookies and cream ice cream with a white chocolate fin on top
w.how: Soften 1L vanilla ice cream slightly and fold through 150g crushed chocolate cream biscuits. Refreeze for 2 hours. Melt white chocolate, pipe little fin shapes onto baking paper and set in the fridge. Scoop the ice cream into bowls and stand a fin on top.

d.note: Blue lemonade spiders with vanilla ice cream floating on top
d.how: Pour cold lemonade into tall glasses and add a drop or two of blue food colouring to each, stirring until ocean blue. Gently add a scoop of vanilla ice cream so it floats and foams up. Serve straight away with a long spoon and a straw.

s.note: Smoked salmon blinis beside tiny warm mince pies
s.how: Top 16 blinis with creme fraiche, a fold of smoked salmon and a sprig of dill. Cut shortcrust into small rounds, press into a patty tin, fill with fruit mince and bake at 190C for 15 minutes. Arrange both on trays for the Slug Club party.

s.note: Cocoa-dusted chocolate truffles with a little pink sugar heart
s.how: Heat 150ml cream until steaming and pour over 250g chopped dark chocolate. Stir until smooth and chill for 2 hours until firm. Roll into small balls, coat in cocoa and press a pink sugar heart on top. Keep chilled and do not give them to anyone you fancy.

m.note: Stuffed turkey breast with roast potatoes and buttered sprouts
m.how: Fry a chopped onion with sage, mix with torn sourdough and season for a stuffing. Butterfly a 1.5kg turkey breast, spread with stuffing, roll and tie. Roast at 180C for 90 minutes with 1kg potatoes around it. Serve with buttered brussels sprouts.

w.note: Chewy candied pineapple chunks rolled in caster sugar
w.how: Cut 1 peeled pineapple into 3cm chunks. Simmer 400g sugar and 400ml water, add the pineapple and cook very gently for 1 hour until translucent. Drain, dry on a rack in a 90C oven for 2 hours until tacky, then roll in caster sugar.

d.note: Honey, lemon and cinnamon topped with ginger beer over ice
d.how: Stir 4 tbsp honey into 250ml warm water with the juice of a lemon and a cinnamon stick. Leave to cool and infuse for 30 minutes. Pour over ice in glasses and top up with cold ginger beer. A drink for a professor's party.

s.note: Soft eggs wrapped in sage sausage meat, crumbed and fried
s.how: Boil 4 eggs for 6 minutes, cool and peel. Mix 400g pork sausage mince with chopped sage and wrap around each egg. Roll in flour, beaten egg and panko, then fry at 170C for 6 minutes. Halve and serve with English mustard.

s.note: Twice-cooked thick chips with malt vinegar and plenty of salt
s.how: Cut 1kg potatoes into thick chips, rinse and dry well. Fry at 140C for 6 minutes until soft, then drain and rest. Fry again at 190C until golden and crisp. Tip into paper, shake over malt vinegar and plenty of sea salt flakes.

m.note: Beef and ale pie under a puff lid with mash and green peas
m.how: Brown 1kg diced beef chuck with 2 sliced onions. Add 375ml brown ale and water to cover and simmer for 3 hours until tender. Thicken, pour into a dish and top with puff pastry. Bake at 200C for 25 minutes. Serve with buttery mash and green peas.

w.note: Custard tart crowned with glossy jam-glazed blackberries
w.how: Blind bake a sweet shortcrust case until golden and cool completely. Fill with 500ml thick vanilla custard and pile 250g blackberries on top. Warm blackberry jam with a splash of water and brush over the fruit to glaze. Dust the edge with icing sugar.

d.note: Deep red cranberry and blood orange with soda over ice
d.how: Fill glasses with ice. Squeeze 4 blood oranges and pour equal parts blood orange juice and cranberry juice over the ice. Top with cold soda water and finish each with a twist of orange peel. Stir once so it swirls dark red.

s.note: Crisp bubble egg waffles, crunchy outside and soft inside
s.how: Whisk 150g flour, 2 tbsp custard powder, 2 tsp baking powder and 80g sugar. Add 2 eggs and 200ml evaporated milk plus 100ml water and whisk smooth. Rest 30 minutes. Cook in a hot greased egg waffle pan for 3 minutes a side until crisp and golden.

s.note: Fish balls simmered in coconut curry sauce and served on skewers
s.how: Fry 2 tbsp curry powder and crushed garlic in oil for a minute. Add 400ml coconut milk, a spoon of sugar and a little water and simmer 5 minutes. Add 500g fish balls and simmer for 10 minutes until hot through. Thread onto skewers and spoon over the sauce.

m.note: Wok-tossed rump with onion, capsicum and lots of cracked black pepper
m.how: Slice 600g rump steak thinly and marinate in soy and a spoon of cornflour for 20 minutes. Stir-fry hard in a very hot wok, then add sliced onion, green capsicum and garlic. Finish with oyster sauce and a big spoon of cracked black pepper. Serve over jasmine rice.

w.note: Silky wobbly egg custard tarts in flaky puff pastry
w.how: Cut puff pastry into rounds and press into a patty tin. Whisk 3 eggs with 150ml milk, 100ml evaporated milk and 80g sugar until dissolved, then strain until silky. Fill the cases and bake at 200C for 15 minutes until just set and still wobbly in the centre.

d.note: Strong strained black tea with evaporated milk, hot or iced
d.how: Simmer 6 black tea bags in 750ml water for 5 minutes until very strong. Strain through a fine cloth or sieve into a jug. Stir in evaporated milk and sugar to taste. Serve hot in cups, or chill and pour over ice in tall glasses.

s.note: Peanut butter and jam, and ham and cheese, packed in a paper bag
s.how: Spread thick white bread with peanut butter and strawberry jam for one set of sandwiches. Butter more bread and fill with sliced ham and cheddar for the other. Cut all of them into triangles and pack into a brown paper bag for lunch.

s.note: Little chocolate squares in a numbered tray with hazelnut or salt
s.how: Melt 150g dark chocolate and 150g milk chocolate separately. Spoon into small squares on baking paper or an ice cube tray. Top half with a toasted hazelnut and half with a pinch of sea salt. Set in the fridge, then line them up in a numbered tray.

m.note: Roast turkey, stuffing, mash, gravy and cranberry, done right
m.how: Brine a 1.5kg turkey breast for a few hours, then roast at 170C until it reaches 70C inside. Bake stuffing mix in a dish alongside. Mash 1kg potatoes with butter and make gravy from the pan juices and stock. Serve with cranberry sauce on proper plates.

w.note: Rich brandy fruit cake with almonds, sliced thin
w.how: Soak 1kg mixed dried fruit in 125ml brandy overnight. Cream 250g butter with 250g brown sugar, beat in 4 eggs, then fold in the fruit, 300g flour, spice and a handful of almonds. Bake in a lined tin at 150C for 2.5 hours. Cool and slice thin.

d.note: Bourbon and ginger ale over ice, or ginger ale with lime
d.how: Fill short glasses with ice. Pour 45ml bourbon into each and top with a splash of cold ginger ale. For anyone driving the sleigh, pour ginger ale over ice with a squeeze of fresh lime instead. Serve without the Santa suit.

s.note: Fanned pears and nectarines with honey, feta and pistachios
s.how: Slice 2 pears and 3 nectarines thinly and fan out on a big board. Drizzle with honey, then scatter with crumbled feta and roughly chopped toasted pistachios. Serve straight away like a market stall spread in the desert heat.

s.note: Yoghurt and cumin lamb skewers grilled fast with tahini sauce
s.how: Cut 600g lamb leg into cubes and marinate in yoghurt, cumin, crushed garlic and salt for an hour. Thread onto skewers and grill hot and fast for 6 minutes, turning. Whisk tahini with lemon juice and water until smooth and drizzle over to serve.

m.note: Harissa chicken roasted on chickpeas with flatbread and cucumber yoghurt
m.how: Rub 1kg chicken thighs with harissa, lemon juice and salt. Spread 2 cans of drained chickpeas and 2 sliced red onions in a tray and sit the chicken on top. Roast at 200C for 40 minutes. Serve with warm flatbread and cucumber yoghurt.

w.n: Duel of the Fates red and blue tart
w.note: Custard tart topped half raspberries and half blueberries
w.how: Blind bake a sweet shortcrust case and cool. Fill with 500ml thick vanilla custard. Cover one half with raspberries and the other half with blueberries, meeting in a clean line down the middle. Brush with warm apricot jam to glaze and chill.

d.note: Icy cold milk and coconut drink tinted blue
d.how: Blend 750ml cold milk with 250ml coconut milk, 2 tbsp honey and a big handful of ice until frothy. Add a few drops of blue food colouring and blend again until evenly pale blue. Pour into glasses and serve icy cold.

s.note: Cinnamon sugar puff pastry cut into little animal shapes
s.how: Cut 2 sheets of puff pastry into little animal shapes with cutters or a knife. Brush with beaten egg and sprinkle generously with cinnamon sugar. Bake at 200C for 12 minutes until puffed and golden. Cool on a rack and arrange like a bakery window.

s.note: Paprika devilled eggs and marinated olives on the bar
s.how: Boil 8 eggs for 10 minutes, cool and peel. Halve and mash the yolks with mayonnaise and Dijon until smooth, then pipe back into the whites and dust with smoked paprika. Set out on the bar beside a bowl of green olives.

m.note: Potato and cheddar dumplings fried in butter with onion and sour cream
m.how: Boil and mash 600g potatoes, then mix with 150g grated cheddar. Fill dumpling wrappers and pinch closed. Boil for 3 minutes until they float, drain, then fry in butter with sliced onion until golden on both sides. Serve with sour cream.

w.note: Flaky filo apple strudel with sultanas and cinnamon
w.how: Toss 4 sliced green apples with 80g sultanas, a teaspoon of cinnamon, sugar and a handful of breadcrumbs. Layer buttered filo sheets, spread the filling along one edge and roll up. Brush with butter and bake at 190C for 35 minutes. Dust with icing sugar.

d.note: Fresh lemonade in teacups, with gin for the grown-ups
d.how: Dissolve 100g sugar in a little hot water and cool. Squeeze 6 lemons into a jug, add the syrup, plenty of ice and top with cold soda water. Pour into teacups so it looks innocent, adding a splash of gin to the cups for the grown-ups.

s.note: Buttered popcorn, pretzels and apple slices in paper lunch bags
s.how: Pop 100g popping corn and toss with melted butter and salt. Mix with a few handfuls of pretzels. Slice 4 red apples and squeeze over a little lemon. Pack popcorn mix and apple slices into paper lunch bags, one per person, for the bus ride.

s.note: Spicy baked cauliflower bites with blue cheese dip.
s.how: Cut 1 cauliflower into florets. Toss in a batter of 3/4 cup flour, 180ml water and 1 tsp garlic powder and bake at 220C for 20 minutes. Toss in 80ml hot sauce mixed with 30g melted butter, bake 10 minutes more and serve with blue cheese dressing.

m.note: Pressed salami, ham and provolone rolls with pickles and mustard
m.how: Split 4 long bread rolls and spread with yellow mustard. Layer with salami, ham, provolone and sliced dill pickles. Press hard in a sandwich press or a heavy pan with a weight on top until flat, crisp and the cheese has melted. Cut in half to serve.

w.note: Vanilla cupcakes with red and blue swirls and a white web
w.how: Beat 125g butter with 150g sugar, then 2 eggs, then fold in 200g self-raising flour and 125ml milk. Bake at 175C for 18 minutes and cool. Pipe swirls of red and blue buttercream on top, then draw a little white icing web over each.

d.note: Sweet milk tea over chewy tapioca pearls
d.how: Cook 150g tapioca pearls as the pack says and soak in 3 tbsp brown sugar syrup. Brew 4 black tea bags in 800ml water, cool and add 250ml milk and sugar to taste. Pour over the pearls and ice.

s.note: Fried pork roll, egg and cheese on soft rolls.
s.how: Cut 400g pork roll or thick ham into 8 slices, nick the edges and fry 2 minutes a side until they curl and brown. Fry 4 eggs. Stack the pork, eggs and 4 slices American cheese into 4 soft rolls and wrap in foil for 2 minutes to melt.

s.note: Prosciutto, provolone, olives and capsicum on toothpicks with bread
s.how: Cut 150g provolone into cubes. Thread onto toothpicks with folded prosciutto, an olive and a strip of roasted red capsicum. Pile onto a board with sliced Italian bread and a small bowl of olive oil for dipping, like a stall at the market.

m.note: Beef and pork meatballs in tomato sauce over spaghetti
m.how: Mix 300g beef mince, 300g pork mince, a cup of breadcrumbs, grated parmesan, parsley and an egg. Roll into balls and brown. Add 2 cans crushed tomatoes and simmer for 40 minutes. Serve over 500g spaghetti with extra parmesan.

w.note: Crisp cannoli shells piped with orange ricotta and chocolate
w.how: Drain 500g ricotta overnight, then beat with 80g icing sugar, orange zest and 50g finely chopped dark chocolate. Spoon into a piping bag and fill 12 cannoli shells just before serving so they stay crisp. Dip each end in chopped pistachios.

d.note: Thick banana, oat and peanut butter shake, no raw eggs
d.how: Blend 2 ripe bananas with 750ml cold milk, 4 tbsp rolled oats, a big spoon of peanut butter and a drizzle of honey until thick and smooth. Pour into tall glasses. Skip the raw eggs, your training will go just fine without them.

s.note: Golden griddled haloumi drizzled with honey, thyme and lemon
s.how: Slice 2 blocks of haloumi about 1cm thick. Cook in a hot dry pan or griddle for 2 minutes a side until golden and marked. Lay on a plate, drizzle with honey, scatter with fresh thyme leaves and squeeze over a little lemon. Eat while hot.

s.note: Spinach, feta and dill filo triangles from Rosie's cookbook
s.how: Wilt 500g spinach and squeeze dry. Mix with 250g crumbled feta, 1 egg, 3 spring onions and dill. Brush 10 sheets of filo with 100g melted butter, cut into strips, fold the filling into triangles and bake at 190C for 25 minutes.

m.note: Lamb shoulder sealed with garlic, oregano, lemon and potatoes, slow roasted
m.how: Rub a 2kg lamb shoulder with garlic, oregano, lemon juice and olive oil. Sit on 1kg potato chunks, wrap tightly in baking paper and then foil. Roast at 160C for 4 hours until it falls apart. Open at the table so the steam rises.

w.note: Golden honey puffs with cinnamon and walnuts
w.how: Mix 250g flour, 7g yeast and 300ml warm water to a sticky batter and rest an hour until bubbly. Drop spoonfuls into hot oil and fry until puffed and golden. Toss in warm honey with a pinch of cinnamon and scatter with chopped walnuts.

d.note: Ouzo over ice turned cloudy and topped with lemonade
d.how: Fill 4 glasses with ice. Pour 30ml ouzo into each and watch it turn cloudy, then top with 200ml cold lemonade and a mint sprig. Make the kids' glasses with lemonade and mint only.

s.note: Garlic thyme mushrooms on sourdough toast with shaved parmesan
s.how: Slice 500g mixed mushrooms and fry in butter over high heat until golden. Add crushed garlic and thyme and cook another minute. Toast thick slices of sourdough, pile the mushrooms on top and finish with shaved parmesan and a crack of pepper.

s.note: Creamy chicken and leek in golden vol-au-vent cases
s.how: Soften a sliced leek in butter, add 300g finely diced chicken breast and cook through. Stir in 150ml cream and chopped tarragon and simmer until thick. Spoon into 16 vol-au-vent cases and bake at 200C for 10 minutes until golden and hot.

m.note: Crisp roast duck with orange and star anise glaze
m.how: Prick a 2kg duck all over, rub with salt and five-spice and roast at 180C for 1 hour 45 minutes. Simmer the juice of 2 oranges, 3 tbsp honey, 2 tbsp soy and 2 star anise until syrupy and brush over for the last 15 minutes. Serve with 300g rice.

w.note: Molten chocolate fondants with raspberry coulis running out like lava
w.how: Melt 150g dark chocolate with 150g butter. Whisk 3 eggs and 3 yolks with 80g sugar until thick, fold in the chocolate and 50g flour. Pour into greased moulds and bake at 200C for 10 minutes. Turn out and pour over a coulis of blended raspberries.

d.note: Orange and pineapple with grenadine sinking like twin suns setting
d.how: Fill tall glasses with ice. Pour in equal parts orange juice and pineapple juice, leaving room at the top. Slowly pour a splash of grenadine down the side so it sinks to the bottom and glows red and orange like a double sunset.

s.note: Honey-whipped ricotta on sourdough toast with walnuts
s.how: Beat 250g ricotta with 2 tbsp honey until light and smooth. Toast thick slices of sourdough until golden and cut into fingers. Spread with the ricotta, drizzle with more honey and scatter with chopped walnuts. Serve straight away on a wooden board.

s.note: Garlic thyme mushrooms on toasted bread with shaved parmesan
s.how: Slice 500g mixed mushrooms and fry in butter over high heat until golden. Add crushed garlic and thyme leaves and cook another minute. Toast slices of crusty bread, spoon the mushrooms on top and finish with shaved parmesan and black pepper.

m.note: Honey and fennel pork belly with golden crackling and roasted apples
m.how: Score a 1.5kg pork belly, rub with salt and crushed fennel seeds and leave uncovered overnight. Roast at 160C for 3 hours, brushing the meat side with honey. Add halved apples for the last 40 minutes, then blast at 240C until the crackling is golden.

w.note: Honey cake soaked in hot honey syrup with golden sprinkles
w.how: Beat 150g butter with 100g brown sugar and 150g honey, then beat in 3 eggs. Fold in 250g self-raising flour. Bake in a lined tin at 175C for 40 minutes. Pour over hot syrup of honey and water while still warm and finish with gold sprinkles.

d.note: Warm milk with honey and cinnamon in big wooden cups
d.how: Heat 1L milk gently until steaming but not boiling. Stir in 3 tbsp honey and a pinch of ground cinnamon until dissolved. Pour into big wooden cups or chunky mugs and dust with a little more cinnamon on top. Serve warm by the fire.

s.note: Buttery salty popcorn in big tubs like the rental counter
s.how: Heat a splash of oil in a big lidded pot and pop 100g popping corn, shaking often. Melt 80g butter and pour it all over the popcorn while tossing. Season with fine sea salt and pour into big tubs like the counter at a nineties video store.

s.note: Crumbed salmon bites baked golden with tartare for dipping
s.how: Cut 600g salmon fillet into bite-sized pieces. Dust in flour, dip in beaten egg and press into panko breadcrumbs. Spread on a lined tray, spray with a little oil and bake at 220C for 12 minutes until golden. Serve with tartare sauce. Keep them away from the cat.

m.note: Dark roux gumbo of chicken, smoked sausage and okra over rice
m.how: Cook 60g flour in 60ml oil, stirring for 20 minutes until dark brown. Add diced onion, green capsicum and celery and soften. Add 600g chicken thighs, 300g sliced smoked sausage, okra and 1.5L water. Simmer an hour and serve over long grain rice.

w.note: Sharp lemon curd pie under browned meringue
w.how: Blind bake a sweet shortcrust case. Whisk the juice and zest of 4 lemons, 200g sugar, 4 tbsp cornflour, 4 yolks and 60g butter over heat until thick, then pour into the case. Whisk the 4 whites with 150g sugar to glossy peaks, pile on top and bake at 200C for 6 minutes.

d.note: Orange and pineapple punch with lemonade and a swirl of blue
d.how: Pour 1L orange juice and 1L pineapple juice into a big jug with ice. Top with 1L cold lemonade. Add a few drops of blue food colouring and give it one slow swirl so it streaks through. Pour into glasses and serve straight away.

s.note: Chewy beef jerky marinated in soy, Worcestershire, pepper and garlic
s.how: Freeze 800g beef topside for an hour, then slice very thin across the grain. Marinate overnight in soy sauce, Worcestershire, cracked pepper and crushed garlic. Lay on racks over trays and dry in the oven at 75C for 4 hours until chewy.

s.note: Crunchy seed cracker shards with soft goat's cheese
s.how: Mix 60g each of sunflower seeds, pepitas, linseeds and sesame seeds with 40g chia and 250ml water. Rest 15 minutes, spread thin on a lined tray and bake at 160C for an hour until crunchy. Break into shards and serve with soft goat's cheese.

m.note: Thick slow-cooked beef chilli with cheddar, sour cream and beans
m.how: Brown 1kg diced beef chuck, then add a can of crushed tomatoes, a spoon of cumin, 2 chopped chipotles and water to cover. Simmer for 3 hours until it falls apart, adding 2 cans of kidney beans for the last 30 minutes. Ladle into bowls with grated cheddar.

w.note: Pavlova ring filled with cream and blackberries, edged in dark chocolate
w.how: Whisk 4 egg whites to stiff peaks, then add 220g caster sugar a spoon at a time until glossy. Pipe into a large ring and bake at 120C for 90 minutes, then cool in the oven. Fill with whipped cream and blackberries and drizzle melted dark chocolate around the edge.

d.note: Strong earl grey with honey and lemon, hot or iced
d.how: Brew 4 earl grey tea bags in a litre of freshly boiled water for 5 minutes until strong. Stir in honey to taste and add a slice of lemon to each cup. Serve hot in big mugs, or chill and pour over ice on a warm night.

s.note: Crisp lime and chilli tortilla chips with fresh tomato salsa
s.how: Cut 12 corn tortillas into wedges and fry at 180C until crisp, then toss in salt, lime zest and chilli powder. Dice 4 tomatoes and half a white onion and mix with lime juice and salt for a fresh salsa. Serve the chips warm with the salsa.

s.note: Charred corn with lime mayo, feta, chilli and coriander
s.how: Grill 4 corn cobs over high heat until charred all over. Brush with mayonnaise mixed with lime juice. Roll in crumbled feta, then sprinkle with chilli powder and chopped coriander. Serve hot with lime wedges for squeezing over at the table.

m.note: Crisp chorizo and potato tacos with avocado and pickled onion
m.how: Dice 2 chorizo and 400g potatoes and fry with a sliced white onion and a little chilli until crisp and golden. Quickly pickle more sliced onion in lime juice. Spoon into warm corn tortillas with sliced avocado, pickled onion and coriander.

w.note: Cinnamon sugar churros with warm chocolate sauce
w.how: Bring 250ml water and 60g butter to the boil, beat in 150g flour, then beat in 2 eggs. Pipe lengths into 180C oil and fry until golden. Roll in cinnamon sugar. Melt 150g dark chocolate with a splash of hot water for a sauce and serve warm.

d.note: Creamy rice and cinnamon drink served over ice
d.how: Soak 200g long grain rice and 2 cinnamon sticks in 1L water overnight. Blend until smooth, then strain through a fine cloth. Stir in 100g sugar and 250ml milk until dissolved. Chill well and pour over ice with a pinch of cinnamon on top.

s.note: Quick soda bread that rises in the oven, torn warm with butter
s.how: Mix 450g flour, a teaspoon of bicarb soda and a teaspoon of salt. Stir in 400ml buttermilk to a soft dough. Shape into a round, cut a deep cross on top and bake at 200C for 30 minutes until it rises and sounds hollow. Tear warm and serve with butter and honey.

s.note: Goat's cheese and walnut stuffed dates with dried fruit
s.how: Slit 16 medjool dates and remove the stones. Fill each with a little goat's cheese and press a walnut half on top. Drizzle with honey and arrange on a board with dried apricots and dried figs, like rations traded for a portion at the outpost.

m.note: Slow roasted paprika lamb pulled apart with flatbreads and yoghurt
m.how: Rub a 2kg lamb shoulder with crushed garlic, rosemary, smoked paprika, olive oil and salt. Roast covered at 150C for 5 hours until it pulls apart easily. Serve on a big board with warm flatbreads, garlic yoghurt and a tray of roasted vegetables.

w.note: Three-ingredient scones with jam and whipped cream
w.how: Mix 450g self-raising flour with 300ml cream and 300ml lemonade until just combined. Pat out on a floured bench, cut into rounds and bake close together at 220C for 15 minutes until risen and golden. Serve warm with strawberry jam and whipped cream.

d.note: Strong black coffee in metal mugs, or a mocha for new crew
d.how: Brew a big pot of strong black coffee and pour into metal mugs. For a mocha, stir a spoon of cocoa and a little sugar into a shot of coffee, then top with hot frothy milk. Hand them round before the jump to lightspeed.

s.note: Smoked trout on rye crispbread with creme fraiche and pickled onion
s.how: Spread rye crispbreads with creme fraiche. Flake 200g smoked trout over the top. Finish each with a sprig of dill and a few thin rings of pickled onion. Serve on a wooden board like a fisherman's supper from the lake.

s.note: Mini beef and gravy pies with puff lids and tomato sauce
s.how: Brown 500g beef mince with a diced onion, add 250ml beef stock and simmer until thick, then cool. Line a muffin tin with shortcrust rounds, fill and top with puff pastry lids. Bake at 200C for 20 minutes and serve with tomato sauce.

m.n: Erebor roast beef and Yorkshire puddings
m.note: Roast beef with Yorkshire puddings and gravy
m.how: Roast a 1.5kg beef sirloin at 220C for 20 minutes, then 180C for 40 minutes and rest. Heat oil in a muffin tin at 230C, pour in a batter of 140g flour, 4 eggs and 200ml milk and bake 20 minutes. Make gravy from the pan juices with 300ml stock.

w.note: Apple and blackberry crumble with oats and warm custard
w.how: Peel and slice 4 green apples and cook with 250g blackberries and 50g brown sugar for 5 minutes. Spoon into a dish. Rub 100g butter into oats, flour and 100g brown sugar and scatter over. Bake at 180C for 35 minutes and serve with warm custard.

d.note: A proper pot of breakfast tea with milk
d.how: Warm the teapot with boiling water and tip it out. Add 4 tea bags and fill with freshly boiled water, then steep for 4 minutes under a tea cosy. Pour into cups with a splash of milk and serve with a slice of cake at the round green door.

s.note: Bite-size ham and cheese quiches in puff pastry cases.
s.how: Cut 2 sheets puff pastry into 12 rounds and press into a greased mini muffin tray. Whisk 4 eggs with 150ml cream, then stir through 100g diced ham and 80g grated cheddar. Fill the cases and bake at 190C for 18 minutes until puffed and set.

s.note: One huge chocolate chip cookie cut into wedges at the table
s.how: Beat 125g butter with 150g brown sugar, then beat in an egg. Mix in 200g flour and 150g dark chocolate chips. Press into a greased ovenproof pan and bake at 180C for 20 minutes until golden at the edges and soft in the centre. Cut into wedges.

m.note: Chipotle lime chicken tacos with pineapple salsa and crema
m.how: Marinate 800g chicken thighs in chopped chipotle, lime juice and salt for an hour. Grill until charred and slice. Dice pineapple with a little onion and lime for salsa. Fill warm corn tortillas with the chicken, salsa and a spoon of sour cream.

w.note: Four colourful jelly layers set one at a time with cream on top
w.how: Make up raspberry jelly with half the water and pour a thin layer into clear glasses, then chill an hour. Repeat with lime, then blue, then orange jelly, letting each set before the next goes on. Top with whipped cream just before serving.

d.note: Root beer over vanilla ice cream in frosty mugs
d.how: Freeze 4 mugs for an hour. Add 2 scoops vanilla ice cream to each and pour over 300ml cold root beer slowly so it foams.

s.note: Cheddar, brie and blue cheese with oatcakes and quince by the fire
s.how: Bring 150g each of aged cheddar, brie and blue cheese to room temperature. Arrange on a wooden board with oatcakes, a slab of quince paste, sliced apple and a handful of walnuts. Set it by the fire with a glass of something warm.

s.note: Toast under bubbling cheddar, mustard and ale sauce
s.how: Melt 20g butter, stir in 1 tbsp flour and 80ml ale, then add 200g grated cheddar, 1 tsp mustard and a dash of Worcestershire until thick. Spread on 6 slices of toast and grill until bubbling.

m.note: Simple tomato and butter spaghetti with basil and lots of parmesan
m.how: Simmer 2 cans crushed tomatoes with 80g butter and a peeled halved onion for 45 minutes, stirring now and then. Remove the onion and season. Toss with 500g cooked spaghetti, then finish with torn basil and plenty of grated parmesan.

w.note: Warm date sponge soaked in toffee sauce with vanilla ice cream
w.how: Soak 200g chopped dates in 250ml boiling water with a pinch of bicarb. Cream 60g butter with 150g brown sugar, add 2 eggs, the dates and 175g self-raising flour. Bake at 180C for 35 minutes, poke holes and pour over hot toffee sauce. Serve with ice cream.

d.note: Slowly warmed red wine with orange, spices and honey
d.how: Pour a bottle of red wine into a pot with a sliced orange, 2 cinnamon sticks, 4 whole cloves, a star anise and 2 tbsp honey. Warm gently for 20 minutes, never letting it boil. Ladle into mugs by the fire with snow falling outside.

s.note: Egg, potato and chorizo breakfast tacos with red salsa
s.how: Dice 300g potatoes and fry until crisp, then add a sliced chorizo. Scramble 6 eggs softly and fold through. Warm flour tortillas, fill with the mix and grated cheddar, and top with a quick red salsa of chopped tomato, onion and chilli.

s.note: Mexican-style prawn cocktail with lime, avocado and hot sauce
s.how: Chop 400g cooked prawns and mix with 500ml cold tomato juice, the juice of 2 limes, diced avocado, finely chopped onion, coriander and a few dashes of hot sauce. Chill for 30 minutes, then spoon into glasses with crackers on the side.

m.note: Cheddar enchiladas baked in a rich chilli gravy
m.how: Make a gravy by cooking 2 tbsp flour in oil, then adding chilli powder, cumin and 500ml beef stock and simmering until thick. Roll corn tortillas around grated cheddar and diced onion, lay in a dish, pour over the gravy and more cheese. Bake at 190C for 20 minutes.

w.note: Sponge soaked in three milks with whipped cream and strawberries
w.how: Whisk 5 eggs with 200g sugar until thick, fold in 150g self-raising flour and bake at 175C for 25 minutes. Prick all over and pour over a can each of condensed and evaporated milk mixed with 125ml milk. Soak overnight, then top with whipped cream and strawberries.

d.note: Fresh watermelon and lime drink with mint over ice
d.how: Blend 1kg watermelon flesh with the juice of 2 limes, 2 tbsp sugar and 500ml cold water until smooth. Strain into a big jug and chill. Pour over ice in tall glasses with a few torn mint leaves on top. Best on a hot Texas afternoon.

s.note: Spiced grilled flatbreads with hummus, beetroot and green yoghurt dips
s.how: Brush flatbreads with olive oil and dust with sumac and a little turmeric, then grill until blistered. Blend roasted beetroot with garlic and a spoon of yoghurt for a pink dip, and stir herbs through more yoghurt for a green dip. Serve with hummus.

s.note: Chicken and ginger dumplings in hot broth with chilli oil
s.how: Mix 400g chicken mince with grated ginger, sliced spring onion and soy. Fill dumpling wrappers, pleat closed and steam for 10 minutes. Serve a few in each bowl with a ladle of hot chicken stock, more spring onion and a drizzle of chilli oil.

m.note: Saffron seafood stew in tomato, fennel and white wine with garlic toast
m.how: Soften sliced fennel and garlic in olive oil, add a pinch of saffron, a can of crushed tomatoes and a cup of white wine and simmer 20 minutes. Add 400g white fish chunks, 300g green prawns and 500g mussels, cover and cook 6 minutes. Serve with garlic toast.

w.note: Pavlova crowned with cream, mango and two passionfruit suns
w.how: Whisk 4 egg whites to stiff peaks, then add 220g caster sugar a spoon at a time until glossy. Shape into a round and bake at 120C for 90 minutes, then cool in the oven. Top with whipped cream, sliced mango and two round pools of passionfruit pulp.

d.note: Cold milk and coconut drink blended pale blue
d.how: Blend 750ml cold milk with 250ml coconut milk, 2 tbsp honey and a handful of ice until frothy. Add a few drops of blue food colouring and blend again until evenly pale blue. Pour into glasses and serve cold, the way the moisture farm does.

s.note: Bright green avocado, pea and mint dip with cucumber and crackers
s.how: Blitz 2 avocados with 200g thawed peas, the juice of 2 limes, a handful of mint and salt until smooth and very green. Spoon into a bowl and serve with cucumber sticks and water crackers. It is green, it is bold, and it is not sorry about it.

s.note: Pink meringue kisses served with fresh raspberries
s.how: Whisk 3 egg whites to stiff peaks, then add 170g caster sugar a spoon at a time until glossy. Fold in a drop of pink food colouring. Pipe small kisses onto lined trays and bake at 100C for an hour, then cool in the oven. Serve popular and pink with raspberries.

m.note: Bright green risotto of peas and spinach with butter and parmesan
m.how: Stir 300g arborio rice in butter, then add 1.25L hot stock a ladle at a time for 20 minutes. Blitz 200g peas with 100g spinach and a splash of stock until smooth. Stir through the risotto with more butter and grated parmesan until bright green.

w.note: Two-colour vanilla cake, one pink layer and one green
w.how: Beat 250g butter with 250g sugar, add 4 eggs, then fold in 250g self-raising flour. Split the batter in two, tint one pink and one green and bake in separate tins at 175C for 25 minutes. Cool and stack with vanilla buttercream made with icing sugar.

d.note: Fresh lemonade made pink with cranberry and raspberries.
d.how: Mix the juice of 6 lemons with 150g sugar until dissolved, then add 1L cold water and 100ml cranberry juice to turn it pink. Pour over ice in 4 glasses and float a few raspberries on top.

s.note: Za'atar flatbreads grilled blistered with pomegranate hummus
s.how: Brush flatbreads with olive oil and sprinkle generously with za'atar. Grill over high heat until blistered and charred in spots. Spoon hummus into a bowl, make a well and scatter with pomegranate seeds and a drizzle of oil. Tear the bread and dip.

s.note: Cucumber and egg cress finger sandwiches with the crusts off
s.how: Spread white bread with cream cheese and layer with thin cucumber slices. Hard boil 4 eggs, mash with mayonnaise and spread on more bread with mustard cress. Close the sandwiches, cut off the crusts and slice into neat fingers.

m.note: Rich chicken mole with rice and warm tortillas
m.how: Toast and soak dried chillies, then blend with almonds, garlic, a little cinnamon and stock. Simmer the sauce 15 minutes and melt in 50g dark chocolate. Add 1kg chicken thighs and simmer 40 minutes until tender. Serve with long grain rice and tortillas.

w.note: Crumbly sesame halva with chopped dates
w.how: Heat 200g honey to 120C and quickly stir into 300g tahini with a pinch of salt. Fold in 100g chopped dates, press into a lined loaf tin, chill overnight and cut into small squares.

d.note: Honey, lemon and ginger topped with soda over ice
d.how: Stir 4 tbsp honey into 250ml warm water with the juice of 2 lemons and a few slices of ginger. Leave to infuse for 30 minutes, then chill. Pour over ice and top up with cold soda water. A drink older than most civilisations.

s.note: A-shaped sumac pita crisps with a pink beetroot dip
s.how: Cut pita bread into A shapes, brush with olive oil and dust with sumac. Bake at 200C for 8 minutes until crisp. Blend 2 roasted beetroot with a crushed garlic clove and 200g Greek yoghurt, then swirl a little extra yoghurt through the top.

s.note: Warm olives with orange, lemon, garlic, chilli and fennel
s.how: Warm 150g green olives and 150g kalamata olives gently in olive oil with strips of orange and lemon peel, sliced garlic, a pinch of chilli and a teaspoon of fennel seeds for 5 minutes. Tip into a bowl and serve warm with toothpicks.

m.note: Rice noodles with egg, tofu, tamarind and peanuts
m.how: Soak 300g flat rice noodles. Fry 200g firm tofu and 2 garlic cloves, add 2 eggs and scramble. Add the noodles, 3 tbsp tamarind, 2 tbsp fish sauce and 2 tbsp brown sugar and toss. Finish with 150g bean sprouts, 60g crushed peanuts and lime.

w.note: Red velvet rounds sandwiched with cream cheese frosting
w.how: Whisk 250g flour, 2 tbsp cocoa, a teaspoon of bicarb, 150g sugar, an egg, 125ml oil, 250ml buttermilk and red colouring to a thick batter. Pipe rounds and bake at 180C for 10 minutes. Sandwich with cream cheese beaten with icing sugar.

d.note: Fresh lemonade with sliced lemons and mint in a big jug
d.how: Dissolve 150g sugar in 150ml hot water and cool. Squeeze 6 lemons into a big jug and add the syrup with 1.5L cold water. Add sliced lemon, bruised mint leaves and plenty of ice. Stir and pour into tall glasses on a sunny afternoon.

s.note: Finely chopped grilled steak in corn tortillas with salsa verde
s.how: Grill 600g skirt steak over high heat, rest and chop finely. Blend charred tomatillos with coriander, lime and a little onion for a sharp salsa verde. Pile the steak into warm corn tortillas with diced white onion, coriander and the salsa.

s.note: Thin crisp double-fried fries in paper boats with tomato sauce
s.how: Cut 1kg potatoes into thin fries and soak in cold water for an hour. Dry well, fry at 140C until soft, then fry again at 190C until golden and crisp. Toss with fine salt and serve in paper boats with tomato sauce on the side.

m.note: Red chilli pork and hominy soup with cabbage, radish and lime
m.how: Toast and soak dried chillies, then blend with garlic and a little water. Simmer 1kg pork shoulder in water for 2 hours, add the chilli sauce and a can of drained hominy and simmer another hour. Shred the pork and serve with cabbage, radish, oregano and lime.

w.note: Creamy cinnamon rice pudding finished with condensed milk
w.how: Simmer 200g short grain rice with a cinnamon stick, a strip of lemon peel and 500ml water until absorbed. Add 750ml milk and stir slowly for 30 minutes until creamy. Stir in half a can of condensed milk, remove the cinnamon and dust with ground cinnamon.

d.note: Thick vanilla malted shakes in tall glasses with straws
d.how: Blend 4 big scoops of vanilla ice cream with 500ml cold milk and 4 tbsp malted milk powder until thick and smooth. Pour into tall chilled glasses, add a straw to each and serve straight away like a fifties soda fountain.

s.note: Grilled lamb kofta skewers with harissa yoghurt dip
s.how: Mix 500g lamb mince with a grated onion, a teaspoon of cumin, chopped parsley and salt. Shape around skewers and grill over high heat until charred and cooked through. Stir a spoon of harissa through Greek yoghurt and serve as a dip.

s.note: Charred baby octopus with lemon, oregano and capers
s.how: Marinate 600g baby octopus in olive oil, lemon juice and oregano for an hour. Grill on a very hot plate for 2 to 3 minutes until charred and just tender. Pile onto a plate, scatter with capers and serve with lemon wedges.

m.note: Chicken with preserved lemon, olives, ginger and saffron over couscous
m.how: Brown 1kg chicken thighs, then soften a sliced onion with grated ginger and a pinch of saffron. Add 500ml water, chopped preserved lemon and a handful of green olives. Cover and simmer for 45 minutes until tender. Serve over fluffy couscous.

w.note: Icy Sicilian almond milk granita served with soft brioche
w.how: Blend 200g ground almonds with 800ml water and 150g sugar, stand 30 minutes and strain well. Add 1 tsp almond extract and freeze in a tray, scraping every 40 minutes for 3 hours. Serve in glasses with brioche.

d.note: Sweet green mint tea poured from a height into small glasses
d.how: Put 2 tbsp green tea leaves and a big bunch of fresh mint into a teapot with sugar to taste. Pour over a litre of just-boiled water and steep for 4 minutes. Pour from a height into small glasses so it froths, then pour back and pour again.

s.n: Scott's book signing coffee and cookies
s.note: Warm chocolate chip cookies with small cups of coffee
s.how: Beat 125g butter with 150g brown sugar and an egg. Mix in 225g flour and 150g dark chocolate chips. Roll into balls and bake at 180C for 10 minutes. Serve warm with small cups of freshly brewed coffee at the signing table.

s.note: Honey chilli roasted vegetables in strange colours with green herb dip
s.how: Halve 2 bunches of broccolini, purple carrots and radishes and toss with oil, honey and chilli flakes. Roast at 220C for 20 minutes until charred at the edges. Blend herbs into Greek yoghurt for a green dip and serve the strange colours on a dark plate.

m.note: Purple coconut black rice with grilled chicken and pickled vegetables
m.how: Simmer 300g black rice in 400ml coconut milk and water for 35 minutes until tender. Grill 800g chicken thighs and slice. Quickly pickle shredded carrot and red cabbage in rice vinegar with sugar. Serve the chicken on the purple rice with the pickles.

w.note: Mini cupcakes and one giant one, all in red buttercream
w.how: Beat 250g butter with 250g sugar, add 4 eggs, then fold in 250g self-raising flour. Bake half as mini cupcakes for 12 minutes and half as one giant cupcake for 40 minutes at 175C. Ice all of them with red buttercream made with icing sugar.

d.note: Blue flower tea swirling purple through lemonade.
d.how: Steep 2 tbsp dried butterfly pea flowers in 500ml boiling water for 5 minutes, strain and chill until deep blue. Fill 4 glasses with ice and 150ml lemonade each, then pour the blue tea over and watch it swirl purple. Add a squeeze of lemon.

s.note: Crisp chipotle beef chimichangas with sour cream and salsa
s.how: Braise 800g beef chuck with chopped chipotle and water for 3 hours, then shred. Roll small amounts with grated cheddar in small flour tortillas, folding in the sides. Fry seam side down until crisp all over. Serve with sour cream and chopped tomato salsa.

s.note: Golden potato and pea samosas with tamarind chutney
s.how: Boil and crush 600g potatoes with 150g peas and a spoon of garam masala. Cut spring roll pastry into strips, spoon filling at one end and fold into triangles. Fry in hot oil until golden and crisp. Serve with tamarind paste mixed with a little sugar and water.

m.note: Butter basted steak with chips and red wine sauce by candlelight
m.how: Cut 1kg potatoes into chips and roast until crisp. Sear 4 sirloin steaks in a very hot pan, add butter and baste for a minute, then rest. Add 150ml red wine and 250ml beef stock to the pan and reduce until glossy. Slice and serve by candlelight.

w.note: Baked cheesecake with a glossy red raspberry coulis
w.how: Crush 250g sweet biscuits with 100g melted butter and press into a tin. Beat 500g cream cheese with 150g sugar, then beat in 3 eggs. Pour over and bake at 160C for 50 minutes, then cool in the oven. Top with raspberries simmered with sugar and pushed through a sieve.

d.note: Strong cold brew coffee over ice, black, no fuss
d.how: Stir 100g coarsely ground coffee into 1L cold water in a jug. Cover and leave in the fridge for 12 hours. Strain through a fine sieve lined with paper. Pour over ice, black and strong, and drink it without making a fuss about it.

s.note: Cinnamon sugar pretzel bites with cream cheese dip
s.how: Mix 500g flour, 7g yeast and 300ml warm water to a dough and rest an hour. Cut into bites, boil briefly in water with bicarb soda and bake at 220C for 12 minutes. Brush with butter and roll in cinnamon sugar. Serve with sweetened cream cheese.

s.note: Parmesan and garlic popcorn in paper bags for flipping comics
