s.how: Pop 100g popping corn and toss straight away with 60g melted butter. Sprinkle with finely grated parmesan and garlic powder, tossing until every piece is coated. Pour into paper bags so you can eat while flipping through the new issues.

m.note: Glazed teriyaki chicken over rice with stir-fried broccoli
m.how: Simmer soy sauce, mirin, a spoon of sugar and grated ginger until syrupy. Grill 800g chicken thighs, brushing with the glaze until sticky and charred. Slice over steamed jasmine rice with quickly stir-fried broccoli and spoon over the extra sauce.

w.note: Big soft chocolate chip cookies with gooey middles
w.how: Beat 125g butter with 150g brown sugar and an egg until creamy. Mix in 225g flour and 200g dark chocolate chips. Roll into big balls and bake at 180C for 10 minutes so the centres stay gooey. Cool for 5 minutes and serve warm.

d.note: Strawberry lemonade with soda in big cups over ice
d.how: Muddle a handful of strawberries in the bottom of a big jug. Add the juice of 6 lemons and sugar syrup to taste, then top with cold soda water. Pour into big cups packed with ice and add a straw to each.

s.note: Peanut butter and strawberry jam triangles, crusts off, for once matching
s.how: Spread 12 slices of thick white bread with 250g smooth peanut butter on half and 250g strawberry jam on the other half. Press together into 6 sandwiches, cut off the crusts and cut each into 4 triangles. Stack on a plate for the porch.

s.note: Little beef sliders topped with grilled ham and melted cheese
s.how: Shape 500g beef mince into 12 small patties and season well. Cook on a hot pan for 2 minutes a side, then top each with a folded slice of ham browned in the pan and half a cheese slice, cover for 1 minute to melt. Put in 12 slider buns with pickles.

m.note: Sticky barbecue drumsticks with buttered corn and potato salad
m.how: Toss 12 chicken drumsticks with salt, pepper and 2 tsp smoked paprika and roast at 200C for 30 minutes. Brush with 250ml barbecue sauce and grill or roast 15 minutes more, basting twice, until sticky. Boil 4 corn cobs for 6 minutes, roll in 40g butter and serve with 500g potato salad.

w.n: Big Worm's ice cream truck cones
w.note: Vanilla cones dipped in hard-set chocolate, cornflakes and sprinkles
w.how: Melt 200g dark chocolate with 3 tbsp coconut oil and let it cool to room temperature. Scoop 1L vanilla ice cream into 8 cones, freeze them for 20 minutes, then dip each top in the chocolate and roll straight away in 40g crushed cornflakes mixed with 2 tbsp sprinkles. Freeze until serving.

d.n: Red drink, with sugar this time
d.note: Homemade red strawberry and cherry drink, properly sweetened, in big cups
d.how: Blend 250g strawberries with 150g caster sugar and the juice of 2 lemons, then strain into a big jug. Add 500ml cherry juice and 1L cold water and stir until the sugar is gone. Pour over plenty of ice in big plastic cups.

s.note: Crisp herb falafel with tahini sauce
s.how: Soak 250g dried chickpeas overnight, then blitz with a chopped onion, garlic, parsley and a teaspoon of cumin. Shape into balls and fry at 180C until deep golden. Whisk tahini with lemon juice and water until smooth and drizzle over to serve.

s.note: Chocolate-dipped dates stuffed with almond butter and pistachios
s.how: Slit 16 medjool dates and remove the stones. Fill each with a teaspoon of almond butter and press closed. Dip halfway into melted dark chocolate and roll the chocolate end in crushed pistachios. Set on baking paper in the fridge for 20 minutes.

m.note: Lentils, rice and macaroni under spicy tomato sauce and crispy onions
m.how: Cook 200g brown lentils, 200g rice and 200g macaroni separately. Simmer a can of crushed tomatoes with garlic, chilli and a splash of vinegar. Fry 2 sliced onions until dark and crisp. Layer lentils, rice, pasta and chickpeas, then top with sauce and onions.

w.n: Book of the Dead honey pastries
w.note: Cinnamon walnut filo pastries soaked in honey syrup
w.how: Layer buttered filo sheets in a tin with chopped walnuts mixed with cinnamon between every few layers. Cut into diamonds and bake at 180C for 40 minutes until golden. Pour over warm honey syrup with lemon juice and leave for several hours to soak.

d.note: Deep red chilled hibiscus tea with lime over ice
d.how: Steep 30g dried hibiscus flowers in 1L just-boiled water with 100g sugar for 15 minutes. Strain into a jug and chill well. Pour over ice in tall glasses with a squeeze of lime. It turns a deep ruby red, perfect for a desert night.

s.note: Roasted nuts with apricots and chocolate chips in paper bags
s.how: Roast 150g almonds and 150g cashews at 180C for 10 minutes and cool. Mix with 150g chopped dried apricots and 100g dark chocolate chips. Portion into small paper bags so everyone has a stash to pull from a vest pocket during the film.

s.note: Quick dill pickles with rye bread and salted butter
s.how: Slice 4 Lebanese cucumbers into spears and pack into a jar with dill and sliced garlic. Pour over 250ml white vinegar heated with 250ml water, a spoon of sugar and a spoon of salt. Chill overnight. Serve with thick rye bread and salted butter.

m.note: Seared beef strips in paprika mushroom sour cream sauce over noodles
m.how: Sear 600g thinly sliced rump in batches and set aside. Cook a sliced onion and 300g mushrooms until golden, add a spoon of sweet paprika, then stir in 300ml sour cream and return the beef. Warm through without boiling and serve over buttered egg noodles.

w.note: Black sesame butter cookies half dipped in white chocolate.
w.how: Grind 50g black sesame seeds fine. Beat 150g butter with 80g sugar, add 200g flour and the sesame and roll into a log. Chill 30 minutes, slice into 20 rounds and bake at 170C for 12 minutes. Dip half of each in 100g melted white chocolate.

d.note: Strong black tea in glasses with a spoon of jam stirred in
d.how: Brew a strong pot of black tea with 4 tea bags and a litre of boiling water for 5 minutes. Pour into heatproof glasses and stir a spoon of strawberry jam into each. Add a slice of lemon if you like and serve hot.

s.note: Little baked cheese and chive omelettes from a muffin tin
s.how: Whisk 8 eggs with 100ml milk, 100g grated cheddar, snipped chives and salt. Butter a 12-hole muffin tin and pour the mix in evenly. Bake at 180C for 15 minutes until puffed and just set. Ease out with a knife and serve warm.

s.note: Brown butter cookies rolled in raw sugar like grains of sand
s.how: Brown 200g butter until nutty and cool until firm. Beat with 150g brown sugar, then mix in 280g flour. Roll into logs, coat in raw sugar and chill for an hour. Slice into rounds and bake at 170C for 15 minutes until golden and sandy.

m.note: Coq au vin with bacon and mushrooms over buttery mash
m.how: Brown 1kg chicken thighs and 150g diced bacon. Add 250g mushrooms and cook until golden, then pour in 500ml red wine and enough water to cover. Simmer for 90 minutes until rich and glossy. Serve over mash from 1kg potatoes and plenty of butter.

w.note: Vanilla custards with a torched crackling sugar top
w.how: Heat 600ml cream with a split vanilla bean until steaming. Whisk 6 yolks with 80g sugar, pour in the cream and strain into 4 ramekins. Bake in a water bath at 150C for 35 minutes and chill. Sprinkle with sugar and torch until amber and crackly.

d.note: Sparkling wine or apple fizz with a raspberry in each glass
d.how: Chill a bottle of sparkling wine and a bottle of sparkling apple juice for at least an hour. Drop a fresh raspberry into each flute. Pour the sparkling wine for the grown-ups and the apple juice for everyone else, and watch the bubbles lift the berries.

s.note: Frozen chocolate banana slices rolled in crushed peanuts
s.how: Slice 3 bananas into thick rounds. Melt 150g dark chocolate and dip each slice halfway, then roll the chocolate side in crushed peanuts. Lay on a lined tray and freeze for 30 minutes until set. Serve straight from the freezer.

s.note: Pineapple, mango, papaya and lychee cups with lime and chilli salt
s.how: Cube half a pineapple, a mango and half a papaya and mix with a drained can of lychees. Spoon into cups, squeeze over lime juice and scatter with torn mint. Finish each cup with a pinch of salt mixed with chilli for a little kick.

m.note: Thick paprika beef goulash with capsicum over buttered noodles
m.how: Brown 1kg diced beef chuck, then add 2 sliced onions and 3 tbsp sweet paprika and stir for a minute. Add a can of crushed tomatoes, a sliced red capsicum and water to cover. Simmer for 3 hours until thick and serve over buttered egg noodles.

w.note: Green jelly glasses with kiwifruit and grapes and a gem on top
w.how: Make up 2 packets of lime jelly and pour into clear glasses with diced kiwifruit and halved green grapes. Chill for 3 hours until set. Top with whipped cream and finish each glass with one perfect green grape like a jewel.

d.note: Watermelon, lime and mint blended and strained over ice
d.how: Blend 1kg watermelon flesh with the juice of 2 limes and a handful of mint until smooth. Strain into a jug and chill well. Pour over ice in tall glasses with a fresh mint sprig on top. Cool relief after crossing the dunes.

s.note: Little glazed meatballs on sticks in a sticky sauce
s.how: Mix 500g pork and beef mince with 1 egg, 40g breadcrumbs and salt, roll into 30 balls and bake at 200C for 15 minutes. Simmer 250ml sweet chilli sauce with 150g grape jelly until glossy, add the meatballs and coat. Serve on toothpicks.

s.note: Dill cream cheese and smoked salmon pinwheels
s.how: Mix 250g cream cheese with chopped dill and lemon zest and spread over 4 large tortillas. Lay 200g smoked salmon over, roll up tightly, wrap and chill 1 hour, then slice into 2cm pinwheels.

m.note: Seared eye fillet with red wine sauce, potato gratin and asparagus
m.how: Layer thinly sliced potatoes with cream and bake at 180C for an hour. Sear 4 eye fillet steaks hard in butter, then roast at 200C to 54C and rest. Deglaze the pan with red wine and stock and reduce until glossy. Serve with charred asparagus.

w.note: Spiced sweet potato pie with whipped cream on top
w.how: Roast 800g sweet potatoes until soft, then mash with 60g butter, 150g brown sugar, 2 eggs, 200ml evaporated milk, nutmeg and vanilla. Pour into a blind-baked sweet shortcrust case and bake at 170C for 50 minutes. Cool and top with whipped cream.

d.note: Gin, lemon and sugar topped with sparkling wine
d.how: Shake 30ml gin, 15ml lemon juice and 10ml sugar syrup with ice and strain into 4 flutes. Top each with 90ml cold sparkling wine and add a lemon twist.

s.note: Sugared strawberries with whipped cream for dipping.
s.how: Hull and halve 2 punnets strawberries and toss with 1 tbsp caster sugar and a squeeze of lemon. Whip 300ml thickened cream with 1 tbsp icing sugar to soft peaks and serve in a bowl beside the berries for dipping.

s.note: Beef and pork dumplings tossed in butter and dill with sour cream
s.how: Mix 250g beef mince and 250g pork mince with salt and pepper. Fill dumpling wrappers and pinch into little round parcels. Boil until they float, then a minute more. Toss in melted butter and chopped dill and serve with plenty of sour cream.

m.note: Miso honey glazed salmon over rice with edamame and avocado
m.how: Mix 2 tbsp white miso with 2 tbsp honey and brush over 4 salmon fillets. Roast at 200C for 12 minutes until glazed. Serve over cooked sushi rice with thawed edamame, sliced avocado and a little pickled ginger.

w.note: Glazed yeast doughnuts, some with sprinkles
w.how: Mix 500g flour, 7g yeast, 50g melted butter, 2 eggs and 250ml warm milk into a soft dough and prove an hour. Roll, cut into rings and prove again. Fry at 175C until golden. Dip in a glaze of icing sugar and milk and add sprinkles to some.

d.note: Glowing blue lemonade over crushed ice with lime
d.how: Fill glasses with crushed ice. Add 30ml blue curacao for the grown-ups, or a splash of blue cordial for everyone else, then top with cold lemonade. Squeeze in a wedge of lime and stir so it glows bright blue like a reactor core.

s.note: Whipped ricotta toasts topped with honey thyme cherries
s.how: Slice a baguette and toast until golden. Simmer 300g frozen cherries with 2 tbsp honey and thyme for 8 minutes until jammy, then cool. Whip 250g ricotta until smooth, spread on the toasts and spoon the cherries on top.

s.note: Smoky honey barbecue wings baked crisp
s.how: Toss 1kg chicken wings with smoked paprika and salt and bake at 220C for 45 minutes until crisp. Warm 125ml barbecue sauce with 2 tbsp honey and 30g butter until glossy. Toss the wings through the glaze and serve with plenty of napkins.

m.note: Dark roux gumbo with chicken, smoked sausage and okra over rice
m.how: Cook 60g flour in 60ml oil for 20 minutes, stirring, until dark brown. Add diced onion, green capsicum and celery and soften. Add 600g chicken thighs, 300g sliced smoked sausage, okra and 1.5L water. Simmer for an hour and serve over long grain rice.

w.note: Pavlova with cream, cherries and pale pink rose petals
w.how: Whisk 4 egg whites to stiff peaks, then add 220g caster sugar a spoon at a time until glossy. Shape into a round and bake at 120C for 90 minutes, then cool in the oven. Top with whipped cream, cherries cooked briefly with sugar and pale pink rose petals.

d.note: Fresh strawberry and lemon soda over ice
d.how: Blitz 250g strawberries with 3 tbsp sugar and the juice of 1 lemon and strain. Divide between 4 glasses of ice and top with 200ml soda water each.

s.note: Soft salted pretzels with butter and yellow mustard
s.how: Mix 500g flour, 7g yeast and 300ml warm water to a dough and rest an hour. Shape into pretzels, dip in boiling water with 2 tbsp bicarb soda and sprinkle with rock salt. Bake at 220C for 12 minutes, brush with butter and serve with yellow mustard.

s.note: Marinated bocconcini pearls with cherry tomatoes on toothpicks
s.how: Toss 250g bocconcini pearls with olive oil, torn basil and a pinch of chilli flakes and leave for an hour. Thread onto toothpicks with cherry tomatoes. Arrange on a dark plate like a string of stolen pearls and drizzle over the leftover oil.

m.note: Meatballs in tomato sauce in a roll with provolone
m.how: Mix 500g beef mince, 1 egg, 40g breadcrumbs and 30g parmesan and roll 16 meatballs. Brown, then simmer in 700g passata for 20 minutes. Fill 4 long rolls, top with provolone slices and grill until melted.

w.note: Vanilla gelato drowned in hot espresso with amaretti
w.how: Brew a strong pot of espresso. Put a big scoop of vanilla ice cream into each glass and set out a few amaretti biscuits alongside. At the table, pour a hot shot of espresso over each scoop and eat straight away while it melts.

d.note: Short strong espresso with a twist of lemon peel
d.how: Brew short, strong espresso and pour into small warmed cups. Peel thin strips of lemon zest and set one on each saucer to twist over the coffee if wanted. Serve it quietly, the way a butler who has seen it all would.

s.note: Golden oat and chocolate chip cookies, best stolen warm
s.how: Cream 125g butter with 150g brown sugar and a teaspoon of vanilla, then beat in an egg. Fold in 150g flour, 100g rolled oats and 150g dark chocolate chips. Roll into balls and bake at 180C for 12 minutes until golden at the edges.

s.note: Cucumber rounds with smoked salmon and little egg finger sandwiches
s.how: Slice 2 Lebanese cucumbers into thick rounds and top each with cream cheese, a fold of smoked salmon and a sprig of dill. Hard boil 4 eggs, mash with salt and spread on white bread. Cut off the crusts and slice into fingers.

m.note: Rosemary lamb chops with buttered mash, peas and mint sauce
m.how: Rub 8 lamb loin chops with rosemary, garlic and salt. Grill for 3 minutes a side and rest. Boil 800g potatoes and mash with butter. Cook peas and serve everything with a spoon of mint sauce, in peace, with no interruptions at all.

w.note: Lattice-topped cinnamon apple pie with vanilla ice cream
w.how: Cook 6 sliced green apples with 50g butter, 100g brown sugar and a teaspoon of cinnamon until just soft, then cool. Line a pie dish with shortcrust, fill and weave a lattice on top. Bake at 190C for 45 minutes and serve warm with ice cream.

d.note: Fresh lemonade with a strawberry in each glass
d.how: Dissolve 150g sugar in 150ml hot water and cool. Squeeze 6 lemons into a jug, add the syrup and 1.5L cold water and stir. Pour into tall glasses over ice and drop a halved strawberry into each. Serve in the backyard on a hot afternoon.

s.note: Honey hot sauce wings baked crisp
s.how: Leave 1kg chicken wings uncovered in the fridge overnight, then toss with garlic powder and salt. Bake at 220C for 45 minutes until crisp. Melt 50g butter with 3 tbsp honey and a good splash of hot sauce and toss the wings through until glossy.

s.note: Creamy deviled eggs with mustard, relish and paprika
s.how: Boil 8 eggs for 10 minutes, cool and peel. Halve and whip the yolks with mayonnaise, yellow mustard, a spoon of sweet relish and a dash of hot sauce. Pipe back into the whites and dust with smoked paprika. Keep chilled until the show starts.

m.note: Baked macaroni in a sharp cheddar custard with a golden top
m.how: Boil 500g macaroni for 2 minutes less than the packet says and drain. Whisk 2 eggs with a can of evaporated milk, 60g melted butter and a teaspoon of mustard powder. Mix with the pasta and 300g grated cheddar, top with more cheese and bake at 180C for 40 minutes.

w.note: Dense lemon pound cake with lemon glaze
w.how: Beat 250g butter and 250g sugar until pale, add 4 eggs and the zest of 2 lemons, then fold in 250g plain flour and 1 tsp baking powder. Bake in a loaf tin at 160C for 60 minutes. Pour over 120g icing sugar mixed with 3 tbsp lemon juice.

d.note: Lime juice, cherry syrup and lemonade over ice
d.how: Fill 4 glasses with crushed ice. Add the juice of half a lime and 2 tbsp maraschino cherry syrup to each, top with 200ml lemonade and add a cherry.

s.note: Crisp paprika sweet potato sticks thin as twigs
s.how: Cut 800g sweet potatoes into thin sticks and toss with a little oil, smoked paprika and salt. Spread in a single layer on lined trays without crowding. Bake at 220C for 25 minutes, turning once, until crisp at the edges. Pile into a little pot.

s.note: Golden saffron arancini with melting mozzarella centres
s.how: Cook 300g arborio rice with stock and a pinch of saffron into a risotto, stir in parmesan and chill overnight. Roll into balls around small cubes of mozzarella. Coat in beaten egg and panko and fry at 180C until perfectly golden all over.

m.note: Beef braised in stout with smoked paprika and crusty bread
m.how: Brown 1kg diced beef chuck, then add 2 sliced onions, 2 carrots and a spoon of smoked paprika. Pour in 375ml stout and enough water to cover. Simmer for 3 hours until thick and tender. Serve in big bowls with crusty bread.

w.note: Ice cream with chocolate sauce and crackling popping candy
w.how: Heat 150ml cream until steaming and pour over 150g chopped dark chocolate, stirring until smooth. Scoop vanilla ice cream into bowls and pour over the warm sauce. Scatter popping candy on top at the table so it crackles like fireworks.

d.note: Pear and passionfruit nectar with mint
d.how: Mix 800ml pear nectar with the pulp of 4 passionfruit. Pour over crushed ice in 4 glasses and top each with a mint sprig. Serve straight away while it is still ice cold.

s.note: Tall stack of buttermilk pancakes with bacon and maple
s.how: Whisk 250g flour, 2 tsp baking powder, 2 eggs and 375ml buttermilk to a thick batter. Cook small pancakes in butter until golden. Fry 8 rashers of bacon until crisp. Stack the pancakes high with bacon between them and pour over maple syrup.

s.note: Smoked salmon on rye crispbread with dill and pickled onion
s.how: Spread rye crispbreads with creme fraiche. Top each with a fold of smoked salmon, a sprig of dill and a few thin rings of pickled onion. Lay them out on a slate and serve cold, like a snack in a fishing village on the edge of the world.

m.note: Lemon and oregano roast lamb with tomato, cucumber and feta salad
m.how: Rub a 2kg lamb leg with lemon juice, crushed garlic, oregano, olive oil and salt. Roast at 180C for 90 minutes, then rest for 15 minutes. Toss chopped tomatoes, cucumber and crumbled feta with olive oil and lemon and serve with the sliced lamb.

w.note: Salted caramel sundae with popping candy scattered on top
w.how: Melt 150g sugar to an amber caramel, then whisk in 150ml cream and 30g butter with a pinch of salt. Scoop vanilla ice cream into bowls and pour over the warm caramel. Scatter with popping candy just before serving so it crackles.

d.note: Whisky over ice, or ginger ale with lime
d.how: Fill short glasses with ice. Pour 45ml whisky over the ice for those drinking. For everyone else, pour ginger ale over ice with a squeeze of fresh lime. Raise a glass to the deep and drink it like a king of the sea.

s.note: Cream cheese crackers dotted with black olives like puppies
s.how: Spread 24 water crackers with cream cheese. Chop black olives into small pieces and dot them over each cracker like spots. Add a tiny snip of chive for a tail and lay them out in long rows on a platter like a litter of puppies.

s.note: Pale golden shortbread with small glasses of cold milk
s.how: Beat 250g butter with 100g caster sugar, then mix in 300g plain flour and 50g rice flour. Press into a tin, prick all over and bake at 160C for 20 minutes until pale gold. Cut into fingers while warm. Serve with small glasses of cold milk.

m.note: Lamb mince pie under golden buttery mash
m.how: Brown 800g lamb mince with a diced onion and 2 grated carrots. Add a cup of peas and 250ml stock and simmer for 30 minutes until thick. Spread in a dish, top with buttery mash from 1kg potatoes and bake at 200C for 25 minutes until golden.

w.note: Soft vanilla cookies iced half vanilla and half chocolate, spotty style
w.how: Beat 125g butter with 150g sugar and an egg, then mix in 300g self-raising flour and 125ml buttermilk. Spoon rounds onto trays and bake at 180C for 12 minutes. Ice half of each with vanilla glaze and half with chocolate glaze made with cocoa.

d.note: Strong pot of breakfast tea with milk and raw sugar
d.how: Warm a teapot with boiling water and tip it out. Add 4 tea bags and pour over a litre of freshly boiled water. Steep for 4 minutes until strong. Pour into cups and set milk and raw sugar on the side, the way Nanny would.

s.note: Cheese board with crackers and grapes, enough to tempt any mouse
s.how: Arrange string cheese, wedges of aged cheddar, gouda and blue cheese on a wooden board. Add water crackers, a bunch of green grapes and a little bowl of nuts. Leave one small wedge of cheese on its own at the edge of the board as bait.

s.note: Cheese toasties cut into wedges with holes poked in the top
s.how: Butter 8 slices of white bread on the outside. Fill with grated cheddar and gruyere and cook in a pan until golden and melting. Cut each into cheese-shaped wedges and poke a few holes in the top with a chopstick so they look like proper cartoon cheese.

m.note: Spinach and ricotta stuffed chicken with mushroom sauce and gratin
m.how: Cut a pocket in 4 chicken breasts and fill with wilted spinach mixed with ricotta. Sear, then roast at 200C for 20 minutes. Cook sliced mushrooms in butter, add 200ml cream and simmer until thick. Serve with potato gratin baked in more cream.

w.note: Baked vanilla cheesecake with lemon curd on top
w.how: Crush 250g sweet biscuits with 100g melted butter and press into a tin. Beat 500g cream cheese with 150g sugar, then beat in 3 eggs. Pour over and bake at 160C for 50 minutes, then cool in the oven. Spread with lemon curd before serving.

d.note: Honey vanilla milk in small glasses with a cheese biscuit
d.how: Pour 1L cold milk into a jar with 2 tbsp honey and a drop of vanilla. Put the lid on and shake hard until frothy. Pour into small glasses and set a little cheese biscuit beside each one, just in case anyone small comes looking.

s.note: Cast iron cornbread with bacon, baked hot and crisp
s.how: Fry 4 rashers of bacon until crisp, chop and keep the fat in the pan. Mix 150g cornmeal, 100g flour, 2 tsp baking powder, an egg and 300ml buttermilk. Stir in the bacon, pour into the hot greased pan and bake at 220C for 20 minutes. Serve with butter.

s.note: Pink beetroot pickled eggs like a jar on the saloon bar
s.how: Boil 8 eggs for 10 minutes, cool and peel. Heat 250ml white vinegar with the juice from a can of beetroot, 2 tbsp sugar, a teaspoon of mustard seeds and peppercorns. Pour over the eggs in a jar with the beetroot and pickle in the fridge for 3 days.

m.n: Rainy night beef and bean stew
m.note: Slow braised beef with chilli, tomato and kidney beans
m.how: Brown 1kg diced beef chuck, then add a sliced onion, crushed garlic and 2 crumbled dried chillies. Pour in a can of crushed tomatoes and water to cover. Braise at 160C for 3 hours, adding 2 cans of drained kidney beans for the last 30 minutes.

w.n: Big Whiskey bread pudding with whiskey sauce
w.note: Spiced raisin bread pudding with warm whiskey butter sauce
w.how: Tear 400g day-old bread into a dish with 80g raisins. Whisk 4 eggs, 600ml milk, 120g brown sugar and 1 tsp cinnamon, pour over and soak 20 minutes, then bake at 170C for 45 minutes. Melt 80g butter with 100g sugar and 100ml cream, simmer 2 minutes and stir in 40ml whiskey. Pour over to serve.

d.note: Black coffee boiled in a pot and poured into tin mugs
d.how: Bring a litre of water to the boil in a pot and stir in a big handful of coarse ground coffee. Simmer for 2 minutes, then take off the heat and add a splash of cold water to settle the grounds. Pour carefully into tin mugs and drink it black.

s.note: Lime-cured prawns on corn tostadas with smashed avocado
s.how: Dice 400g green prawns and cover with the juice of 4 limes for 20 minutes until opaque. Drain and toss with diced red onion and coriander. Spread smashed avocado on crisp corn tostadas and pile the prawns on top just before serving.

s.note: Crisp plantain chips with a spicy chilli peanut dip
s.how: Peel 3 green plantains and slice very thin. Fry at 180C in batches until crisp and golden, then salt well. Whisk 4 tbsp peanut butter with warm water, a pinch of chilli flakes and a squeeze of lime to a smooth dip and serve alongside.

m.note: Achiote and citrus pork slow cooked in banana leaves with tortillas
m.how: Blend achiote paste with the juice of 2 oranges and 2 limes and rub over 1.5kg pork shoulder. Wrap in banana leaves and roast covered at 150C for 4 hours until it falls apart. Shred and serve in corn tortillas with lime-pickled red onion.

w.note: Baked coconut custard under dark caramel
w.how: Melt 150g sugar to a deep caramel and pour into a 20cm dish. Blend 400ml coconut milk, 395g condensed milk, 4 eggs and 1 tsp vanilla and pour in. Bake in a water bath at 160C for 50 minutes, chill overnight and turn out.

d.note: Coconut and pineapple cooler tinted ocean blue
d.how: Fill tall glasses with ice. Pour in equal parts coconut water and pineapple juice, then add a drop of blue food colouring and stir until ocean blue. Squeeze in a wedge of lime and serve cold, deep as the sea beneath Talokan.

s.note: Egg, bacon and cheese muffins wrapped to eat on the run
s.how: Fry 4 rashers of bacon until crisp and fry 4 eggs until just set. Split and toast 4 English muffins and butter them. Fill each with bacon, an egg and a slice of cheddar, then wrap tightly in paper so the cheese melts on the way.

s.note: Chilli lime butter popcorn ready in a flash
s.how: Pop 100g popping corn in a big lidded pot. Melt 60g butter with the zest of a lime and a pinch of chilli flakes. Pour over the popcorn while tossing hard so every piece is coated, then squeeze over a little lime juice and serve straight away.

m.note: Slow tomato, garlic and basil sauce over spaghetti with parmesan
m.how: Soften a diced onion and crushed garlic in olive oil. Add 2 cans crushed tomatoes and simmer gently for 45 minutes. Stir in torn basil and season. Toss through 500g cooked spaghetti and finish with grated parmesan, just like the family kitchen.

w.note: Fudgy brownies with a yellow icing lightning bolt on each
w.how: Melt 200g dark chocolate with 150g butter, whisk in 250g sugar and 3 eggs, then fold in 100g flour. Bake at 170C for 25 minutes and cool. Cut into squares and pipe a yellow lightning bolt of icing sugar mixed with a drop of colouring on each.

d.note: Orange and lemon with a pinch of salt over ice
d.how: Mix 500ml orange juice with the juice of 2 lemons and a small pinch of salt in a big jug. Top up with 1L cold water and plenty of ice. Stir well and pour fast, before anyone else gets there first.

s.note: Hot puffed beignets buried under icing sugar
s.how: Mix 500g flour, 7g yeast, 2 eggs, 50g melted butter and 250ml evaporated milk with warm water to a soft dough and prove 2 hours. Roll out, cut into squares and fry at 180C until puffed and golden. Bury under icing sugar and serve hot.

s.note: Pressed cob loaf of salami, ham, provolone and olive salad
s.how: Chop green olives and giardiniera together for an olive salad. Hollow a cob loaf slightly and layer with olive salad, salami, ham and provolone, then more olive salad. Wrap tightly, press under a heavy weight overnight and cut into small wedges.

m.note: Garlic bacon Cajun prawns over creamy cheesy polenta
m.how: Simmer 200g polenta in 1L water, stirring, until thick, then beat in grated cheddar. Fry 150g diced bacon until crisp, add crushed garlic and 500g peeled green prawns with Cajun seasoning and cook 3 minutes. Spoon over the polenta with spring onion.

w.note: Flamed rum bananas in butterscotch over vanilla ice cream
w.how: Melt 60g butter with 80g brown sugar and a pinch of cinnamon until bubbling. Add 4 halved bananas and cook 2 minutes. Pour in 60ml dark rum and carefully light it, letting the flames die down. Spoon over bowls of vanilla ice cream straight away.

d.note: Strong coffee and hot milk, half and half, New Orleans style.
d.how: Brew 500ml strong coffee from 50g dark-roast ground coffee, chicory blend if you can get it. Heat 500ml milk until steaming and frothy. Pour coffee and milk into 4 mugs at the same time, half and half.

s.note: Bright green avocado, pea and feta dip with pita crisps
s.how: Blitz 2 avocados with 200g thawed peas, the juice of 2 limes, a handful of mint and 100g feta until smooth and very green. Cut pita bread into wedges, brush with oil and bake until crisp. Serve the goo with the crisps and some sugar snap peas.

s.note: Light cheddar and paprika choux puffs, puffed and hollow
s.how: Bring 250ml water and 100g butter to the boil, beat in 150g flour until smooth, then beat in 4 eggs one at a time. Stir in 100g grated cheddar and a pinch of paprika. Pipe small balls onto trays and bake at 200C for 20 minutes until puffed and hollow.

m.note: Lemon thyme roast chicken with buttered potatoes and green beans
m.how: Rub 4 chicken breasts with lemon juice, thyme, oil and salt. Roast at 200C for 20 minutes with 800g halved baby potatoes started 20 minutes earlier. Steam green beans and toss everything with butter. The dinner he should have been at, three times over.

w.note: Wobbling green lime jelly ring with cream and kiwifruit
w.how: Make up 3 packets of lime jelly with a little less water than the packet says so it holds its shape. Pour into a ring mould and chill overnight. Dip the mould briefly in hot water and turn out wobbling onto a plate. Fill the centre with cream and sliced kiwifruit.

d.note: Lime lemonade spiders with floating vanilla ice cream
d.how: Pour a splash of lime cordial into tall glasses and top with cold lemonade. Gently add a scoop of vanilla ice cream so it floats and foams up green. Serve straight away with a long spoon and a straw before it bubbles over like an experiment.

s.note: Salami, provolone, olives, artichokes and capsicum with crusty bread
s.how: Fold 150g salami and slices of provolone onto a big board. Warm 200g olives gently in olive oil and spoon over. Add marinated artichoke hearts, strips of roasted red capsicum and torn Italian bread for mopping up the oil.

s.note: Date, oat and peanut butter bites rolled in coconut
s.how: Blitz 250g pitted medjool dates, 100g rolled oats, 3 tbsp peanut butter, 2 tbsp cocoa and a pinch of salt in a food processor until it clumps. Roll into small balls, coat in desiccated coconut and chill for an hour. Fuel for the next round.

m.note: Shaved rib eye with onions, capsicum and provolone in long rolls
m.how: Freeze a 600g rib eye steak for 30 minutes and shave it paper thin. Fry sliced onion and green capsicum on a hot plate until soft, add the beef and sear fast. Lay provolone over the top to melt, then scoop into split long bread rolls.

w.note: Three-colour almond sponge layers with apricot jam and chocolate
w.how: Beat 250g almond meal, 4 eggs, 200g sugar and 200g melted butter. Split in three, tint one green and one red, and bake each in a thin layer at 175C for 12 minutes. Stack with apricot jam between, press overnight, spread with melted chocolate and slice.

d.note: Lemon, honey and salt water in a squeeze bottle on ice
d.how: Squeeze 2 lemons into a large squeeze bottle. Add a spoon of honey and a small pinch of salt, then top up with cold water. Shake well until the honey dissolves and keep it in a tub of ice between rounds.

s.note: Fiery hot sauce honey wings with a cooling sour cream dip
s.how: Toss 1kg chicken wings with salt and bake at 220C for 45 minutes until crisp. Melt 50g butter with 100ml hot sauce and 2 tbsp honey and toss the wings through. Serve with sour cream mixed with herbs and celery sticks to put the fire out.

s.note: Crosshatched cob loaf stuffed with mozzarella and garlic butter
s.how: Cut a cob loaf in a deep crosshatch without slicing through the base. Mix 100g softened butter with crushed garlic and chopped parsley and push into the cuts with 250g grated mozzarella. Wrap in foil and bake at 180C for 20 minutes, then unwrap for 5 minutes more.

m.note: Dark-crusted slow-cooked beef ribs with corn and slaw
m.how: Rub 2kg beef short ribs with smoked paprika, garlic, brown sugar and salt. Cook uncovered at 140C for 5 hours until a dark crust forms and the meat is tender. Serve with buttered grilled corn and a crunchy cabbage slaw.

w.note: Blueberry sauce over ice cream with cream and popping candy
w.how: Simmer 250g blueberries with 80g sugar and a splash of water for 8 minutes until jammy, then cool. Scoop vanilla ice cream into tall glasses, spoon over the blueberry sauce and top with whipped cream. Scatter popping candy on top just before serving.

d.note: Thick blueberry, banana and yoghurt smoothie
d.how: Blend 300g frozen blueberries, 2 bananas, 300g Greek yoghurt, 400ml milk and 2 tbsp honey until smooth. Pour into 4 glasses. Serve straight away while it is still ice cold.

s.note: Creamy bacon and clam chowder in small cups with oyster crackers
s.how: Fry 150g diced bacon, then soften a diced onion and 400g diced potatoes in butter. Add 2 cans of clams with their juice and 500ml milk and simmer 10 minutes. Stir in 150ml cream, season well and ladle into small cups with oyster crackers.

s.note: Frozen grapes served straight from the freezer like ice marbles
s.how: Wash 500g green grapes and 500g red grapes, pull from the stems and dry well. Spread on a lined tray and freeze for 3 hours until solid. Serve straight from the freezer in a cold bowl with a few mint leaves, like little marbles of ice.

m.note: Red wine beef stew with carrots over buttery mash
m.how: Brown 1kg diced beef chuck in batches. Soften 2 onions and 3 carrots, add the beef back with 375ml red wine and water to cover. Simmer for 3 hours until tender. Boil 1kg potatoes and mash with plenty of butter, then spoon the stew on top.

w.note: Soft chocolate cookies sandwiched around thick vanilla ice cream
w.how: Beat 125g butter with 150g sugar and an egg, then mix in 200g flour and 40g cocoa. Roll into balls, flatten and bake at 180C for 10 minutes. Cool completely, then sandwich thick slabs of vanilla ice cream between pairs and freeze for an hour.

d.note: Cloudy apple juice, soda and apple slices
d.how: Fill 4 glasses with ice and thin apple slices. Add 150ml cloudy apple juice to each and top with 100ml soda water. Serve straight away while it is still ice cold.

s.note: Cucumber, egg and cress, and ham finger sandwiches on a tiered plate
s.how: Spread white bread with cream cheese and layer with thin cucumber. Mash 4 hard-boiled eggs with salt and spread with mustard cress. Fill more with ham and a little mustard. Cut off the crusts, slice into fingers and stack on a tiered plate.

s.note: Crimped pastry with beef, potato, swede and onion
s.how: Mix 400g diced chuck steak with 250g diced potato, 150g swede, 1 onion and plenty of pepper. Fill 4 rounds of shortcrust, crimp closed, brush with egg and bake at 180C for 50 minutes.

m.note: Roast beef with Yorkshire puddings, roast potatoes, peas and gravy
m.how: Roast a 1.5kg beef topside at 200C to medium and rest. Whisk 150g flour, 3 eggs and 300ml milk into a batter and bake in hot oiled muffin tins for 20 minutes. Roast 1kg potatoes alongside, cook peas and make gravy with pan juices and stock.

w.note: Fluffy raspberry ice scraped by hand and served with wafers
w.how: Dissolve 150g sugar in 150ml hot water and cool. Blend 500g raspberries with the syrup and the juice of a lemon, then strain out the seeds. Freeze in a tray, scraping with a fork every hour for 4 hours. Serve in glass dishes with ice cream wafers.

d.note: Breakfast tea with milk and sugar cubes on the side
d.how: Warm the teapot with boiling water and tip it out. Add 4 tea bags and a litre of freshly boiled water and steep for 4 minutes. Pour into cups with milk and serve with a bowl of sugar cubes and a spoon for each.

s.note: Rosemary roasted nuts with smoked salt and marinated olives
s.how: Toss 150g almonds and 150g cashews with a little oil, chopped rosemary and smoked salt. Roast at 180C for 10 minutes. Serve warm in one bowl beside a second bowl of mixed green and kalamata olives on the card table.

s.note: Crisp-bottomed pork and cabbage dumplings with chilli oil and vinegar
s.how: Mix 400g pork mince with finely shredded wombok, grated ginger and salt. Fill dumpling wrappers and pleat closed. Fry in oil until crisp underneath, add a splash of water, cover and steam 5 minutes. Serve with chilli oil and black vinegar.

m.note: Crackling roast pork knuckles with warm sauerkraut and mustard
m.how: Simmer 2 pork knuckles with an onion, bay and caraway for 1.5 hours. Pat dry, rub with salt and roast at 220C for 45 minutes until crackling. Serve with 500g warm sauerkraut, mustard and potatoes.

w.note: Dark chocolate bark with popping candy and raspberries
w.how: Melt 300g dark chocolate and spread thin on a lined tray. Scatter with 2 sachets popping candy, 15g freeze-dried raspberries and sea salt flakes. Set in the fridge and snap into shards.

d.note: Bourbon stirred with honey and orange over a big ice cube
d.how: Stir a spoon of honey into a little warm water to make a syrup. For each drink, stir 60ml bourbon, 10ml honey syrup and 2 dashes orange bitters with ice, then strain over one big ice cube. Twist a strip of orange peel over the top.

s.note: Seared steak bites in garlic butter with a little horseradish
s.how: Season 500g rump steak and sear hard in a very hot pan for 3 minutes a side. Rest for 5 minutes, then cut into bite-sized pieces. Toss in melted butter with crushed garlic and sea salt. Serve on toothpicks with a small bowl of horseradish.

s.note: Cast iron cornbread with honey butter
s.how: Mix 150g cornmeal, 100g flour, 2 tsp baking powder, an egg, 300ml buttermilk and 50g melted butter until just combined. Pour into a hot greased cast iron pan and bake at 220C for 20 minutes. Beat softened butter with honey and serve with warm wedges.

m.note: Rump steak with fried eggs, hash browns and buttered toast
m.how: Grate 600g potatoes, squeeze dry and fry as hash brown cakes in butter until crisp. Season 4 rump steaks with cracked pepper and sear to medium-rare, then rest. Fry 8 eggs. Serve each steak with two eggs, hash browns and buttered toast.

w.note: Tart lemon curd pie under a tall browned meringue
w.how: Blind bake a sweet shortcrust case. Whisk the juice and zest of 4 lemons, 200g sugar, 4 tbsp cornflour, 4 yolks and 60g butter over heat until thick, then pour in. Whisk the whites with 150g sugar to stiff glossy peaks, pile on top and bake at 200C for 6 minutes.

d.note: Strong black drip coffee in thick mugs, refilled without asking
d.how: Brew a big pot of strong drip coffee from freshly ground beans. Pour into thick diner mugs and keep the pot on the warmer. When a mug gets low, top it up without asking, the way a good diner always does.

s.note: Devilled eggs and cheese and pineapple sticks in a grapefruit
s.how: Boil 8 eggs for 10 minutes, halve and mash the yolks with mayonnaise, then pipe back and dust with paprika. Cube 200g cheddar and pineapple and thread onto toothpicks. Stick them into a halved grapefruit set cut side down, a proper sixties spread.

s.note: Garlic rosemary baby potatoes roasted in foil with sour cream
s.how: Halve 800g baby potatoes and divide among 4 squares of foil. Add butter, crushed garlic, rosemary and salt to each and wrap tightly into silver parcels. Roast at 200C for 40 minutes. Open at the table and add a spoon of sour cream.

m.note: Lemon thyme roast chicken with glazed carrots, mash and peas
m.how: Rub a whole chicken with butter, lemon and thyme and roast at 200C for 75 minutes. Glaze sliced carrots in butter and a little sugar. Mash 1kg potatoes with butter and cook peas. Serve everything on one big platter like a sixties advertisement.

w.note: Giant strawberry jelly ring with fruit set inside and cream
w.how: Make up 3 packets of strawberry jelly with a little less water than the packet says. Pour a layer into a ring mould with sliced strawberries and green grapes, chill until set, then fill with the rest. Chill overnight, turn out and serve with whipped cream.

d.note: Orange and vanilla ice cream shake with cream.
d.how: Blend 400ml orange juice with 4 scoops vanilla ice cream, 200ml milk and 1 tsp vanilla until thick and creamy. Pour into 4 tall glasses and top with a little whipped cream and an orange slice.

s.note: A big bowl of chocolate pieces, chocolate peanuts and honeycomb
s.how: Break 4 chocolate bars into rough pieces. Tip into a big bowl with 200g chocolate-coated peanuts and 150g broken honeycomb and toss together. Set it in the middle of the couch and keep an eye on it, because someone in the room is always hungry.

s.note: Crumbed baked chicken bites with honey mustard dip
s.how: Cut 600g chicken thighs into chunks. Dip in beaten egg and press into panko breadcrumbs. Spread on a lined tray, spray with oil and bake at 220C for 15 minutes until golden. Mix honey with Dijon mustard for a dipping sauce.

m.note: Scrambled eggs, bacon and toast with dark chocolate on the side
m.how: Fry 8 rashers of bacon until crisp. Whisk 8 eggs with salt and scramble slowly in butter until soft. Toast and butter thick white bread. Pile it all onto plates and add a square of dark chocolate on the side, because the symbiote insists.

w.note: Red velvet layer cake with cream cheese frosting
w.how: Whisk 300g flour, 2 tbsp cocoa, a teaspoon of bicarb, 300g sugar, 2 eggs, 250ml oil, 250ml buttermilk and red colouring until smooth. Bake in 2 tins at 175C for 30 minutes. Cool and stack with cream cheese beaten with icing sugar, covering the whole cake.

d.note: Thick chocolate shakes blended with cocoa
d.how: Blend 4 big scoops of chocolate ice cream with 500ml cold milk and a spoon of cocoa until thick and smooth. Pour into tall glasses and serve with wide straws. Make extra, because one is never enough for two.

s.note: Honey berries on whipped ricotta and toasted brioche
s.how: Toss 125g blackberries and 125g raspberries with a spoon of honey and torn mint. Whip 250g ricotta until smooth. Toast slices of brioche and cut into squares. Spread with ricotta and spoon the berries on top just before serving.

s.note: Rough black olive and caper tapenade on toasted baguette
s.how: Blitz 250g pitted black olives with 2 tbsp capers, a garlic clove, the juice of half a lemon and a splash of olive oil until rough. Slice a baguette, brush with oil and toast until crisp. Spread the tapenade thickly on the toasts.

m.note: Crackling pork shoulder with roasted apples, potatoes and greens
m.how: Score a 2kg pork shoulder, rub with salt and dry overnight. Roast at 160C for 4 hours, adding apple halves and 1kg potato chunks for the last hour. Blast at 240C until the crackling bubbles. Serve with steamed broccolini on a long platter.

w.note: Pastel jam and cream sponge decorated with edible flowers
w.how: Beat 250g butter with 250g sugar, add 4 eggs and fold in 250g self-raising flour. Bake in 2 tins at 175C for 25 minutes. Stack with strawberry jam and whipped cream, ice in pastel colours and decorate with edible flowers. Slightly lopsided is fine.

d.note: Lime soda with cucumber and mint over crushed ice
d.how: Fill glasses with crushed ice, thin cucumber ribbons and a few mint leaves. Add a good splash of lime cordial and top with cold soda water. Stir gently until it glows green, like the fire at the edge of the Moors.

s.note: Grilled beef sausages with caramelised onion and mustard
s.how: Cook 2 sliced onions slowly with a spoon of brown sugar for 30 minutes until jammy. Grill 8 thick beef sausages over coals until blistered and cooked through. Slice thickly, spear on toothpicks and serve with the onions and wholegrain mustard.

s.note: Crumbed scotch eggs halved like hatching eggs.
s.how: Boil 6 eggs for 6 minutes, cool and peel. Wrap each in about 80g sausage meat, 500g in total, roll in flour, 1 beaten egg and breadcrumbs. Deep fry at 170C for 6 minutes, or bake at 200C for 25 minutes, then halve to serve.

m.note: Lime, garlic and chilli chicken with rice and black beans
m.how: Marinate 1kg chicken thighs in lime juice, crushed garlic, chopped red chilli and salt for an hour. Grill until charred and cooked through. Serve with steamed long grain rice and a can of black beans warmed with a little cumin.

w.note: Bananas baked in the skin with chocolate and marshmallow
w.how: Slit 4 bananas along one side, open slightly and stuff with 100g chopped chocolate and 50g mini marshmallows. Wrap in foil and bake on the coals or at 200C for 10 minutes.

d.note: Blue lemonade with lime over crushed ice
d.how: Fill glasses with crushed ice. Pour in cold lemonade and add a drop of blue food colouring to each, stirring until bright blue. Squeeze in a wedge of lime and serve straight away. Name it after the cleverest raptor on the island.

s.note: Thin crisp fries in paper cones with tomato sauce
s.how: Cut 1kg potatoes into thin fries and soak in cold water for an hour. Dry well, fry at 140C until soft, then fry again at 190C until golden and crisp. Toss with fine salt and pile into paper cones with tomato sauce on the side.

s.note: Gruyere and Swiss cheese fondue with bread and apple to dip
s.how: Rub a pot with a cut garlic clove. Warm 250ml white wine, then stir in 200g grated gruyere and 200g grated Swiss cheese tossed with a spoon of cornflour until smooth. Keep warm over low heat and dip in cubes of baguette and apple.

m.note: Creamy chicken, mushroom and rice bake, golden on top
m.how: Brown 800g chicken thighs and 250g sliced mushrooms. Spread 300g rice in a baking dish, add the chicken and mushrooms, then pour over 750ml hot stock and 200ml cream with thyme. Cover and bake at 180C for 50 minutes until golden on top. Nothing moves.

w.note: Thin crêpes with lemon and sugar or banana and chocolate
w.how: Whisk 150g flour, 2 eggs and 375ml milk until smooth and rest for an hour. Cook thin crepes in a buttered pan for a minute a side. Fold with a squeeze of lemon and sugar, or with sliced banana and melted dark chocolate.

d.note: Fresh lemon juice, sugar syrup and iced water to mix yourself
d.how: Squeeze 6 lemons into a jug. Dissolve 100g sugar in 100ml hot water and cool. Put lemon juice, syrup and a jug of iced water on the table and let everyone mix their own glass to taste.

s.note: Mini pastry dogs and cheesy bacon potato skins on a tray
s.how: Wrap 16 cocktail franks in strips of puff pastry and bake at 200C for 15 minutes. Bake 6 small potatoes (about 800g) until soft, halve, scoop out a little and fill with cheddar and crisp bacon. Grill until bubbling and serve both with sour cream.

s.note: Marinated olives and feta with lemon and oregano and warm pita
s.how: Toss 150g green olives, 150g kalamata olives and 200g cubed feta with strips of lemon peel, a teaspoon of oregano and olive oil. Leave to marinate for an hour. Serve in a shallow bowl with warm pita torn into pieces.

m.note: Barbecue glazed ribs with potato salad and corn on the cob
m.how: Rub 1.5kg pork ribs with salt and bake covered at 150C for 2.5 hours. Brush with barbecue sauce and grill until sticky. Boil 1kg potatoes, cool and dress with mayonnaise and spring onion. Grill 4 corn cobs and serve it all picnic style.

w.note: Soft cinnamon scrolls with cream cheese icing
w.how: Roll 500g sweet bread dough into a rectangle, spread with 80g soft butter mixed with 100g brown sugar and 2 tsp cinnamon, roll up and cut 8 scrolls. Prove 30 minutes and bake at 180C for 25 minutes. Ice with 100g cream cheese beaten with 120g icing sugar.

d.note: Sparkling wine or grape juice over a sugar cube with bitters
d.how: Drop a sugar cube into each flute and add a dash of orange bitters. Pour sparkling wine for the grown-ups or sparkling grape juice for everyone else, so the bubbles stream up from the cube. Be careful what you wish for.

s.note: Little pastry tarts filled with homemade berry jam
s.how: Simmer 300g mixed berries with 150g sugar and a squeeze of lemon for 15 minutes until jammy, then cool. Cut shortcrust into rounds, press into a patty tin and fill with the jam. Bake at 190C for 15 minutes until the pastry is golden.

s.note: Loaded nachos with beans, cheese, guacamole and sour cream
s.how: Layer corn chips on a tray with black beans, grated cheddar and sliced jalapenos. Bake at 200C for 8 minutes until melted. Top with fresh salsa, smashed avocado and sour cream. Serve on the tray before anyone starts dancing.

m.note: Red chilli chicken enchiladas baked under melted cheese
m.how: Toast and soak dried chillies, then blend with a can of crushed tomatoes. Simmer 800g chicken thighs in the sauce for 30 minutes and shred. Roll in flour tortillas, cover with more sauce and grated cheddar and bake at 190C for 20 minutes. Serve with sour cream.

w.note: Grape jelly cups with cream and banana goggles
w.how: Make up 2 packets of grape jelly and pour into clear cups. Chill for 3 hours until set. Top with a swirl of whipped cream and two banana slices side by side like goggles. Serve to small helpers with a spoon each.

d.note: Thick banana smoothies blended with milk, honey and ice
d.how: Peel 3 ripe bananas and drop into a blender with 750ml cold milk, 2 tbsp honey and a big handful of ice. Blend until thick and smooth, then pour into tall glasses. A drink built for anyone who gets excited about bananas.

s.note: Seasoned curly fries in paper cones
s.how: Bake 1kg frozen curly fries at 220C for 20 minutes until crisp. Toss with 1 tsp smoked paprika and salt and serve in paper cones with 150g garlic aioli.

s.note: Charred corn brushed with chilli lime butter
s.how: Boil 4 corn cobs for 6 minutes, then drain. Mix 60g soft butter with a pinch of chilli flakes and the zest and juice of a lime. Brush over the corn and char on a hot grill, turning, until blistered all over. Brush with more butter to serve.

m.note: Cheeseburgers with bacon and fried onion and twice-cooked fries
m.how: Cut 1kg potatoes into crinkle chips and fry twice until crisp. Shape 600g beef mince into 4 patties and grill, melting cheddar on top. Fry bacon and sliced onion until golden. Stack it all in toasted buns and serve with the fries.

w.note: Hot fudge sundae with whipped cream and a cherry
w.how: Heat 150ml cream until steaming and pour over 150g chopped dark chocolate, stirring until glossy hot fudge. Scoop vanilla ice cream into tall glasses, pour over the fudge and top with whipped cream and a maraschino cherry. Winner takes all.

d.note: Cola floats with vanilla ice cream in tall glasses
d.how: Pour cold cola into tall glasses, leaving room at the top. Gently add a scoop of vanilla ice cream to each so it fizzes and foams up dark like an oil can. Serve with a long spoon and a straw straight away.

s.note: Steamed pork and prawn dumplings with soy, vinegar and chilli oil
s.how: Mix 250g pork mince with 150g chopped green prawns, soy and salt. Fill dumpling wrappers and pleat closed. Steam in a lined bamboo basket for 8 minutes. Serve with small dishes of soy sauce, black vinegar and chilli oil for dipping.

s.note: Honey butter peanut clusters with smoked salt
s.how: Melt 30g butter with 3 tbsp honey and toss through 300g peanuts with a pinch of smoked salt. Spread on a lined tray and roast at 180C for 10 minutes, stirring once. Cool until crunchy, then break into clusters. A snack fit for a captain in a strange place.

m.note: Crab in sticky chilli tomato sauce with egg
m.how: Fry 3 garlic cloves, ginger and 2 chillies, add 150ml tomato sauce, 3 tbsp sweet chilli, 1 tbsp soy and 250ml water. Add 1.5kg cleaned crab pieces, cover and cook 10 minutes. Stir in 2 beaten eggs and serve with crusty bread.

w.note: Silky green pandan coconut pudding with toasted coconut and mango
w.how: Whisk 800ml coconut milk, 100g sugar, a teaspoon of pandan paste and 5 tbsp cornflour over low heat until thick and glossy. Pour into glasses and chill for 3 hours. Top with toasted shredded coconut and diced mango. Watch for the green flash.

d.note: Gin, cherry liqueur, pineapple and lime
d.how: Shake 30ml gin, 15ml cherry liqueur, 90ml pineapple juice, 15ml lime juice and a dash of grenadine with ice. Strain into 4 tall ice-filled glasses.

s.note: French onion dip with potato chips and pretzels
s.how: Cook 3 sliced onions slowly in butter for 40 minutes until deep golden. Cool and fold through 300ml sour cream and 125g cream cheese with snipped chives. Chill and serve with a bowl of potato chips and a bowl of pretzels.

s.note: Hot-smoked salmon, dill and caper spread on rye crispbread
s.how: Flake 200g hot-smoked salmon and fold through 200g cream cheese with chopped dill, lemon zest and a spoon of capers. Spread thickly on rye crispbread and finish each with a squeeze of lemon. Serve cold on a Seattle kind of grey afternoon.

m.note: Herb-crusted Dijon salmon with crushed potatoes and green beans
m.how: Spread 4 salmon fillets with Dijon and press on breadcrumbs mixed with parsley and lemon zest. Roast at 220C for 10 minutes. Boil 800g potatoes, crush with butter and salt. Steam green beans and toss with butter to serve alongside.

w.note: Mixed berry crumble with oats and vanilla ice cream
w.how: Toss 500g mixed berries with 50g sugar and a squeeze of lemon and spread in a dish. Rub 100g butter into 100g oats, 100g flour and 80g sugar and scatter over. Bake at 180C for 35 minutes until bubbling and serve with vanilla ice cream.

d.note: Slow pour-over coffee with a splash of hot milk
d.how: Grind beans fresh and set a paper filter in a cone over a jug. Pour freshly boiled water slowly in circles over the grounds, waiting between pours. Serve in big mugs with a splash of hot milk on a rainy afternoon in Seattle.

s.note: Mini bagels with cream cheese, smoked salmon and capers
s.how: Split and toast 12 mini bagels. Spread with cream cheese and top with a fold of smoked salmon, a few capers, thinly sliced red onion and a sprig of dill. Lay them out on a tray like the morning spread at a newsroom.

s.note: Shaved cucumber, radish and fennel with lemon on crushed ice
s.how: Shave 2 Lebanese cucumbers, a bunch of radishes and a fennel bulb paper thin with a peeler or mandoline. Toss with lemon juice and sea salt flakes. Pile onto a plate of crushed ice so it looks like a crystal fortress and serve straight away.

m.n: Ma and Pa Kent's farm dinner
m.note: Farmhouse pot roast with carrots, potatoes and gravy from the pot
m.how: Brown a 1.5kg piece of beef chuck all over. Add a sliced onion, 3 carrots, 500ml beef stock and thyme. Cover and braise at 160C for 3 hours, adding 800g potatoes for the last hour. Thicken the juices into gravy and serve family style.

w.note: Split shortcake scones with cream and sugared strawberries
w.how: Slice 500g strawberries and toss with 2 tbsp sugar, then leave 30 minutes. Rub 80g butter into 450g self-raising flour, add 300ml cream and mix to a soft dough. Cut rounds and bake at 220C for 15 minutes. Split and fill with whipped cream and strawberries.

d.note: Cold milk shaken with honey and vanilla
d.how: Pour 1L cold milk into a big jar with 2 tbsp honey and a drop of vanilla. Put the lid on and shake hard until frothy. Pour into tall glasses and serve straight away, the way it would be at a Kansas farmhouse table.

s.note: Smoky bacon and molasses beans served in tin cups
s.how: Soak 400g navy beans overnight and simmer until tender. Fry 150g diced bacon with a chopped onion, then stir in the beans, 3 tbsp molasses, a spoon of Dijon and enough water to cover. Simmer an hour until thick and smoky. Serve in tin cups.

s.note: Crackers, cheese, salami and pickled onions packed like rations
s.how: Cut 200g cheddar into cubes and slice 150g salami. Pack small tins with water crackers, the cheese, salami and a few pickled onions. Close the lids and hand them out to the crew like rations on a long voyage to the bottom of the sea.

m.note: Lime garlic grilled fish with mango salsa and coconut rice
m.how: Rub 4 white fish fillets with lime juice, crushed garlic and salt and grill until just cooked. Dice a mango with chilli, red onion and lime for salsa. Cook jasmine rice in coconut milk with a pinch of salt. Serve the fish on the rice with the salsa.

w.note: Pavlova crowned with cream, blueberries and passionfruit
w.how: Whisk 4 egg whites to stiff peaks, then add 220g caster sugar a spoon at a time until glossy. Shape into a round and bake at 120C for 90 minutes, then cool in the oven. Top with whipped cream, blueberries and passionfruit pulp.

d.note: Strong stovetop coffee poured black into tin mugs
d.how: Bring a pot of water to the boil on the stove and stir in a big handful of ground coffee. Simmer for 2 minutes, then let the grounds settle. Pour carefully into tin mugs and set raw sugar on the side for the crew.

s.note: A bit of everything on one board so nobody is caught short
s.how: Arrange cubes of cheddar, water crackers, bunches of red grapes, roasted almonds, baby carrots and a bowl of hummus on one big board. Fill every gap. Then add a few more crackers just in case, because you can never be too prepared.

s.note: Golden yellow buttery popcorn with a pinch of turmeric
s.how: Heat a splash of oil in a large lidded pot and pop 100g popping corn. Melt 60g butter with a small pinch of ground turmeric and pour over the popcorn while tossing so it glows sunny yellow. Season with salt and pour into a big bright bowl.

m.note: Spiced beef tacos with all the toppings on the table
m.how: Brown 600g beef mince with a spoon each of cumin and paprika, then stir in 2 tbsp tomato paste and a splash of water and simmer 10 minutes. Warm taco shells and set out shredded lettuce, diced tomato, grated cheddar and sour cream so everyone builds their own.

w.note: Fudgy chocolate brownies with a crackly top
w.how: Melt 200g dark chocolate with 180g butter. Whisk in 300g sugar and 3 eggs, then fold in 100g flour and 30g cocoa. Bake in a lined 20cm tin at 170C for 28 minutes and cool before cutting.

d.note: Chilled honey chamomile with apple juice over ice
d.how: Brew 4 chamomile tea bags in 500ml boiling water for 5 minutes and stir in 2 tbsp honey. Cool completely, then mix with 500ml apple juice. Pour over ice in tall glasses and take a slow deep breath before the first sip.

s.note: Charred lemon oregano chicken on toothpicks with lemon aioli
s.how: Cut 600g chicken thighs into chunks and marinate in lemon juice, crushed garlic, oregano and olive oil for an hour. Grill until charred and cooked through. Spear on toothpicks and serve with mayonnaise mixed with lemon zest and juice.

s.note: Figure eight soft pretzels with rock salt and mustard
s.how: Mix 500g flour, 7g yeast and 300ml warm water to a dough and rest an hour. Shape into figure eights, dip in boiling water with 2 tbsp bicarb soda and sprinkle with rock salt. Bake at 220C for 12 minutes, brush with butter and serve with yellow mustard.

m.note: Shaved rib eye with onions and melted provolone in long rolls
m.how: Freeze a 600g rib eye steak for 30 minutes, then shave it paper thin. Fry 2 sliced onions in oil until soft, add the beef and sear fast on high heat. Lay provolone over the top to melt and pile into split long bread rolls.

w.note: Smooth Philadelphia-style lemon water ice in paper cups
w.how: Boil 750ml water with 250g sugar until dissolved and cool. Stir in 200ml lemon juice and the zest of 2 lemons. Freeze in a shallow tray, scraping and stirring with a fork every 40 minutes for 3 hours until smooth and icy, then scoop into cups.

d.note: Fresh lemonade with sliced lemons and mint in a big jug
d.how: Dissolve 150g sugar in 150ml hot water and cool. Squeeze 6 lemons into a big jug and add the syrup with 1.5L cold water. Add sliced lemon, bruised mint and plenty of ice. Stir and pour into tall glasses while you search for clues.

s.note: Goat's cheese crostini with roasted pumpkin, sage and honey
s.how: Roast 400g diced butternut pumpkin with olive oil until soft and golden. Slice a baguette, brush with oil and toast. Spread with goat's cheese, top with pumpkin and crisp sage leaves fried in oil, then drizzle with honey.

s.note: Rosemary smoked salt almonds with marinated olives
s.how: Toss 300g almonds with olive oil, chopped rosemary and smoked salt. Spread on a tray and roast at 180C for 10 minutes until fragrant. Serve warm in a bowl beside green olives, a taste of the valley the film keeps leaving and coming home to.

m.note: Creamy cheesy chicken, broccoli and rice bake that waits in the oven
m.how: Brown 800g diced chicken thighs. Spread 300g rice in a dish, add the chicken and broccoli florets, then pour over 750ml hot stock mixed with 150ml cream. Cover and bake at 180C for 40 minutes, then top with cheddar and bake uncovered until golden.

w.note: Fudgy brownies wrapped in paper for the bake sale stall
w.how: Melt 200g dark chocolate with 150g butter. Whisk in 250g sugar and 3 eggs, then fold in 100g flour and 2 tbsp cocoa. Bake in a lined tin at 170C for 25 minutes. Cool completely, cut into squares and wrap each in paper for the stall.

d.note: Espresso with steamed milk and an optional splash of vanilla
d.how: Brew a shot of espresso into each glass. Steam milk until silky and pour it in slowly so it holds a little foam on top. Add a spoon of vanilla syrup to anyone who wants it sweet. Serve on a Sacramento morning before school.

s.note: Dill and Dijon devilled eggs with a pinch of paprika
s.how: Boil 8 eggs for 10 minutes, cool and peel. Halve and mash the yolks with mayonnaise, a spoon of Dijon and chopped dill until smooth. Pipe back into the whites and finish with a pinch of smoked paprika and a tiny sprig of dill on each.

s.note: Fiery red chilli and honey glazed wings
s.how: Toss 1kg chicken wings with salt and bake at 220C for 45 minutes until crisp. Warm 30g butter with 3 tbsp honey, 2 tbsp soy sauce and 2 finely chopped red chillies until sticky. Toss the wings through the glaze until glossy and red.

m.note: Deep red beetroot and cabbage soup with sour cream and rye
m.how: Grate 3 beetroot, 2 carrots and shred a quarter cabbage. Simmer with 400g diced potatoes in 1.5L beef stock for 40 minutes until tender. Season with dill and a splash of vinegar. Serve in bowls with sour cream and dark rye bread.

w.note: Chewy chocolate chip cookies with glasses of cold milk
w.how: Beat 125g butter with 150g brown sugar and an egg until creamy. Mix in 225g flour and 150g dark chocolate chips. Roll into balls and bake at 180C for 10 minutes. Serve warm with tall glasses of cold milk, kitten optional.

d.note: Cold milk, or strawberry milk shaken with ice
d.how: Pour cold full cream milk into tall glasses for the purists. For strawberry milk, blend 250g strawberries with 2 tbsp sugar, then shake with more cold milk and ice in a jar until pink and frothy.

s.note: Grilled franks in soft buns with mustard and caraway sauerkraut
s.how: Warm 300g sauerkraut in a small pan with a pinch of caraway seeds. Grill 8 hot dog franks until they split. Tuck into soft buns, add a stripe of yellow mustard and a pile of sauerkraut, then wrap each in wax paper like a boardwalk stand.

s.note: Steamed pork and prawn dumplings with soy and chilli oil
s.how: Mix 250g pork mince with 150g chopped green prawns, grated ginger and a splash of soy. Fill dumpling wrappers and pleat closed. Steam in a lined bamboo basket for 8 minutes. Serve hot with soy sauce and chilli oil for dipping.

m.note: Glazed beef meatloaf with mash and peas
m.how: Mix 800g beef mince with a grated onion, a cup of breadcrumbs, an egg and salt. Press into a loaf tin and spread with tomato sauce mixed with brown sugar. Bake at 180C for an hour. Serve thick slices with buttery mash from 1kg potatoes and peas.

w.note: Lattice cinnamon apple pie served warm with ice cream
w.how: Cook 6 sliced green apples with 50g butter, 100g brown sugar and a teaspoon of cinnamon until just soft, then cool. Line a pie dish with shortcrust, fill and weave a lattice on top. Bake at 190C for 45 minutes and serve warm with vanilla ice cream.

d.note: Strong black coffee in thick diner mugs, refilled without asking
d.how: Brew a big pot of strong black coffee from freshly ground beans. Pour into thick diner mugs and keep the pot hot. Set a small jug of milk on the table for anyone who wants it, and refill every mug without being asked.

s.note: Buttery popcorn with coloured sprinkles and crackling popping candy
s.how: Heat a splash of oil in a large lidded pot and pop 100g popping corn. Toss with 60g melted butter and a big handful of coloured sprinkles. Scatter popping candy over just before serving so it crackles like a joke shop firework display.

s.note: Vanilla cupcakes piped with very pink buttercream and a sugar flower
s.how: Beat 125g butter with 150g sugar, then 2 eggs, then fold in 200g self-raising flour and 125ml milk. Bake at 175C for 18 minutes and cool. Beat butter and icing sugar with pink colouring and pipe on top. Finish each with a little sugar flower.

m.n: Grimmauld Place steak and kidney pie
m.note: Steak and kidney in gravy under puff pastry
m.how: Brown 800g diced chuck and 200g lamb kidney, add an onion, 2 tbsp flour, 500ml beef stock and Worcestershire and simmer 2 hours. Spoon into a dish, cover with puff pastry, brush with egg and bake at 200C for 30 minutes.

w.note: Golden syrup and lemon tart served warm with cream
w.how: Blind bake a shortcrust case. Warm 400g golden syrup with 100g fresh breadcrumbs and the zest and juice of a lemon, then pour into the case. Bake at 180C for 30 minutes until just set. Serve warm slices with a pour of cream.

d.note: Chilled pumpkin juice blended with apple, honey and cinnamon
d.how: Roast 300g butternut pumpkin until soft and cool completely. Blend with 1L apple juice, a spoon of honey and a pinch of cinnamon until smooth. Strain into a jug, chill well and pour into goblets over ice.

s.note: White chocolate popcorn clusters like a snowfall
s.how: Pop 100g popping corn and toss with 30g melted butter. Spread on a lined tray. Melt 200g white chocolate and drizzle all over, then sprinkle with a pinch of sea salt flakes. Leave to set for 30 minutes and break into clusters like snow.

s.note: Charred garlic chilli prawns with lemon aioli
s.how: Butterfly 600g green prawns and toss with crushed garlic, chopped red chilli, lemon zest and olive oil. Grill over high heat for 2 minutes a side until charred. Pile onto a platter and serve with mayonnaise mixed with lemon juice.

m.note: Fried chicken brushed with cayenne hot oil on white bread with pickles
m.how: Marinate 1kg chicken thighs in buttermilk overnight. Dredge in seasoned flour and fry at 165C until crisp and cooked through. Whisk hot oil with cayenne, brown sugar and paprika and brush over the chicken. Serve on white bread with pickles.

w.note: Coconut-covered vanilla cake with marshmallow ears
w.how: Beat 250g butter with 250g sugar, add 4 eggs and fold in 250g self-raising flour. Bake in 2 round tins at 175C for 30 minutes. Cut one round into ears and a bow tie, assemble into a bunny, cover in white icing and desiccated coconut and add marshmallows.

d.note: Thick chocolate malted milkshakes you can stand a straw in
d.how: Blend 1L chocolate ice cream with 500ml cold milk and 6 tbsp malted milk powder until thick and smooth. Pour into 4 chilled glasses and dust with a little extra malt powder.

s.note: Buttermilk fried chicken bites with honey for dipping
s.how: Marinate 600g chicken thigh pieces in buttermilk overnight. Dredge in flour mixed with paprika and salt. Fry at 180C for 5 minutes until crisp and cooked through. Drain on paper and serve hot with a small bowl of honey for dipping.

s.note: Golden corn fritters with a sour cream and chive dip
s.how: Mix a drained can of corn with 100g flour, 2 eggs, sliced spring onions and a pinch of paprika. Fry spoonfuls in a little oil until golden on both sides. Stir chopped chives through sour cream for the dip and serve the fritters warm.

m.note: Slow roasted garlic thyme beef with potatoes, carrots and gravy
m.how: Rub a 1.5kg beef blade with garlic, thyme and salt. Roast covered at 160C for 3 hours until tender, adding 1kg potatoes and 4 carrots for the last hour. Make gravy from the pan juices and beef stock. Serve after church.

w.note: Popcorn bound in caramel and rolled into balls
w.how: Pop 100g popcorn kernels. Boil 200g brown sugar, 100g golden syrup and 60g butter for 3 minutes, add a pinch of salt and pour over the popcorn. Toss, cool slightly and shape 12 balls with buttered hands.

d.note: Pineapple orange punch with lemonade and lemon sorbet
d.how: Pour 1L pineapple juice and 1L orange juice into a big punch bowl. Add sliced oranges and top with 1L cold lemonade. Float big scoops of lemon sorbet on top so it foams. Leave a ladle in the bowl and let everyone cut loose.

s.note: Soft salted pretzels with yellow mustard
s.how: Mix 500g flour, 7g yeast and 300ml warm water to a dough and rest an hour. Shape into pretzels, dip in boiling water with 2 tbsp bicarb soda and sprinkle with rock salt. Bake at 220C for 12 minutes, brush with butter and serve with yellow mustard.

s.note: Thin fried purple sweet potato chips
s.how: Slice 2 purple sweet potatoes paper thin on a mandoline and soak in cold water 20 minutes. Dry well and fry in batches at 170C until crisp. Drain and season with salt flakes.

m.note: Garlic butter rump steak with roast potatoes and green beans
m.how: Roast 1kg potato chunks at 220C for 45 minutes. Grill 4 rump steaks to medium and rest. Melt butter with crushed garlic and pour over. Steam green beans and toss with more butter. Serve a big plate for anyone lifting heavy.

w.note: Clear lemon jelly set over blueberries and raspberries
w.how: Warm 500ml water with the juice of 3 lemons and 120g sugar. Soak 5 gelatine sheets, squeeze and stir in until dissolved. Divide 125g blueberries and 125g raspberries among round glasses and pour over the jelly. Chill for 4 hours until clear and set.

d.note: Hot green tea with honey and lemon on a rainy night
d.how: Brew 4 green tea bags in a litre of water just off the boil for 3 minutes. Stir in honey to taste and add a slice of lemon to each cup. Serve hot while the rain comes down outside, poncho optional.

s.note: Turmeric lemongrass chicken skewers with peanut sauce
s.how: Marinate 600g chicken thigh strips in coconut milk, turmeric and finely chopped lemongrass for 2 hours. Thread onto skewers and grill until charred. Warm peanut butter with more coconut milk, lime juice and a little sugar for a thick dipping sauce.

s.note: Boiled pork and cabbage dumplings with black vinegar
s.how: Mix 400g pork mince with shredded wombok, grated ginger, sliced spring onion and salt. Fold into dumpling wrappers around the table together. Boil until they float, then a minute more. Serve with black vinegar for dipping.

m.note: Prawns in sweet spicy tomato chilli sauce with egg swirled through
m.how: Fry crushed garlic, grated ginger and chopped red chilli in oil. Add 150ml tomato sauce, a spoon of sugar and 200ml water and simmer. Add 1kg green prawns and cook 4 minutes. Swirl in 2 beaten eggs and serve with soft buns to mop up the sauce.

w.note: Tall light green pandan chiffon cake cooled upside down
w.how: Whisk 6 yolks with 60g sugar, 120ml coconut milk, 80ml oil and a teaspoon of pandan paste, then fold in 150g flour. Whisk 6 whites with 100g sugar to stiff peaks and fold in. Bake in an ungreased tube tin at 170C for 45 minutes and cool upside down.

d.note: Strong coffee sweetened with condensed milk over ice
d.how: Brew strong coffee and stir 2 tbsp condensed milk into each cup while hot until dissolved. Cool slightly, then pour over glasses packed with ice. Stir well and drink it the way the hawker stalls serve it, sweet and strong.

s.note: Smoked salmon blinis and gruyere gougeres on silver trays
s.how: Top 16 blinis with creme fraiche, smoked salmon and dill. For gougeres, boil 125ml water with 50g butter, beat in 75g flour, then 2 eggs and 75g grated gruyere. Pipe small balls and bake at 200C for 20 minutes. Arrange both on silver trays.

s.note: Lemony crab on toasted sourdough with a pinch of paprika
s.how: Fold 250g crab meat through 3 tbsp mayonnaise with lemon zest, a squeeze of juice and snipped chives. Toast slices of sourdough and cut into fingers. Pile the crab on top and finish with a pinch of smoked paprika. Serve by the sea if you can.

m.note: Whole trout over the fire with lemon and herbs
m.how: Stuff 4 cleaned trout with lemon slices, dill and butter, season and wrap in oiled foil. Cook on a hot barbecue or at 200C for 18 minutes. Serve with 800g boiled potatoes tossed in butter and parsley.

w.note: Lemon sponge filled with lemon curd and cream, topped with flowers
w.how: Beat 250g butter with 250g sugar, add 4 eggs and the zest of a lemon, then fold in 250g self-raising flour. Bake in 2 tins at 175C for 30 minutes. Fill with lemon curd and whipped cream, dust with icing sugar and top with white flowers.

d.note: Cinnamon hot chocolate in tin mugs
d.how: Heat 1L milk until steaming. Whisk in 150g chopped dark chocolate and a pinch of cinnamon until smooth and frothy. Pour into tin mugs and wrap your hands around it while the wind shakes the tent outside.

s.note: Chewy Brazilian cheese bread puffs baked golden
s.how: Bring 250ml milk and 125ml oil to the boil and pour over 250g tapioca flour, mixing well. Cool slightly, then beat in 2 eggs and 100g grated parmesan to a sticky dough. Roll into balls and bake at 200C for 20 minutes until puffed and golden.

s.note: Chunky smashed guacamole with green chilli and corn chips
s.how: Halve 3 ripe avocados and smash roughly with a fork, leaving it chunky. Stir in the juice of 2 limes, chopped coriander, a finely diced red onion, a chopped green chilli and salt. Serve straight away with warm corn chips.

m.note: Grilled rump with toasted cassava farofa, black beans and vinaigrette
m.how: Grill 800g rump steak over high heat and rest. Toast 200g cassava flour in 60g butter until golden and nutty. Chop tomatoes with onion and red wine vinegar for a vinaigrette. Slice the steak and serve with farofa, warm black beans and the vinaigrette.

w.note: Brazilian chocolate fudge balls in sprinkles
w.how: Cook 395g condensed milk, 2 tbsp cocoa and 20g butter, stirring, for 10 minutes until it pulls from the pan. Cool, roll into 20 balls with buttered hands and coat in chocolate sprinkles.

d.note: Ice-cold Brazilian guaraná soda with lime.
d.how: Chill 1.2L guaraná soda in the fridge for at least 2 hours. Fill 4 tall glasses with ice, pour the soda over slowly so it does not foam over, and squeeze a lime wedge into each glass before serving.

s.note: Bocconcini rolled in hazelnuts and chives to look like acorns
s.how: Toast 100g hazelnuts, rub off the skins and chop finely with a handful of chives. Pat 250g bocconcini dry and roll each ball in the hazelnut mix so it looks like a little acorn. Arrange on a plate and drizzle with a little honey.

s.note: Warm soft rolls with herb butter and brie
s.how: Mix 500g flour, 7g yeast, a spoon of butter and 300ml warm water to a dough and prove an hour. Shape into rolls and bake at 200C for 18 minutes. Mash butter with chopped parsley and chives and serve the warm rolls with it and a wedge of brie.

m.note: Beef and root vegetables braised in dark ale
m.how: Brown 1kg diced beef chuck, then add sliced onion, 3 carrots and 2 parsnips. Pour in 375ml stout and water to cover, add thyme and a bay leaf and simmer for 3 hours until rich. Serve in bowls with crusty bread at the tavern table.

w.note: Blackberries set in almond cream in short pastry
w.how: Line a 23cm tin with sweet shortcrust and chill. Beat 100g butter, 100g sugar, 2 eggs and 100g almond meal, spread in the case and press in 300g blackberries. Bake at 180C for 40 minutes.

d.note: Warm spiced apple cider with cinnamon, cloves and orange
d.how: Pour 1.5L apple cider into a pot with 2 cinnamon sticks, 6 whole cloves and a few strips of orange peel. Warm gently for 15 minutes without boiling. Ladle into mugs and serve by the fire after a long walk.

s.note: Charred garlic chilli lime butter prawns
s.how: Toss 600g green prawns with crushed garlic, chopped red chilli, lime zest and melted butter. Grill for 2 minutes a side until charred. Pile high on a platter with lime wedges and pour over any butter left in the pan. Eat with your fingers.

s.note: Garlic toasts piled with tomato, basil and olive oil.
s.how: Slice 1 baguette and toast the slices. Dice 4 ripe tomatoes and mix with 1 crushed garlic clove, a handful of torn basil, 2 tbsp olive oil and salt. Rub the toasts with a cut garlic clove and pile the tomato on just before serving.

m.note: Peppercorn cream sirloin with twice-cooked chips and salad
m.how: Cut 1kg potatoes into thick chips and fry twice until crisp. Grill 4 sirloin steaks to medium-rare and rest. In the pan, toast cracked peppercorns, add 200ml cream and simmer until thick. Serve with the chips and a green salad.

w.note: Fudgy brownies with a scoop of vanilla ice cream
w.how: Melt 200g dark chocolate with 150g butter. Whisk in 250g sugar and 3 eggs, then fold in 100g flour. Bake in a lined tin at 170C for 25 minutes. Cut into squares and serve each warm with a scoop of vanilla ice cream. Good job.

d.note: Whisky over ice, or iced tea with lemon for the sober version
d.how: Fill short glasses with ice and pour 45ml whisky over for those drinking. For the sober version, brew strong black tea, cool it, and pour over ice with lemon slices. Either way, drink it slowly and keep your feet on the ground.

s.note: Cornmeal-crusted green tomatoes with lemony remoulade
