s.how: Slice 4 green tomatoes thickly and salt lightly. Dip in beaten egg, then in fine cornmeal. Fry in hot oil until golden on both sides and drain on paper. Mix mayonnaise with lemon juice and a little chopped pickle for a remoulade to serve alongside.

s.note: Glossy brown sugar pecans with a pinch of cayenne
s.how: Toss 300g pecans with 30g melted butter, 3 tbsp brown sugar, a pinch of cayenne and sea salt. Spread on a lined tray and roast at 170C for 12 minutes, stirring once. Cool on the tray until glossy and crisp, then break apart.

m.note: Buttermilk fried drumsticks with mash and gravy
m.how: Soak 8 chicken drumsticks in buttermilk overnight. Dredge in flour seasoned with smoked paprika and salt, then fry at 170C for 12 minutes until crisp and cooked through. Serve with buttery mash from 1kg potatoes and gravy made with chicken stock.

w.note: Golden syrup pecan pie served with cream
w.how: Line a pie dish with shortcrust and blind bake. Whisk 3 eggs with 250g golden syrup, 100g brown sugar and 60g melted butter. Scatter 200g pecans in the case and pour over the filling. Bake at 170C for 45 minutes until set and serve with cream.

d.note: Strong sweet tea over ice with lemon on the porch
d.how: Brew 6 black tea bags in 1L boiling water for 5 minutes and remove the bags. Stir in 150g sugar while hot, then add 1L cold water. Cool and pour over plenty of ice in tall glasses with lemon slices. Sit on the porch and drink slowly.

s.note: Crisp potato and pea samosas with mint coriander yoghurt
s.how: Boil and crush 600g potatoes with 150g peas, fried onion and a spoon of garam masala. Cut spring roll pastry into strips, fill and fold into triangles. Fry at 180C until crisp. Blend mint into Greek yoghurt for a cool dipping sauce.

s.note: Chilli lime butter popcorn in silver bowls
s.how: Heat a splash of oil in a large lidded pot and pop 100g popping corn. Melt 60g butter with lime zest and a pinch of chilli flakes and toss through. Squeeze over a little lime juice and serve in silver bowls like a snack on a space station.

m.note: Layered yoghurt chicken biryani with saffron and fried onions
m.how: Marinate 1kg chicken thighs in yoghurt and garam masala for 2 hours. Fry 2 sliced onions until crisp. Par-cook 400g basmati for 5 minutes. Layer chicken, rice and onions in a pot, drizzle with saffron soaked in milk, seal tightly and bake at 170C for 45 minutes.

w.note: Red, blue and gold buttercream cupcakes topped with a star
w.how: Beat 125g butter with 150g sugar, then 2 eggs, then fold in 200g self-raising flour and 125ml milk. Bake at 175C for 18 minutes and cool. Pipe swirls of red, blue and gold buttercream on top and finish each with a little star.

d.note: Mango yoghurt lassi with cardamom over ice
d.how: Blend the flesh of 2 ripe mangoes with 300g Greek yoghurt, 250ml cold milk, a spoon of sugar and a pinch of ground cardamom until smooth. Pour over ice in tall glasses. Thick, cold and good for a family movie night.

s.note: Peanut and chilli spiced beef skewers with onion and tomato
s.how: Mix 100g finely ground peanuts with smoked paprika, ground ginger, chilli flakes and salt. Thread 600g thin rump strips onto skewers, coat in the spice and grill until charred. Serve with sliced red onion and tomato, sprinkled with more spice.

s.note: Sliced bratwurst in curry tomato sauce with hot fries
s.how: Cut 800g potatoes into fries and bake until crisp. Grill 4 bratwurst until browned and slice into rounds. Warm 200ml tomato sauce with 2 tsp curry powder and a pinch of smoked paprika. Pour over the sausage and dust with more curry powder. Serve with the fries.

m.note: Thick paprika beef goulash with noodles and sour cream
m.how: Brown 1kg diced beef chuck, then add 2 sliced onions and 3 tbsp sweet paprika. Add a can of crushed tomatoes and water to cover and simmer for 3 hours until thick. Serve over buttered egg noodles with a spoon of sour cream.

w.note: Moist date and walnut loaf sliced and buttered
w.how: Pour 250ml boiling water over 200g chopped dates and a teaspoon of bicarb soda and leave 10 minutes. Beat in 60g butter, 150g brown sugar and an egg, then fold in 250g self-raising flour and 80g walnuts. Bake at 175C for 50 minutes. Slice and butter.

d.note: Red cranberry soda and blue lemonade served side by side
d.how: Fill pairs of glasses with ice. Pour cranberry juice and soda water into one for the red team. Pour lemonade with a drop of blue colouring into the other for the blue team. Serve side by side and pick a side.

s.note: Ham, cheese and pickle sandwiches with apple slices and nuts
s.how: Butter white bread and fill with sliced ham, cheddar and a spoon of pickle relish. Cut into triangles. Slice 2 red apples and twist a handful of mixed nuts into a paper cone. Pack it all together like a lunch hidden away in a school attic.

s.note: Chunky dark chocolate rocky road smashed into rocks
s.how: Melt 300g dark chocolate. Stir in 150g marshmallows, 100g roasted almonds, 100g broken sweet biscuits and a handful of coconut. Press into a lined tray and chill for 2 hours. Smash into rough chunky rocks with the handle of a knife.

m.note: Chicken barley soup with lemon and herbs and brown bread
m.how: Simmer 600g chicken thighs with 100g pearl barley, 2 carrots, a leek and 2 celery sticks in 1.5L water for an hour. Shred the chicken back in, then stir through chopped parsley and a squeeze of lemon. Serve with brown bread.

w.note: Big fluffy meringue clouds with cream and strawberries
w.how: Whisk 4 egg whites to stiff peaks, then add 220g caster sugar a spoon at a time until thick and glossy. Spoon big fluffy clouds onto lined trays and bake at 100C for 90 minutes. Cool in the oven and serve with whipped cream and strawberries.

d.note: Honey chamomile tea, warm or chilled with apple juice
d.how: Brew 4 chamomile tea bags in 1L boiling water with a strip of lemon peel for 5 minutes. Stir in honey. Serve warm in small cups, or cool it and mix half and half with apple juice over ice. Calm enough for any oracle.

s.note: Salted dark chocolate peanut clusters in little paper bags
s.how: Melt 200g dark chocolate and stir in 250g roasted peanuts with a pinch of sea salt. Spoon small clusters onto baking paper and chill for 30 minutes until set. Pile them into paper bags like the peanuts sold under the big top.

s.note: Caramel popcorn in red striped cones
s.how: Heat a splash of oil in a large lidded pot and pop 100g popping corn. Melt 50g butter with 100g brown sugar and a pinch of salt until bubbling and toss through. Spread out to cool, then pour into red and white striped paper cones.

m.note: Fennel roast pork loin with apples, onions and potatoes
m.how: Rub a 1.5kg pork loin with crushed fennel seeds, garlic and salt. Roast at 200C for an hour with wedges of apple and onion around it and 1kg potato chunks alongside. Rest, slice and spoon over pan gravy made with the juices.

w.note: Fluffy pink marshmallow slice on a biscuit base with coconut
w.how: Crush 250g biscuits with 100g melted butter and press into a tin. Soak 4 gelatine sheets, dissolve in 150ml hot water with 300g sugar and simmer 5 minutes. Cool slightly, whip until thick and white, add pink colouring, spread over the base, dust with coconut and set overnight.

d.note: Sweet raspberry pink lemonade poured over ice in tall glasses
d.how: Dissolve 150g sugar in 150ml hot water and cool. Crush 125g raspberries in a jug, add the juice of 6 lemons, the syrup and 1.5L cold water, then strain. Pour over ice in tall glasses. Pink, sweet and gentle as a big-eared baby.

s.note: Little pepperoni pizzas baked crisp, eaten on a pool float
s.how: Roll pizza dough thin and cut into small rounds. Top each with a spoon of pizza sauce, grated mozzarella, a slice of pepperoni and a pinch of oregano. Bake at 220C for 10 minutes until crisp and bubbling. Eat them floating in the pool, again and again.

s.note: Bacon-wrapped jalapeños stuffed with cream cheese.
s.how: Halve 12 large jalapeños lengthways and scrape out the seeds. Mix 200g cream cheese with 80g grated cheddar and fill each half. Wrap with half a rasher of streaky bacon and bake at 200C for 20 minutes until the bacon is crisp.

m.note: Chilli cumin fish tacos with slaw, lime crema and pickled onion
m.how: Dust 600g white fish in chilli, cumin and salt and pan-fry until just cooked. Quickly pickle sliced red onion in lime juice. Mix sour cream with lime for a crema. Fill warm corn tortillas with shredded cabbage, fish, crema and pickled onion.

w.note: Lemon curd and cream sponge iced white, same as yesterday
w.how: Beat 250g butter with 250g sugar, add 4 eggs and fold in 250g self-raising flour. Bake in 2 tins at 175C for 30 minutes. Fill with lemon curd and whipped cream and ice white. Serve it today, and probably tomorrow, and the day after that.

d.note: Cold lager from the esky, or lemonade with lime
d.how: Fill an esky with ice and cold water and bury the bottles for 30 minutes. Hand out cold lager for the grown-ups, and pour lemonade over ice with a squeeze of lime for everyone else. Drink it on a pool float in the desert sun.

s.note: Garlic butter pizza balls stuffed with mozzarella and pepperoni
s.how: Cut pizza dough into small pieces and wrap each around a cube of mozzarella and a slice of pepperoni. Roll into balls and pack into a greased tin. Bake at 200C for 15 minutes, brush with garlic butter and serve with warm pizza sauce.

s.note: Chicken and ginger momos with spicy tomato achar
s.how: Mix 400g chicken mince with sliced spring onion and grated ginger. Fill dumpling wrappers, pleat and steam for 10 minutes. Char 3 tomatoes in a dry pan and blitz with chilli flakes, salt and a little garlic for a spicy achar to dip.

m.note: Miso ramen with braised pork belly, soft eggs, corn and nori
m.how: Braise 600g pork belly in soy and water for 2 hours, then slice. Whisk white miso into hot stock for the broth. Cook ramen noodles and soft-boil 4 eggs for 6 minutes. Build each bowl a little differently with pork, halved eggs, corn and nori.

w.note: Crisp sweet rice flour rings with cardamom
w.how: Mix 300g rice flour, 100g sugar, 50g melted butter, 1 tsp ground cardamom and 250ml milk into a thick batter and rest 1 hour. Pour rings into oil at 175C and fry until golden on both sides.

d.note: Spiced milky tea with cardamom, cinnamon and ginger.
d.how: Simmer 500ml water with 4 crushed cardamom pods, 1 cinnamon stick, 4 slices ginger and 4 cloves for 5 minutes. Add 4 black tea bags and 500ml milk, bring just to the boil, sweeten with 3 tbsp sugar and strain into cups.

s.note: Twice-fried wings in sticky gochujang honey glaze with sesame
s.how: Fry 1kg chicken wings at 160C for 10 minutes, rest, then fry again at 190C until crackly. Warm 3 tbsp gochujang with 3 tbsp honey, crushed garlic and a splash of soy until glossy. Toss the wings through and scatter with sesame seeds.

s.note: Potato cheese dumplings fried in butter with onion
s.how: Boil and mash 600g potatoes with 150g grated cheddar. Fill dumpling wrappers and pinch closed. Boil for 3 minutes until they float, drain, then fry in butter with sliced onion until golden on both sides. Serve with sour cream.

m.note: Lemon thyme roast chicken with potatoes, carrots and gravy
m.how: Rub 2 whole chickens with lemon, thyme, oil and salt. Roast at 200C for 75 minutes with 1.5kg potatoes and 6 carrots in the tray. Make gravy from the juices and chicken stock. Serve at a big farmhouse table with room for everyone.

w.note: Pavlova with cream and berries on a raised cake stand
w.how: Whisk 4 egg whites to stiff peaks, then add 220g caster sugar a spoon at a time until glossy. Shape into a round and bake at 120C for 90 minutes, then cool in the oven. Top with whipped cream, strawberries and blueberries and lift onto a tall stand.

d.note: Honey lemon cinnamon topped with ginger beer
d.how: Stir 4 tbsp honey into 250ml warm water with the juice of a lemon and a cinnamon stick. Leave to infuse for 30 minutes, then chill. Pour over ice and top with ginger beer. Not quite strong enough to knock over a god.

s.note: Tomato, bocconcini, salami and basil skewers with balsamic
s.how: Thread cherry tomatoes, bocconcini, folded salami and basil leaves onto skewers. Lay on a platter and drizzle with olive oil and balsamic vinegar. Season with salt and pepper. Go go gadget skewers.

s.note: Puff pastry swirls with tomato, ham and cheese
s.how: Spread 2 sheets puff pastry with 4 tbsp tomato paste, scatter with 150g chopped ham and 150g grated mozzarella and roll up. Slice into 2cm rounds and bake at 200C for 18 minutes until golden.

m.note: Hearty spaghetti bolognese with lots of parmesan
m.how: Brown 600g beef mince, then add diced carrot and celery and soften. Add 2 cans crushed tomatoes and simmer for an hour, stirring now and then. Toss with 500g cooked spaghetti and cover with plenty of grated parmesan.

w.note: Grey-iced cupcakes with chocolate button wheels
w.how: Beat 125g butter with 150g sugar, then 2 eggs, then fold in 200g self-raising flour and 125ml milk. Bake at 175C for 18 minutes and cool. Ice with grey icing made from icing sugar with a tiny drop of black, then press on chocolate buttons for wheels.

d.note: Fresh lemonade topped with soda over ice
d.how: Dissolve 150g sugar in 150ml hot water and cool. Squeeze 6 lemons into a jug, add the syrup and top with 1L cold soda water. Pour over ice with sliced lemon. Simple and clever, like the real brains of the operation.

s.note: Lettuce cups of baby leaves, pea shoots and herbs with parmesan
s.how: Separate baby cos lettuce into small cups. Toss pea shoots and mint leaves with lemon juice and olive oil and spoon into each cup. Top with shaved parmesan and toasted pepitas. Serve on a platter in the spring sunshine.

s.note: Garden crudites around a whipped feta, honey and dill dip
s.how: Whip 200g feta with 200g Greek yoghurt, a spoon of honey and chopped dill until smooth. Spread in a shallow dish and arrange baby carrots, radishes and snow peas around it like a garden bed. Serve chilled.

m.note: Mushroom, leek and thyme pie under golden puff pastry
m.how: Slice 600g mixed mushrooms and a leek and cook in butter with thyme until soft and golden. Add 200ml cream and simmer until thick. Spoon into a pie dish, top with puff pastry, brush with milk and bake at 200C for 25 minutes.

w.note: Flat pavlova pond with cream like snow and fresh berries
w.how: Whisk 4 egg whites to stiff peaks, then add 220g caster sugar a spoon at a time until glossy. Fold in a teaspoon of cornflour. Spread into a flat round like a frozen pond and bake at 120C for 90 minutes. Cool and top with whipped cream and berries.

d.note: Apple elderflower soda with cucumber and mint
d.how: Fill tall glasses with ice, cucumber ribbons and mint leaves. Pour in apple juice to halfway and add a splash of elderflower cordial. Top with cold soda water and stir gently. Fresh as the first day of spring in the meadow.

s.note: Grilled franks with mustard and relish, wrapped like at the stand
s.how: Grill 8 hot dog franks until they split and blister. Tuck each into a soft bun with a stripe of yellow mustard and a spoon of pickle relish. Wrap tightly in paper so the bun steams, then hand them out like the stand behind home plate.

s.note: Golden cornmeal and onion fritters, Southern style.
s.how: Whisk 1 cup fine cornmeal, 1/2 cup self-raising flour, 1 tbsp sugar and 1 grated onion with 1 egg and 180ml buttermilk. Drop teaspoons into 5cm hot oil and fry for 3 minutes until golden. Drain and serve with butter or hot sauce.

m.note: Vinegar pulled pork in buns with crunchy slaw
m.how: Rub a 2kg pork shoulder with salt and roast covered at 150C for 5 hours until it pulls apart. Simmer 250ml apple cider vinegar with 3 tbsp brown sugar and chilli flakes and toss through the shredded pork. Pile into buns with shredded cabbage slaw.

w.note: Vanilla custard, banana and biscuits under cream
w.how: Cook 750ml milk, 120g sugar, 50g cornflour and 4 egg yolks until thick, add vanilla and cool. Layer 250g vanilla wafer biscuits, 4 sliced bananas and custard in a dish, top with 300ml whipped cream and chill 4 hours.

d.note: Cold lager in plastic cups, or lime lemonade
d.how: Chill the lager in an esky of ice for at least an hour. Pour into plastic cups like at the ballpark. For anyone not drinking, pour lemonade over ice with a squeeze of lime. Raise a cup in the seventh inning.

s.note: Smoked salmon blinis and honey fig goat's cheese bites on silver
s.how: Top 16 blinis with creme fraiche and smoked salmon. Halve 6 fresh figs, top each with a little goat's cheese and drizzle with honey. Arrange both on silver trays and hand them round like a billionaire's library gala.

s.note: Smoked trout on rye crispbread with pickled onion and dill
s.how: Spread rye crispbreads with creme fraiche. Flake 200g smoked trout over the top. Finish each with a few thin rings of pickled onion and a sprig of dill. Serve cold on a slate, the way they might at a glass house on a lake.

m.note: Beef fillet in mushroom and puff pastry
m.how: Sear a 1kg beef fillet all over and brush with mustard. Cook 400g chopped mushrooms with garlic until dry. Lay prosciutto on puff pastry, spread with mushrooms, wrap the beef, brush with egg and bake at 210C for 35 minutes. Rest 10 minutes.

w.note: Hot dark chocolate soufflés with cold cream
w.how: Butter and sugar 4 ramekins. Melt 150g dark chocolate, stir in 3 egg yolks. Whisk 4 egg whites with 60g sugar to soft peaks, fold in and fill the ramekins. Bake at 190C for 12 minutes and serve with 200ml cream.

d.note: Spicy ginger beer, lime and fresh ginger over ice
d.how: Fill 4 glasses with ice, add a few thin slices of fresh ginger and the juice of half a lime to each and top with 250ml cold ginger beer.

s.note: Fried dough rounds with garlic butter, sour cream and cheese
s.how: Mix 500g flour, 7g yeast and 300ml warm water to a soft dough and prove an hour. Stretch into rounds and fry in hot oil until puffed and golden. Brush with butter mixed with crushed garlic, then spread with sour cream and top with grated cheddar.

s.note: Smoked salmon on rye crispbread with cucumber, dill and lemon
s.how: Spread rye crispbreads with creme fraiche. Top each with folds of smoked salmon, thin cucumber slices and a sprig of dill. Squeeze over a little lemon just before serving, the kind of snack you eat at a safe house in the north.

m.note: Pork chops with apples and onions, mash and braised cabbage
m.how: Sear 4 pork chops until golden, then add sliced apples and onions to the pan and roast at 200C for 15 minutes. Mash 1kg potatoes with butter. Braise shredded cabbage in a little butter and water until soft. Serve it all on big plates.

w.note: Pastel buttercream cupcakes covered in sprinkles, like a childhood birthday
w.how: Beat 125g butter with 150g sugar, then 2 eggs, then fold in 200g self-raising flour and 125ml milk. Spoon into patty pans and bake at 175C for 18 minutes. Cool and pipe with pastel buttercream made with icing sugar, then cover with sprinkles.

d.note: Strong black tea in glasses with lemon and a spoon of jam
d.how: Brew a strong pot of black tea with 4 tea bags and a litre of boiling water for 5 minutes. Pour into heatproof glasses and stir a spoon of strawberry jam into each. Add a slice of lemon and serve hot, family style.

s.note: Sprinkle popcorn mixed with chocolate buttons and pretzels
s.how: Pop 100g popping corn and toss with 60g melted butter. Add a big handful of coloured sprinkles while the butter is warm so they stick. Stir in chocolate buttons and broken pretzel pieces and tip into a bowl like a toy box.

s.note: Golden pumpkin, feta and sage filo triangles
s.how: Roast 400g diced butternut pumpkin until soft, then mash with 150g crumbled feta and chopped sage. Cut buttered filo into strips, spoon the filling at one end and fold into triangles. Brush with butter and bake at 190C for 20 minutes.

m.note: Foil-baked ribs glazed over coals with corn and coleslaw
m.how: Rub 1.5kg pork ribs with smoked paprika, brown sugar and salt. Wrap in foil and bake at 150C for 3 hours. Brush with barbecue sauce and finish over hot coals until sticky. Serve with grilled corn and a crunchy cabbage coleslaw.

w.note: Chocolate biscuit base with green peppermint icing and dark chocolate
w.how: Crush 250g sweet biscuits with 100g melted butter and press into a tin. Beat 300g icing sugar with a little butter, peppermint essence and green colouring and spread over. Pour melted dark chocolate on top, chill and cut into small squares.

d.note: Ice-cold lime cordial served in tin cups.
d.how: Mix 200ml lime cordial with 1L chilled water in a jug and add plenty of ice and sliced lime. Pour into 4 metal camping mugs or tin cups, army canteen style, and serve cold.

s.note: Pork pies, bread, cheddar, pickled onions and apples on a cloth
s.how: Spread a cloth on the floor or table. Lay out 4 small pork pies, torn crusty bread, wedges of aged cheddar, a jar of pickled onions and sliced green apples. Let everyone help themselves like outlaws picnicking in the forest.

s.note: Honey mustard chicken and capsicum on long skewers
s.how: Cut 600g chicken thighs and 2 red capsicums into chunks and thread onto long skewers. Marinate in honey, wholegrain mustard and crushed garlic for an hour. Grill until charred and cooked through. Aim straight for the centre of the platter.

m.note: Lamb, barley and leek stew with rosemary and crusty bread
m.how: Brown 1kg lamb neck pieces, then add 150g pearl barley, 3 sliced carrots, 2 sliced leeks, rosemary and 1.5L water. Simmer for 2 hours until the lamb falls from the bone. Serve in deep bowls with crusty bread around the campfire.

w.note: Little honey cakes topped with a gold chocolate coin
w.how: Beat 125g butter with 125g honey, then beat in 2 eggs. Fold in 200g self-raising flour. Spoon into patty pans and bake at 175C for 15 minutes. Brush with warm honey and press a gold chocolate coin on top of each. Take from the rich, give to the table.

d.note: Warm spiced cider, or sparkling apple juice for the kids
d.how: Warm 1L apple cider gently in a pot with 2 cinnamon sticks and a few whole cloves for 15 minutes. Ladle into mugs for the grown-ups. Pour chilled sparkling apple juice for the kids so everyone has something to toast the king with.

s.note: Crisp chips with melting mozzarella under hot beef gravy
s.how: Cut 1kg potatoes into thick chips and fry twice until crisp. Melt 30g butter, stir in 2 tbsp flour, then whisk in 500ml beef stock and simmer until thick. Pile chips into bowls, scatter with torn mozzarella and pour over the hot gravy.

s.note: Sticky dates wrapped in crisp bacon
s.how: Cut 8 rashers of bacon in half. Wrap each half around a pitted medjool date and secure with a toothpick. Lay on a lined tray and bake at 200C for 15 minutes, turning once, until the bacon is crisp and the dates are sticky.

m.note: Pancakes, eggs and bacon on one big plate with maple syrup
m.how: Whisk 250g flour, 2 tsp baking powder, 2 eggs and 375ml buttermilk into a batter and cook pancakes in butter. Fry 8 rashers of bacon and 4 eggs. Pile it all on one big plate and drown it in maple syrup.

w.note: Silky Canadian maple pie in a crisp shortcrust shell
w.how: Blind bake a shortcrust case. Whisk 250ml maple syrup with 3 eggs and 200ml cream until smooth. Pour into the case and bake at 170C for 40 minutes until just set with a slight wobble. Cool completely before slicing.

d.note: Cold lager in frosted glasses, or ginger beer
d.how: Put glasses in the freezer for 20 minutes until frosted. Pour cold lager for the drinkers and ginger beer for everyone else. Drink it in a roadside bar somewhere in the Canadian Rockies, looking moody.

s.note: Tomato soup in mugs with grilled cheese fingers for dunking
s.how: Soften a diced onion and crushed garlic in butter, add 2 cans crushed tomatoes and simmer 20 minutes, then blend smooth. Make cheddar toasties in butter, cut into fingers and serve with mugs of soup for dunking.

s.note: Little gruyere and pepper choux puffs
s.how: Bring 250ml water and 100g butter to the boil, beat in 150g flour until smooth, then beat in 4 eggs one at a time. Stir in 100g grated gruyere and cracked pepper. Pipe small balls and bake at 200C for 20 minutes until puffed and golden.

m.note: Beef bourguignon with bacon and mushrooms over buttery mash
m.how: Brown 1kg diced beef chuck and 150g bacon. Add 250g mushrooms and cook until golden, then pour in a bottle of red wine. Simmer for 3 hours until tender and glossy. Serve over mash from 1kg potatoes and plenty of butter.

w.note: Warm chocolate fondue with strawberries, marshmallows and sponge
w.how: Melt 250g dark chocolate gently with 250ml cream in a fondue pot or small pan. Keep warm at the table. Set out strawberries, marshmallows and cubes of sponge cake on forks for dipping. Very Paris, 1973.

d.note: Blue lemonade with lime over crushed ice
d.how: Fill glasses with crushed ice. Add 30ml blue curacao for the grown-ups, or a few drops of blue colouring for everyone else, and top with cold lemonade. Squeeze in a wedge of lime. It changes depending on who is drinking it.

s.note: Grilled lemon dill salmon skewers with herby yoghurt
s.how: Cut 600g salmon fillet into chunks and marinate in lemon juice, chopped dill and olive oil for 20 minutes. Thread onto skewers and grill for 2 minutes a side. Stir more dill and lemon through Greek yoghurt for a dip.

s.note: Thin crisp chips with sea salt and smoked paprika showing red
s.how: Slice 800g potatoes paper thin on a mandoline and rinse well. Dry thoroughly and fry at 170C in batches until crisp and golden. Toss straight away with sea salt and a good dusting of smoked paprika so the red shows through like the salt flats.

m.note: Lemon oregano chicken over rice with capsicum, cucumber and feta
m.how: Marinate 800g chicken thighs in lemon juice, oregano and oil, then grill and slice. Roast 2 red capsicums until soft. Build bowls of long grain rice with the chicken, capsicum strips, diced cucumber, crumbled feta and a drizzle of tahini.

w.note: Pale green pistachio panna cotta with honey
w.how: Blend 100g pistachios with 250ml milk until fine, then strain. Warm with 300ml cream and 80g sugar. Stir in 3 soaked gelatine sheets until dissolved. Pour into glasses and set overnight. Top with crushed pistachios and a drizzle of honey.

d.note: Cranberry pomegranate soda with seeds over ice
d.how: Fill tall glasses with ice and a spoon of pomegranate seeds. Pour in equal parts cranberry juice and pomegranate juice to halfway, then top with soda water. Stir once so it swirls deep red, like a throne room with nowhere to hide.

s.note: Sage pork sausage rolls with English mustard
s.how: Mix 500g pork mince with a grated onion, chopped sage and salt. Lay along 2 halved puff pastry sheets, roll up and seal. Brush with beaten egg, cut into pieces and bake at 200C for 25 minutes. Serve hot with English mustard and a dream.

s.note: Baked crisp apple slices with cinnamon
s.how: Slice 4 apples paper thin with a mandoline. Lay on lined trays, dust with cinnamon and bake at 100C for 2 hours, turning once, until crisp. Cool on the trays.

m.note: Creamy toasted hazelnut soup with chives
m.how: Toast 150g hazelnuts and rub off the skins. Soften a diced onion and 2 celery sticks in butter, add 400g diced potatoes, most of the hazelnuts and 1L chicken stock. Simmer 25 minutes, blend smooth and stir in 150ml cream. Top with crushed hazelnuts and chives.

w.note: Orange almond cakes glazed with orange syrup and candied slices
w.how: Boil 2 whole oranges for an hour, cool and blend smooth. Whisk 6 eggs with 220g sugar and a teaspoon of baking powder, then fold in the orange and 250g almond meal. Bake in muffin tins at 170C for 25 minutes. Glaze with orange syrup and honey.

d.note: Lavender syrup, lemon juice and soda over ice
d.how: Simmer 150g sugar, 150ml water and 1 tbsp dried culinary lavender for 5 minutes, cool and strain. Fill 4 glasses with ice, add 40ml syrup and the juice of half a lemon to each and top with 200ml soda water.

s.note: Crisp honey banana chips mixed with roasted peanuts
s.how: Slice 4 bananas thinly and toss with a spoon of honey. Lay on lined trays and bake at 120C for 90 minutes, turning once, until crisp. Cool completely, then toss with 200g roasted peanuts. Yellow, crunchy and very popular.

s.note: Golden twisted cheddar and parmesan pastry straws
s.how: Brush 2 sheets of puff pastry with beaten egg and cover with grated cheddar and parmesan. Cut into thin strips, twist each a few times and lay on lined trays. Bake at 200C for 12 minutes until golden as a crown.

m.note: Cold chicken in curried mayo with apricot and sultanas
m.how: Poach 800g chicken breast for 15 minutes, cool and shred. Mix 200g mayonnaise, 100g Greek yoghurt, 2 tsp curry powder, 3 tbsp apricot jam and 50g sultanas, fold through the chicken and serve with 300g cooked rice and salad leaves.

w.note: Classic banana split with three scoops, hot fudge and a cherry
w.how: Heat 150ml cream and pour over 150g chopped dark chocolate, stirring into hot fudge. Split 4 bananas lengthways into long dishes. Add three scoops of vanilla ice cream to each, pour over the fudge and top with whipped cream and a maraschino cherry.

d.note: Thick banana milkshake blended with ice cream
d.how: Blend 3 ripe bananas with 4 scoops of vanilla ice cream and 500ml cold milk until thick and smooth. Pour into tall glasses with straws. Banana, banana, banana, and nothing else needed.

s.note: One big bowl of buttery salted popcorn for the couch
s.how: Heat a splash of oil in a large lidded pot and pop 100g popping corn, shaking often. Pour over 60g melted butter while tossing and season with sea salt flakes. Tip into one big bowl and settle in on the couch for late-night television.

s.note: Overnight dill pickles in a jar with rye crackers
s.how: Slice 4 Lebanese cucumbers into spears and pack into a jar with dill and sliced garlic. Pour over 250ml white vinegar heated with 250ml water and a spoon each of salt and sugar. Chill overnight. Serve in the jar with rye crispbread alongside.

m.note: Glazed beef meatloaf with mash and peas, diner style
m.how: Mix 800g beef mince with a grated onion, a cup of breadcrumbs, an egg and salt. Press into a loaf tin and spread with tomato sauce mixed with brown sugar. Bake at 180C for an hour. Serve thick slices with buttery mash from 1kg potatoes and peas.

w.note: Shiny red toffee apples on sticks
w.how: Push sticks into 6 apples. Heat 400g sugar, 125ml water and 1 tbsp vinegar to 150C with red food colouring. Dip and twirl each apple and set on baking paper.

d.note: Bourbon, sweet vermouth and bitters with a cherry.
d.how: Stir 240ml bourbon, 120ml sweet vermouth and 8 dashes aromatic bitters with plenty of ice for 30 seconds. Strain into 4 chilled glasses and garnish each with a cocktail cherry.

s.note: Charred garlic chilli lime prawns piled high
s.how: Toss 600g green prawns with crushed garlic, chopped red chilli, lime zest and melted butter. Grill for 2 minutes a side until charred. Pile high on a platter with lime wedges, ready for the crowd at feeding time.

s.note: Cheese balls rolled in walnuts and paprika like little spheres
s.how: Mix 200g grated cheddar, 250g cream cheese and snipped chives. Roll into small balls and coat in finely chopped walnuts mixed with smoked paprika. Chill for an hour until firm. Serve with water crackers and stay inside the sphere.

m.note: Chilli cumin fish tacos with pineapple salsa and lime crema
m.how: Dust 600g flathead in chilli, cumin and salt and pan-fry until just cooked. Dice half a pineapple with a little red onion and lime for salsa. Mix sour cream with lime for a crema. Fill corn tortillas with cabbage, fish, salsa and crema.

w.note: Chocolate mousse with biscuit dirt and a speckled egg on top
w.how: Melt 200g dark chocolate and cool slightly. Whip 300ml cream and whisk 3 egg whites to soft peaks. Stir the yolks into the chocolate, then fold in cream and whites. Spoon into glasses, chill, top with crushed chocolate biscuits and a speckled chocolate egg.

d.note: Slushy frozen lemonade in big cups with straws
d.how: Squeeze 6 lemons and dissolve 150g sugar in the juice with 500ml water. Freeze in a tray for 2 hours. Blitz with a few handfuls of ice until slushy and pour into big cups with straws. Perfect for a long queue in the heat.

s.note: Crunchy coconut prawns with sweet chilli lime sauce
s.how: Peel 500g green prawns, leaving tails on. Dip in beaten egg, then press into shredded coconut mixed with panko. Fry at 180C for 2 minutes until golden. Stir lime juice into sweet chilli sauce and serve for dipping.

s.note: Thin crisp taro chips with sea salt and chilli
s.how: Peel 600g taro and slice very thin on a mandoline. Rinse and dry well. Fry at 170C in batches until crisp and pale golden. Toss straight away with sea salt flakes and a pinch of chilli flakes. Serve in a woven bowl.

m.note: Coconut lime snapper grilled in banana leaves with coconut rice
m.how: Marinate 4 snapper fillets in coconut milk, lime juice and chopped red chilli for 20 minutes. Wrap each in a softened banana leaf and grill for 10 minutes. Cook jasmine rice in more coconut milk with salt. Serve the fish in its leaf.

w.note: Set coconut pudding cups with mango and toasted coconut
w.how: Whisk 800ml coconut milk, 100g sugar and 5 tbsp cornflour over low heat until thick and glossy. Pour into cups and chill for 3 hours until set. Top with diced mango and toasted shredded coconut before serving.

d.note: Chilled coconut water with lime and pineapple
d.how: Fill glasses with ice and a few chunks of fresh pineapple. Pour in cold coconut water and squeeze in a wedge of lime. Stir and serve, or drink straight from a coconut if you have the arm strength to open one.

s.note: Blue cheese with pears, walnuts and honey on a board
s.how: Set a wedge of blue cheese at room temperature on a wooden board. Slice 2 pears thinly and fan them beside it. Add toasted walnuts, a pot of honey and water crackers. A board fit for a mouse with very good taste.

s.note: Mini croque monsieurs with ham, gruyere and bechamel
s.how: Make a quick bechamel with 30g butter, a spoon of flour and 250ml milk. Spread bread with Dijon, fill with ham and grated gruyere, then top with bechamel and more cheese. Grill until bubbling and cut into small squares. Serve on a silver tray.

m.note: Chicken braised with bacon, mushrooms and red wine over mash
m.how: Brown 1kg chicken thighs and 150g diced bacon. Add 250g mushrooms and cook until golden, then pour in 500ml red wine and water to cover. Simmer for 90 minutes until rich and glossy. Serve over mash from 1kg potatoes and butter.

w.note: Plain vanilla creme brulee with a torched sugar top
w.how: Heat 600ml cream with a split vanilla bean until steaming. Whisk 6 yolks with 80g sugar, pour in the cream and strain into ramekins. Bake in a water bath at 150C for 35 minutes and chill. Sprinkle with sugar and torch until amber. Nothing added.

d.note: Cold milk shaken with honey and vanilla, in saucers or glasses
d.how: Pour 1L cold milk into a big jar with 2 tbsp honey and a drop of vanilla. Shake hard until frothy. Pour into small glasses for people, or a saucer for any cat in the house. Drink it delicately, like a lady.

s.note: Crisp roasted garlic and parmesan bread
s.how: Roast a whole head of garlic at 200C for 40 minutes, then squeeze into 100g soft butter with chopped parsley and grated parmesan. Split a baguette, spread thickly and bake at 200C for 12 minutes until crisp. Keeps certain guests away.

s.note: Deep red roasted beetroot dip with pita crisps
s.how: Wrap 3 beetroot in foil and roast at 200C for an hour, then peel. Blitz with 200g Greek yoghurt, a garlic clove, lemon juice and a pinch of cumin until deep red and smooth. Serve with warm pita cut into wedges and baked crisp.

m.note: Rib eye basted with a whole head of garlic, with garlic mash
m.how: Sear 4 rib eye steaks in a hot pan, then add butter and a whole head of crushed garlic and baste for 2 minutes. Rest. Boil 1kg potatoes and mash with more butter and roasted garlic. Serve with steamed broccolini. No vampires at this table.

w.note: Sweet tart of blood orange curd with candied slices
w.how: Blind bake a sweet shortcrust case. Whisk the juice of 4 blood oranges, 150g sugar, 3 eggs, 2 tbsp cornflour and 80g butter over heat until thick. Pour into the case and chill to set. Top with blood orange slices simmered in sugar syrup.

d.note: Cranberry pomegranate soda with lime over ice
d.how: Fill tall glasses with ice. Pour in equal parts cranberry juice and pomegranate juice to halfway, then top with soda water. Squeeze in a wedge of lime and stir until it runs deep red. Serve cold at the rave.

s.note: Chive Dijon devilled eggs dusted with paprika
s.how: Boil 8 eggs for 10 minutes, cool and peel. Halve and mash the yolks with mayonnaise, a spoon of Dijon and snipped chives until smooth. Pipe back into the whites and dust with smoked paprika so they look speckled like eggs from a nest.

s.note: Twice-fried smashed green plantains with lime salt
s.how: Peel 3 green plantains and cut into 3cm pieces. Fry at 165C for 4 minutes, smash flat with a glass and fry again at 185C until crisp. Toss with salt mixed with crushed garlic and lime zest.

m.note: Black beans and rice with fried eggs and fresh salsa
m.how: Soften a diced onion and red capsicum in oil, add 300g rice and a can of black beans with their liquid and 500ml water. Simmer covered until the rice is tender, then stir through coriander. Serve topped with fried eggs and fresh tomato salsa.

w.note: Little meringue nests with cream, passionfruit and berry eggs
w.how: Whisk 3 egg whites to stiff peaks, then add 170g caster sugar a spoon at a time until glossy. Pipe into small nests and bake at 120C for 60 minutes, then cool in the oven. Fill with whipped cream and passionfruit and add three blueberries to each like eggs.

d.note: Pineapple orange passionfruit punch with soda in a big jug
d.how: Pour 1L pineapple juice and 1L orange juice into a big jug. Scoop in the pulp of 3 passionfruit and stir well. Top with 1L cold soda water and plenty of ice. Pour into glasses while waiting for the rescue boat.

s.note: Crisp pork and vermicelli spring rolls with sweet chilli
s.how: Soak 50g rice vermicelli and chop. Mix with 300g pork mince, shredded wombok and grated carrot. Roll tightly in spring roll pastry and fry at 180C until crisp and blistered. Serve hot with sweet chilli sauce for dipping.

s.note: Crunchy bite-size chicken with honey mustard.
s.how: Cut 600g chicken thigh into bite-size pieces. Dip in 2 beaten eggs, then in 1 cup flour mixed with 1 cup panko, 1 tsp paprika and salt. Shallow fry in batches for 4 minutes until golden, drain and serve with honey mustard.

m.note: Crisp battered chicken in honey soy glaze with sesame and rice
m.how: Toss 800g chicken thigh pieces in cornflour and fry until crisp. Warm 4 tbsp honey with 2 tbsp soy sauce until bubbling and toss the chicken through. Scatter with sesame seeds and serve over steamed jasmine rice.

w.note: Crisp folded cookies hiding paper fortunes
w.how: Whisk 2 egg whites with 80g sugar, then mix in 60g flour, 30g melted butter and a drop of vanilla. Spread thin rounds on a lined tray and bake at 180C for 6 minutes. Working quickly while hot, lay a fortune on each, fold and bend over a cup. Be careful what they say.

d.note: Fragrant jasmine tea served in small cups
d.how: Warm a teapot with hot water and tip it out. Add 2 tbsp jasmine tea leaves and pour over a litre of water just off the boil. Steep for 3 minutes, then pour into small cups. Sip slowly and try not to swap bodies with anyone.

s.note: Crusty bread, aged cheddar, pickled onions and apples on a board
s.how: Tear a loaf of crusty bread into thick chunks and pile onto a big wooden board. Add wedges of aged cheddar, a bowl of pickled onions and green apple wedges. Set it in the middle of the table like a lord's supper in a draughty castle hall.

s.note: Honey cinnamon nut clusters roasted crunchy
s.how: Toss 100g each of walnuts, hazelnuts and almonds with 3 tbsp honey and a pinch of cinnamon. Spread on a lined tray and roast at 170C for 15 minutes, stirring once. Cool completely so they set, then break into clusters for little paws.

m.note: Beef and ale pie under a puff lid with mash and peas
m.how: Brown 1kg diced beef chuck with 2 sliced onions. Add 375ml brown ale and water to cover and simmer for 3 hours. Thicken, spoon into a dish and top with puff pastry. Bake at 200C for 25 minutes. Serve with buttery mash and peas.

w.note: Jam roly-poly sliced and served with hot custard
w.how: Rub 100g butter into 300g self-raising flour, then add enough milk to make a soft dough. Roll into a rectangle, spread with raspberry jam and roll up. Wrap loosely in baking paper and bake at 180C for 40 minutes. Slice and pour over hot custard.

d.note: Breakfast tea with milk and sugar cubes
d.how: Warm a teapot with boiling water and tip it out. Add 4 tea bags and a litre of freshly boiled water and steep for 4 minutes. Pour into cups and serve with milk and a bowl of sugar cubes. A sugar bowl that walks on its own is optional.

s.note: Pepperoni and mozzarella pizza scrolls, baked golden.
s.how: Roll 500g pizza dough into a rectangle, spread with 125ml pizza sauce and scatter with 150g mozzarella and 80g sliced pepperoni. Roll up from the long side, cut into 12 rolls, sit in a lined tin and bake at 200C for 20 minutes.

s.note: Guacamole served in a hollowed cob loaf like a shell
s.how: Mash 3 avocados with lime juice, chopped coriander, a chopped green chilli and salt. Cut the top off a cob loaf and hollow it out, then spoon the guacamole in so it looks like a turtle shell. Serve with corn chips and the torn bread.

m.note: Thin New York pepperoni pizza folded to eat
m.how: Stretch pizza dough thin on a floured tray. Spread with pizza sauce, scatter with grated mozzarella, pepperoni and a pinch of oregano. Bake on a very hot tray at 250C for 10 minutes. Cut into big slices and fold each in half to eat.

w.note: Vanilla cupcakes with green buttercream dripping like ooze
w.how: Beat 125g butter with 150g sugar, then 2 eggs, then fold in 200g self-raising flour and 125ml milk. Bake at 175C for 18 minutes and cool. Beat butter, icing sugar and green colouring until soft and spoon on top so it drips down the sides like ooze.

d.note: Glowing green lime lemonade over crushed ice
d.how: Fill glasses with crushed ice. Add a splash of lime cordial and top with cold lemonade. Add a drop of green food colouring and stir until it glows like mutagen. Serve straight away with a bendy straw.

s.note: Smoked trout and pickled herring on rye with creme fraiche and dill
s.how: Spread rye crispbreads with creme fraiche. Top half with flaked smoked trout and half with pieces of pickled herring. Finish each with a sprig of dill and a few thin slices of red onion. Serve on a board, Norwegian fishing village style.

s.note: Goat's cheese balls in pistachio and chive on crackers with fig jam
s.how: Roll 200g soft goat's cheese into small balls. Roll each in finely chopped pistachios mixed with snipped chives. Set each on a water cracker with a small spoon of fig jam underneath. Arrange in rows and keep any screaming goats well away.

m.note: Beef short ribs braised in dark beer over mashed potato
m.how: Brown 2kg beef short ribs all over. Add 2 sliced onions, thyme and 375ml stout, then water to come halfway. Cover and braise at 160C for 4 hours until falling apart. Mash 1kg potatoes with plenty of butter and serve the ribs on top.

w.note: Buttered filo and nuts soaked in honey syrup
w.how: Layer 375g filo brushed with 200g melted butter with 300g chopped walnuts and pistachios mixed with cinnamon. Cut into diamonds and bake at 170C for 45 minutes. Pour over 250g honey simmered with 150ml water and lemon.

d.note: Pineapple passionfruit punch with lemonade in a big jug
d.how: Pour 1L pineapple juice into a big jug and scoop in the pulp of 3 passionfruit. Add plenty of ice and top with 1L cold lemonade just before serving. Stir gently and pour into glasses. Brought to you by a gentle rock man.

s.note: Cornmeal battered mini franks with mustard and tomato sauce
s.how: Whisk 100g cornmeal, 100g flour, a teaspoon of baking powder and 250ml buttermilk to a thick batter. Pat 24 cocktail franks dry, push a skewer into each, dip in batter and fry at 180C for 3 minutes until golden. Serve with mustard and tomato sauce.

s.note: Little cups of corn, tomato, cucumber and avocado salad with sporks
s.how: Mix a drained can of corn, halved cherry tomatoes, diced cucumber and diced avocado with lime juice and salt. Spoon into little cups and stick a spork in each one. Whatever happens, do not throw the sporks in the bin.

m.note: Chips, chicken and melty cheese under hot gravy.
m.how: Bake 1kg frozen thick-cut chips at 220C for 25 minutes until crisp. Heat 500ml beef gravy until bubbling. Pile the chips into 4 bowls with 400g shredded barbecue chicken, scatter over 200g torn fresh mozzarella and pour the hot gravy over so the cheese goes melty.

w.note: Swirled fried batter dusted with icing sugar and strawberries
w.how: Whisk 200g flour, 2 eggs, 250ml milk and a spoon of sugar into a smooth batter. Pipe in looping swirls into 180C oil and fry until golden on both sides. Drain, dust thickly with icing sugar and serve warm with sliced strawberries.

d.note: Fresh strawberry lemonade in big cups over ice
d.how: Dissolve 150g sugar in 150ml hot water and cool. Crush a handful of strawberries in a jug, add the juice of 6 lemons, the syrup and 1.5L cold water. Pour over ice in big cups. Exactly what a carnival should taste like.

s.note: Toasted crumpets with mustard and bubbling cheddar
s.how: Toast 8 crumpets until golden and spread with butter. Mix 200g grated cheddar with a spoon of English mustard and pile onto each crumpet. Grill until bubbling and golden. Serve hot on a plate for a hungry detective.

s.note: Scotch eggs in sausage meat, crumbed and fried
s.how: Boil 4 eggs for 6 minutes, cool and peel. Wrap each in 100g pork sausage mince. Roll in flour, beaten egg and panko, then fry at 170C for 6 minutes until golden. Halve and serve with English mustard, like a bar snack in a dodgy pub.

m.note: Lamb mince pie under buttery golden mash
m.how: Brown 800g lamb mince with a diced onion and 2 grated carrots. Add a cup of peas and a little water and simmer for 30 minutes until thick. Spread in a dish, top with mash from 1kg potatoes and plenty of butter and bake at 200C until golden.

w.note: Jam and cream sponge dusted with icing sugar
w.how: Beat 200g butter with 200g sugar, add 4 eggs and fold in 200g self-raising flour. Bake in 2 tins at 180C for 25 minutes. Cool, then sandwich with strawberry jam and whipped cream. Dust the top with icing sugar and serve at half past four.

d.note: A pot of breakfast tea with milk and shortbread
d.how: Warm a teapot with boiling water and tip it out. Add 4 tea bags and a litre of freshly boiled water and steep for 4 minutes. Pour into cups with milk and serve with a plate of shortbread, elementary.

s.note: Salmon rice triangles wrapped in nori with pickled ginger
s.how: Cook 2 cups sushi rice and season lightly. Salt and grill 200g salmon, then flake. Wet your hands and shape rice into triangles around a little salmon. Wrap the base in a strip of nori, sprinkle with sesame and serve with pickled ginger.

s.note: Sticky teriyaki chicken skewers with spring onion
s.how: Simmer 4 tbsp soy sauce, 4 tbsp mirin and 2 tbsp sugar until syrupy. Thread 600g chicken thigh pieces onto skewers and grill, brushing with the glaze, until sticky and charred. Scatter with sliced spring onion and serve hot.

m.note: Mushroom and capsicum pizza baked hot
m.how: Stretch pizza dough thin on a floured tray. Spread with pizza sauce, then scatter with grated mozzarella, sliced mushrooms and green capsicum. Bake at 250C for 10 minutes until bubbling and crisp. Cut into slices and celebrate being back home.

w.note: Soft mochi wrapped around vanilla ice cream and mango sorbet
w.how: Mix 150g glutinous rice flour, 60g sugar and 200ml water and microwave in bursts, stirring, until thick and stretchy. Roll out on cornflour and cut into rounds. Wrap each around a small frozen scoop of vanilla ice cream or mango sorbet. Freeze until firm.

d.note: Cold toasted Japanese barley tea, served over ice
d.how: Steep 4 barley tea bags in 1.5L cold water in the fridge for 3 hours, or brew in hot water and chill. Serve over ice.

s.note: Grilled smoked sausages in buns with chilli and onion.
s.how: Simmer 300g beef mince with 1 onion, 2 tsp chilli powder, 200g crushed tomatoes and 125ml water for 25 minutes. Split 4 smoked half-pork, half-beef sausages and grill 6 minutes. Serve in 4 buns with the chilli, yellow mustard and chopped onion.

s.note: Toasted mini bagels with cream cheese and smoked salmon
s.how: Split and toast 12 mini bagels. Spread with 250g cream cheese and top with 200g smoked salmon, thin red onion rings, capers and black pepper.

m.note: Garlic chilli basil chicken over jasmine rice with a fried egg
m.how: Stir-fry 600g minced or chopped chicken thighs with crushed garlic and chopped red chilli in a hot wok. Add a splash of fish sauce and a pinch of sugar, then toss through Thai basil. Serve over jasmine rice with a crisp fried egg on top.

w.note: Cherry and blueberry lattice pie with vanilla ice cream
w.how: Toss 400g frozen cherries and 200g blueberries with 100g sugar and 3 tbsp cornflour. Line a pie dish with shortcrust, fill and weave a lattice top. Bake at 190C for 45 minutes until bubbling. Serve warm with vanilla ice cream.

d.note: Cherry syrup, lemon and soda, soda fountain style
d.how: Fill 4 glasses with ice. Add 3 tbsp maraschino cherry syrup and a squeeze of lemon to each and top with 200ml soda water. Add a cherry.

s.note: Cheddar, pork pie, pickled onions, apples and bread to grab
s.how: Pile wedges of aged cheddar, sliced pork pies, a jar of pickled onions, apple wedges and torn crusty bread onto a big board. Set it out so a dozen unexpected guests can raid it at once.

s.note: Leaves, pea shoots, cucumber and herbs with lemon and seeds
s.how: Toss mixed salad leaves with pea shoots, thinly sliced cucumber and torn mint. Dress with lemon juice and olive oil and scatter with toasted pepitas. Pile it lightly onto a pale platter, as elegant as an Elvish table.

m.note: Sausages, bacon, mushrooms, tomatoes and eggs in one pan
m.how: Fry 8 thick pork sausages until browned. Add 8 rashers bacon, 200g sliced mushrooms and halved tomatoes to the pan. Fry 4 eggs in the fat at the end. Serve with buttered toast, because this is the second breakfast of the day.

w.note: Buttery caraway seed cake sliced with tea
w.how: Beat 175g butter with 175g sugar, then beat in 3 eggs. Fold in 225g self-raising flour, 2 tsp caraway seeds and a splash of milk. Bake in a lined loaf tin at 170C for 50 minutes. Cool and slice to serve with a cup of tea.

d.note: Brown ale in big mugs, or ginger beer for hobbits
d.how: Chill brown ale and pour into big heavy mugs, letting it foam over the top. For anyone not drinking, pour ginger beer into the same mugs. Bang them on the table and sing as loud as you like.

s.note: Soft pretzels with grainy mustard and butter
s.how: Mix 500g flour, 7g yeast and 300ml warm water to a dough and rest an hour. Shape into pretzels, dip in boiling water with 2 tbsp bicarb soda and sprinkle with rock salt. Bake at 220C for 12 minutes. Serve with butter and wholegrain mustard.

s.note: Chicken ginger momos with chilli tomato dip
s.how: Mix 400g chicken mince with sliced spring onion and grated ginger. Fill dumpling wrappers, pleat and steam for 10 minutes. Char 3 tomatoes in a dry pan and blitz with chilli flakes and salt for a dipping sauce.

m.note: Crisp pork schnitzel with warm potato salad and lemon
m.how: Pound 4 pork loin steaks thin, then crumb in flour, beaten egg and panko. Fry in butter until golden on both sides. Boil 800g potatoes, slice and toss warm with a little vinegar, oil and salt. Serve the schnitzel with lemon wedges.

w.note: Three-layer vanilla cake with raspberry jam and white icing
w.how: Beat 300g butter with 300g sugar, add 5 eggs and fold in 300g self-raising flour. Bake in 3 tins at 175C for 25 minutes. Stack with buttercream and raspberry jam and ice white with icing sugar beaten into butter. Fit for a bakery wedding.

d.note: Sparkling wine or apple fizz with a raspberry in each glass
d.how: Chill a bottle of sparkling wine and a bottle of sparkling apple juice for at least an hour. Drop a fresh raspberry into each flute. Pour the wine for the grown-ups and the apple juice for everyone else, then toast the happy couple.

s.note: White chocolate popcorn clusters in big bowls
s.how: Pop 100g popping corn and toss with 30g melted butter. Spread on a lined tray. Melt 200g white chocolate and drizzle all over, then sprinkle with sea salt flakes. Leave to set for 30 minutes and break into clusters for game night.

s.note: Honey thyme roasted baby carrots with whipped feta
s.how: Toss 500g baby carrots with honey, thyme and oil and roast at 200C for 25 minutes until sticky. Whip 150g feta with 150g Greek yoghurt until smooth. Serve the carrots warm around the dip. Keep one aside for a snowman's nose.

m.note: Creamy salmon, fish and prawn stew with leek, potato and dill
m.how: Soften 2 sliced leeks in butter, add 400g diced potatoes and 1L water and simmer until tender. Add 300g salmon and 300g white fish chunks and 200g green prawns and cook 5 minutes. Stir in cream and dill and serve with rye bread.

w.note: Frosty pavlova with cream and blueberries
w.how: Whisk 4 egg whites to stiff peaks, then add 220g caster sugar a spoon at a time until glossy. Shape into a round and bake at 120C for 90 minutes, then cool in the oven. Top with whipped cream and blueberries and dust with icing sugar like frost.

d.note: Warm spiced apple juice ladled into mugs
d.how: Pour 1.5L apple juice into a pot with 2 cinnamon sticks, a few strips of orange peel and 4 whole cloves. Warm gently for 15 minutes. Ladle into mugs and serve to anyone who has been out in the cold with a reindeer.

s.note: Crisp-bottomed pork dumplings with chilli oil and soy
s.how: Mix 400g pork mince with shredded wombok, grated ginger and salt. Fill dumpling wrappers and pleat. Fry in oil until crisp underneath, add a splash of water, cover and steam 5 minutes. Serve with chilli oil and soy sauce.

s.note: Smoky roasted chickpeas and peanuts, crunchy enough for a raccoon
s.how: Drain and dry 2 cans of chickpeas. Toss with 150g peanuts, olive oil, smoked paprika, garlic powder and salt. Roast at 200C for 30 minutes, shaking the tray, until crunchy. Cool and pile into a bowl. Do not call them trash snacks.

m.note: Crackling pork belly over mash with apple sauce
m.how: Score a 1.5kg pork belly, rub with salt and dry overnight. Roast at 160C for 3 hours, then blast at 240C until the crackling bubbles. Simmer chopped apples with a little water into sauce. Slice the pork over buttery mash from 1kg potatoes.

w.note: Chocolate fudge cake with sprinkles and a candle
w.how: Beat 200g butter with 250g sugar, then 3 eggs. Fold in 250g self-raising flour, 50g cocoa and 250ml milk. Bake at 175C for 35 minutes. Cover with fudge icing of butter, icing sugar and cocoa, then sprinkles and one little candle on top.

d.note: Ginger beer with lime and dark rum over ice
d.how: Fill glasses with ice. Pour 30ml dark rum into each for those drinking, squeeze in half a lime and top with cold ginger beer. Leave out the rum for everyone else. Drink it on a ship with a lot of dents.

s.note: Charred corn with lime mayo, feta and chilli
s.how: Grill 4 corn cobs over high heat until charred all over. Brush with mayonnaise mixed with lime juice. Roll in crumbled feta and sprinkle with chilli flakes. Serve hot with lime wedges for squeezing over at the table.

s.note: Crackling pork belly bites with lime and hot sauce.
s.how: Score the skin of 1kg pork belly, rub with 2 tsp salt and dry uncovered in the fridge overnight. Roast at 240C for 30 minutes, then 180C for 45 minutes until puffed and crackling. Cut into bites and serve with lime wedges and hot sauce.

m.note: Red chilli pork and hominy soup with crunchy toppings
m.how: Simmer 1kg pork shoulder pieces in 2L water with onion and garlic for 2 hours. Blend 4 soaked dried guajillo chillies with garlic and stir in with 800g tinned hominy and simmer 30 minutes. Serve with shredded cabbage, sliced radish, oregano and lime.

w.note: Sweet buns with a crackly sugar shell
w.how: Mix 500g flour, 7g yeast, 80g sugar, 2 eggs, 80g butter and warm milk into a soft dough and prove an hour. Shape into buns. Mix flour, sugar, butter and a little cocoa into a paste, press a round on each and score. Prove again and bake at 180C for 20 minutes.

d.note: Creamy rice cinnamon drink over ice
d.how: Soak 200g long grain rice and 2 cinnamon sticks in 1L water overnight. Blend until smooth, then strain through a fine cloth. Stir in 100g sugar and 250ml milk. Chill and pour over ice with a pinch of cinnamon on top.

s.note: Crackers with cheddar, salami and pickle like ship's rations
s.how: Top water crackers with a slice of aged cheddar, a round of salami and a slice of dill pickle. Lay them out in rows on a wooden board like rations rationed out on a long voyage to the end of the world.

s.note: Warm olives with lemon, garlic and chilli with crusty bread
s.how: Warm 150g green olives and 150g kalamata olives gently in olive oil with strips of lemon peel, sliced garlic and a pinch of chilli flakes for 5 minutes. Tip into a bowl and serve warm with torn crusty bread for mopping up.

m.note: Crisp-skinned snapper with lemon caper butter and potatoes
m.how: Boil 800g baby potatoes until tender and crush lightly. Pan-fry 4 snapper fillets skin side down until crisp, then flip for a minute. Add butter, lemon juice and capers to the pan and spoon over the fish. Serve with the potatoes.

w.note: Pavlova topped with cream and white peaches
w.how: Whisk 4 egg whites to stiff peaks, then add 220g caster sugar a spoon at a time until glossy. Shape into a round and bake at 120C for 90 minutes, then cool in the oven. Top with whipped cream and thin slices of white peach like lilies.

d.note: Fresh lemonade with torn mint, poured over plenty of ice
d.how: Dissolve 150g sugar in 150ml hot water and cool. Squeeze 6 lemons into a jug, add the syrup and 1.5L cold water, then tear in a handful of mint. Pour over ice. Sweet as the water at the edge of the world.

s.note: A big bowl of lollies, marshmallows and honeycomb
s.how: Tip 200g gummy lollies, 200g jelly beans, 100g marshmallows and 100g chocolate buttons into a big bowl. Break 100g honeycomb into chunks and scatter over the top. Set it out like a racetrack made of sweets.

s.note: White chocolate pretzel rods rolled in sprinkles
s.how: Melt 200g white chocolate. Dip 20 pretzel rods two-thirds of the way in, letting the extra drip off. Roll in sprinkles straight away and lay on baking paper to set. Stand them in a glass like a bunch of candy karts ready to race.

m.note: Giant beef meatballs in tomato sauce over spaghetti.
m.how: Mix 600g beef mince with 1/2 cup breadcrumbs, 1 egg, 50g grated parmesan and 2 crushed garlic cloves. Roll into 8 big wrecking ball meatballs, brown all over, then simmer in 700g passata for 25 minutes. Serve over 400g cooked spaghetti.

w.note: Lattice apple pie with a gold star piped on top
w.how: Cook 6 sliced green apples with 50g butter, 100g brown sugar and cinnamon until just soft, then cool. Line a pie dish with shortcrust, fill and weave a lattice top. Bake at 190C for 45 minutes. Pipe a gold star on top and serve with ice cream.

d.note: Cola poured over vanilla ice cream so it froths over
d.how: Put a scoop of vanilla ice cream into each tall glass. Slowly pour cold cola over the top so it fizzes up and froths over the rim like a volcano. Stand the glasses on plates and serve with long spoons.

s.note: Baguette toasts three ways: cod, prosciutto fig and artichoke
s.how: Toast baguette slices with olive oil. Whip 200g poached smoked cod with olive oil and garlic until creamy and spread on a third. Top a third with prosciutto and fresh fig, and the rest with marinated artichoke and parsley.

s.note: Thick double-fried fries in cones with mayonnaise
s.how: Cut 1kg potatoes into thick fries, rinse and dry. Fry at 140C until soft, rest, then fry at 190C until crisp. Toss with sea salt and pile into paper cones with a big spoon of mayonnaise on top, the Dutch way.

m.note: Garlic chilli seafood spaghetti with white wine and parsley
m.how: Soften crushed garlic and a pinch of chilli in olive oil. Add 250ml white wine, 300g green prawns, 500g mussels and 500g clams, cover and cook until the shells open. Toss through 500g cooked spaghetti with chopped parsley.

w.note: Coffee-soaked biscuits layered with mascarpone and cocoa
w.how: Whisk 3 yolks with 80g sugar until pale, then fold in 250g mascarpone and 200ml whipped cream. Dip savoiardi briefly in cooled strong coffee and layer with the cream in a dish. Repeat, chill overnight and dust with cocoa.

d.note: Peach purée topped with sparkling apple juice.
d.how: Blend 4 ripe peaches, peeled and stoned, with 1 tbsp sugar and a squeeze of lemon until smooth. Spoon 3 tbsp purée into each of 4 glasses and slowly top with 150ml chilled sparkling apple juice, stirring gently.

s.note: Golden ham and cheddar puff pastry parcels
s.how: Cut 2 sheets of puff pastry into squares. Fill each with ham and grated cheddar, fold into triangles and press the edges with a fork. Brush with beaten egg and bake at 200C for 15 minutes until golden. Serve warm at the inn.

s.note: Plums, red grapes and figs with honey and lime
s.how: Halve 4 purple plums and 4 fresh figs and pile on a platter with bunches of red grapes. Drizzle with honey and squeeze over a little lime juice. Serve straight away, the closest thing on Earth to a purp.

m.note: Beef and stout stew with potatoes and crusty bread
m.how: Brown 1kg diced beef chuck, then add 2 onions, 3 carrots and 375ml stout with water to cover. Simmer 2 hours, add 600g potato chunks and simmer another hour until thick. Serve in bowls with crusty bread, ship's cook style.

w.note: Fudgy brownies topped with gold chocolate coins
w.how: Melt 200g dark chocolate with 150g butter. Whisk in 250g sugar and 3 eggs, then fold in 100g flour. Bake at 170C for 25 minutes and cool. Cut into rectangles like chests and pile gold chocolate coins on top.

d.note: Blueberry lemonade with lime over ice
d.how: Fill tall glasses with ice. Pour in blueberry juice to halfway and top with cold lemonade. Squeeze in a wedge of lime and stir once so it swirls deep blue like the space between stars.

s.note: Paprika wedges with cheddar, bacon and sour cream.
s.how: Cut 1kg potatoes into wedges, toss with 2 tbsp oil and 1 tsp paprika and roast at 220C for 35 minutes. Top with 120g grated cheddar and 100g crisp bacon, bake 5 minutes more, then add sour cream and sliced spring onion.

s.note: Corn chips with chicken, black beans and cheese
s.how: Spread 300g corn chips on a tray. Top with 250g shredded cooked chicken, a drained tin of black beans and 200g grated cheese and bake at 200C for 10 minutes. Finish with salsa and sour cream.

m.note: Foil-baked barbecue ribs charred with coleslaw
m.how: Rub 1.5kg pork ribs with smoked paprika, brown sugar and salt. Wrap in foil and bake at 150C for 3 hours. Brush with barbecue sauce and char over hot coals. Serve with a coleslaw of shredded cabbage and grated carrot in a light mayo dressing.

w.note: Fudgy brownie cubes dusted with edible glitter
w.how: Melt 200g dark chocolate with 150g butter. Whisk in 250g sugar and 3 eggs, then fold in 100g flour. Bake at 170C for 25 minutes and cool completely. Cut into neat cubes and dust with edible glitter so they shimmer like the cube.

d.note: Thick dark chocolate milkshakes, black and glossy
d.how: Blend 1L chocolate ice cream, 400ml milk and 3 tbsp cocoa until thick. Pour into 4 glasses and drizzle with chocolate topping. Serve straight away while it is still ice cold.

s.note: Toasts with brie and apple or goat's cheese and honey
s.how: Slice a baguette, brush with olive oil and toast until golden. Top half with brie and thin slices of red apple. Top the rest with goat's cheese and a drizzle of honey. Lay them out on a wooden board like a village market stall.

s.note: A big platter of Dijon chive devilled eggs
s.how: Boil 12 eggs for 10 minutes, cool and peel. Halve and mash the yolks with mayonnaise, Dijon and snipped chives until smooth. Pipe back into the whites and dust with smoked paprika. Pile onto one big platter, because no one eats eggs like Gaston.

m.note: Beef bourguignon with bacon, mushrooms and baby onions
m.how: Brown 1kg diced beef chuck and 150g bacon. Add 250g mushrooms and 200g peeled pickling onions and cook until golden. Pour in a bottle of red wine and simmer for 3 hours until rich. Serve over buttery mash from 1kg potatoes.

w.note: Custard tart topped with apple slices fanned into a rose
w.how: Blind bake a sweet shortcrust case. Fill with 500ml thick custard. Slice 3 red apples paper thin, soften briefly in lemony water, then arrange in overlapping circles into a rose. Bake at 180C for 20 minutes and glaze with warm apricot jam.

d.note: Golden peach and apple sparkle, or sparkling wine
d.how: Pour peach nectar into tall glasses to halfway and top with sparkling apple juice. Add a slice of orange to each. For the grown-ups, top the peach with sparkling wine instead. Serve before the ballroom dance.

s.note: Mini fried beef, bean and cheese burritos
s.how: Brown 400g beef mince with 1 tbsp taco seasoning, add 400g refried beans and cool. Fill 8 small tortillas with the mix and 120g grated cheese, roll tightly and fry seam down at 180C until golden. Halve and serve with 200g sour cream and 300g salsa.

s.note: Thin crisp chips with smoked paprika and garlic
s.how: Slice 800g potatoes paper thin on a mandoline and rinse well. Dry thoroughly and fry at 170C in batches until crisp. Toss straight away with smoked paprika, garlic powder and sea salt. Serve in a big bowl, dusty as a wasteland.

m.note: Beef and bean chilli with cheddar and corn chips.
m.how: Brown 800g beef mince with 1 diced onion and 3 crushed garlic cloves. Add 2 tbsp chilli powder, 1 tsp ground cumin, a 400g can crushed tomatoes and a 400g can drained kidney beans. Simmer for 40 minutes, then serve with grated cheddar and corn chips.

w.note: Vanilla sundae half raspberry sauce and half mango
w.how: Blend 200g raspberries with a spoon of sugar and strain. Blend a mango until smooth. Scoop vanilla ice cream into tall glasses, spoon raspberry sauce down one side and mango down the other, then pile whipped cream on top.

d.note: Whisky over one big ice cube, or ginger ale with lime
d.how: Set one big ice cube in each short glass. Pour 45ml whisky over it for those drinking. For everyone else, pour ginger ale over ice with a squeeze of fresh lime. Drink with a scowl.

s.note: Tropical fruit on banana leaves with lime and chilli salt
s.how: Lay banana leaves on a big platter. Cut a pineapple, 2 mangoes and half a papaya into wedges and pile on top with halved passionfruit. Squeeze over lime juice and sprinkle with a little salt mixed with chilli.

s.note: Charred garlic chilli lime butter prawns
s.how: Toss 600g green prawns with crushed garlic, chopped red chilli, lime zest and melted butter. Grill for 2 minutes a side until charred. Pile onto a platter with lime wedges and pour over the butter from the pan.

m.note: Lime chilli snapper grilled in banana leaves with coconut rice
m.how: Rub 4 snapper fillets with lime juice, chopped red chilli and salt. Wrap each in a softened banana leaf and grill for 10 minutes. Cook jasmine rice in coconut milk with a pinch of salt. Serve the fish in its leaf on the rice.

w.note: Chocolate mousse with biscuit soil and a speckled egg
w.how: Melt 200g dark chocolate and cool slightly. Whip 300ml cream and whisk 3 egg whites to soft peaks. Stir yolks into the chocolate, then fold in cream and whites. Spoon into glasses and chill 3 hours. Top with crushed chocolate biscuits and a speckled egg.

d.note: Coconut water and pineapple with lime and mint
d.how: Fill tall glasses with ice and a few mint leaves. Pour in equal parts coconut water and pineapple juice, then squeeze in a wedge of lime. Stir and serve cold, like a drink on a boat heading somewhere it should not.

s.note: White chocolate pretzel rods with neon blue lines
s.how: Melt 200g white chocolate and dip 20 pretzel rods two-thirds of the way. Set on baking paper. Mix icing sugar with a little water and blue colouring and pipe thin straight lines along each rod like light cycle trails. Let set before serving.

s.note: Smoked salmon on black rye with creme fraiche on slate
s.how: Cut dark rye bread into neat squares. Spread with creme fraiche and top with a fold of smoked salmon, a sprig of dill and a tiny squeeze of lemon. Lay them out in sharp rows on black slate, as clean as a nightclub inside a computer.

m.note: Sticky soy honey chicken noodles with capsicum and broccoli
m.how: Stir-fry 500g sliced chicken thighs in a hot wok until browned. Add a sliced red capsicum and broccoli florets and cook 3 minutes. Toss through 400g cooked egg noodles with 3 tbsp soy sauce and 2 tbsp honey until sticky and glossy.

w.n: End of Line Club neon cookies
w.note: Butter cookies iced in neon straight lines
w.how: Beat 200g butter with 100g icing sugar, add 1 egg yolk, then 300g plain flour. Roll, cut into squares and bake at 170C for 12 minutes. Ice with 250g icing sugar mixed with water and neon food colouring in straight lines.

d.note: Gently steeped green tea in small cups.
d.how: Warm a teapot with hot water, then add 4 green tea bags. Pour over 1L water heated to just below boiling, about 80C, and steep for 2 to 3 minutes. Pour into small cups and serve plain.

s.note: Cheddar, brie and goat's cheese with grapes, fig jam and walnuts
s.how: Bring 150g each of aged cheddar, brie and goat's cheese to room temperature. Arrange on a wooden board with bunches of red grapes, a pot of fig jam, toasted walnuts and a stack of crackers. Serve with the vineyard view.

s.note: Lemonade scones with jam and clotted cream
s.how: Mix 450g self-raising flour with 300ml cream and 300ml lemonade until just combined. Pat out, cut into rounds and bake close together at 220C for 15 minutes until risen and golden. Serve warm with strawberry jam and clotted cream.

m.note: Eye fillet with red wine sauce, gratin and beans by candlelight
m.how: Layer thinly sliced potatoes with cream and bake at 180C for an hour. Roast a 1kg beef eye fillet to medium-rare and rest. Deglaze the pan with red wine and stock and reduce until glossy. Serve with green beans by candlelight on a boat.

w.note: Crushed meringue, cream and strawberries folded together.
w.how: Hull 500g strawberries. Blitz 100g of them with 1 tbsp sugar into a sauce and quarter the rest. Whip 300ml cream to soft peaks, fold in 6 broken meringue nests and the quartered strawberries, spoon into 4 glasses and drizzle with the sauce.

d.note: Strong breakfast tea with milk and shortbread
d.how: Warm a teapot with boiling water and tip it out. Add 4 tea bags and a litre of freshly boiled water and steep for 5 minutes until strong. Pour into cups with milk and serve with a plate of shortbread, the way a good butler would.

s.note: Crisp chicken in soy honey glaze coated in black sesame
s.how: Toss 600g chicken thigh pieces in cornflour and fry until crisp. Warm 3 tbsp soy sauce with 3 tbsp honey until bubbling and toss the chicken through. Roll in black sesame seeds until coated and dark. Serve on toothpicks.

s.note: Crunchy potato gems with chilli garlic mayo.
s.how: Bake 1kg frozen potato gems at 220C for 20 minutes, turning once, until crunchy. Mix 150g mayonnaise with 2 tbsp sriracha and 1 crushed garlic clove. Serve the gems in a big bowl with the mayo for dunking.

m.note: Garlic herb butter lobster tails with fries and lemon
m.how: Cut 1kg potatoes into fries and fry twice until crisp. Split 4 lobster tails, brush with butter mixed with crushed garlic and parsley, and grill for 6 minutes until just cooked. Serve with the fries and lemon wedges. Tater tots optional.

w.note: Silky mango pudding with evaporated milk
w.how: Dissolve 3 tsp gelatine in 100ml hot water. Blend 2 mangoes with 80g sugar and 150ml cream, stir in the gelatine and set in 4 glasses for 3 hours. Pour over a little evaporated milk to serve.

d.note: Sweet black tea with condensed milk over ice.
d.how: Steep 4 black tea bags in 500ml boiling water for 5 minutes, remove, stir in 4 tbsp sweetened condensed milk and chill. Pour over ice in 4 glasses and top each with a splash of cold milk.

s.note: Pepperoni pizza cut into squares and eaten from the tray
s.how: Stretch pizza dough thin on a big tray. Spread with pizza sauce, scatter with grated mozzarella, pepperoni and a pinch of oregano. Bake at 250C for 10 minutes until bubbling. Cut into squares and eat straight from the tray at the firehouse.

s.n: Phoebe's chess club pigs in blankets
s.note: Cocktail sausages wrapped in puff pastry
s.how: Cut 2 sheets puff pastry into strips and wrap around 24 cocktail sausages. Brush with egg, sprinkle with sesame seeds and bake at 200C for 18 minutes. Serve with tomato sauce.

m.note: Grilled corned beef, sauerkraut and Swiss cheese on rye
m.how: Mix mayonnaise with a little tomato sauce and chopped pickle for dressing. Layer rye bread with sliced corned beef, sauerkraut, Swiss cheese and dressing. Butter the outsides and grill in a pan until golden and melting. Cut in half to serve.

w.note: Toasted marshmallow and chocolate biscuit sandwiches
w.how: Toast marshmallows over a flame or under a hot grill until golden and gooey. Sandwich each between two plain sweet biscuits with a square of dark chocolate, squashing so the chocolate melts. Eat them before they start causing trouble.

d.note: Lime cordial, soda and a melting scoop of lime sorbet
d.how: Fill 4 tall glasses with crushed ice. Add 40ml lime cordial to each, top with 200ml soda water and float a scoop of lime sorbet on top so it fizzes and turns cloudy green.

s.note: Small brie, ham and chutney sandwiches with olives
s.how: Split a loaf of crusty bread and fill with sliced brie, ham and a spread of tomato chutney. Cut into small pieces and pin with toothpicks. Serve on a board with a bowl of green olives, like lunch from a market stall.

s.note: Pan-toasted cheddar, tomato and pickle sandwich in quarters
s.how: Butter thick white bread on the outside. Fill with sliced cheddar, tomato and a spoon of pickle relish. Toast in a pan over medium heat until golden and melting, pressing down. Cut into quarters. Simple enough even for a flatmate.

m.note: Creamy white wine tarragon chicken with mash and beans
m.how: Brown 1kg chicken thighs, then add 250g mushrooms and cook until golden. Pour in 250ml white wine and simmer 20 minutes, then stir in 200ml cream and chopped tarragon. Serve with mashed potato and green beans at a small birthday dinner.

w.note: Fudgy brownies, the last one saved for the saddest story
w.how: Melt 200g dark chocolate with 150g butter. Whisk in 250g sugar and 3 eggs, then fold in 100g flour and 2 tbsp cocoa. Bake at 170C for 25 minutes. Cut into squares and keep the very last one aside for whoever tells the saddest story.

d.note: Fresh orange juice over ice, best kept in the glass
d.how: Squeeze 8 oranges and strain into a jug. Pour over ice in short glasses. Carry them carefully and look where you are going, because orange juice is best kept in the glass and not on a famous film star.

s.note: Toasted sesame nori strips, crisp and salty
s.how: Brush 6 nori sheets lightly with sesame oil and sprinkle with sesame seeds and a pinch of salt. Toast one at a time in a dry pan for 30 seconds a side until crisp. Cut into strips with scissors and pile into a bowl like a kelp forest.

s.note: Bright fruit in colour patches with yoghurt for dipping.
s.how: Arrange 2 cups watermelon cubes, 1 punnet hulled strawberries, 2 sliced kiwi fruit, 1 punnet blueberries and 500g green grapes in colour blocks on a big platter so the fruit 'hides' in patches. Serve with 200g vanilla yoghurt in a bowl for dipping.

m.note: Lime chilli chicken over rice with avocado, corn and beans
m.how: Marinate 800g chicken thighs in lime juice, chilli and salt, then grill and slice. Build bowls of long grain rice with the chicken, sliced avocado, corn, black beans and a spoon of salsa. A California beach lunch in a bowl.

w.note: Blue jelly glasses with cream and an orange slice for Nemo
w.how: Make up 2 packets of blue jelly and pour into glasses. Chill for 3 hours until set. Top with whipped cream and tuck a slice of orange on top of each for a little orange fish. Just keep eating.

d.note: Blue lemonade spiders with vanilla ice cream
d.how: Pour cold lemonade into tall glasses and add a drop of blue colouring, stirring until ocean blue. Gently add a scoop of vanilla ice cream so it floats and foams. Serve straight away with a long spoon.

s.note: Baked egg, ham and cheddar bites from a muffin tin
s.how: Whisk 8 eggs with 100ml milk, 100g grated cheddar, sliced spring onion and diced ham. Pour into a greased 12-hole muffin tin and bake at 180C for 15 minutes until puffed and set. Serve warm to someone who came home late again.

s.note: Puff pastry rolls with pepperoni and mozzarella
s.how: Spread 2 sheets puff pastry with 4 tbsp pizza sauce, add 100g sliced pepperoni and 150g grated mozzarella and roll up tightly. Slice into 3cm pieces and bake at 200C for 18 minutes.

m.note: Braised beef brisket with onions and roast carrots
m.how: Brown a 1.5kg brisket, then soften 3 sliced onions. Add 250ml red wine, 500ml beef stock and 2 tbsp tomato paste and braise covered at 160C for 3.5 hours. Roast 6 carrots for the last 40 minutes and slice the meat across the grain.

w.note: Soft vanilla cookies iced half white, half chocolate
w.how: Beat 120g butter with 150g sugar, add 2 eggs, 150ml milk and vanilla, then 300g self-raising flour. Spoon 12 rounds onto trays and bake at 180C for 12 minutes. Ice half of each with white icing and half with icing mixed with 2 tbsp cocoa.

d.note: Frothy vanilla hot chocolate in mugs
d.how: Heat 1L milk until steaming with a drop of vanilla. Whisk in 150g chopped dark chocolate until smooth and frothy. Pour into mugs and drink slowly in a quiet library corner, waiting for someone to swing by.

s.note: Puff pastry chocolate croissants, golden and flaky
s.how: Cut 2 puff pastry sheets into long triangles. Lay a stick of dark chocolate at the wide end and roll up towards the point. Curve into crescents, brush with beaten egg and bake at 200C for 15 minutes until puffed and golden.

s.note: Plum jam doughnuts dusted with icing sugar
s.how: Mix 500g flour, 7g yeast, 2 eggs, 50g butter and warm milk into a soft dough and prove an hour. Roll into balls, prove again and fry at 175C until golden. Pipe plum jam into each and dust with icing sugar. A proper bakery treat.

m.note: Chicken braised in red wine with bacon and mushrooms
m.how: Brown 1.2kg chicken pieces and 150g bacon lardons. Add 12 small onions and 250g mushrooms, then 500ml red wine, 250ml stock and thyme. Simmer covered 45 minutes and serve with 800g potatoes mashed with butter.
