w.note: Crisp filo apple strudel with sultanas and cinnamon
w.how: Toss 4 sliced green apples with 80g sultanas, a teaspoon of cinnamon and a handful of breadcrumbs. Layer buttered filo sheets, spread the filling along one edge and roll up. Brush with butter and bake at 190C for 35 minutes. Dust with icing sugar.

d.note: Strong coffee with hot milk in big cups
d.how: Brew a strong pot of coffee. Heat 1L milk until steaming and froth it with a whisk. Pour coffee and milk into big wide cups at the same time, half and half. Drink it at a Paris cafe table watching the street go by.

s.note: Soy sesame tuna poke spooned onto rice crackers
s.how: Cut 300g sashimi tuna into small cubes. Toss with 2 tbsp soy sauce, a teaspoon of sesame oil and sliced spring onion. Spoon onto rice crackers just before serving so they stay crisp. Eat by the pool at a Hawaiian resort.

s.note: Honey lime pineapple spears grilled until charred
s.how: Cut a pineapple into long spears. Brush with honey mixed with lime juice. Grill over high heat, turning, until caramelised and charred at the edges. Serve warm with extra lime. Do less, and the pineapple does more.

m.note: Smoky salt pork slow cooked in banana leaves with rice
m.how: Rub a 2kg pork shoulder with smoked salt. Wrap tightly in banana leaves, then foil, and cook at 150C for 5 hours until it falls apart. Shred and serve over jasmine rice with a crunchy shredded cabbage salad on the side.

w.note: Bright mango and lime sorbet scraped by hand
w.how: Dissolve 150g sugar in 150ml hot water and cool. Blend the flesh of 3 ripe mangoes with the syrup and the juice of 2 limes until smooth. Freeze in a tray, scraping with a fork every hour for 4 hours. Scoop into glasses.

d.note: Dark rum with orange, lime and mint over crushed ice
d.how: For each drink, shake 45ml dark rum with 60ml orange juice, 20ml lime juice and 15ml sugar syrup over ice. Strain over crushed ice and top with a sprig of mint. Make an orange and lime version without rum for anyone not drinking.

s.note: Soft eggs wrapped in herby sausage meat and crumbed
s.how: Boil 6 eggs for 6 minutes, cool and peel. Mix 500g sausage meat with sage and pepper, wrap around each egg, roll in flour, beaten egg and breadcrumbs and fry at 170C for 8 minutes. Halve and serve with mustard.

s.note: Smoked salmon on oatcakes with cream cheese and dill
s.how: Spread oatcakes with cream cheese. Top with folds of smoked salmon and a sprig of dill. Squeeze over a little lemon and lay them out on a slate. Any bears in the house will want the lot.

m.note: Lamb, barley and vegetable broth finished with parsley
m.how: Simmer 1kg lamb neck with 150g pearl barley in 2L water for an hour. Add 2 sliced leeks, 3 diced carrots and 2 diced turnips and simmer another hour. Shred the lamb back in, season well and stir through chopped parsley.

w.note: Honey oat cake with berries, a raspberry on top
w.how: Beat 125g butter with 150g honey, then 2 eggs. Fold in 200g self-raising flour, 50g rolled oats and a handful of raspberries. Bake at 175C for 40 minutes. Glaze with warm honey and set a single raspberry on top. Do not feed it to your mum.

d.note: Raspberry, honey and toasted oat shake with cream
d.how: Toast 2 tbsp rolled oats in a dry pan until golden. Blend 200g raspberries with 750ml cold milk, 2 tbsp honey and most of the oats until smooth. Pour into tall glasses, top with whipped cream and the rest of the oats.

s.note: Golden corn fritters with sour cream and chive dip
s.how: Mix a drained can of corn with 100g flour, 2 eggs, sliced spring onions and a pinch of paprika. Fry spoonfuls in a little oil until golden on both sides. Stir chopped chives through sour cream for the dip and serve the fritters warm.

s.note: Paprika fried flathead bites with lemon and tartare
s.how: Cut 500g flathead into bite-sized pieces and dust in flour mixed with smoked paprika and salt. Fry at 180C for 3 minutes until crisp. Drain on paper and serve with lemon wedges and tartare sauce, like a meal on the deck of a trawler.

m.note: Slow braised beef with carrots, celery and potatoes
m.how: Brown a 1.5kg piece of beef chuck all over. Add a sliced onion, 3 carrots, 2 celery sticks and 500ml beef stock. Cover and braise at 160C for 3 hours, adding 800g potatoes for the last hour. Slice and serve with the juices.

w.note: Lattice cinnamon apple pie with vanilla ice cream
w.how: Cook 6 sliced green apples with 50g butter, 100g brown sugar and a teaspoon of cinnamon until just soft, then cool. Line a pie dish with shortcrust, fill and weave a lattice top. Bake at 190C for 45 minutes and serve warm with ice cream.

d.note: Fresh mint lemonade in a big jug over ice
d.how: Dissolve 150g sugar in 150ml hot water and cool. Squeeze 6 lemons into a big jug and add the syrup with 1.5L cold water. Add bruised mint and plenty of ice. Pour into tall glasses on the farmhouse porch.

s.note: Fanned apples with honey peanut butter dip and cinnamon
s.how: Slice 2 red and 2 green apples and fan them on a board. Warm 4 tbsp peanut butter with 2 tbsp honey until loose and spoon into a bowl in the middle. Dust the apples with a little cinnamon. The orchard at the old castle still grows them.

s.note: Simple damper torn warm and served with butter
s.how: Rub 60g butter into 450g self-raising flour with a pinch of salt. Mix in 300ml milk with a knife until it just comes together. Shape into a round, score and bake at 200C for 30 minutes. Tear warm and serve with plenty of butter.

m.note: Lamb, barley and leek stew with rosemary and bread
m.how: Brown 1kg diced lamb shoulder, then add 150g pearl barley, 3 sliced carrots, 2 sliced leeks, rosemary and 1.5L water. Simmer for 2 hours until the lamb is tender. Serve in deep bowls with crusty bread for an army hiding underground.

w.note: Cinnamon apple crumble with oats and custard
w.how: Peel and slice 5 green apples and cook with 30g butter and cinnamon for 5 minutes. Spoon into a dish. Rub 70g butter into oats, flour and 80g brown sugar and scatter over. Bake at 180C for 35 minutes and serve with warm custard.

d.note: Strong mugs of station tea with milk and sugar.
d.how: Brew 4 black tea bags in a warmed pot with 1L just-boiled water for 4 minutes. Pour into 4 mugs with a splash of milk and 2 sugars each, the way a station tea stand makes it.

s.note: Gruyere and cheddar sourdough toasties cut into fingers
s.how: Butter thick slices of sourdough on the outside. Fill with grated gruyere and cheddar. Cook in a pan over medium heat for 3 minutes a side, pressing down, until golden and melting. Cut into fingers and serve to anyone who has just come home very late from work.

s.note: Smoked salmon blinis and honey fig goat's cheese bites
s.how: Top 16 blinis with creme fraiche, smoked salmon and snipped chives. Halve 6 fresh figs, top each with goat's cheese and a drizzle of honey. Arrange both in neat rows on a white platter, as sharp as a front row seat.

m.note: Butter basted sirloin with creamed spinach and crispy potatoes
m.how: Roast 1kg potato chunks at 220C for 45 minutes. Sear 4 sirloin steaks in a smoking pan, baste with butter and garlic and rest. Wilt 300g spinach and simmer with 150ml cream until thick. Serve sliced, exactly when expected. That's all.

w.note: Custard tart crowned with glazed blueberries
w.how: Blind bake a sweet shortcrust case and cool. Fill with 500ml thick custard and pile 250g blueberries on top. Warm apricot jam with a splash of water and brush over to glaze. Dust the edge with icing sugar. The colour was chosen for you years ago.

d.note: Hot strong latte with an extra shot, served exactly on time
d.how: Pull a double shot of strong espresso into each cup and add an extra shot on top. Steam milk until silky and pour in. Serve hot and on time, because a cold one will be sent back without a word.

s.note: Sticky honey barbecue wings with ranch dip
s.how: Toss 1kg chicken wings with salt and bake at 220C for 45 minutes until crisp. Warm 125ml barbecue sauce with 2 tbsp honey and toss the wings through. Mix sour cream with mayonnaise and chives for a ranch dip and serve alongside.

s.note: Crisp fries under cheese sauce with jalapeños
s.how: Bake 1kg frozen chips at 220C until crisp. Melt 30g butter, stir in 2 tbsp flour, whisk in 300ml milk until thick and stir in 150g grated cheddar. Pour over the chips and top with sliced spring onion and pickled jalapeños.

m.note: Meatball spaghetti with garlic bread for the whole study group
m.how: Roll 600g beef mince into meatballs and brown. Add 2 cans crushed tomatoes and simmer 40 minutes. Split a baguette, spread with garlic butter and bake until crisp. Toss the sauce through 500g spaghetti with parmesan and serve the lot.

w.note: Shaggy blue buttercream cupcakes with purple sprinkles
w.how: Beat 125g butter with 150g sugar, then 2 eggs, then fold in 200g self-raising flour and 125ml milk. Bake at 175C for 18 minutes and cool. Beat butter, icing sugar and blue colouring and pipe with a grass tip for shaggy fur. Add purple sprinkles.

d.note: Green apple, lime and mint cooler.
d.how: Pour 750ml cloudy apple juice and 400ml soda water into a jug with the juice of 1 lime and a handful of mint. Stir in a few drops of green food colouring and pour over ice, with a thin round of green apple floating on top.

s.note: Lager-battered cod with lemon and tartare
s.how: Cut 500g cod into bite-sized pieces. Whisk flour with ice-cold lager to a thin batter. Dust the fish in flour, dip in batter and fry at 180C for 3 minutes until crisp. Drain and serve with lemon wedges and tartare, like dinner at a lighthouse.

s.note: Hot sauce butter wings with blue cheese dip
s.how: Leave 1kg chicken wings uncovered in the fridge overnight, then bake at 220C for 45 minutes until crisp. Melt 50g butter with 100ml hot sauce and toss through. Mash blue cheese into sour cream for the dip and serve with celery.

m.note: Garlic butter roasted prawns, mussels, scallops and fish
m.how: Spread 400g green prawns, 500g mussels, 300g scallops and 400g white fish chunks in a big roasting tray. Dot with garlic butter and roast at 220C for 10 minutes until the mussels open. Squeeze over lemon and serve with crusty bread.

w.note: Salted caramel and chocolate tart with sea salt
w.how: Blind bake a sweet shortcrust case. Melt 200g sugar to amber caramel, whisk in 150ml cream and 60g butter, pour into the case and chill. Melt 150g dark chocolate into 150ml hot cream, pour over and set overnight. Finish with sea salt flakes.

d.note: Coconut water and lemonade tinted ocean blue with lime
d.how: Fill glasses with crushed ice. Pour in equal parts coconut water and lemonade, add a drop of blue colouring and stir until ocean blue. Squeeze in a wedge of lime. Drink it like the king of the seven seas.

s.note: Charred garlic chilli lime prawn skewers
s.how: Toss 600g green prawns with crushed garlic, chopped red chilli, lime zest and melted butter. Thread onto skewers and grill for 2 minutes a side until charred. Serve with lime wedges and spoon over any butter left in the pan.

s.note: Tropical fruit wedges with lime and toasted coconut
s.how: Cut 2 mangoes, half a pineapple and half a papaya into wedges and pile on a platter with halved passionfruit. Squeeze over lime juice and scatter with toasted shredded coconut. Serve chilled on a hot afternoon by the reef.

m.note: Snapper poached in lemongrass coconut milk over rice
m.how: Bruise 2 lemongrass stalks and simmer in 800ml coconut milk with sliced red chilli for 10 minutes. Add 4 snapper fillets and poach gently for 10 minutes. Squeeze in lime juice and serve over steamed jasmine rice with fresh herbs.

w.note: Set coconut pudding with mango and passionfruit
w.how: Warm 800ml coconut milk with 100g sugar until dissolved. Soak 4 gelatine sheets, squeeze and stir in. Pour into glasses and chill for 4 hours until set. Top with diced mango and passionfruit pulp before serving.

d.note: Chilled coconut water with lime and pineapple
d.how: Fill glasses with ice. Pour in cold coconut water and add a splash of pineapple juice and a squeeze of lime. Stir and serve. As close as you can get to the water of Pandora without a long flight.

s.note: A big bowl of party lollies for a thirteenth birthday
s.how: Tip 200g gummy lollies, 150g sour straps cut into pieces, 200g jelly beans and 100g chocolate buttons into a big bowl and toss together. Set it in the middle of the room for a thirteenth birthday party.

s.note: Pale pink iced sugar cookies dusted with glitter
s.how: Beat 200g butter with 150g sugar and an egg, then mix in 300g flour. Chill, roll and cut into rounds. Bake at 180C for 10 minutes and cool. Ice pale pink with icing sugar and a drop of colouring, then dust with edible glitter like wishing dust.

m.note: Sticky soy honey chicken noodles in takeaway boxes
m.how: Stir-fry 500g sliced chicken thighs until browned. Add broccoli florets and a sliced red capsicum and cook 3 minutes. Toss through 400g cooked egg noodles with soy sauce and honey until sticky. Pack into takeaway boxes.

w.note: Pink buttercream birthday cake with sprinkles and thirteen candles
w.how: Beat 250g butter with 250g sugar, add 4 eggs and fold in 250g self-raising flour. Bake at 175C for 30 minutes and cool. Ice with pink buttercream made from butter and icing sugar, cover in sprinkles and add thirteen candles. Make a wish.

d.note: Pineapple and coconut blended with ice, rum for adults
d.how: Blend 500ml pineapple juice with 200ml coconut cream and a big handful of ice until thick and smooth. Pour into glasses for the kids. Add 30ml white rum to each glass for the grown-ups who turned thirty overnight.

s.note: Homemade hard lollipops poured onto baking paper
s.how: Boil 200g sugar, 80ml glucose syrup and 80ml water to 150C without stirring. Take off the heat and stir in a drop of food colouring. Pour small rounds onto baking paper and press a lollipop stick into each. Leave to harden for 20 minutes.

s.note: Mini bagels with cream cheese, smoked salmon and capers
s.how: Split and toast 12 mini bagels. Spread with cream cheese and top each with a fold of smoked salmon, a few capers and thin slices of red onion. Lay them out on a tray, the kind of snack you eat in a barber's chair talking about life.

m.note: Thin, blistered New York pizza, folded to eat.
m.how: Stretch 2 balls pizza dough (500g total) as thin as you can into big rounds. Spread with 200ml pizza sauce and 300g grated mozzarella. Bake on a very hot tray at 250C for 8 minutes until blistered, then dust with dried oregano and parmesan, cut into big slices and fold to eat.

w.note: Maple pecan cookies, soft in the middle
w.how: Cream 125g butter with 100g brown sugar and 3 tbsp maple syrup, then beat in an egg. Fold in 200g flour and 80g chopped pecans. Roll into balls, flatten slightly and bake at 180C for 12 minutes. Cool on the tray and watch them spin down like seeds.

d.note: Strong black coffee, or decaf with hot milk
d.how: Brew a strong pot of black coffee and pour into small cups for the band. For the late set, brew decaf and pour with a splash of hot milk. Sip slowly while the piano plays in a small New York jazz club.

s.note: Chilled prawns on crushed ice with cocktail sauce
s.how: Pile crushed ice onto a platter and arrange 500g cooked prawns on top. Mix 4 tbsp mayonnaise with 2 tbsp tomato sauce, a squeeze of lemon and a dash of hot sauce. Serve in a small bowl in the middle. Everybody chill.

s.note: Lettuce cups of leaves, pea shoots and feta with lemon honey dressing
s.how: Separate baby cos lettuce into small cups. Toss pea shoots, sliced cucumber and mint with lemon juice and a little honey and olive oil. Spoon into the cups and crumble feta over the top. Green, leafy and only slightly dangerous.

m.note: Chicken noodle soup with parsley and lemon
m.how: Simmer 600g chicken thighs with 2 carrots, 2 celery sticks and an onion in 2L water for 40 minutes. Shred the chicken back in, add 150g egg noodles and cook 5 minutes. Finish with chopped parsley and a squeeze of lemon.

w.note: Vanilla and mint ice cream cake with meringue snow
w.how: Crush 250g chocolate biscuits with 80g melted butter and press into a tin. Soften 1L vanilla and 1L mint ice cream and layer over the base. Freeze overnight. Top with crushed meringue nests like fresh snow just before slicing.

d.note: Icy blue lemonade slushie with lime
d.how: Blitz 1L lemonade with a drop of blue colouring, the juice of a lime and a big bag of ice in a blender until slushy. Pour into tall glasses and serve straight away with spoons and straws, frozen solid like a villain.

s.note: Goat's cheese and caramelised onion tartlets
s.how: Cook 3 sliced onions slowly with a spoon of brown sugar and thyme for 30 minutes. Cut shortcrust into rounds and press into a patty tin. Bake at 190C for 12 minutes, then fill with the onions and a piece of goat's cheese and bake 5 more minutes.

s.note: Smoked salmon toasts with capers and lemon zest
s.how: Slice a baguette and toast until golden. Spread with cream cheese, top with folds of smoked salmon, a scatter of capers and a little lemon zest. Serve on a plate at a dinner party where at least one thing will go badly.

m.note: Creamy leek and potato soup, tied with twine not blue string
m.how: Slice 3 leeks and soften in butter with 500g diced potatoes. Add 1L chicken stock and simmer 25 minutes, then blend smooth with 150ml cream. Serve with crusty bread. Tie the leeks with kitchen twine, not blue string.

w.note: Steamed sponge pudding with marmalade and custard
w.how: Spoon 4 tbsp orange marmalade into a greased pudding basin. Beat 125g butter with 125g sugar, add 2 eggs and fold in 175g self-raising flour. Spoon on top, cover tightly and steam for 90 minutes. Turn out and serve with hot custard.

d.note: Chilled chardonnay, or sparkling apple juice
d.how: Chill a bottle of chardonnay in the fridge for a couple of hours. Pour a generous glass for anyone writing in a diary tonight. For non-drinkers, pour cold sparkling apple juice into the same glasses.

s.note: Crumbed risotto balls with a mozzarella centre and tomato sauce
s.how: Cook 300g arborio rice into a risotto with stock and parmesan and chill overnight. Roll into ovals around a cube of mozzarella. Coat in beaten egg and panko and fry at 180C until golden. Serve hot with a little warm napoli sauce.

s.note: Garlic toasted ciabatta with tomato and basil
s.how: Slice a ciabatta, brush with olive oil and toast until golden. Rub each slice with a cut garlic clove. Chop 4 ripe tomatoes with torn basil, olive oil and salt and pile on top. Eat quickly before you zoom off on a scooter.

m.note: Spaghetti in creamy pecorino and black pepper
m.how: Cook 500g spaghetti and keep a cup of the pasta water. Toast a spoon of cracked black pepper in a little butter. Add the pasta and a splash of water, then toss in 150g finely grated pecorino off the heat until creamy. Serve straight away.

w.note: Vanilla and lemon gelato with crushed amaretti
w.how: Scoop vanilla ice cream and lemon sorbet into waffle cones or small glasses. Crush a few amaretti biscuits and scatter over the top. Eat it sitting on the steps, the way a runaway princess would on her one day off.

d.note: Short strong espresso, or a glass of sparkling
d.how: Brew short, strong espresso and pour into small warmed cups. For a celebration, pour sparkling wine into small glasses instead. Drink at a cafe table near the fountain, without telling anyone who you really are.

s.note: Crisp pork and cabbage dumplings with black vinegar
s.how: Mix 400g pork mince with shredded wombok, grated ginger, sliced spring onion and salt. Fill dumpling wrappers and pleat. Fry in oil until crisp underneath, add a splash of water, cover and steam 5 minutes. Serve with black vinegar.

s.note: Steamed buns filled with sweet red bean paste
s.how: Take 12 frozen bao buns and gently open each one. Spoon in a teaspoon of sweet red bean paste and pinch the edges closed. Steam in a lined basket for 12 minutes until soft and puffy. Serve warm in the basket.

m.note: Glossy soy braised chicken with rice and garlic bok choy
m.how: Brown 1kg chicken thighs, then add 125ml soy sauce, 250ml water, sliced ginger, 2 star anise and a spoon of sugar. Braise 40 minutes until glossy. Serve over jasmine rice with bok choy stir-fried with garlic.

w.note: Silky mango pudding topped with fresh mango
w.how: Blend 2 mangoes into a puree and warm with 80g sugar. Soak 4 gelatine sheets, squeeze and stir in until dissolved. Stir in 250ml evaporated milk. Pour into glasses and chill for 4 hours. Top with diced fresh mango.

d.note: Milk tea with brown sugar syrup over tapioca pearls
d.how: Cook tapioca pearls as the packet says and soak in syrup of brown sugar and water. Brew 4 strong black tea bags in 500ml water and cool. Spoon pearls into glasses, add ice, pour over the tea and top with milk. Serve with wide straws.

s.note: Sticky gochujang honey wings with sesame
s.how: Toss 1kg chicken wings with salt and bake at 220C for 45 minutes until crisp. Warm 3 tbsp gochujang with 3 tbsp honey, crushed garlic and a splash of soy until glossy. Toss the wings through and scatter with sesame seeds. Super spicy, like the cafe special.

s.note: White chocolate marshmallows with Baymax faces
s.how: Melt 200g white chocolate. Dip 20 marshmallows until fully coated and set on baking paper. Melt a little dark chocolate and pipe two small dots joined by a line on each one for the face. Leave to set. On a scale of one to ten, very cute.

m.note: Miso ramen with chashu pork, soft eggs and nori
m.how: Braise 600g pork belly in soy and water for 2 hours, then slice. Whisk white miso into hot stock for the broth. Cook ramen noodles and soft-boil 4 eggs for 6 minutes. Build bowls with pork, halved eggs, nori and sliced spring onion.

w.note: Crisp choux puffs filled with custard cream
w.how: Bring 250ml water and 100g butter to the boil, beat in 150g flour, then beat in 4 eggs. Pipe small mounds and bake at 200C for 25 minutes until puffed and dry. Fold whipped cream into custard, fill each puff and dust with icing sugar.

d.note: Black tea with honey and lemon, hot or iced
d.how: Brew 4 black tea bags in 1L boiling water for 4 minutes. Stir in 3 tbsp honey and the juice of a lemon. Serve hot in mugs, or cool it down and pour over ice with lemon slices. Good for healthcare companions and humans alike.

s.note: Smoked salmon on rye crispbread with dill and capers
s.how: Spread rye crispbreads with cream cheese. Top with folds of smoked salmon, a sprig of dill and a few capers. Squeeze over a little lemon just before serving. A taste of an Alaskan town for a reluctant New York visitor.

s.note: Baked crab and cream cheese dip with crackers
s.how: Mix 250g crab meat with 250g cream cheese, 2 tbsp mayonnaise and sliced spring onion. Spread in a small dish and bake at 190C for 20 minutes until golden and bubbling. Serve hot with water crackers at the welcome party.

m.note: Maple mustard salmon with baby potatoes and green beans
m.how: Mix 2 tbsp maple syrup with a spoon of wholegrain mustard and brush over 4 salmon fillets. Roast at 200C for 15 minutes. Boil 800g baby potatoes and steam green beans, then toss both with butter. Serve together.

w.note: Jam and cream sponge iced white with fresh flowers
w.how: Beat 250g butter with 250g sugar, add 4 eggs and fold in 250g self-raising flour. Bake in 2 tins at 175C for 25 minutes. Sandwich with strawberry jam and whipped cream, ice white and top with fresh flowers for a barn wedding.

d.note: Strong espresso with steamed milk in takeaway cups
d.how: Pull a strong double shot of espresso into each takeaway cup. Steam milk until silky and pour in. Snap on a lid and hand it over fast, before your boss reaches the lift.

s.note: Raw young carrots with a creamy herb dip
s.how: Peel a bag of baby carrots and stand them upright in a glass. Mix 300ml sour cream with snipped chives, chopped dill and a squeeze of lemon. Serve the carrots with the dip, a better roadside meal than the one in the film.

s.note: Ham, cheese and mustard sandwiches wrapped in wax paper
s.how: Butter white bread and fill with sliced ham, cheddar and a stripe of yellow mustard. Cut in halves and wrap each in wax paper. Pack them into a bag for a long overnight bus ride from Miami to New York.

m.note: Scrambled eggs, bacon and toast on tin plates
m.how: Fry 8 rashers of bacon until crisp. Whisk 8 eggs with salt and scramble slowly in butter until soft. Toast and butter white bread. Serve it all on tin plates with chives scattered over the eggs, behind the walls of Jericho.

w.note: Cinnamon sugar doughnuts for dunking in coffee
w.how: Mix 500g flour, 7g yeast, 2 eggs, 50g butter and warm milk into a soft dough and prove an hour. Roll, cut into rings and prove again. Fry at 175C until golden, then roll in cinnamon sugar. Dunk them properly, the way the film teaches.

d.note: Strong black coffee in thick mugs for dunking
d.how: Brew a big pot of strong black coffee. Pour into thick mugs and set milk and raw sugar on the side. Dunk a doughnut, count to two and get it into your mouth before it falls apart.

s.note: Glossy chilli honey roasted cashews and peanuts
s.how: Toss 200g cashews and 200g peanuts with 2 tbsp honey, a pinch of chilli flakes and smoked paprika. Spread on a lined tray and roast at 170C for 12 minutes until glossy. Cool until crunchy and serve hot to the touch in flavour only.

s.note: Cucumber rounds with lemon whipped feta and dill
s.how: Slice 2 Lebanese cucumbers into thick rounds. Whip 150g feta with 150g Greek yoghurt and a squeeze of lemon until smooth. Pipe or spoon onto each round and finish with dill and cracked pepper. Cool and refreshing, a little teary.

m.note: Harissa lamb braised with chickpeas and tomato, with flatbread
m.how: Brown 1kg diced lamb shoulder, then stir in 2 tbsp harissa and a teaspoon of cumin. Add a can of crushed tomatoes, a can of drained chickpeas and water to cover. Braise at 160C for 3 hours until it pulls apart. Serve with warm flatbread.

w.note: Pavlova with cream, blueberries and purple flowers
w.how: Whisk 4 egg whites to stiff peaks, then add 220g caster sugar a spoon at a time until glossy. Shape into a round and bake at 120C for 90 minutes, then cool in the oven. Top with whipped cream, blueberries and edible purple flowers.

d.note: Hot apple juice spiced with cinnamon and orange.
d.how: Heat 1L apple juice with 2 cinnamon sticks, 4 cloves, 3 strips orange peel and 2 slices ginger until steaming, then keep warm for 10 minutes. Strain into mugs and serve with a cinnamon stick in each.

s.note: Little iced cakes with eat me piped on top
s.how: Beat 125g butter with 125g sugar, add 2 eggs and fold in 125g self-raising flour. Spoon into a mini muffin tin and bake at 175C for 12 minutes. Cool, ice white and pipe eat me on top in pink icing. Watch out for growing spurts.

s.note: Puff pastry hearts filled with jam and cream
s.how: Cut 2 sheets of puff pastry into hearts and bake at 200C for 12 minutes until puffed. Cool, split in half and fill with strawberry jam and whipped cream. Dust the tops with icing sugar. Keep a close eye on them, someone always steals the tarts.

m.note: Creamy chicken and leek pie under golden puff pastry
m.how: Brown 800g diced chicken thighs, then soften 2 sliced leeks. Stir in a spoon of flour, 250ml chicken stock, 200ml cream and thyme and simmer until thick. Pour into a dish, top with puff pastry and bake at 200C for 25 minutes.

w.note: Pastel jam and cream sponge with candles for nobody
w.how: Beat 250g butter with 250g sugar, add 4 eggs and fold in 250g self-raising flour. Bake in 2 tins at 175C for 25 minutes. Sandwich with strawberry jam, ice in pastel colours with icing sugar and add candles. Happy unbirthday to everyone.

d.note: Chilled earl grey with lemonade and honey in teacups
d.how: Brew 4 earl grey tea bags in 500ml boiling water and stir in a spoon of honey. Cool, then mix with 500ml lemonade and a squeeze of lemon. Pour over ice in mismatched teacups. Drink me, but not too much at once.

s.note: Toasted baguette with whipped ricotta and roast tomatoes
s.how: Slice a baguette, brush with oil and toast at 200C for 8 minutes. Roast 250g cherry tomatoes with oil and salt for 15 minutes. Whip 250g ricotta with lemon zest and pepper, spread on the toasts and top with tomatoes, basil and a little honey.

s.note: Fried pea and ham risotto balls with marinara
s.how: Make a firm risotto with 300g arborio rice and 1L stock, stir through 100g peas, 100g diced ham and 50g parmesan, then cool. Roll into 16 balls, crumb in flour, egg and breadcrumbs and fry at 180C for 4 minutes. Serve with 400g warm marinara.

m.note: Beef and pork meatballs in tomato sauce over rigatoni
m.how: Mix 300g beef mince and 300g pork mince with breadcrumbs and an egg, roll into balls and brown. Add 2 cans crushed tomatoes and torn basil and simmer 40 minutes. Toss through 500g cooked rigatoni with plenty of parmesan.

w.note: Silky lemon curd tart, bright as the yellow dress
w.how: Blind bake a sweet shortcrust case. Whisk the juice and zest of 4 lemons with 4 eggs, 150g sugar and 150ml cream. Pour into the case and bake at 150C for 20 minutes until just set. Chill and serve with whipped cream.

d.note: Cold lager in plastic cups, or lemonade
d.how: Chill the lager well and pour into plastic cups like at the game. For anyone not drinking, pour lemonade over ice. Cheer loudly and ask a lot of questions during the important bits.

s.note: Golden grilled crab and cream cheese toasts
s.how: Mix 250g crab meat with 125g cream cheese, a spoon of mayonnaise, lemon zest and sliced spring onion. Slice a baguette, spread the mix on each slice and grill until golden at the edges. Serve hot on game day.

s.note: Sticky tomato glazed mini meatballs on toothpicks
s.how: Mix 250g beef mince and 250g pork mince with grated parmesan, breadcrumbs and an egg. Roll into small balls and bake at 200C for 15 minutes. Warm tomato sauce with brown sugar until sticky and toss the meatballs through. Serve on toothpicks.

m.note: Shaved rib eye with onions, capsicum and provolone
m.how: Freeze a 600g rib eye steak for 30 minutes and shave it thin. Fry sliced onion and green capsicum on a hot plate until soft, add the beef and sear fast. Lay provolone on top to melt and pile into long bread rolls. Go Birds.

w.note: Warm raisin bran muffins with butter
w.how: Soak 100g wheat bran in 300ml buttermilk for 10 minutes. Stir in 100g brown sugar, an egg, 60ml oil and 100g raisins, then fold in 200g self-raising flour. Bake in a muffin tin at 190C for 20 minutes. Serve warm with butter.

d.note: Cold lager in pint glasses, or ginger beer
d.how: Chill the lager and pint glasses in the fridge. Pour slowly down the side of the tilted glass. Pour ginger beer for anyone not drinking. Raise a glass every time the team scores and keep the remote within reach.

s.note: Crumbed fried mozzarella sticks with marinara
s.how: Cut 400g firm mozzarella into 16 sticks. Roll in flour, beaten egg and breadcrumbs twice and freeze 30 minutes. Fry at 180C for 1 minute until golden and serve with 300g warm marinara.

s.note: Mini beef sliders with cheese and pickles
s.how: Shape 500g beef mince into 12 small patties, season and cook on a hot pan for 2 minutes a side, adding a slice of cheese at the end. Put in 12 slider buns with pickles and tomato sauce.

m.note: Honey garlic thyme drumsticks with roast potatoes and carrots
m.how: Toss 8 chicken drumsticks with honey, crushed garlic, thyme and oil. Roast at 200C for 40 minutes alongside 1kg potato chunks and 4 sliced carrots, turning once. Serve on one big tray for two brothers on a quest.

w.note: Hot fudge sundae with cream and sprinkles
w.how: Heat 150ml cream until steaming and pour over 150g chopped dark chocolate, stirring into hot fudge. Scoop vanilla ice cream into tall glasses, pour over the fudge and top with whipped cream and sprinkles. One more day well spent.

d.note: Purple apple and blackcurrant potion with soda
d.how: Fill glasses with ice. Pour in apple juice to halfway, add a splash of blackcurrant cordial and top with soda water. Stir until it turns purple like a potion. Serve with a pinch of magic.

s.note: Crisp garlic, parsley and parmesan Italian bread
s.how: Mash 100g butter with crushed garlic, chopped parsley and grated parmesan. Split a loaf of Italian bread, spread thickly and bake at 200C for 12 minutes until crisp at the edges. Cut into thick slices and serve in the alley behind the restaurant.

s.note: Salami, provolone, olives and artichoke with torn bread
s.how: Fold 150g salami and slices of provolone onto a board. Add kalamata olives, marinated artichoke hearts and strips of roasted red capsicum. Tear a loaf of Italian bread beside it. Set it out for two by candlelight.

m.note: One big plate of spaghetti and meatballs to share
m.how: Mix 300g beef mince and 300g pork mince with parmesan, parsley and an egg, roll into balls and brown. Add 2 cans crushed tomatoes and torn basil and simmer 40 minutes. Pile over 500g spaghetti on one big plate. Leave the last meatball for your date.

w.note: Crisp cannoli with orange ricotta and chocolate chips
w.how: Drain 500g ricotta overnight, then beat with 80g icing sugar, orange zest and 50g dark chocolate chips. Spoon into a piping bag and fill 12 cannoli shells just before serving. Dip each end in crushed pistachios.

d.note: Blood orange sparkling water with rosemary, or a red
d.how: Fill glasses with ice and a sprig of rosemary. Pour in blood orange juice and top with sparkling water. For the grown-ups, pour a glass of red wine instead. Serve at a small table with a checked cloth.

s.note: Cocktail franks in puff pastry with mustard and sauce
s.how: Simmer 24 cocktail franks for 3 minutes and drain. Cut puff pastry into strips and roll one around each frank. Brush with beaten egg and bake at 200C for 15 minutes until golden. Serve with mustard and tomato sauce at the reception.

s.note: Walnut-coated cheese ball with crackers, served on a lace doily
s.how: Mix 200g grated cheddar, 250g cream cheese and sliced spring onion. Shape into one big ball, roll in chopped walnuts and chill for an hour. Serve with crackers on a doily, eighties party style.

m.note: Parmesan meatballs in tomato sauce over spaghetti
m.how: Mix 300g beef mince, 300g pork mince, grated parmesan, chopped parsley, breadcrumbs and an egg. Roll into balls and brown. Add 2 cans crushed tomatoes and simmer 40 minutes. Serve over 500g spaghetti, the way Grandma Rosie pays for lessons.

w.note: Jam and cream sponge iced white with silver cachous
w.how: Beat 250g butter with 250g sugar, add 4 eggs and fold in 250g self-raising flour. Bake in 2 tins at 175C for 25 minutes. Sandwich with strawberry jam, ice white with buttercream and scatter silver cachous over the top.

d.note: Pineapple orange punch with lemonade and orange slices
d.how: Pour 1L pineapple juice and 1L orange juice into a big punch bowl. Add sliced oranges and plenty of ice, then top with 1L cold lemonade. Leave a ladle in the bowl and set out cups for the guests on the dance floor.

s.note: Chilli cumin peanuts and crunchy roasted chickpeas in little bowls
s.how: Drain and dry a can of chickpeas. Toss with 200g peanuts, a little oil, chilli flakes, ground cumin and sea salt. Roast at 200C for 30 minutes, shaking the tray, until crunchy. Serve in small bowls on the bar between sets.

s.note: Crisp potato and pea samosas with mint and coriander chutney
s.how: Boil and crush 600g potatoes with 150g peas, fried onion and a spoon of garam masala. Cut spring roll pastry into strips, fill and fold into triangles. Fry at 180C until crisp. Blitz mint and coriander with a little water, lemon and salt for chutney.

m.note: Layered yoghurt chicken biryani with saffron and fried onions
m.how: Marinate 1kg chicken thighs in yoghurt and garam masala for 2 hours. Fry 2 sliced onions until crisp. Par-cook 400g basmati for 5 minutes. Layer chicken, rice and onions in a pot, drizzle with saffron soaked in warm milk, seal and bake at 170C for 45 minutes.

w.note: Creamy cardamom rice pudding with pistachios
w.how: Simmer 100g basmati rice in 1.5L milk over low heat, stirring often, for 45 minutes until thick and creamy. Stir in 100g sugar and a pinch of ground cardamom. Serve warm or chilled with chopped pistachios scattered on top.

d.note: Spiced milky black tea strained into cups
d.how: Bring 500ml water to the boil with sliced ginger, a few crushed cardamom pods and a cinnamon stick. Add 4 black tea bags and simmer 2 minutes. Pour in 500ml milk and raw sugar to taste, simmer 5 minutes more and strain into cups.

s.note: Golden parmesan crisps like coins with fig jam
s.how: Mix 150g grated parmesan with chopped thyme. Spoon small rounds onto a lined tray and flatten into coins. Bake at 190C for 6 minutes until golden and lacy. Cool on the tray and pile them up like a vault full of gold with a pot of fig jam.

s.note: Fiery chilli honey soy wings scattered with sesame
s.how: Toss 1kg chicken wings with salt and bake at 220C for 45 minutes until crisp. Warm 3 tbsp honey with 2 tbsp soy sauce and 2 chopped red chillies until sticky. Toss the wings through and scatter with sesame seeds. Hot enough to escape a bank on.

m.note: Lamb braised in stout with carrots, mash and crusty bread
m.how: Brown 1kg diced lamb shoulder, then add 2 onions and 3 carrots. Pour in 375ml stout and water to cover and simmer for 3 hours until tender. Serve over buttery mash from 1kg potatoes with crusty bread on the side.

w.n: Platform nine and three-quarters treacle tart
w.note: Golden syrup and lemon tart served warm with cream
w.how: Blind bake a shortcrust case. Warm 400g golden syrup with 100g breadcrumbs and the zest and juice of a lemon and pour into the case. Bake at 180C for 30 minutes until just set. Serve warm with a pour of cream.

d.note: Chilled pumpkin, apple, honey and cinnamon juice
d.how: Roast 300g butternut pumpkin until soft and cool. Blend with 1L apple juice, a spoon of honey and a pinch of cinnamon until smooth. Strain into a jug, chill and pour over ice. Raise a glass to everyone who stayed to fight.

s.note: White chocolate dipped berries dusted with freeze-dried raspberry
s.how: Melt 200g white chocolate. Dip 250g strawberries and 125g blackberries halfway and set on baking paper. While still wet, dust with crushed freeze-dried raspberries. Chill for 15 minutes and serve like a forest picnic.

s.note: A pink beetroot dip and a blue cheese dip with pita
s.how: Blend 2 roasted beetroot with 200g Greek yoghurt and garlic until bright pink. Mash 100g blue cheese into 200ml sour cream. Serve side by side with warm pita crisps and let everyone argue about pink or blue.

m.note: Beef stewed with carrots, parsnips and thyme with bread
m.how: Brown 1kg diced beef chuck, then add a sliced onion, 3 carrots, 2 parsnips and thyme. Cover with water and simmer gently for 3 hours until tender. Serve in bowls with crusty bread and butter at a cottage in the woods.

w.note: Three-layer jam cake iced pink and blue, proudly crooked
w.how: Beat 300g butter with 300g sugar, add 5 eggs and fold in 300g self-raising flour. Bake in 3 tins at 175C for 25 minutes. Stack with raspberry jam and buttercream, then ice half pink and half blue. Leave it proudly a little crooked.

d.note: Sparkling apple and pomegranate with orange, or sparkling wine
d.how: Pour pomegranate juice into glasses to a third and top with sparkling apple juice. Add a slice of orange. For the grown-ups, top the pomegranate with sparkling wine instead. Raise a toast to the new princess.

s.note: Small golden crab cakes with lemon
s.how: Mix 400g crab meat with 2 tbsp mayonnaise, a spoon of Dijon, sliced spring onion and half a cup of breadcrumbs. Shape into small cakes and chill 30 minutes. Pan-fry until golden on both sides and serve with lemon wedges.

s.note: Crisp hash brown cakes with sour cream and chives
s.how: Grate 800g potatoes and a small onion, then squeeze out as much liquid as you can. Season and shape into small flat cakes. Fry in butter over medium heat for 5 minutes a side until crisp. Serve hot with sour cream and chives.

m.note: Poached eggs and ham on muffins under hollandaise
m.how: Melt 150g butter. Whisk 3 yolks with lemon juice over a gentle simmer, then slowly pour in the butter until thick. Poach 8 eggs for 3 minutes. Toast 4 English muffins, top with ham and the eggs and spoon over the hollandaise. Finish with chives.

w.note: Jam and cream sponge iced white, ready for a wedding
w.how: Beat 250g butter with 250g sugar, add 4 eggs and fold in 250g self-raising flour. Bake in 2 tins at 175C for 25 minutes. Sandwich with strawberry jam and whipped cream and ice white. Keep a running start in case the bride bolts.

d.note: Fresh squeezed orange juice over ice
d.how: Squeeze 8 oranges and strain into a jug. Pour over ice in tall glasses. Serve at the small-town diner counter while everyone in Hale talks about the wedding that might not happen.

s.note: Rice cups with spinach, carrot, beef, egg and gochujang
s.how: Cook beef mince with soy and garlic. Saute spinach and julienned carrot separately. Spoon jasmine rice into small bowls, arrange the beef and vegetables on top and add a fried egg and a dot of gochujang. Mix it all up before eating.

s.note: Twice-fried gochujang honey wings with sesame
s.how: Fry 1kg chicken wings at 160C for 10 minutes, rest, then fry again at 190C until crackly. Warm 3 tbsp gochujang with 3 tbsp honey and crushed garlic until glossy. Toss the wings through and scatter with sesame seeds.

m.note: Pork and kimchi stew with tofu and spring onion
m.how: Fry 400g sliced pork belly until browned, then add 300g chopped kimchi, crushed garlic and a spoon of gochugaru. Pour in 750ml water and simmer 20 minutes. Add sliced firm tofu and spring onion for the last 5 minutes. Serve with rice.

w.note: Golden pancakes folded around sweet red bean paste
w.how: Whisk 150g flour, an egg and 250ml milk into a smooth batter. Cook small thin pancakes in butter. Spoon a little red bean paste into each, fold over and press. Fry again in butter until golden on both sides and serve warm.

d.note: Nutty roasted barley tea served hot or iced
d.how: Steep 3 tbsp roasted barley tea in 1L of just-boiled water for 10 minutes. Strain and serve hot in small cups, or cool it down and pour over ice in tall glasses. Toasty, nutty and good with spicy food.

s.note: Beef, cumin and olive empanadas with chimichurri
s.how: Brown 400g beef mince with a diced onion and a teaspoon of cumin, then stir in chopped green olives. Cut shortcrust into rounds, fill, fold and crimp. Bake at 200C for 20 minutes. Blitz parsley with garlic, vinegar and oil for chimichurri.

s.note: Bocconcini and tomato skewers with dots of balsamic
s.how: Thread bocconcini, cherry tomatoes and basil leaves onto toothpicks. Lay on a white platter and drizzle with olive oil. Reduce balsamic vinegar until syrupy and dot it all over the plate in polka dots. Do not look at your mother.

m.note: Lime garlic chilli chicken with rice, beans and salsa
m.how: Marinate 1kg chicken thighs in lime juice, crushed garlic, chopped red chilli and salt for an hour. Grill until charred. Serve with long grain rice, warm black beans and a quick fresh salsa of tomato, onion and lime.

w.note: Pink and blue iced shortbread starfish with white dots
w.how: Beat 250g butter with 100g sugar, then mix in 350g flour. Roll out and cut into starfish shapes. Bake at 160C for 15 minutes. Cool, then ice pink and blue with icing sugar and colouring, and pipe little white dots along each arm.

d.note: Blended mango, coconut milk and lime, rum optional for adults
d.how: Blend 2 mangoes, 200ml coconut milk, the juice of 2 limes, 2 tbsp sugar and 2 cups ice until smooth. Pour into 4 glasses, adding 30ml white rum to adult glasses.

s.note: Frozen chocolate banana bites with peanuts and coconut
s.how: Slice 3 bananas into thick rounds. Dip each halfway into 150g melted dark chocolate, then roll in crushed peanuts mixed with coconut. Lay on a lined tray and freeze for 30 minutes. Serve straight from the freezer on a hot afternoon.

s.note: Tropical fruit and lychees on banana leaves with chilli salt
s.how: Lay banana leaves on a platter. Pile on wedges of mango, pineapple and papaya with a drained can of lychees. Squeeze over lime juice and sprinkle with salt mixed with a pinch of chilli. Fit for a king of the ancient ruins.

m.note: Tomato coconut chicken curry with basmati rice
m.how: Soften grated ginger and garlic in oil, add 2 tsp garam masala and fry a minute. Add 1kg chicken thighs, a can of crushed tomatoes and 400ml coconut milk and simmer 30 minutes. Serve with basmati rice and warm naan.

w.note: Set coconut pudding with mango and toasted coconut
w.how: Warm 800ml coconut milk with 100g sugar until dissolved. Soak 4 gelatine sheets, squeeze and stir in. Pour into glasses and chill for 4 hours. Top with diced mango and toasted shredded coconut.

d.note: Mango yoghurt lassi with cardamom over ice
d.how: Blend the flesh of 2 ripe mangoes with 300g Greek yoghurt, 250ml cold milk, a spoon of sugar and a pinch of cardamom until smooth. Pour over ice in tall glasses. Cool enough for the hottest day in the jungle.

s.note: Mini waffles stacked into little houses with maple syrup
s.how: Whisk 250g flour, 2 tsp baking powder, 2 eggs, 375ml buttermilk and 60g melted butter into a batter. Cook in a hot waffle iron until golden. Cut into squares and stack into little houses, then drizzle with maple syrup.

s.note: Soy sesame tuna over sushi rice in small cups
s.how: Cube 300g sashimi tuna and toss with 2 tbsp soy sauce, a teaspoon of sesame oil and sliced spring onion. Spoon cooked sushi rice into small cups and top with the tuna. Serve chilled, the same way every day.

m.note: Beef patties on rice with a fried egg and onion gravy
m.how: Shape 600g beef mince into 4 patties and sear until cooked. Soften a sliced onion in the pan, stir in a spoon of flour and 500ml beef stock and simmer 15 minutes. Serve the patties on jasmine rice, topped with a fried egg and the gravy.

w.note: Set Hawaiian coconut squares with toasted coconut
w.how: Whisk 800ml coconut milk, 100g sugar and 6 tbsp cornflour over low heat until very thick. Pour into a lined tray and chill for 3 hours until firm. Cut into squares and scatter with toasted shredded coconut.

d.note: Fresh pineapple and lime blended with ice
d.how: Peel and chop a ripe pineapple and blend with the juice of a lime and a handful of ice until smooth. Strain into tall glasses. Tastes like a Hawaiian morning, every single morning, for the first time.

s.note: Crisp oven bacon pieces with maple syrup for dipping
s.how: Lay 12 rashers of thick bacon on a rack over a tray. Bake at 200C for 15 minutes until crisp. Cut into pieces and serve warm with a small bowl of maple syrup for dipping. Save a piece for the dog.

s.note: Little toasts with scrambled egg, bacon and chives
s.how: Fry 4 rashers of bacon until crisp and chop. Scramble 6 eggs softly in butter. Toast white bread, cut into small squares and top each with egg, bacon pieces and snipped chives. Serve on a plate at the usual table.

m.note: Golden crab cakes with lemon and green salad
m.how: Mix 500g crab meat with 3 tbsp mayonnaise, a spoon of Dijon, sliced spring onion and breadcrumbs. Shape into 8 cakes and chill. Pan-fry until golden on both sides and serve with lemon and a green salad.

w.note: Biscuit crust, vanilla custard, sliced banana and whipped cream
w.how: Crush 250g plain sweet biscuits with 110g melted butter and press into a 23cm pie dish. Cook 600ml milk, 4 egg yolks, 100g sugar and 50g cornflour until thick, add 1 tsp vanilla and cool. Layer 3 sliced bananas in the crust, spread over the custard and top with 300ml whipped cream. Chill 3 hours.

d.note: Strong drip coffee refilled without asking
d.how: Brew a big pot of strong drip coffee. Pour into thick mugs and set milk and raw sugar on the side. Bring your own plastic cutlery if you must, but the coffee keeps coming.

s.n: Lewis's peanut butter and jelly bites
s.note: Crustless peanut butter and jam triangles stacked high
s.how: Spread white bread with butter, peanut butter and strawberry jam. Cut off the crusts and slice each sandwich into four small triangles. Stack them high on a plate. Simple, but an inventor needs fuel.

s.note: Little pepperoni pizzas baked crisp, delivered from outer space
s.how: Roll pizza dough thin and cut into small rounds. Top each with pizza sauce, grated mozzarella, a slice of pepperoni and a pinch of oregano. Bake at 220C for 10 minutes until crisp and bubbling. Delivered from outer space.

m.note: Beef and pork meatballs in tomato sauce over spaghetti
m.how: Mix 300g beef mince and 300g pork mince with parmesan and an egg, roll into balls and brown. Add 2 cans crushed tomatoes and torn basil and simmer 40 minutes. Pile over 500g spaghetti for the whole wild family.

w.note: Bright buttercream cupcakes with a little arrow on top
w.how: Beat 125g butter with 150g sugar, then 2 eggs, then fold in 200g self-raising flour and 125ml milk. Bake at 175C for 18 minutes and cool. Pipe bright buttercream on top and add a little icing arrow pointing forward on each.

d.note: Thick purple grape and banana smoothie.
d.how: Freeze 500g red grapes overnight. Blend with 1 banana, 250ml grape juice and 200g vanilla yoghurt until smooth and thick. Pour into 4 glasses and serve straight away with straws.

s.note: Crepes with ham and gruyere, or sugar and lemon
s.how: Whisk 150g flour, 2 eggs and 375ml milk and rest an hour. Cook thin crepes in a buttered pan. Fill half with ham and gruyere and fold, warming until melted. Sprinkle the rest with sugar and lemon juice and fold into quarters.

s.note: Baguette toasts with brie and fig, or tomato and basil
s.how: Slice a baguette, brush with olive oil and toast. Top half with brie and a spoon of fig jam. Top the rest with chopped tomato, torn basil and salt. Lay them out like a stall at the Paris market below the bell tower.

m.note: Red wine beef with bacon, mushrooms and baby onions over mash
m.how: Brown 1kg diced beef chuck and 150g bacon. Add 250g mushrooms and 200g peeled pickling onions and cook until golden. Pour in a bottle of red wine and simmer for 3 hours. Serve over buttery mash from 1kg potatoes.

w.note: Lemon madeleines baked in shell tins
w.how: Melt 100g butter and cool. Whisk 2 eggs with 100g sugar and lemon zest until thick, then fold in 100g flour and the butter. Rest for an hour. Spoon into greased shell tins and bake at 200C for 10 minutes. Dust with icing sugar.

d.note: Grenadine syrup in iced soda water
d.how: Fill 4 glasses with ice. Pour 30ml grenadine into each, top slowly with 200ml soda water and let it sit in a red layer at the bottom until stirred.

s.note: Paprika butter peanuts and pickled onions on the bar
s.how: Melt 30g butter and toss through 300g peanuts with smoked paprika and sea salt. Roast at 180C for 10 minutes. Serve warm in a bowl beside a dish of pickled onions on the bar, before the band strikes up.

s.note: Chilled poached prawns on ice with cocktail sauce
s.how: Bring a pot of salted water to the boil with lemon slices. Add 500g green prawns and poach for 2 minutes, then plunge into iced water. Peel and serve on ice with mayonnaise mixed with tomato sauce, lemon and hot sauce.

m.note: Garlic butter lobster tails with potatoes and beans
m.how: Split 4 lobster tails and brush with butter mixed with crushed garlic. Grill for 6 minutes until just cooked. Boil 800g baby potatoes and steam green beans, then toss both with butter. Serve with lemon wedges. Well, nobody's perfect.

w.note: Three-layer jam and cream cake iced white with candles
w.how: Beat 300g butter with 300g sugar, add 5 eggs and fold in 300g self-raising flour. Bake in 3 tins at 175C for 25 minutes. Stack with strawberry jam and whipped cream, ice white and top with candles. Watch who jumps out.

d.note: Bourbon Manhattans stirred in a jug, with a cherry
d.how: For each drink, stir 60ml bourbon, 30ml sweet vermouth and 2 dashes aromatic bitters with ice in a jug. Strain into chilled glasses and drop in a maraschino cherry. Use a jug, not a hot water bottle in an upper berth.

s.note: Golden cornmeal mini corn dogs with mustard
s.how: Whisk 100g cornmeal, 100g flour, a teaspoon of baking powder and 250ml buttermilk to a thick batter. Pat 24 cocktail franks dry, push a skewer into each, dip and fry at 180C for 3 minutes. Serve with mustard. A queen's first.

s.note: Blue cheese and pear toasts with honey and walnuts
s.how: Slice a baguette and toast until golden. Top each with a little blue cheese and a thin slice of pear. Drizzle with honey and scatter with chopped walnuts. Serve on a silver tray, as befits a small European kingdom.

m.note: Spinach ricotta chicken with lemon butter and gratin
m.how: Cut a pocket into 4 chicken breasts and fill with wilted spinach mixed with ricotta. Sear, then roast at 200C for 20 minutes. Bake a potato gratin alongside. Whisk lemon juice into melted butter and spoon over the chicken.

w.note: Lemon sorbet with poached pear and mint
w.how: Simmer 2 sliced pears in water with a spoon of sugar for 8 minutes until tender, then cool. Scoop lemon sorbet into small chilled glasses and add a few pear slices and a mint leaf. Eat it neatly, and do not launch it across the table.

d.note: Pear juice and sparkling water with lemon over ice
d.how: Fill glasses with ice. Pour in pear juice to halfway and top with cold sparkling water. Squeeze in a little lemon and stir once. The national drink of a kingdom famous for its pears.

s.note: Garlic and tomato rubbed toast with olive oil and salt
s.how: Toast thick slices of crusty bread until golden. Rub each with a cut garlic clove, then with half a ripe tomato so the flesh soaks in. Drizzle with olive oil and sprinkle with sea salt flakes. Serve on a board like a Mediterranean market.

s.note: Goat's cheese balls rolled in parsley and pistachio with honey
s.how: Roll 200g soft goat's cheese into small balls. Roll half in chopped parsley and half in crushed pistachios. Arrange on a plate and drizzle with honey. Serve to a goat who would very much like a pair of trousers.

m.note: Chicken and chorizo paella with a crisp bottom and lemon
m.how: Brown 600g chicken thighs and a sliced chorizo in a wide pan. Add a sliced red capsicum, 300g paella rice and a pinch of saffron, then 1L hot stock. Simmer without stirring for 20 minutes until the bottom crisps. Serve with lemon wedges.

w.note: Yellow iced shortbread stars with edible glitter
w.how: Beat 250g butter with 100g sugar, then mix in 350g flour. Roll out and cut into stars. Bake at 160C for 15 minutes. Cool, ice yellow with icing sugar and a drop of colouring, then dust with edible glitter. Make a wish on each one.

d.note: Orange blossom lemonade with sparkling water
d.how: Dissolve 100g sugar in a little hot water and cool. Squeeze 5 lemons into a jug and add the syrup with a few drops of orange blossom water. Top with cold sparkling water and ice. Fragrant as a wish made on a star.

s.note: Grilled garlic chilli prawns with fish sauce dip
s.how: Toss 500g green prawns with crushed garlic, chopped red chilli and lime zest. Thread onto skewers and grill for 2 minutes a side. Mix fish sauce, lime juice and a spoon of sugar for a dipping sauce. Serve from the boat.

s.note: Fresh rice paper rolls with peanut hoisin dip
s.how: Soak rice paper sheets one at a time and fill with cooked prawns, soaked vermicelli, mint, coriander and lettuce. Roll tightly. Warm 3 tbsp peanut butter with 2 tbsp hoisin and a splash of water for a thick dipping sauce.

m.note: Creamy ginger lemongrass congee with prawns and bamboo
m.how: Simmer 200g jasmine rice in 2L chicken stock with bruised lemongrass and sliced ginger for an hour, stirring often, until creamy. Add 400g green prawns and sliced bamboo shoots for the last 5 minutes. Top with chilli and a pinch of sugar.

w.note: Sweet coconut sticky rice with fresh mango and sesame
w.how: Soak 300g glutinous rice overnight, then steam for 25 minutes. Warm 400ml coconut milk with 80g sugar and a pinch of salt, pour most over the hot rice and rest 20 minutes. Serve with sliced mango, the rest of the coconut and sesame.

d.note: Sugarcane juice over ice with lime
d.how: Pour 1L fresh sugarcane juice over ice in 4 glasses and add a good squeeze of calamansi or lime to each. Serve straight away while it is still ice cold.

s.note: Crisp radishes with soft butter and flaky salt
s.how: Wash a bunch of radishes, leaving the leaves on, and pile them on a board with baby carrots. Set out a dish of soft butter and a pile of sea salt flakes. Swipe each radish through the butter, then dip in the salt.

s.note: Toasts with brie and fig jam, or ham and Dijon
s.how: Slice a baguette and toast until golden. Top half with brie and a spoon of fig jam. Spread the rest with Dijon and top with folded ham. Lay them out on a wooden board at a small Montmartre cafe.

m.note: White wine chicken with mushrooms and cream over mash
m.how: Brown 1kg chicken thighs, then add 250g mushrooms and cook until golden. Pour in 250ml white wine and simmer 30 minutes, then stir in 150ml cream. Serve over buttery mash from 1kg potatoes. Small pleasures.

w.note: Vanilla creme brulee with a crackly top to break
w.how: Heat 600ml cream with a split vanilla bean. Whisk 6 yolks with 80g sugar, pour in the cream and strain into ramekins. Bake in a water bath at 150C for 35 minutes and chill. Sprinkle with sugar and torch. Crack the top with a spoon.

d.note: Strong coffee with frothed hot milk in wide cups
d.how: Brew strong coffee. Heat 1L milk until steaming and froth it with a whisk. Pour the coffee into wide cups and top with the frothy milk. Drink it at a cafe table counting how many people are having a good time right now.

s.note: Honey ricotta sourdough toasts with walnuts
s.how: Beat 250g ricotta with 2 tbsp honey until light. Toast thick slices of sourdough, cut into fingers and spread with the ricotta. Drizzle with more honey and scatter with crushed walnuts. A bear would steal the lot.

s.note: Mango, pineapple, banana and lychee with lime and chilli
s.how: Cut a mango, half a pineapple and 2 bananas into chunks and toss with a drained can of lychees. Squeeze over lime juice and sprinkle with a little salt mixed with chilli flakes. Pile it high in a big bowl for a temple full of monkeys.

m.note: Cumin garlic lamb slow roasted and pulled with flatbread
m.how: Rub a 2kg lamb shoulder with ground cumin, crushed garlic, oil and salt. Roast covered at 150C for 5 hours until it pulls apart. Serve on a board with warm flatbread and garlic yoghurt for the whole pack.

w.note: Golden homemade honeycomb chunks half dipped in dark chocolate
w.how: Boil 200g sugar, 3 tbsp golden syrup and 2 tbsp honey to 150C. Take off the heat and whisk in 2 tsp bicarb soda so it foams up. Pour into a lined tin and leave to set. Break into chunks and dip half of each in melted dark chocolate.

d.note: Mango yoghurt lassi with cardamom over ice
d.how: Blend 2 mangoes with 300g Greek yoghurt, 250ml cold milk and a pinch of ground cardamom until smooth. Pour over ice in tall glasses. Cool and thick, made for a hot day at the Peace Rock.

s.note: Smoky roasted carrot fries with a garlic yoghurt dip
s.how: Cut 800g carrots into fries and toss with olive oil, smoked paprika and sea salt. Roast at 220C for 25 minutes until caramelised at the edges. Stir crushed garlic into Greek yoghurt for a dip. Fresh from the farm.

s.note: Cinnamon sugar doughnut holes, warm from the fryer
s.how: Mix 500g flour, 7g yeast, 2 eggs, 50g butter and warm milk into a soft dough and prove an hour. Roll into small balls and fry at 175C until golden. Roll in cinnamon sugar while warm. One for every doughnut-loving cheetah at the front desk.

m.note: Chicken with preserved lemon, olives and saffron over couscous
m.how: Brown 1kg chicken thighs, then soften a sliced onion with grated ginger and a pinch of saffron. Add 500ml water, chopped preserved lemon and green olives. Cover and simmer for 90 minutes until tender. Serve over fluffy couscous.

w.note: Frozen strawberry and watermelon ice blocks on sticks
w.how: Blend 250g strawberries with 500g watermelon, the juice of a lime and 2 tbsp sugar until smooth. Pour into ice block moulds, push in sticks and freeze overnight. Sell them at a good markup, or just hand them out.

d.note: Kiwifruit cucumber mint cooler with soda
d.how: Blend 3 peeled kiwifruit with a Lebanese cucumber, a handful of mint, the juice of a lime and 2 tbsp sugar. Strain into a jug. Pour over ice and top with soda water. Green and misty like the rainforest district.

s.note: Pepperoni pizza eaten straight from the box at the office
s.how: Stretch pizza dough thin on a tray. Spread with pizza sauce, scatter with grated mozzarella, pepperoni and oregano. Bake at 250C for 10 minutes until bubbling. Cut and put back in a box, then eat on the office floor at midnight.

s.note: Grilled franks with mustard and fried onions in paper
s.how: Fry 2 sliced onions slowly until soft and golden. Grill 8 hot dog franks until they split. Tuck into soft buns with the onions and yellow mustard and wrap in paper. Hand them to the bosses as the kiss cam swings around.

m.note: Peppercorn sirloin with crispy potatoes and buttered asparagus
m.how: Roast 1kg potato chunks at 220C for 45 minutes. Sear 4 sirloin steaks and rest. Toast cracked peppercorns in the pan, add 200ml cream and simmer until thick. Steam asparagus and toss with butter. Serve on white plates.

w.note: Vanilla buttercream cupcakes with sprinkles for the break room
w.how: Beat 125g butter with 150g sugar, then 2 eggs, then fold in 200g self-raising flour and 125ml milk. Bake at 175C for 18 minutes and cool. Pipe vanilla buttercream on top and finish with sprinkles. Leave a tray in the break room.

d.note: Espresso with steamed milk in takeaway cups
d.how: Pull a strong double shot of espresso into each takeaway cup. Steam milk until silky and pour in. Snap on a lid and run it upstairs before the boss notices you have been busy setting up a love life.

s.note: Freshly shucked oysters with eschalot vinegar and lemon
s.how: Finely dice 2 eschalots and stir into 100ml red wine vinegar with cracked black pepper. Lay a dozen freshly shucked oysters on crushed ice. Spoon a little dressing over each and serve with lemon wedges, like a fancy Chicago lunch.

s.note: Honey soy garlic wings with sesame
s.how: Toss 1kg chicken wings with salt and bake at 220C for 45 minutes until crisp. Warm 3 tbsp honey, 2 tbsp soy sauce and crushed garlic until sticky. Toss the wings through and scatter with sesame seeds. Sing badly between bites.

m.note: Peppercorn sirloin with thin fries and a green salad
m.how: Cut 1kg potatoes into thin fries and fry twice until crisp. Sear 4 sirloin steaks and rest. Toast cracked peppercorns in the pan, add 200ml cream and simmer until thick. Serve with the fries and a green salad, reviewed harshly.

w.note: Creme brulee beside a little cup of raspberry jelly
w.how: Make up a packet of raspberry jelly and set in small cups. Heat 600ml cream with a split vanilla bean, whisk into 6 yolks and 80g sugar, strain into ramekins and bake in a water bath at 150C for 35 minutes. Chill, torch the sugar and serve with the jelly.

d.note: Sparkling wine or sparkling grape juice in flutes
d.how: Chill a bottle of sparkling wine and a bottle of sparkling grape juice for an hour. Pour into flutes, wine for the grown-ups and grape juice for the rest. Toast the happy couple, whatever you are secretly planning.

s.note: Glittering white chocolate strawberries and pink meringue kisses
s.how: Whisk 2 egg whites with 120g sugar and a drop of pink colouring to stiff peaks, pipe small kisses and bake at 100C for an hour. Dip 250g strawberries in melted white chocolate and dust with edible glitter. Serve both together.

s.note: Honey cinnamon hazelnut and almond clusters
s.how: Toss 150g hazelnuts and 150g almonds with 3 tbsp honey and a pinch of cinnamon. Spread on a lined tray and roast at 170C for 12 minutes. Cool on baking paper and break into clusters. A chipmunk would talk all day about them.

m.note: Pancakes, scrambled eggs, bacon and strawberries on one plate
m.how: Whisk 250g flour, 2 tsp baking powder, 2 eggs and 375ml buttermilk and cook pancakes. Fry 8 rashers of bacon and scramble 4 eggs softly. Pile it all onto big plates with sliced strawberries and maple syrup on the side.

w.note: Shiny red toffee apples on sticks
w.how: Push sticks into 6 red apples. Boil 400g sugar with 150ml water and red colouring to 150C without stirring. Dip each apple and twist to coat, then set on baking paper. Leave to harden. Maybe do not take a bite from a stranger.

d.note: Pink raspberry lemonade with lemon sorbet
d.how: Crush a handful of raspberries in a jug and top with cold lemonade and ice. Pour into glasses and float a small scoop of lemon sorbet on top of each. Pink, fizzy and worthy of true love's kiss.

s.note: Homemade drinkable honey lemon yoghurt in small bottles
s.how: Blend 300g Greek yoghurt with 300ml cold milk, 2 tbsp honey and a squeeze of lemon until smooth and drinkable. Pour into small bottles and chill well. Shake before drinking, a favourite snack on the school bus.

s.note: Chocolate marshmallows rolled in crushed peppermint
s.how: Melt 150g dark chocolate. Dip 20 marshmallows halfway and roll the chocolate end in crushed peppermint lollies. Set on baking paper for 20 minutes. Pack them for the school ski trip, especially the hot tub bit.

m.note: Soy pear marinated beef with rice and cucumber kimchi
m.how: Slice 600g beef rump thin and marinate in soy, grated pear, crushed garlic and sesame oil for an hour. Sear hot in batches. Serve with jasmine rice and cucumbers tossed with salt, chilli and a little vinegar as quick kimchi.

w.note: Soft middle chocolate chip cookies piled on a plate
w.how: Beat 125g butter with 150g brown sugar, an egg and a teaspoon of vanilla. Mix in 225g flour and 150g dark chocolate chips. Roll into balls and bake at 180C for 10 minutes until soft in the middle. Pile them on a plate.

d.note: Fresh strawberry syrup topped with cold milk
d.how: Mash 300g strawberries with 4 tbsp sugar and stand 15 minutes. Spoon into 4 glasses, add ice and top with 250ml cold milk each. Stir before drinking.

s.note: Cream cheese and apricot puff pastry parcels
s.how: Cut 2 sheets of puff pastry into squares. Spoon a little sweetened cream cheese and apricot jam into the centre and fold the corners in. Brush with beaten egg and bake at 200C for 15 minutes. Dust with icing sugar and eat at a shop window.

s.note: Paprika devilled eggs and cream cheese stuffed celery
s.how: Boil 8 eggs, halve, mash the yolks with mayonnaise and pipe back, then dust with paprika. Beat cream cheese with chives and fill short celery sticks. Lay both out on silver trays for a crowded apartment party.

m.note: Peppercorn sirloin with thin fries and green salad
m.how: Cut 1kg potatoes into thin fries and fry twice until crisp. Sear 4 sirloin steaks and rest. Toast cracked peppercorns in the pan, add 200ml cream and simmer until thick. Serve with fries and a green salad.

w.note: Custard and berry puff pastries glazed with apricot
w.how: Cut 2 sheets of puff pastry into rounds. Spoon custard into the centre of each and top with blueberries. Brush the edges with beaten egg and bake at 200C for 15 minutes. Brush with warm apricot jam. Best eaten outside a jewellery shop.

d.note: Takeaway coffee, or sparkling wine for the party
d.how: Brew strong coffee, add milk and pour into a paper takeaway cup for the early morning walk. For the party later, pour sparkling wine into coupes. Wear sunglasses either way.

s.note: Roe blinis and white chocolate strawberries on black trays
s.how: Top blinis with creme fraiche and a little black lumpfish roe. Dip strawberries halfway in melted white chocolate and set on baking paper. Lay both out on black trays in strict rows, black and white only.

s.note: Twice-cooked chips with malt vinegar and salt
s.how: Cut 1kg potatoes into thick chips, rinse and dry. Fry at 140C until soft, rest, then fry at 190C until crisp. Tip into paper and shake over plenty of malt vinegar and salt. Eat on the street in 1970s London.

m.note: Beef Wellington with mushroom duxelles and prosciutto
m.how: Sear a 1kg beef eye fillet all over and brush with Dijon. Cook 400g chopped mushrooms until dry. Lay prosciutto on plastic wrap, spread with the mushrooms, roll around the beef and chill. Wrap in puff pastry, egg wash and bake at 200C for 30 minutes.

w.note: Chocolate sponge layered with white chocolate cream
w.how: Beat 200g butter with 200g sugar, add 4 eggs, then fold in 200g self-raising flour and 40g cocoa. Bake in 2 tins at 175C for 30 minutes. Split each layer and fill with cream whipped with melted white chocolate. Chill and slice to show the stripes.

d.note: Deep red cranberry and pomegranate soda poured over ice
d.how: Fill tall glasses with ice. Pour in equal parts cranberry juice and pomegranate juice to halfway and top with soda water. Stir once so it runs deep red, the colour of a dress that burns away to reveal another.

s.note: Cold king prawns on ice with seafood sauce
s.how: Pile crushed ice onto a platter and arrange 500g cooked prawns on top with lemon wedges. Mix 4 tbsp mayonnaise with 2 tbsp tomato sauce and a dash of hot sauce. Serve in a bowl beside the prawns for a Sydney Harbour wedding.

s.note: Mini beef and gravy pies with tomato sauce
s.how: Brown 500g beef mince with a diced onion, add 250ml beef stock and simmer until thick, then cool. Line a muffin tin with shortcrust rounds, fill and top with puff lids. Bake at 200C for 20 minutes and serve with tomato sauce.

m.note: Crisp-skinned barramundi with lemon caper butter and potatoes
m.how: Boil 800g baby potatoes and crush lightly. Pan-fry 4 barramundi fillets skin side down until crisp, then flip for a minute. Add butter, lemon juice and capers to the pan and spoon over the fish. Serve with the potatoes.

w.note: Pavlova with cream, passionfruit, kiwifruit and strawberries
w.how: Whisk 4 egg whites to stiff peaks, then add 220g caster sugar a spoon at a time until glossy. Shape into a round and bake at 120C for 90 minutes, then cool in the oven. Top with whipped cream, passionfruit, kiwifruit and strawberries.

d.note: Sparkling wine or apple fizz with a strawberry
d.how: Chill sparkling wine and sparkling apple juice for an hour. Drop a halved strawberry into each flute and pour the wine for the grown-ups and apple juice for the rest. Toast with the harbour in the background.

s.note: Za'atar flatbreads with hummus and labneh
s.how: Brush flatbreads with olive oil and sprinkle generously with za'atar. Grill until blistered. Tear into pieces and serve with a bowl of hummus and a bowl of labneh drizzled with more oil. Market stall style.

s.note: Chocolate dates stuffed with almond butter and pistachio
s.how: Slit 16 medjool dates and remove the stones. Fill each with a teaspoon of almond butter and press closed. Dip halfway in melted dark chocolate and roll the end in crushed pistachios. Set in the fridge. Keep them away from any monkey.

m.note: Spiced slow-roasted lamb over saffron rice with almonds
m.how: Rub a 2kg lamb shoulder with garlic, cumin, cinnamon and salt. Roast covered at 150C for 5 hours until it pulls apart. Cook 400g basmati with a pinch of saffron. Pile the lamb over the rice and scatter with toasted almonds.

w.note: Pistachio walnut cardamom baklava in honey syrup
w.how: Layer buttered filo sheets in a tin with chopped pistachios and walnuts mixed with cardamom between every few layers. Cut into diamonds and bake at 180C for 40 minutes. Pour over warm honey syrup and leave to soak for hours.

d.note: Sweet mint green tea, hot or iced
d.how: Put 2 tbsp green tea leaves and a big bunch of fresh mint into a teapot with sugar to taste. Pour over a litre of just-boiled water and steep 4 minutes. Pour from a height into small glasses, or chill and serve over ice.

s.note: Warm soda bread with salted butter
s.how: Mix 450g flour, a teaspoon of bicarb soda and a teaspoon of salt. Stir in 400ml buttermilk to a soft dough. Shape into a round, cut a deep cross and bake at 200C for 35 minutes until it sounds hollow. Serve warm with salted butter.

s.note: Smoked salmon on buttered brown bread with capers
s.how: Spread thin slices of brown bread thickly with butter. Top with folds of smoked salmon, a few capers and a crack of black pepper. Squeeze over a little lemon and cut into triangles. Serve in a country pub by the fire.

m.note: Lamb, potato and carrot stew thickened by the potatoes
m.how: Layer 1kg lamb neck pieces with 1kg sliced potatoes, 3 carrots and a sliced onion in a heavy pot. Add thyme and 750ml chicken stock. Cover and simmer for 2 hours until the potatoes break down and thicken it. Serve in deep bowls.

w.note: Cinnamon apple crumble with oats and custard
w.how: Peel and slice 5 green apples and cook with 30g butter and cinnamon for 5 minutes. Spoon into a dish. Rub 70g butter into oats, flour and 80g brown sugar and scatter over. Bake at 180C for 35 minutes and serve with warm custard.

d.note: Hot coffee with brown sugar, whiskey and cream
d.how: Stir a spoon of brown sugar into a cup of hot strong coffee until dissolved. Add 30ml whiskey for the grown-ups. Lightly whip cream until just thick and pour it gently over the back of a spoon so it floats on top.

s.note: Puffed rice noodle grubs with chilli lime salt
s.how: Heat oil to 190C and drop in small handfuls of dry rice vermicelli so they puff up instantly into crunchy grubs. Drain and toss with chilli flakes, sea salt and a squeeze of lime. Pile onto a leaf and dig in.

s.note: Rockmelon, papaya, mango and passionfruit with lime
s.how: Cut a rockmelon, half a papaya and 2 mangoes into wedges and arrange on a platter with halved passionfruit. Squeeze over lime juice and sprinkle with a pinch of chilli salt. Serve on a hot day on the savanna.

m.note: Charred peri peri chicken with yellow rice
m.how: Blitz red chillies with lemon juice, garlic, smoked paprika, oil and salt into a peri peri sauce. Marinate 1kg chicken thighs for 2 hours and grill until charred. Cook long grain rice with a pinch of turmeric and serve together.

w.note: Sticky apricot sponge soaked in hot cream sauce with custard
w.how: Beat 2 eggs with 200g sugar, add a spoon of apricot jam, then fold in 150g self-raising flour, 30g melted butter and 250ml milk. Bake at 180C for 40 minutes. Pour over hot sauce of 250ml cream, 100g butter and sugar. Serve with custard.

d.note: Iced rooibos tea with honey and orange peel
d.how: Brew 4 rooibos tea bags in 1L boiling water with a few strips of orange peel for 5 minutes. Stir in 2 tbsp honey and cool. Pour over ice in tall glasses with a slice of orange. Everyone meets at the watering hole.

s.note: Toasted crumpets with butter and golden syrup
s.how: Toast 8 crumpets until crisp on the edges. Spread generously with 80g butter so it melts into the holes and serve with honey and golden syrup on the side.

s.note: Lacy cheese-crusted toasts fried cheese side down
s.how: Scatter grated cheddar in a hot buttered pan and press a slice of white bread on top. Fry until the cheese forms a golden lacy crust, then flip and toast the other side. Cut into fingers and sprinkle with chives. Upside down, of course.

m.note: Pork sausages on buttery mash with onion gravy and peas
m.how: Brown 8 thick pork sausages slowly in a pan. Cook 2 sliced onions in the same pan until soft, then add 500ml beef stock and simmer 20 minutes until thick. Serve the sausages on mash from 1kg potatoes with peas and plenty of gravy.

w.note: Little jam tarts in three bright colours
w.how: Cut shortcrust into rounds and press into a patty tin. Fill a third with strawberry jam, a third with apricot and a third with blackcurrant. Bake at 190C for 15 minutes until the pastry is golden. Dust the edges with icing sugar.

d.note: Strawberry lemonade with soda over ice
d.how: Muddle a handful of strawberries in a big jug. Add the juice of 6 lemons and sugar syrup to taste, then top with cold soda water. Pour over ice in tall glasses and take it to the park on a windy day.

s.note: Creamy gravy meatballs with lingonberry jam on toothpicks
s.how: Mix 250g pork mince and 250g beef mince with a grated onion and a pinch of allspice. Roll into small balls and brown. Add 200ml cream and a splash of water and simmer 10 minutes. Serve on toothpicks with lingonberry jam. Bork bork.

s.note: Twice-cooked fries in paper cones with tomato sauce
s.how: Cut 1kg potatoes into thick fries, rinse and dry. Fry at 140C until soft, then fry again at 190C until crisp. Toss with sea salt and pile into paper cones with tomato sauce on the side. Smalltown, USA approved.

m.note: Steak frites with bearnaise, and definitely not pork
m.how: Cut 1kg potatoes into thin fries and fry twice until crisp. Sear 4 sirloin steaks and rest. Reduce white wine vinegar with tarragon, whisk in 2 yolks over gentle heat, then slowly add 150g melted butter. Serve the steak over the fries. Not pork.

w.note: Peppermint slice with green icing and chocolate top
w.how: Crush 250g sweet biscuits with 100g melted butter and press into a tin. Beat 300g icing sugar with a little butter, peppermint essence and green colouring and spread over. Pour melted dark chocolate on top, chill and cut into squares.

d.note: Layered orange, pineapple and cranberry with lemonade
d.how: Fill tall glasses with ice. Pour in cranberry juice first, then slowly add pineapple juice and orange juice over the back of a spoon so they layer. Top with lemonade. A rainbow in a glass for the show.

s.note: Crunchy seed cracker shards with sea salt
s.how: Mix 60g each of sunflower seeds, pepitas, linseeds and sesame seeds with 40g chia, a pinch of salt and 250ml water. Rest 15 minutes, spread thin and bake at 160C for an hour until crunchy. Break into shards. An offering fit for any colony.

s.note: Berry, feta and mint toothpicks in marching lines
s.how: Thread blueberries, raspberries, small cubes of feta and a mint leaf onto toothpicks. Lay them out on a long platter in neat marching lines, like ants on the way to the harvest.

m.note: Creamy corn, potato and bacon chowder with chives
m.how: Fry 150g diced bacon, then soften a diced onion. Add 500g diced potatoes, 2 cans of corn, thyme and 1L water and simmer 20 minutes. Stir in 150ml cream and blitz a little for body. Serve topped with chives.

w.note: Shortbread butterflies iced in bright colours for a caterpillar
w.how: Beat 250g butter with 100g sugar, then mix in 350g flour. Roll out and cut into butterfly shapes. Bake at 160C for 15 minutes and cool. Ice in bright colours with icing sugar and food colouring. One day, a beautiful butterfly.

d.note: Cucumber mint lime cooler topped with soda
d.how: Blend a Lebanese cucumber with a handful of mint, the juice of 2 limes and 2 tbsp sugar. Strain into a jug and pour over ice. Top with soda water. Fresh as a dewdrop that looks huge to a very small bug.

s.note: Soft chocolate chip cookies piled high
s.how: Beat 125g butter with 150g brown sugar, an egg and vanilla. Mix in 225g flour and 150g dark chocolate chips. Roll into balls and bake at 180C for 10 minutes until soft in the middle. Keep them handy to stop any baby from bursting into flames.

s.note: Pesto and parmesan puff pastry spirals
