s.how: Spread 2 sheets of puff pastry with basil pesto and sprinkle with grated parmesan. Roll up tightly and slice into rounds. Lay on a tray, brush with beaten egg and bake at 200C for 15 minutes. Do not stare at the spirals too long.

m.note: Spaghetti bolognese with plenty of parmesan on homework night
m.how: Brown 600g beef mince, then add diced carrot and celery and soften. Add 2 cans crushed tomatoes and simmer for an hour. Toss with 500g spaghetti and plenty of parmesan. Math is math, but dinner is dinner.

w.note: Fudgy brownies with a glass of milk
w.how: Melt 200g dark chocolate with 150g butter. Whisk in 250g sugar and 3 eggs, then fold in 100g flour. Bake at 170C for 25 minutes. Cut into squares and serve each with a glass of cold milk. Watch out for raccoons by the bins.

d.note: Fresh lemonade made red with raspberry syrup.
d.how: Simmer 150g raspberries with 100g sugar and 100ml water for 5 minutes, then strain to make a syrup. Mix with the juice of 4 lemons and 1L cold water in a jug, add ice and the rest of the raspberries, and stir well.

s.note: Hot salted edamame with sesame oil and chilli
s.how: Boil 500g frozen edamame in salted water for 4 minutes and drain. Toss while hot with a teaspoon of sesame oil, a pinch of chilli flakes and sea salt flakes. Pile into small bowls for a fancy Tokyo party.

s.note: Crisp folded ham and gruyere crepes in triangles
s.how: Whisk 150g flour, 2 eggs and 375ml milk and rest an hour. Cook thin crepes in a buttered pan. Fill each with ham and grated gruyere, fold into quarters and crisp again in the pan. Cut into triangles and serve hot.

m.note: Garlic chilli prawn and cherry tomato spaghetti
m.how: Soften crushed garlic and a pinch of chilli in olive oil. Add 400g green prawns and 250g halved cherry tomatoes and a splash of white wine. Cook until the prawns turn pink. Toss through 500g spaghetti with chopped parsley.

w.note: Pistachio ice cream with crushed pistachios and honey
w.how: Scoop pistachio ice cream into chilled bowls. Scatter with crushed roasted pistachios and drizzle with a little honey. Serve straight away. Do not mistake the wasabi for it, as one tow truck learned the hard way.

d.note: Limoncello, prosecco and soda over ice
d.how: Fill 4 wine glasses with ice. Add 60ml limoncello and 90ml prosecco to each, top with a splash of soda and finish with a lemon wheel and mint.

s.note: Vanilla and lemon gelato cups with amaretti and zest
s.how: Scoop vanilla ice cream and lemon sorbet side by side into small cups. Crush amaretti biscuits over the top and finish with a little lemon zest. Eat them fast on a hot Italian summer afternoon in the town square.

s.note: Golden zucchini ricotta fritters with lemon
s.how: Grate 3 zucchini and squeeze dry. Mix with 200g ricotta, an egg, 50g grated parmesan and 80g flour. Fry spoonfuls in olive oil until golden on both sides. Serve with lemon wedges by the harbour.

m.note: Linguine with potato, green beans and fresh basil pesto
m.how: Blitz 2 bunches basil with 50g pine nuts, a garlic clove, 50g parmesan and olive oil into pesto. Cook 500g linguine with sliced potato and green beans in the same pot. Drain and toss with the pesto. Simple Ligurian food.

w.note: Light lemon ricotta cake dusted with icing sugar
w.how: Beat 500g ricotta with 150g sugar, 3 eggs and the zest of 2 lemons until smooth. Fold in 150g self-raising flour. Pour into a lined tin and bake at 170C for 45 minutes until set. Cool and dust with icing sugar.

d.note: Fresh lemon soda over ice with peel
d.how: Squeeze 4 lemons into a jug and stir in sugar syrup to taste. Top with cold soda water. Pour over ice in tall glasses and add a strip of lemon peel to each. Silenzio, Bruno, and drink up.

s.note: Golden corn fritters with a sour cream and chive dip
s.how: Mix a drained can of corn with 100g flour, 2 eggs, sliced spring onions and salt. Fry spoonfuls in a little oil until golden on both sides. Stir chopped chives through sour cream for the dip and serve the fritters warm.

s.note: Honey lime berries over whipped cream in small bowls
s.how: Toss 125g each of blueberries, raspberries and blackberries with a spoon of honey and a squeeze of lime. Spoon over whipped cream in small bowls. Berries a wild boy might bring you from the forest.

m.note: Slow-cooked paprika beef ribs with corn and coleslaw
m.how: Rub 2kg beef short ribs with smoked paprika, cracked pepper and salt. Cook at 140C for 5 hours until tender with a dark crust. Serve with charred corn cobs and a crunchy cabbage coleslaw, like the T-rex ranchers would.

w.note: Cast iron cornbread with honey butter
w.how: Mix 150g cornmeal, 100g flour, 2 tsp baking powder, an egg, 300ml buttermilk and 50g melted butter until just combined. Bake in a hot greased cast iron pan at 220C for 20 minutes. Serve wedges with butter beaten with honey.

d.note: Cold lemon mint water in a big jug
d.how: Fill a big jug with ice, sliced lemon and a handful of mint. Top up with cold water and let it sit for 10 minutes so the flavour comes through. Pour into glasses for anyone who has crossed a river today.

s.note: Toast fingers with sardines and lemon, or honey
s.how: Toast white bread and butter it while hot. Top half with mashed sardines and a squeeze of lemon. Drizzle the rest with honey. Cut into fingers and serve with a pot of tea, as a faun would to a lost girl.

s.note: Lemonade scones with jam and cream
s.how: Mix 450g self-raising flour with 300ml cream and 300ml lemonade until just combined. Pat out, cut into rounds and bake close together at 220C for 15 minutes. Serve warm with strawberry jam and whipped cream in a big old house.

m.note: Butter-fried fish with parsley potatoes and peas
m.how: Pan-fry 4 flathead fillets in butter until golden. Boil 800g potatoes and toss with parsley butter. Cook peas and toss with butter and a squeeze of lemon. Serve together at a cosy table in a beaver dam.

w.note: Rosewater Turkish delight dusted in icing sugar
w.how: Boil 500g sugar, 120g cornflour and 750ml water with the juice of a lemon, stirring, over low heat for an hour until very thick. Stir in rosewater and pink colouring, pour into a lined tin and set overnight. Cut into cubes and roll in icing sugar.

d.note: Cinnamon hot chocolate topped with whipped cream
d.how: Heat 1L milk until steaming. Whisk in 150g chopped dark chocolate and a pinch of cinnamon until frothy. Pour into mugs and top with whipped cream. A gift for anyone who has spent too long in an endless winter.

s.note: Twisted crullers dipped in a honey glaze while warm
s.how: Bring 250ml water and 100g butter to the boil, beat in 150g flour, then beat in 4 eggs. Pipe twisted rings onto squares of baking paper and fry at 180C until golden. Dip in a glaze of icing sugar, honey and a splash of milk.

s.note: Swirled homemade lollipops on sticks in bright colours
s.how: Boil 200g sugar, 80ml glucose syrup and 80ml water to 150C without stirring. Pour into two pans, tint each a different colour, then pour small rounds onto baking paper, swirling colours. Press a stick into each and leave to harden.

m.note: Buttermilk fried drumsticks with mash and gravy
m.how: Soak 8 chicken drumsticks in buttermilk overnight. Dredge in flour seasoned with smoked paprika and salt. Fry at 170C for 12 minutes until crisp. Serve with buttery mash from 1kg potatoes and gravy made with chicken stock. No place like it.

w.note: Raspberry jelly with berries and edible glitter
w.how: Make up a packet of raspberry jelly and pour into glasses with a few raspberries in each. Chill for 3 hours until set. Dust with edible glitter so it sparkles like ruby slippers, then top with a little whipped cream.

d.note: Golden pineapple lemonade over ice in tall glasses
d.how: Dissolve 100g sugar in a little hot water and cool. Squeeze 5 lemons into a jug, add the syrup and 1L pineapple juice and stir. Pour over ice in tall glasses. Golden yellow, like a road to follow.

s.note: Grilled franks with mustard and caraway sauerkraut
s.how: Warm 300g sauerkraut with a pinch of caraway seeds. Grill 8 hot dog franks until they split. Tuck into soft buns with yellow mustard and sauerkraut and wrap in wax paper. Eat them at the world's fair, 1943.

s.note: Cheddar, ham, pickled onions and chutney with bread
s.how: Lay wedges of aged cheddar, sliced ham, a bowl of pickled onions and a pot of tomato chutney on a board. Add thick slices of crusty bread and butter. A ploughman's lunch at a London pub between missions.

m.note: Thick beef, carrot and potato stew in tin bowls
m.how: Brown 1kg diced beef chuck, then add a sliced onion, 3 carrots and 600g potato chunks with 1L beef stock. Simmer for 3 hours until thick and tender. Ladle into tin bowls with crusty bread, army style.

w.note: Lattice cherry blueberry pie with vanilla ice cream
w.how: Toss 400g frozen cherries and 200g blueberries with 100g sugar and 3 tbsp cornflour. Line a pie dish with shortcrust, fill and weave a lattice. Bake at 190C for 45 minutes until bubbling. Serve warm with vanilla ice cream.

d.note: Cold frothy vanilla malted milk in tall glasses
d.how: Blend 1L cold milk with 4 scoops vanilla ice cream and 5 tbsp malted milk powder until frothy. Pour into 4 tall glasses. Serve straight away while it is still ice cold.

s.note: Salmon rice triangles wrapped in nori in a bento
s.how: Cook 2 cups sushi rice. Salt and grill 200g salmon, then flake. Shape rice into triangles around a little salmon, wrap the base in nori and sprinkle with sesame. Pack into a bento box with pickled ginger for the train.

s.note: Sticky glazed chicken skewers with spring onion
s.how: Simmer 4 tbsp soy sauce, 4 tbsp mirin and 2 tbsp sugar until syrupy. Thread 600g chicken thigh pieces onto skewers and grill, basting with the glaze, until sticky and charred. Scatter with spring onion.

m.note: Miso ramen with braised pork, soft eggs and nori
m.how: Braise 600g pork belly in soy and water for 2 hours, then slice. Whisk white miso into hot stock. Cook ramen noodles and soft-boil 4 eggs for 6 minutes. Build bowls with pork, halved eggs, nori and spring onion.

w.note: Vanilla ice cream whisked with matcha
w.how: Soften 1L vanilla ice cream for 10 minutes. Whisk 2 tbsp matcha powder with a splash of hot water to a paste and fold through until pale green. Refreeze for an hour and scoop into small bowls.

d.note: Gently warmed sake in small cups, or green tea
d.how: Pour sake into a small jug and stand it in a pot of hot water for 5 minutes until warm. Pour into small cups. For anyone not drinking, brew a pot of green tea instead and serve in the same cups.

s.note: Crisp cheese and chicken quesadillas with salsa
s.how: Fill 4 tortillas with 200g grated cheese, 200g shredded cooked chicken and a diced capsicum, fold and cook in a dry pan for 3 minutes a side. Cut into wedges and serve with salsa.

s.note: Cheddar cracker fish served in a round glass bowl
s.how: Rub 100g butter into 150g flour, then mix in 150g grated cheddar and a pinch of smoked paprika. Add cold water to bring together and chill 30 minutes. Roll thin, cut into fish and bake at 180C for 12 minutes. Serve in a round glass bowl.

m.note: Smoky chipotle beef chilli with sour cream
m.how: Brown 1kg diced beef chuck, then add a can of crushed tomatoes, a spoon of cumin, 2 chopped chipotles and water to cover. Simmer for 3 hours, adding 2 cans of kidney beans for the last 30 minutes. Serve with sour cream.

w.note: Blue velvet cupcakes with cream cheese frosting
w.how: Whisk 250g flour, a spoon of cocoa, 150g sugar, an egg, 125ml oil, 250ml buttermilk and blue colouring to a smooth batter. Bake in cases at 175C for 18 minutes. Pipe with cream cheese beaten with icing sugar. Presentation is everything.

d.note: Cola poured over vanilla ice cream
d.how: Put 2 scoops vanilla ice cream in each of 4 tall glasses and slowly pour over 300ml cold cola. Serve with spoons and straws. Serve straight away while it is still ice cold.

s.note: Flaky buttermilk scones with butter and honey
s.how: Rub 100g cold butter into 450g self-raising flour with a pinch of salt. Stir in 300ml buttermilk until just combined. Pat out, cut into rounds and bake at 220C for 14 minutes. Serve warm with butter and honey.

s.note: Honey mint berries over whipped cream in cups
s.how: Toss 125g blackberries and 125g blueberries with a spoon of honey and torn mint. Spoon over whipped cream in small cups. A sweet snack for two friends playing by the creek.

m.note: Chicken stew topped with fluffy herb dumplings
m.how: Simmer 800g chicken thighs with sliced carrot, celery and onion in 1.5L water for 40 minutes. Rub butter into 200g self-raising flour, add chopped parsley and water to a soft dough. Drop spoonfuls on top, cover and cook 20 minutes.

w.note: Blackberry cobbler with vanilla ice cream
w.how: Toss 500g blackberries with 80g sugar and spread in a dish. Rub 80g butter into 250g self-raising flour, add 150ml milk and drop rough spoonfuls over the fruit. Bake at 180C for 40 minutes. Serve warm with vanilla ice cream.

d.note: Honey vanilla milk, cold or warmed for bedtime
d.how: Pour 1L milk into a big jar with 2 tbsp honey and a drop of vanilla. Shake hard and pour cold into glasses, or warm it gently for bedtime. Good for a little fox who has found a new home.

s.note: Smoked salmon on rye crispbread with dill and lemon
s.how: Spread rye crispbreads with cream cheese. Top with folds of smoked salmon and a sprig of dill. Squeeze over a little lemon and lay them on a wooden board. Fresh from the salmon run.

s.note: Maple roasted pecan and walnut clusters with a pinch of salt
s.how: Toss 150g pecans and 150g walnuts with 4 tbsp maple syrup and a pinch of salt. Spread on a lined tray and roast at 170C for 12 minutes. Cool until set and break into clusters. Take off, eh, they are good.

m.n: Kenai's venison steaks with berry sauce
m.note: Seared venison steaks with blueberry red wine sauce
m.how: Sear 4 venison steaks in a hot pan for 3 minutes a side and rest. Add 150ml red wine, 150g blueberries and 1 tbsp brown sugar to the pan and simmer until syrupy. Serve with roast potatoes.

w.note: Honey berry crumble with oats and cream
w.how: Toss 500g mixed berries with 3 tbsp honey and spread in a dish. Rub 100g butter into oats, flour and 80g brown sugar and scatter over. Bake at 180C for 35 minutes until bubbling and serve with cream.

d.note: Cucumber mint water over plenty of ice
d.how: Fill a big jug with ice, cucumber ribbons and a handful of mint. Top up with cold water and leave for 10 minutes so the flavour comes through. Pour into glasses, clear and cold as a mountain stream.

s.note: Tropical fruit with lime and chilli salt
s.how: Cut 2 mangoes, half a pineapple and half a papaya into wedges and pile on a platter with halved passionfruit. Squeeze over lime juice and sprinkle with a little salt mixed with chilli flakes. Serve in the Caribbean sun.

s.note: Crisp plantain chips with lime coriander dip
s.how: Peel 3 green plantains and slice thin. Fry at 180C in batches until crisp and salt well. Stir chopped coriander and lime juice through sour cream for a dip. Serve on the beach, or at least near a bath.

m.note: Charred allspice and thyme jerk chicken with rice
m.how: Blitz allspice, thyme, red chilli, lime juice and spring onion into a paste. Marinate 1kg chicken thighs for 2 hours and grill until charred. Serve with long grain rice cooked with kidney beans, the castle kitchen's best.

w.note: Blue jelly glasses with fruit fish inside
w.how: Cut mango and kiwifruit into little fish shapes. Make up 2 packets of blue jelly and pour into clear glasses with the fruit fish suspended inside. Chill 3 hours, then top with whipped cream like sea foam.

d.note: Coconut water and pineapple with lime and mint
d.how: Fill tall glasses with ice and mint leaves. Pour in equal parts coconut water and pineapple juice, then squeeze in a wedge of lime. Stir and serve cold, the kind of drink you would trade your voice for.

s.note: Chilled poached prawns on ice with cocktail sauce
s.how: Bring a pot of salted water to the boil with lemon slices. Add 500g green prawns and poach 2 minutes, then plunge into iced water. Peel and serve on crushed ice with mayonnaise mixed with tomato sauce and hot sauce.

s.note: Marinated olives with orange and chilli, with manchego
s.how: Toss 150g green olives and 150g kalamata olives with strips of orange peel, sliced garlic, a pinch of chilli and olive oil. Leave for an hour. Serve with thin wedges of manchego for a Spanish galleon crew.

m.note: Saffron rice with chicken, chorizo and seafood
m.how: Brown 400g chicken thighs and 1 sliced chorizo, add an onion and capsicum, then 300g paella rice, saffron, paprika and 900ml stock. Simmer 15 minutes without stirring, add 300g prawns and 500g mussels and cook 6 minutes more.

w.note: Choux puffs filled with custard cream and icing sugar
w.how: Bring 250ml water and 100g butter to the boil, beat in 150g flour, then beat in 4 eggs. Pipe small mounds and bake at 200C for 25 minutes. Fold whipped cream into custard, fill each puff and dust with icing sugar. Royal treats.

d.note: Coconut pineapple lime punch, rum optional
d.how: Fill glasses with ice. Pour in equal parts coconut water and pineapple juice and squeeze in half a lime. Add 30ml dark rum for those drinking. Two chalices, one with a tear, is optional.

s.note: Golden parmesan coin crisps with fig jam
s.how: Mix 150g grated parmesan with chopped thyme. Spoon small rounds onto a lined tray and flatten into coins. Bake at 190C for 6 minutes until golden. Cool and pile them high like a stolen bank vault with fig jam.

s.note: Crisp puffed tempura prawns with sweet chilli and lime
s.how: Whisk 100g flour and 50g cornflour with ice-cold soda water to a thin lumpy batter. Dip 500g green prawns and fry at 180C until puffed and crisp. Stir lime juice into sweet chilli sauce and serve for dipping.

m.note: Snapper simmered in coconut tomato chilli sauce over rice
m.how: Soften crushed garlic and chopped chilli in oil, add 2 diced tomatoes and 400ml coconut milk and simmer 5 minutes. Add 4 snapper fillets and simmer 10 minutes. Squeeze in lime and serve over jasmine rice.

w.note: Steamed guava roll with buttery rum sauce
w.how: Make a soft dough of 250g self-raising flour, 60g butter, 60g sugar and 150ml milk. Roll out, spread with 250g guava paste, roll up, wrap in buttered foil and steam 1 hour. Serve with 80g butter, 100g icing sugar and 30ml rum beaten together.

d.note: Dark rum over ice with lime, or ginger beer
d.how: Fill short glasses with ice. Pour 45ml dark rum over the ice for the pirates and squeeze in a wedge of lime. For the landlubbers, pour ginger beer over ice with lime instead.

s.note: Flaky ricotta and pea pastry parcels
s.how: Mix 250g ricotta with an egg. Separately cook 200g peas with a diced onion and a pinch of curry powder. Fill puff pastry squares with one or the other, fold into parcels and bake at 200C for 20 minutes until flaky.

s.note: Charred chilli lime butter corn rounds
s.how: Boil 4 corn cobs for 6 minutes. Brush with butter mixed with chilli flakes and lime zest and juice. Char on a hot grill, turning, until blistered all over. Cut into thick rounds and pile them high, before the locusts arrive.

m.note: Creamy polenta under mushroom and sausage ragu
m.how: Brown 4 Italian sausages squeezed from their skins, add 250g sliced mushrooms and a can of crushed tomatoes and simmer an hour. Cook 200g polenta in 1L water until thick, then beat in butter and parmesan. Spoon the ragu over the polenta.

w.note: Homemade honeycomb broken into amber shards
w.how: Boil 200g sugar, 3 tbsp golden syrup and 2 tbsp honey to 150C. Take off the heat and whisk in 2 tsp bicarb soda so it foams. Pour into a lined tin and leave to set. Break into amber shards. No mosquitoes trapped inside.

d.note: Chilled Maltese almond drink with vanilla
d.how: Blend 200g almonds soaked overnight with 1L water, strain through a cloth and sweeten with 3 tbsp sugar, vanilla and a pinch of ground cloves. Chill and serve over ice.

s.note: Chocolate dipped shortbread fingers with a pot of tea
s.how: Beat 250g butter with 100g sugar, then mix in 300g flour and 50g rice flour. Press into a tin and bake at 160C for 25 minutes. Cut into fingers and dip half of each in melted dark chocolate. Serve with tea at Number Ten.

s.note: Lemon chive lobster in toasted brioche rolls
s.how: Toss cooked lobster meat from 2 tails with mayonnaise, lemon zest and chives. Split small brioche buns, toast and pile the lobster in. Dust with a pinch of paprika. Every nativity needs a lobster.

m.note: Stuffed turkey breast with roast potatoes, sprouts and cranberry
m.how: Fry a chopped onion with sage, mix with breadcrumbs for stuffing. Butterfly a 1.5kg turkey breast, spread, roll and tie. Roast at 180C for 90 minutes with 1kg potatoes. Serve with roasted brussels sprouts and cranberry sauce.

w.note: Sherry trifle with raspberry jelly, custard and cream
w.how: Cut a sponge cake into cubes, press into a glass bowl and splash with sweet sherry. Pour over raspberry jelly and chill until set. Layer with 500ml custard and whipped cream, chill overnight and top with raspberries.

d.note: Gently warmed red wine with orange, spices and honey
d.how: Pour a bottle of red wine into a pot with a sliced orange, 2 cinnamon sticks, 4 whole cloves and 2 tbsp honey. Warm gently for 20 minutes without boiling. Ladle into mugs on Christmas Eve.

s.note: Smoked salmon blinis and prosciutto asparagus
s.how: Top 16 blinis with creme fraiche, smoked salmon and dill. Blanch a bunch of asparagus for a minute, wrap each spear in prosciutto and grill until crisp. Arrange both on trays for the first of several weddings.

s.note: Smoked salmon on oatcakes with cream cheese and dill
s.how: Spread oatcakes with cream cheese. Top with folds of smoked salmon and a sprig of dill. Squeeze over a little lemon and lay them out on a slate for a castle wedding in the Highlands.

m.note: Roast beef with Yorkshire puddings and gravy
m.how: Roast a 1.5kg beef topside at 200C to medium and rest. Whisk 150g flour, 3 eggs and 300ml milk into a batter and bake in hot oiled muffin tins for 20 minutes. Roast 1kg potatoes alongside and make gravy with pan juices and stock.

w.note: Lemon curd and cream sponge with fresh flowers
w.how: Beat 250g butter with 250g sugar, add 4 eggs and lemon zest, then fold in 250g self-raising flour. Bake in 2 tins at 175C for 30 minutes. Fill with lemon curd and whipped cream, ice white and decorate with fresh flowers.

d.note: Sparkling wine, or sparkling elderflower for the drivers
d.how: Chill a bottle of sparkling wine. For drivers, mix elderflower cordial with cold soda water. Pour both into flutes and raise them for the happy couple, and for whoever turns up late again.

s.note: Pink white chocolate popcorn clusters with sea salt
s.how: Pop 100g popping corn and spread on a lined tray. Melt 200g white chocolate with a drop of pink colouring and drizzle all over. Sprinkle with sea salt flakes and leave to set, then break into clusters. Very pink.

s.note: White chocolate strawberries with pink sprinkles
s.how: Melt 200g white chocolate. Dip 250g strawberries halfway and roll in pink sprinkles straight away. Set on baking paper for 15 minutes. Serve at the salon while explaining the rules of hair care.

m.note: Creamy chicken penne with sun-dried tomato and spinach
m.how: Sear 2 sliced chicken breasts, add crushed garlic and chopped sun-dried tomatoes, then 300ml cream. Wilt 100g spinach through. Toss with 500g cooked penne and parmesan. What, like it's hard?

w.note: Lemon cupcakes with raspberry pink buttercream
w.how: Beat 125g butter with 150g sugar, add 2 eggs and lemon zest, then fold in 200g self-raising flour and 125ml milk. Bake at 175C for 18 minutes. Beat butter and icing sugar with crushed raspberries until pink and pipe on top.

d.note: Strained raspberry pink lemonade over ice
d.how: Dissolve 150g sugar in 150ml hot water and cool. Crush 125g raspberries in a jug with the juice of 6 lemons, the syrup and 1.5L cold water, then strain. Pour over ice in pink glasses if you have them.

s.note: Turmeric lemongrass chicken skewers with lime peanut sauce
s.how: Marinate 600g chicken thigh strips in coconut milk, turmeric and chopped lemongrass for 2 hours. Thread onto skewers and grill until charred. Warm peanut butter with more coconut milk and lime juice for a thick sauce.

s.note: Puffed prawn crackers with sweet chilli sauce
s.how: Heat oil to 190C and drop in prawn crackers a few at a time. They puff up in seconds. Scoop out and drain on paper. Pile into a big bowl with sweet chilli sauce for dipping, and keep the ping pong balls well away.

m.note: Smoky fried rice with chicken, kecap manis and a fried egg
m.how: Stir-fry 400g diced chicken thighs with crushed garlic and chopped red chilli in a very hot wok. Add 4 cups cold cooked jasmine rice and 3 tbsp kecap manis and toss until smoky. Serve topped with a fried egg and cucumber slices.

w.note: Black sticky rice pudding with salted coconut cream
w.how: Soak 200g black rice overnight, then simmer in 1L water for 40 minutes until thick and soft. Stir in palm sugar to taste. Warm coconut milk with a pinch of salt and pour over each bowl. A Balinese breakfast as dessert.

d.note: Coconut water and pineapple with lime and mint
d.how: Fill tall glasses with ice and mint leaves. Pour in equal parts coconut water and pineapple juice, then squeeze in a wedge of lime. Stir and serve cold, watching the sun go down on a beach in Bali.

s.note: Crisp panko fish fingers with lemon and quick tartare.
s.how: Cut 600g white fish fillets into fingers. Dip in 50g flour, then 2 beaten eggs, then 120g panko. Fry at 180C for 3 minutes until golden and drain. Mix 150g mayonnaise with 2 chopped dill pickles and 1 tbsp capers for tartare and serve with lemon wedges.

s.note: Peanuts, pretzels, raisins, chocolate and dried apple for the drive.
s.how: Tip 150g roasted peanuts, 100g mini pretzels, 100g raisins, 100g chocolate buttons and 80g chopped dried apple into a big bowl and toss together. Portion into 4 paper bags, fold the tops over and keep them in the car for the long drive.

m.note: Grilled beef sausages in rolls with onions and corn on the side.
m.how: Grill 8 thick beef sausages over hot coals or a barbecue for 12 minutes, turning, until charred. Fry 2 sliced onions in oil until soft and sweet. Grill 4 corn cobs for 10 minutes and brush with butter. Serve the sausages in 8 long rolls with the onions, yellow mustard and tomato sauce.

w.note: Toasted marshmallow and melting chocolate between biscuits.
w.how: Toast 16 large marshmallows on skewers over a gas flame or under a hot grill until golden. Squash each between 2 plain biscuits with a square of milk chocolate, 32 biscuits and 200g chocolate in total, and leave 30 seconds so the chocolate starts to melt.

d.note: Icy cherry slushie with a squeeze of lime.
d.how: Blend 200ml cherry cordial with 600g ice, 200ml cold water and the juice of 1 lime until smooth and slushy. Pour into 4 tall cups and serve straight away with straws before it melts.

s.note: Crisp chips under brown gravy and melted mozzarella.
s.how: Cut 1kg potatoes into thick chips, soak 30 minutes and dry. Fry at 150C for 6 minutes, then at 190C for 3 minutes until crisp. Melt 30g butter, stir in 2 tbsp flour, whisk in 400ml beef stock and simmer until thick. Pile the chips on a tray, pour over the gravy and cover with 150g grated mozzarella, then grill until melted.

s.note: Bagel halves grilled with pizza sauce and pepperoni.
s.how: Split 4 bagels and toast lightly. Spread each half with 1 tbsp pizza sauce, top with 150g grated mozzarella and 60g sliced pepperoni, and grill for 4 minutes until bubbling. Cut into halves to share.

m.note: Fried franks with potatoes, peppers and onions in pizza bread.
m.how: Fry 600g diced potatoes in oil until golden, then add 2 sliced green capsicums and 2 sliced onions and cook 10 minutes more until soft. Fry 8 hot dog franks until blistered. Split 4 pizza bread rounds, fill each with 2 franks and a big scoop of the potato and pepper mix, and finish with mustard.

w.note: Creamy vanilla rice pudding, chilled, with cinnamon on top.
w.how: Simmer 150g arborio rice in 1L milk with 80g caster sugar over low heat for 35 minutes, stirring often, until thick and creamy. Stir in 1 tsp vanilla, pour into 4 glasses and chill for 2 hours. Dust with cinnamon before serving.

d.note: Ice-cold birch beer, a New Jersey diner soda.
d.how: Chill 1.2L birch beer for at least 2 hours. Pour into 4 tall diner glasses over ice, adding a scoop of vanilla ice cream to any glass where someone wants it made into a float.

s.note: Beer-battered cheese curds, fried until puffed, with ranch.
s.how: Whisk 150g flour, 1 egg, 200ml lager and a pinch of salt into a smooth batter. Dip 400g cheese curds in batches and fry at 185C for 90 seconds until puffed and golden. Drain on paper and serve straight away with 150ml ranch dressing.

s.note: Thin double-fried fries dusted with paprika salt.
s.how: Cut 1kg russet potatoes into thin fries, soak 30 minutes and dry well. Fry at 140C for 5 minutes and cool, then fry again at 190C for 3 minutes until golden. Toss with 1 tsp salt and 1/2 tsp sweet paprika and serve in paper cones.

m.note: Smashed beef burgers with cheese, pickles and sweet sauce.
m.how: Roll 600g beef mince into 8 balls. Smash each flat on a smoking griddle, season and cook 2 minutes, flip and top with American cheese. Mix 4 tbsp mayonnaise with 1 tbsp tomato sauce and 1 tbsp chopped pickle. Stack 2 patties per toasted bun with sauce, pickles and diced onion.

w.note: Shortbread, golden caramel and chocolate, cut into squares.
w.how: Rub 125g butter into 200g flour with 50g sugar, press into a lined 20x30cm tin and bake at 180C for 15 minutes. Simmer 395g condensed milk, 60g butter and 2 tbsp golden syrup for 6 minutes until thick and golden, pour over and bake 10 minutes. Cool, top with 200g melted milk chocolate and cut into squares.

d.note: Thick vanilla shakes blended fast-food style.
d.how: Blend 1L vanilla ice cream with 500ml cold milk and 1 tsp vanilla extract until thick and smooth. Pour into 4 tall cups and serve with straws straight away.

s.note: Cheese, crackers, salami and pickles boxed up for the road.
s.how: Cut 150g sharp cheddar and 150g pepper jack into cubes. Slice 100g salami and 4 dill pickles. Pack into a box or onto a board with 1 box crackers, the kind of spread you could eat in the back of a stranger's car.

s.note: Cut fruit on a big platter with honey yoghurt dip.
s.how: Cut half a pineapple and half a rockmelon into wedges, halve 250g strawberries and snip 300g grapes into small bunches. Arrange on a big platter. Mix 250g Greek yoghurt with 2 tbsp honey for dipping and keep it all chilled until serving.

m.note: Two smashed patties with cheese and sauce on toasted buns.
m.how: Roll 600g beef mince into 8 balls and smash flat on a smoking griddle, season and cook 2 minutes. Flip, add American cheese and cook 1 minute more. Stack 2 patties per toasted bun with pickles and 4 tbsp mayonnaise mixed with tomato sauce, then wrap in paper.

w.note: Classic banana splits with three ice creams and hot fudge.
w.how: Split 4 bananas lengthways into 4 dishes. Add a scoop each of vanilla, chocolate and strawberry ice cream. Melt 100g dark chocolate with 100ml cream for hot fudge and pour over. Top with whipped cream, chopped peanuts and a cherry.

d.note: Icy raspberry slushies with a squeeze of lemon.
d.how: Blend 200ml raspberry cordial with 600g ice, 200ml cold water and the juice of 1 lemon until smooth and slushy. Pour into 4 big cups and serve straight away with straws.

s.note: Crunchy buttermilk onion rings with smoky ketchup.
s.how: Slice 3 large onions into thick rings and soak in 300ml buttermilk for 20 minutes. Dredge in 200g flour mixed with 1 tsp smoked paprika and salt, and fry at 180C for 3 minutes until crunchy. Serve with 125ml tomato sauce stirred with a pinch more smoked paprika.

s.note: Bacon-wrapped jalapeños stuffed with cream cheese and cheddar.
s.how: Halve 12 jalapeños lengthways and scrape out the seeds. Mix 150g cream cheese with 80g grated cheddar and fill each half. Wrap each in half a rasher of bacon (6 rashers in total) and bake at 200C for 20 minutes until the bacon is crisp.

m.note: Double smashed cheeseburgers on toasted sesame buns.
m.how: Roll 600g beef mince into 8 balls. Smash each flat on a smoking griddle, season and cook 2 minutes, flip and add a slice of American cheese. Stack 2 per toasted sesame bun with pickles, diced onion and 4 tbsp mayonnaise mixed with 1 tbsp tomato sauce.

w.note: Vanilla sheet cake with buttercream and a goodbye message.
w.how: Beat 200g butter with 200g sugar, add 4 eggs, then fold in 300g self-raising flour and 125ml milk. Bake in a lined 20x30cm tin at 175C for 35 minutes and cool. Beat 150g butter with 300g icing sugar for buttercream, spread over and pipe a goodbye message across the top.

d.note: Thick chocolate shakes from the machine behind the counter.
d.how: Blend 1L chocolate ice cream with 500ml cold milk and 4 tbsp chocolate syrup until thick and smooth. Pour into 4 tall paper cups and serve with straws.

s.note: Warm cheddar dip with corn chips from the register warmer.
s.how: Toss 250g grated cheddar with 1 tbsp cornflour. Heat 375ml evaporated milk until steaming and stir in the cheese a handful at a time over low heat until smooth. Season with a pinch of chilli and keep warm with 230g corn chips for dunking.

s.note: Buttery cake under a thick cinnamon crumb, cut into squares.
s.how: Rub 100g butter into 150g self-raising flour, 100g brown sugar and 2 tsp cinnamon for the crumb. Beat 100g butter with 100g sugar, 2 eggs and 200g self-raising flour, spread in a lined 20cm tin, cover with the crumb and bake at 175C for 40 minutes. Dust with icing sugar.

m.note: The New Jersey breakfast roll, done properly.
m.how: Cut 400g pork roll into 8 slices, nick the edges and fry 2 minutes a side until curled and browned. Fry 4 eggs. Stack pork roll, egg and a slice of American cheese into 4 soft rolls, add tomato sauce, salt and pepper, and wrap in foil for 2 minutes to melt.

w.note: Sour cream coffee cake with a cinnamon walnut ripple.
w.how: Beat 125g butter with 200g sugar, add 2 eggs and 250g sour cream, then fold in 300g self-raising flour. Mix 80g chopped walnuts, 50g brown sugar and 2 tsp cinnamon. Layer half the batter, the walnut mix, then the rest in a ring tin and bake at 175C for 45 minutes.

d.note: A big pot of strong drip coffee, milk and sugar on the side.
d.how: Brew 1L strong drip coffee from 60g ground coffee and keep it hot on the warmer. Pour into paper cups and put milk and sugar on the counter so everyone fixes their own.

s.note: Little red cocktail sausages with tomato sauce, Kiwi party style.
s.how: Bring a pot of water to a simmer, add 500g cocktail frankfurts and heat for 5 minutes without boiling so the skins don't split. Drain, pile into a bowl with toothpicks and serve with 125ml tomato sauce for dipping.

s.note: Classic reduced cream onion dip with salted chips.
s.how: Stir 1 packet French onion soup mix into 300ml thickened cream with 1 tbsp lemon juice. Chill for at least 1 hour until thick, stirring once. Serve in a bowl surrounded by 200g salted potato chips for dipping.

m.note: Kiwi takeaway burgers with beetroot, cheese and salad.
m.how: Shape 600g beef mince into 4 patties and fry 4 minutes a side, adding a slice of tasty cheese at the end. Toast 4 buns and build with lettuce, tomato, 4 slices tinned beetroot, the patty and tomato sauce.

w.note: Crunchy cocoa cornflake biscuits with chocolate icing and walnuts.
w.how: Beat 200g butter with 75g sugar, then mix in 175g flour, 25g cocoa and 50g cornflakes. Roll into 16 balls, flatten slightly and bake at 180C for 15 minutes. Cool, ice with 150g icing sugar mixed with 1 tbsp cocoa and water, and top each with a walnut half.

d.note: Pink lemon, lime and bitters over ice.
d.how: Fill 4 glasses with ice. Add 30ml lime cordial and 4 dashes aromatic bitters to each, top with 200ml lemonade and stir until it turns pink. Garnish with lemon and lime wedges.

s.note: Paraoa parai, puffed and golden, with butter and syrup.
s.how: Mix 500g flour, 7g dried yeast, 1 tbsp sugar and 1 tsp salt with 325ml warm water into a soft dough. Prove 1 hour, roll 2cm thick and cut into 12 squares. Fry at 175C for 2 minutes a side until puffed and golden. Serve warm with 60g butter and golden syrup.

s.note: Golden corn fritters with spring onion and sweet chilli.
s.how: Mix 420g creamed corn, 200g corn kernels, 150g self-raising flour, 2 eggs and 3 sliced spring onions. Fry heaped tablespoons in oil for 2 minutes a side until golden. Drain and serve hot with 125ml sweet chilli sauce.

m.note: Slow-roasted pork, kūmara and pumpkin, wrapped and steamed tender.
m.how: Season 1.2kg pork shoulder well. Line a deep roasting tin with cabbage leaves, add the pork, 600g kūmara, 600g pumpkin and 400g potatoes in chunks, then cover with more cabbage and wrap tightly in foil. Roast at 160C for 4 hours until the pork falls apart.

w.note: Vanilla ice cream with homemade crunchy honeycomb.
w.how: Heat 100g sugar and 2 tbsp golden syrup until bubbling and golden, about 4 minutes. Take off the heat, whisk in 1 tsp bicarbonate of soda and pour onto baking paper to set. Smash into small pieces and fold through 1L slightly softened vanilla ice cream, then refreeze 1 hour.

d.note: A thick green lime milkshake, dairy style.
d.how: Blend 600ml cold milk with 4 scoops vanilla ice cream and 4 tbsp lime cordial until frothy. Pour into 4 tall glasses and serve straight away with straws.

s.note: Double-fried hot chips with garlic aioli for the humans.
s.how: Cut 1kg potatoes into thick chips, soak and dry. Fry at 150C for 6 minutes, rest, then fry at 190C for 3 minutes until crunchy and salt well. Mix 150g mayonnaise with 1 crushed garlic clove and a squeeze of lemon for aioli and serve on the side.

s.note: Goat's cheese, roast beetroot and blood orange on toast.
s.how: Wrap 2 beetroot in foil and roast at 200C for 50 minutes, cool, peel and dice. Slice 1 baguette into 16 rounds and toast. Spread with 150g goat's cheese, top with the beetroot and segments from 2 blood oranges, and drizzle with honey.

m.note: Rare roast beef with horseradish cream and rocket in soft rolls.
m.how: Season 800g beef sirloin, sear on all sides in a hot pan, then roast at 200C for 18 minutes for rare. Rest 15 minutes and slice thin. Fill 4 soft rolls with the beef, 4 tbsp horseradish cream and a handful of rocket each.

w.note: Chocolate sponge layered with cherries, cream and chocolate shavings.
w.how: Whisk 4 eggs and 150g sugar until thick, fold in 100g self-raising flour and 30g cocoa, and bake in a 20cm tin at 180C for 25 minutes. Split in two, soak with the syrup from a 680g jar of morello cherries, fill with cherries and 300ml whipped cream, cover in cream and grate 50g dark chocolate on top.

d.note: Blood orange juice and soda, deep red and alcohol-free.
d.how: Squeeze 6 blood oranges. Fill 4 wine glasses with ice, pour 70ml juice into each and top with 150ml soda water. Finish with a slice of blood orange on the rim.

s.note: Warm damper with butter and golden syrup.
s.how: Rub 60g butter into 450g self-raising flour with 1 tsp salt, then stir in 300ml milk to a soft dough. Shape into a round, cut a cross on top and bake at 200C for 30 minutes until it sounds hollow. Serve warm, torn, with butter and golden syrup.

s.note: Pork, apple and sage sausage rolls in flaky pastry.
s.how: Mix 500g pork sausage mince with 1 grated green apple, 1 finely diced onion and 1 tbsp chopped sage. Roll into logs along 2 sheets of puff pastry, roll up, cut each into 6 and brush with 1 beaten egg. Bake at 200C for 25 minutes until golden.

m.note: Roast pork with crackling, apples, onions and roast kūmara.
m.how: Score 1.5kg pork shoulder, rub with salt and leave uncovered in the fridge for an hour. Roast at 230C for 30 minutes, then at 170C for 2 hours on a bed of 2 quartered apples and 2 onions, with 800g kūmara chunks for the last hour. Make gravy with 1 tbsp flour and the pan juices.

w.note: Chocolate birthday cake with chocolate icing and candles.
w.how: Beat 200g butter with 200g sugar, add 3 eggs, then fold in 250g self-raising flour, 50g cocoa and 200ml milk. Bake in a 22cm tin at 175C for 40 minutes and cool. Ice with 250g icing sugar, 2 tbsp cocoa and 50g butter, then add candles and sing badly.

d.note: Rich hot cocoa poured into tin mugs.
d.how: Whisk 4 tbsp cocoa powder and 4 tbsp sugar with a splash of milk into a paste. Whisk in 1L milk and heat until steaming without boiling. Pour into 4 tin mugs and drink around the fire.

s.note: Crisp potato pancakes with apple sauce and sour cream.
s.how: Grate 800g potatoes and 1 onion, squeeze out as much liquid as you can, then mix with 2 eggs, 3 tbsp flour and 1 tsp salt. Fry heaped spoonfuls in oil for 3 minutes a side until crisp. Serve hot with 200g apple sauce and 150g sour cream.

s.n: Brown bread with butter and radishes
s.note: Rye bread with salted butter, radishes, chives and flaky salt.
s.how: Slice 1 dark rye loaf thin. Spread each slice with salted butter, about 100g in total, right to the crust. Top with 1 bunch thinly sliced radishes, snipped chives and a pinch of flaky salt, then cut into fingers.

m.note: Smoked sausage, cabbage and potato stew with caraway.
m.how: Fry 1 sliced onion in a big pot, add 500g sliced smoked sausages and brown. Add 600g diced potatoes, half a cabbage shredded, 1 tsp caraway seeds and 750ml stock. Simmer 30 minutes until the potatoes are soft and the stew is thick, then serve with crusty bread.

w.note: Yeasted plum cake with cinnamon sugar, baked in a tray.
w.how: Mix 300g flour, 7g dried yeast, 50g sugar, 150ml warm milk, 1 egg and 50g soft butter into a dough and prove 1 hour. Press into a lined tray, cover with 1kg halved plums cut side up, sprinkle with 50g sugar and 1 tsp cinnamon, and bake at 190C for 35 minutes.

d.note: Apple juice and sparkling water, half and half.
d.how: Fill 4 tall glasses with ice. Pour 150ml apple juice into each and top with 150ml sparkling water, stirring once. Serve straight away while it's still fizzing.

s.note: Paper-thin taro chips with lime and chilli salt.
s.how: Peel 600g taro and slice paper thin on a mandoline. Fry in batches at 175C for 2 to 3 minutes until crisp and pale golden. Drain and toss with 1 tsp salt mixed with the zest of 1 lime and 1/2 tsp chilli flakes.

s.note: Raw fish cured in lime with coconut cream and vegetables.
s.how: Cut 400g very fresh white fish fillets into 1cm cubes and cover with the juice of 4 limes. Chill 30 minutes until the fish turns white. Drain most of the juice, then stir in 200ml coconut cream, 1 diced cucumber, 2 diced tomatoes and half a finely diced red onion. Season and serve cold.

m.note: Samoan chop suey with glass noodles, chicken and vegetables.
m.how: Soak 250g glass noodles in hot water for 10 minutes and drain. Fry 600g sliced chicken thighs with 3 garlic cloves and a thumb of ginger until browned, then add 2 sliced carrots and 1 onion. Add the noodles, 80ml soy sauce and 250ml water and toss until the noodles soak it all up.

w.note: Soft buns baked in sticky sweet coconut cream.
w.how: Mix 500g flour, 7g dried yeast, 50g sugar, 50g soft butter and 300ml warm water into a dough and prove 1 hour. Shape 12 buns into a baking dish. Mix 400ml coconut cream with 100g sugar, pour over and bake at 180C for 30 minutes until golden and sticky.

d.note: Rich Samoan cocoa, served hot or over ice.
d.how: Melt 150g dark chocolate into 500ml hot water, then whisk in 500ml milk and 3 tbsp sugar and heat until steaming. Serve hot in mugs, or cool it down and pour over ice for a hot afternoon.

s.note: Warm spiced olives with preserved lemon and smoked almonds.
s.how: Warm 300g green olives in 60ml olive oil with the chopped rind of 1 preserved lemon, 1 tsp ground cumin and a pinch of chilli for 5 minutes. Toss 150g almonds with 1 tbsp oil and salt and roast at 180C for 8 minutes. Serve both warm in small bowls.

s.note: Crisp filo triangles with cinnamon-spiced beef.
s.how: Fry 400g beef mince with 1 onion, 1 tsp cinnamon, 1 tsp cumin and salt until browned, then stir in chopped coriander. Cut 8 sheets filo into long strips, brush with 80g melted butter, add a spoonful of filling and fold into triangles. Bake at 190C for 15 minutes until crisp.

m.note: Chicken braised with saffron, preserved lemon and olives, with couscous.
m.how: Brown 1kg chicken thighs, then soften 2 onions with a thumb of grated ginger and a pinch of saffron. Return the chicken with 375ml water, the chopped rind of 1 preserved lemon and 150g green olives and simmer 40 minutes. Pour 300g couscous into 375ml boiling stock, cover 5 minutes and fluff.

w.note: Almond cake soaked in orange blossom syrup, with yoghurt.
w.how: Beat 4 eggs with 200g sugar until pale, then fold in 250g almond meal, the zest of 2 oranges and 1 tsp baking powder. Bake in a 20cm tin at 170C for 40 minutes. Simmer the juice of 2 oranges with 80g sugar and 1 tsp orange blossom water, pour over the warm cake and serve with Greek yoghurt.

d.note: Sweet green tea with fresh mint, poured from a height.
d.how: Rinse 2 tbsp green tea in a teapot with a splash of boiling water and tip it out. Add a big bunch of mint, 4 tbsp sugar and 1L boiling water, brew 4 minutes, then pour from a height into small glasses so it froths.

s.note: Golden coconut macaroons, chewy in the middle.
s.how: Mix 250g desiccated coconut with 395g condensed milk, 1 tsp vanilla and a pinch of salt. Whisk 2 egg whites to stiff peaks and fold through. Scoop 20 mounds onto lined trays and bake at 160C for 20 minutes until golden on the edges.

s.note: Twisted puff pastry straws with cheddar and parmesan.
s.how: Sprinkle 1 sheet puff pastry with 80g grated sharp cheddar, 30g parmesan and a pinch of cayenne, top with a second sheet and press. Cut into 2cm strips, twist each one and bake at 200C for 12 minutes until crisp.

m.note: Crackling-skinned roast chicken with garlic, thyme and potatoes.
m.how: Rub a 1.8kg whole chicken with 50g soft butter mixed with 2 crushed garlic cloves, thyme leaves and salt. Roast at 200C for 75 minutes on a rack over 1kg potatoes in chunks, turning the potatoes halfway, until the juices run clear. Rest 10 minutes and carve.

w.note: Chocolate ice cream with hot fudge, cream and a cherry.
w.how: Melt 100g dark chocolate with 100ml cream into a hot fudge sauce. Scoop 1L chocolate ice cream into 4 tall glasses, pour over the fudge and top with 200ml whipped cream and a maraschino cherry. No coconut.

d.note: Thick homemade eggnog with nutmeg, served cold for Christmas Eve.
d.how: Whisk 4 egg yolks with 80g sugar. Heat 500ml milk and 250ml cream until steaming, whisk into the yolks, then return to the pan and stir over low heat until it coats a spoon. Add 1 tsp vanilla, chill 3 hours and serve with grated nutmeg.

s.note: Ice-cold cucumber, yoghurt and herb soup in small glasses.
s.how: Blend 2 cucumbers with 250g Greek yoghurt, a handful each of dill and mint, 1 small garlic clove and the juice of 1 lemon until smooth. Season well, chill for 2 hours and pour into 8 small glasses.

s.note: Ham and Swiss on rye with mustard, cut into quarters.
s.how: Spread 8 slices rye bread with Dijon mustard. Fill 4 with 250g sliced ham and 8 slices Swiss cheese and close. Cut each into quarters and stack on a plate by the window, the way Stella leaves them.

m.note: Lobster thermidor with buttered potatoes and green beans.
m.how: Halve 4 lobster tails and bake at 200C for 8 minutes. Simmer 250ml cream with 1 tbsp Dijon until thick, stir in 40g parmesan, spoon over the lobster and grill until bubbling. Serve with 800g boiled potatoes tossed in butter and 300g steamed green beans.

w.note: No-bake lemon pie set cold, with whipped cream.
w.how: Crush 250g plain biscuits with 100g melted butter and press into a pie dish. Whisk 395g condensed milk with the juice of 4 lemons and the zest of 1 until it thickens, pour into the base and chill 4 hours. Top with 200ml whipped cream.

d.note: Strong iced coffee with milk over plenty of ice.
d.how: Brew 500ml strong coffee from 50g ground coffee, stir in 4 tsp sugar and chill for an hour. Fill 4 tall glasses with ice, pour in the coffee and top each with 100ml cold milk.

s.note: Little gruyère choux puffs, warm from the oven.
s.how: Boil 125ml water with 50g butter, beat in 75g flour until it leaves the pan, cool 5 minutes and beat in 2 eggs, then 80g grated gruyère. Pipe 20 small puffs and bake at 200C for 22 minutes until hollow and golden.

s.note: Crisp vegetables, olives and pickles on ice with cream cheese.
s.how: Cut 4 celery sticks and 2 carrots into sticks and trim 1 bunch radishes. Arrange on crushed ice with 150g mixed olives and 4 dill pickles cut into spears, and add a small dish of 125g cream cheese for spreading.

m.note: Pan-fried trout with brown butter, almonds and lemon.
m.how: Dust 4 cleaned whole trout in flour and season. Fry 2 at a time in 40g butter for 4 minutes a side until crisp. Brown another 40g butter with 40g flaked almonds, add the juice of 1 lemon and chopped parsley and spoon over the fish.

w.note: Sponge, ice cream and toasted meringue, a 1950s showpiece.
w.how: Lay a 20cm sponge round on a tray and dome 1L firm vanilla ice cream on top, then freeze. Whisk 4 egg whites with 200g sugar to stiff, glossy peaks. Cover the ice cream completely in meringue and bake at 230C for 4 minutes until browned. Serve straight away.

d.note: A dry gin Gibson with a cocktail onion.
d.how: For each drink, stir 60ml gin and 10ml dry vermouth over ice for 30 seconds and strain into a chilled glass with a cocktail onion. Pour sparkling water over ice with onions for anyone off the gin.

s.note: Bacon-wrapped prunes stuffed with almonds, baked crisp on sticks
s.how: Push an almond into each of 24 pitted prunes. Wrap each in a third of a bacon rasher, secure with a toothpick and bake at 200C for 15 minutes until the bacon is crisp.

s.note: Golden cheese toasties cut into soldiers with tomato soup.
s.how: Butter 8 slices white bread on the outside and fill 4 with 200g grated cheddar. Toast in a pan over medium heat for 3 minutes a side until golden and melted. Cut into soldiers and serve with 800ml hot tomato soup in mugs for dunking.

m.note: Creamy chicken, mushrooms and capsicum in pastry cases.
m.how: Fry 600g diced chicken breast in butter, then add 200g sliced mushrooms and 1 diced red capsicum. Stir in 1 tbsp flour, then 300ml cream and 125ml stock and simmer 8 minutes until thick. Spoon into 8 puff pastry cases baked at 200C for 15 minutes.

w.note: Tall vanilla layer cake with pink buttercream and sprinkles.
w.how: Beat 250g butter with 250g sugar, add 4 eggs, then fold in 300g self-raising flour and 125ml milk. Bake in two 20cm tins at 175C for 30 minutes. Beat 200g butter with 400g icing sugar and a drop of pink colouring, stack and cover the layers, then shower with sprinkles.

d.note: Fresh lemon syrup topped with sparkling water in coupe glasses.
d.how: Simmer 100g sugar with 100ml water and the zest of 2 lemons until dissolved, cool and add the juice of 4 lemons. Pour 40ml into each of 4 coupe glasses and top with chilled sparkling water and a lemon twist.

s.note: Oranges, fennel, red onion, olives and mint.
s.how: Peel and slice 4 oranges into rounds. Shave 1 fennel bulb and half a red onion paper thin. Arrange on a platter with 60g black olives and torn mint, then dress with 3 tbsp olive oil and flaky salt.

s.note: Crisp pork and vegetable spring rolls with dipping sauces.
s.how: Fry 300g pork mince until browned, then add 2 cups shredded cabbage and 1 grated carrot and cook until soft, seasoning with soy. Roll tablespoons into 16 spring roll wrappers, seal with water and fry at 180C for 4 minutes until crisp. Serve with sweet chilli sauce and soy.

m.note: Whole snapper grilled with lemon and herbs, head and all.
m.how: Score 2 whole snapper (about 800g each) three times on each side. Stuff with lemon slices, parsley and sliced garlic, rub with olive oil and salt. Grill or bake at 220C for 20 minutes until the flesh flakes at the thickest part. Serve whole, heads on.

w.note: Light orange chiffon cake with orange glaze.
w.how: Whisk 5 egg yolks with 125ml oil, 125ml orange juice, the zest of 2 oranges, 150g sugar and 200g self-raising flour. Whisk 5 egg whites stiff with 50g sugar and fold in. Bake in an ungreased tube tin at 165C for 50 minutes, cool upside down and glaze with 150g icing sugar mixed with orange juice.

d.note: Fresh-squeezed orange juice from a jug, poured over ice.
d.how: Squeeze 12 oranges through a strainer into a chilled jug, about 1L. Pour into 4 glasses over a couple of ice cubes each and serve straight away.

s.note: Skillet cornbread cut into squares with butter.
s.how: Heat a greased 25cm pan in the oven at 210C. Mix 200g cornmeal, 125g flour, 2 tsp baking powder and 1 tsp salt with 350ml buttermilk, 2 eggs and 80g melted butter. Pour into the hot pan and bake 20 minutes, then cut into squares and serve with butter.

s.note: Chunky guacamole with lime, chilli and coriander, corn chips alongside.
s.how: Mash 3 ripe avocados roughly with the juice of 2 limes and salt. Stir in half a finely diced red onion, 1 diced jalapeño and a handful of chopped coriander. Serve straight away with 230g warm corn chips.

m.note: Thick beef stew with potatoes and carrots, bread to mop.
m.how: Brown 1kg diced beef chuck in batches, then soften 2 onions. Return the beef with 2 tbsp flour, 750ml beef stock, 600g potatoes and 3 carrots in chunks. Cover and simmer 2 hours until tender. Ladle into bowls with thick white bread.

w.note: Rough-cut rocky road with marshmallows, peanuts and biscuits.
w.how: Melt 400g milk chocolate gently. Stir in 150g marshmallows, 100g roasted peanuts and 100g broken plain biscuits. Spread into a lined 20cm tin, chill 2 hours until set and cut into rough rocks.

d.note: Ice-cold lager, or ginger beer for the drivers.
d.how: Chill 4 bottles of lager and 2 bottles of ginger beer for at least 3 hours. Hand them out cold, the way the tarring crew got theirs on the roof, sitting in the sun.

s.n: Chicken liver pâté with broad beans
s.note: Smooth liver pâté with smashed broad beans on toast.
s.how: Fry 1 shallot in 30g butter, add 400g trimmed chicken livers and thyme and cook 4 minutes until just pink inside. Blitz with 100g more butter until smooth and chill. Boil 300g broad beans, peel and smash with oil and salt. Serve both on toasted baguette slices.

s.note: Lacy parmesan crisps baked in wing shapes.
s.how: Grate 150g parmesan finely. Spoon into small wing shapes on 2 lined trays, grind over black pepper and bake at 200C for 6 minutes until lacy and golden. Cool on the tray for 5 minutes so they crisp.

m.note: Lamb shanks braised in red wine with rosemary, over polenta.
m.how: Brown 4 lamb shanks, then soften 1 onion and 4 garlic cloves. Add 375ml red wine, 400g crushed tomatoes and 2 sprigs rosemary, cover and braise at 160C for 2.5 hours. Cook 200g polenta in 1L salted water for 5 minutes, stir in butter and serve the shanks on top.

w.note: Pears poached deep red in wine, with mascarpone.
w.how: Peel 4 pears, keeping the stalks. Simmer 375ml red wine with 125ml water, 100g sugar, 1 cinnamon stick and 2 strips orange peel, add the pears and poach 25 minutes, turning. Reduce the syrup and serve the pears with 150g mascarpone.

d.note: Chianti at room temperature, or sour cherry juice.
d.how: Open a bottle of Chianti 30 minutes before serving and pour into big glasses at room temperature. Serve chilled sour cherry juice in the same glasses for anyone not drinking.

s.note: Icy cucumber spears with honey miso for dipping.
s.how: Soak 6 small cucumbers in a bowl of iced water for 30 minutes, the way Granny cools them in the stream. Cut into spears. Mix 3 tbsp white miso with 1 tbsp honey and 1 tbsp water and serve in a little dish for dipping.

s.note: Charred corn brushed with soy butter.
s.how: Grill 4 corn cobs over high heat for 10 minutes, turning, until charred in spots. Melt 40g butter with 2 tbsp soy sauce and 1 tsp sugar and brush all over the corn while it's hot.

m.note: Rice, teriyaki chicken, rolled omelette and pickles in a box.
m.how: Cook 400g sushi rice. Fry 500g chicken thighs, then glaze with 3 tbsp soy and 2 tbsp sugar until sticky. Whisk 4 eggs with a pinch of sugar and roll into a thin omelette in a pan. Pack each box with rice topped with peas, sliced chicken, omelette and pickled ginger.

w.note: Honey pancakes sandwiched with sweet red bean paste.
w.how: Whisk 3 eggs with 100g sugar and 2 tbsp honey, then 150g flour, 1 tsp baking powder and 60ml water. Cook 16 small pancakes in a lightly oiled pan for 1 minute a side. Sandwich in pairs with 300g red bean paste.

d.note: Roasted barley tea, chilled and poured over ice.
d.how: Steep 3 roasted barley tea bags in 1.5L just-boiled water for 10 minutes, then remove the bags and chill for 2 hours. Pour into 4 tall glasses over ice.

s.note: Glossy spiced nuts with brown sugar, cayenne and rosemary.
s.how: Melt 30g butter with 2 tbsp brown sugar, 1/2 tsp cayenne, 1 tbsp chopped rosemary and 1 tsp salt. Toss through 350g mixed nuts, spread on a lined tray and roast at 170C for 12 minutes, stirring halfway. Cool 5 minutes so they crisp.

s.note: Pastry cases filled with creamy chicken and mushroom.
s.how: Fry 300g diced chicken breast in butter, add 150g sliced mushrooms, then stir in 1 tbsp flour and 200ml cream and simmer until thick. Warm 16 vol-au-vent cases at 180C for 5 minutes, fill them and pass around on a tray.

m.note: Braised chicken with buttered rice and peas in neat portions.
m.how: Brown 800g chicken thighs, then add 1 diced onion and 2 garlic cloves. Pour in 500ml chicken stock, cover and simmer 25 minutes. Cook 300g long grain rice, stir through 20g butter and 200g peas. Plate in tidy single portions, like the airline trays.

w.note: Rich dark chocolate pots, set in small cups.
w.how: Heat 300ml cream with 2 tbsp sugar until steaming. Pour over 200g chopped dark chocolate and stir until smooth. Divide between 4 small cups and chill for 3 hours until set.

d.note: Cold cans of lager, or ginger beer.
d.how: Chill 4 cans of lager and 2 cans of ginger beer for at least 3 hours. Serve straight from the can, ice cold, with no glasses required.

s.note: Warm yeasted donut holes rolled in cinnamon sugar.
s.how: Mix 300g flour, 7g dried yeast, 30g sugar, 160ml warm milk, 1 egg and 30g soft butter into a soft dough and prove 1 hour. Roll into 24 small balls, prove 20 minutes, then fry at 175C for 2 minutes until golden. Roll in 100g sugar mixed with 2 tsp cinnamon while hot.

s.note: Light choux cheese puffs made with gruyère
s.how: Bring 250ml water and 100g butter to the boil, beat in 150g flour until it pulls away, then cool 5 minutes. Beat in 4 eggs one at a time and 120g grated gruyère. Pipe walnut-sized balls onto trays and bake at 200C for 25 minutes until puffed and golden.

m.note: Garlic and thyme rib roast carved pink, with horseradish and potatoes.
m.how: Rub a 1.5kg beef rib roast with 3 crushed garlic cloves, thyme and salt. Roast at 220C for 20 minutes, then 180C for 45 minutes for medium rare, and rest 20 minutes. Roast 1kg potatoes in chunks alongside. Carve at the table with 4 tbsp horseradish cream.

w.note: Chocolate layer cake with fudge frosting and candles.
w.how: Beat 200g butter with 250g sugar, add 3 eggs, then fold in 250g self-raising flour, 60g cocoa and 250ml milk. Bake in two 20cm tins at 175C for 30 minutes. Melt 200g dark chocolate with 100g butter, beat in 150g icing sugar, then stack and frost the layers and add candles.

d.note: Big mugs of strong drip coffee, cream and sugar on the side.
d.how: Brew 1L strong drip coffee from 60g ground coffee. Pour into 4 big mugs and set out 100ml cream and sugar so everyone fixes their own. Check whose mug you're drinking from first.

s.note: Hummus, tzatziki, olives and warm pita on a big board.
s.how: Blitz 400g drained chickpeas with 2 tbsp tahini, 1 garlic clove, lemon and ice water until smooth. Mix 250g Greek yoghurt with half a grated cucumber, garlic and salt for tzatziki. Lay both out with 150g kalamata olives, cherry tomatoes and 4 warm pita breads.

s.note: Crisp wings tossed in homemade chilli hot sauce with blue cheese dip
s.how: Toss 1.2kg chicken wings with 2 tsp baking powder and salt and bake at 220C for 45 minutes, turning once. Blitz 6 red chillies with 3 garlic cloves, 80ml vinegar and 2 tbsp honey, simmer 5 minutes and toss through the wings. Serve with celery and 150g blue cheese stirred into 150g sour cream.

m.note: Lemon and oregano lamb skewers in pita with tzatziki.
m.how: Cut 800g lamb leg into cubes and marinate 2 hours with the juice of 1 lemon, 3 garlic cloves, 2 tsp dried oregano and 3 tbsp oil. Thread onto skewers and grill 8 minutes, turning. Serve in 4 warm pitas with 250g Greek yoghurt mixed with grated cucumber, plus tomato and onion.

w.note: Buttery cake baked over caramel and pineapple rings, turned out warm
w.how: Melt 60g butter with 100g brown sugar in a 23cm tin and lay over 8 pineapple rings from a 440g tin. Beat 125g butter and 125g sugar, add 2 eggs, then fold in 175g self-raising flour and 80ml pineapple juice. Spread over and bake at 180C for 40 minutes, then turn out while warm.

d.note: Chilled ginger kombucha over ice, spiked with vodka if you like
d.how: Fill 4 tall glasses with ice, mint leaves and a squeeze of lime. Pour 250ml cold ginger kombucha into each and add 30ml vodka to the glasses of anyone who wants it spiked. Stir once and serve straight away.

s.note: Toasted mini bagels with scallion cream cheese and everything seasoning.
s.how: Halve and toast 8 mini bagels. Beat 200g cream cheese with 3 finely sliced spring onions. Spread thickly on each half and shower generously with 2 tbsp everything bagel seasoning.

s.note: Pan-fried pork and cabbage dumplings with black vinegar and chilli oil.
s.how: Mix 400g pork mince with 2 cups finely chopped cabbage, 2 tbsp soy sauce and 1 tsp sesame oil. Fill 30 dumpling wrappers and pleat closed. Fry flat side down until golden, add 125ml water, cover and steam 6 minutes. Serve with black vinegar and chilli oil.

m.note: Hibachi-style steak, prawns and vegetables with garlic butter fried rice.
m.how: Cook 300g rice the day before. Sear 500g sliced sirloin and 300g peeled prawns on a smoking plate with 30g garlic butter and soy. Add sliced zucchini and onion. Fry the rice with 2 eggs, butter and soy alongside, and serve everything together.

w.note: Crisp sesame balls with sweet red bean paste inside.
w.how: Mix 250g glutinous rice flour with 60g sugar and 200ml hot water into a soft dough. Wrap 16 balls around teaspoons of red bean paste (200g total), wet and roll in 80g sesame seeds. Fry at 160C for 6 minutes, pressing gently, until puffed and golden.

d.note: Milk tea with brown sugar syrup and chewy tapioca pearls.
d.how: Brew 4 black tea bags in 750ml boiling water for 5 minutes and chill. Cook 150g tapioca pearls as the packet says and toss in 80g brown sugar melted with 60ml water. Spoon pearls into 4 glasses, add ice, the tea and 250ml milk, and serve with wide straws.

s.note: Rolled white bread pinwheels filled with pink strawberry cream cheese.
s.how: Blitz 100g strawberries and beat into 250g cream cheese. Trim the crusts from 8 slices white bread and roll each flat. Spread with the pink cream cheese, roll up tightly, chill 20 minutes and slice into pinwheels.

s.note: Bright fruit skewers with honey yoghurt dip.
s.how: Cut a quarter of a watermelon and half a pineapple into chunks and halve 250g strawberries and 3 kiwi fruit. Thread onto 12 skewers in a rainbow and chill. Mix 250g Greek yoghurt with 2 tbsp honey for dipping.

m.note: Penne in a bright pink roasted beetroot and ricotta sauce.
m.how: Roast 3 beetroot wrapped in foil at 200C for 50 minutes, peel and blend with 250g ricotta, 1 garlic clove, 40g parmesan and a splash of pasta water. Toss through 500g cooked penne until glossy and pink, and crumble 100g goat's cheese over the top.

w.note: Waffles with strawberries, cream and pink strawberry sauce.
w.how: Make 8 waffles from 300g waffle mix. Blitz 150g strawberries with 2 tbsp sugar for a pink sauce. Whip 300ml cream. Stack the waffles with cream, 250g sliced strawberries and the pink sauce poured over.

d.note: Fresh strawberry milk, pink and frothy.
d.how: Blend 300g hulled strawberries with 1L cold milk and 2 tbsp honey until smooth and frothy. Strain if you like it silky and pour into 4 glasses over ice.

s.n: Blue corn chips with red chile salsa
s.note: Blue corn chips with smoky dried red chile salsa.
s.how: Toast 4 dried red chillies in a dry pan, soak in hot water 15 minutes and drain. Blitz with 3 tomatoes, 2 garlic cloves, the juice of 1 lime and salt until smooth. Serve with 230g blue corn chips.

s.note: Egg salad with mustard and celery on soft white bread.
s.how: Boil 6 eggs for 10 minutes, cool, peel and chop. Mix with 4 tbsp mayonnaise, 1 tsp Dijon and 1 finely diced celery stick, season well. Fill 8 slices white bread and cut into triangles.

m.note: New Mexico pork and potato stew with roasted green chillies.
m.how: Brown 1kg diced pork shoulder, then soften 1 onion and 3 garlic cloves. Char 6 large green chillies, peel, chop and add with 600g diced potatoes and 1L chicken stock. Simmer 90 minutes until the pork is tender. Serve with 8 warm flour tortillas.

w.note: Puffy fried dough pillows filled with honey.
w.how: Mix 250g flour, 2 tsp baking powder, 1/2 tsp salt and 20g butter, then add 160ml warm water to a soft dough. Rest 20 minutes, roll 5mm thick and cut into 12 squares. Fry at 185C for 1 minute a side until puffed. Tear open and fill with honey.

d.note: Very dry gin martinis, rim touched with lime and honey.
d.how: Touch the rim of 4 chilled glasses with a little honey and lime. For each drink, stir 60ml gin with a splash of dry vermouth over ice and strain in. Serve iced lime soda the same way for anyone off the gin.

s.note: Crunchy chickpeas roasted with cumin, paprika and cinnamon.
s.how: Drain and dry 800g chickpeas well. Toss with 2 tbsp oil, 1 tsp cumin, 1 tsp smoked paprika, 1/2 tsp cinnamon and salt. Roast at 200C for 35 minutes, shaking twice, until crunchy. Cool 5 minutes before serving.

s.note: Dates stuffed with almond and goat's cheese, honey on top.
s.how: Split 16 medjool dates and remove the stones. Fill each with a little goat's cheese (100g total) and a toasted almond. Lay on a plate and drizzle with 2 tbsp warm honey just before serving.

m.note: Slow-roasted spiced lamb shoulder with golden saffron rice.
m.how: Rub a 1.5kg lamb shoulder with 2 tsp cumin, 2 tsp coriander, 1 tsp cinnamon, chilli and salt. Roast covered at 160C for 3.5 hours until it pulls apart. Steep a pinch of saffron in hot water and cook 300g basmati rice with it until golden and fluffy.

w.note: Honey spice cake with cardamom, cinnamon and ginger.
w.how: Melt 150g butter with 150g honey and 100g brown sugar. Mix with 250g self-raising flour, 2 tsp cardamom, 1 tsp cinnamon, 1 tsp ginger, 2 eggs and 125ml milk. Bake in a loaf tin at 170C for 50 minutes and brush with warm honey.

d.note: Cardamom coffee, sweet and strong, in small cups.
d.how: Brew 500ml strong coffee from 50g ground coffee with 1 tsp ground cardamom and a pinch of cinnamon in the grounds. Sweeten with 4 tsp sugar and pour into small cups.

s.note: Fresh garden vegetables with whipped feta.
s.how: Trim 1 bunch radishes and 1 bunch baby carrots, slice 1 cucumber into spears and string 150g snow peas. Whip 200g feta with 3 tbsp olive oil and lemon until smooth. Arrange the vegetables around the feta like a fresh garden.

s.note: Charred smoked sausage bites in barbecue sauce.
s.how: Slice 500g smoked sausages into thick rounds. Char in a hot pan for 4 minutes until blistered, then toss with 4 tbsp barbecue sauce until sticky. Serve on toothpicks straight from the pan.

m.note: Rosemary and lemon lamb chops grilled hot, with charred corn.
m.how: Marinate 12 lamb chops for 1 hour with 2 sprigs chopped rosemary, 3 garlic cloves, the juice of 1 lemon and 3 tbsp oil. Grill over high heat 3 minutes a side. Grill 4 corn cobs for 10 minutes alongside and brush with butter.

w.note: Caramelised grilled peaches with honey, thyme and ice cream.
w.how: Halve and stone 4 peaches. Brush the cut sides with a little oil and grill cut side down for 4 minutes until charred and soft. Drizzle with 2 tbsp honey warmed with thyme and serve with 500ml vanilla ice cream.

d.note: Thick, cold vanilla milkshakes sweetened with a little honey.
d.how: Blend 1L cold milk with 500ml vanilla ice cream and 2 tbsp honey until thick and frothy. Pour into 4 tall glasses and serve straight away.

s.note: Cooked king prawns on ice with lemon and cocktail sauce.
s.how: Pile 1kg cooked king prawns on crushed ice with lemon wedges. Mix 125ml tomato sauce with 1 tsp horseradish and a squeeze of lemon. Serve with buttered white bread, the way you would on the harbour.

s.note: Grilled snags in white bread with onions and sauce.
s.how: Grill 8 beef sausages for 12 minutes, turning, until browned. Fry 2 sliced onions on the hotplate until soft and golden. Wrap each sausage in a slice of white bread with onions and tomato sauce.

m.note: Beer-battered flathead with thick chips and tartare.
m.how: Cut 1kg potatoes into chips and fry at 150C for 6 minutes, then 190C for 3 minutes. Whisk 150g flour with 250ml cold lager into a batter, dip 600g flathead fillets and fry at 180C for 4 minutes. Mix 125g mayonnaise with chopped pickles for tartare and serve with lemon.

w.note: Crisp pavlova with cream, passionfruit and strawberries.
w.how: Whisk 4 egg whites to stiff peaks, then add 220g caster sugar a spoon at a time until glossy. Fold in 1 tsp cornflour and 1 tsp vinegar, shape into a round and bake at 120C for 90 minutes, then cool in the oven. Top with 300ml whipped cream, 4 passionfruit and 250g strawberries.

d.note: Aussie iced coffee with ice cream and cream.
d.how: Brew 500ml strong coffee from 50g ground coffee and chill. Pour into 4 tall glasses with ice and 400ml cold milk, then top each with a scoop of vanilla ice cream and a spoon of whipped cream.

s.note: Butter and thick-cut marmalade on soft white bread.
s.how: Spread 8 slices white bread with 60g soft butter and a thick layer of orange marmalade, about 200g in total. Sandwich together, keep the crusts on as Paddington would, and cut into squares.

s.note: Layered lime potato squares with chicken and avocado.
s.how: Boil 800g potatoes, mash smooth with the juice of 2 limes, 2 tbsp ají amarillo paste, 3 tbsp oil and salt. Mix 300g cooked shredded chicken breast with 3 tbsp mayonnaise. Layer potato, chicken, sliced avocado and more potato in a tin, chill 1 hour and cut into squares.

m.note: Peruvian beef and onion stir-fry tossed through chips, with rice.
m.how: Bake 500g frozen fries until crisp. Sear 600g sliced beef rump in a smoking wok, add 1 sliced red onion and 2 tomatoes in wedges, then 3 tbsp soy and 1 tbsp vinegar. Toss through the chips and serve with 300g cooked rice.

w.note: Cornflour biscuits with dulce de leche and coconut.
w.how: Beat 150g butter with 80g icing sugar, then mix in 150g cornflour and 100g flour. Roll 5mm thick, cut 24 rounds and bake at 170C for 10 minutes until pale. Sandwich in pairs with 300g dulce de leche and roll the edges in coconut.

d.note: Spiced purple corn drink with pineapple and lime.
d.how: Simmer 250g dried purple corn with the peel and core of 1 pineapple, 2 cinnamon sticks and 4 cloves in 2L water for 45 minutes. Strain, stir in 100g sugar and the juice of 2 limes, and chill. Serve over ice.

s.note: Crumbly Yorkshire cheese with crackers, chutney and apple.
s.how: Cut 300g crumbly white cheese into rough chunks on a board. Add 1 box cream crackers, a pot of tomato chutney and 2 sliced apples. Leave out 20 minutes before serving so the cheese warms up a bit.

s.note: Hot buttered toast with jam, stacked in a rack.
s.how: Toast 8 slices white bread until golden. Butter right to the edges straight away, spread with strawberry jam and cut into triangles. Stack them in a toast rack, the way the breakfast machine would.

m.note: Pork sausages on creamy mash with onion gravy.
m.how: Brown 8 pork sausages slowly in a pan for 15 minutes. Boil 1kg potatoes and mash with 60g butter and 100ml milk. Fry 2 sliced onions in the sausage pan until soft, stir in 1 tbsp flour and 400ml beef stock and simmer until thick. Serve the sausages on mash with gravy.

w.note: Baked jam roly-poly in slices with hot custard.
w.how: Rub 100g cold butter into 250g self-raising flour, add 150ml milk to make a soft dough and roll into a rectangle. Spread with 200g strawberry jam, roll up and bake on a lined tray at 190C for 35 minutes. Serve in slices with 500ml custard made from custard powder and milk.

d.note: Strong pot of black tea with milk and sugar.
d.how: Warm a teapot, add 4 tsp black tea and 1L just-boiled water and brew 4 minutes. Pour into big mugs with milk and sugar to taste, and take a moment, like Gromit with his knitting.

s.note: Crisp-skinned baked potatoes with butter and chives.
s.how: Prick 4 large potatoes, rub with oil and salt and bake at 200C for 70 minutes until the skins are crisp. Split open, press to fluff and fill each with butter (60g total), more salt and snipped chives.

s.note: Choc chip cookie dough baked in a tray and cut into blocks.
s.how: Beat 125g butter with 150g brown sugar and 1 egg, then mix in 200g flour, 1/2 tsp bicarb and 150g chocolate chips. Press into a lined 20cm square tin and bake at 175C for 22 minutes. Cut into neat squares while warm.

m.note: Sticky honey chilli drumsticks, roasted until charred.
m.how: Toss 12 chicken drumsticks with 4 tbsp honey, 1 tsp chilli flakes, 2 tsp smoked paprika, 2 tbsp oil and salt. Roast at 200C for 45 minutes, turning and basting twice, until sticky and charred at the edges.

w.note: Spiced pumpkin pie with whipped cream.
w.how: Roast 600g pumpkin until soft and purée. Whisk with 395g condensed milk, 2 eggs, 2 tsp cinnamon and a pinch of nutmeg. Pour into a blind-baked shortcrust case and bake at 180C for 45 minutes until just set. Cool and serve with 200ml whipped cream.

d.note: Cold milk with chocolate syrup on the side.
d.how: Chill 1.2L milk well and pour into 4 big mugs. Put a jug with 125ml chocolate syrup on the table so everyone stirs in as much as they like.

s.note: Seaweed rice rolls with egg, carrot and spinach.
s.how: Season 300g cooked sushi rice with sesame oil and salt. Lay rice on 4 nori sheets, add strips of omelette from 2 eggs, sautéed carrot, blanched spinach and pickled radish, then roll tightly and slice into rounds.

s.note: Battered sausage and mozzarella sticks, fried and rolled in sugar
s.how: Thread 8 frankfurts onto skewers with a stick of mozzarella above each. Whisk 250g self-raising flour, 1 egg, 2 tbsp sugar and 250ml milk into a thick batter, pour into a tall glass, dip each skewer and roll in 100g panko. Fry at 170C for 4 minutes, roll in sugar and drizzle with ketchup and mustard.

m.note: Spicy noodles with soft egg, kimchi and melted cheese.
m.how: Bring 2L water to the boil with 2 tbsp gochugaru, 2 tbsp soy and a stock cube. Cook 4 packets ramen noodles for 3 minutes, crack in 4 eggs and cover 1 minute. Divide into bowls with 200g kimchi, sliced spring onions and a slice of cheese melting on top.

w.note: Crisp sweet pancakes filled with brown sugar and walnuts.
w.how: Mix 300g flour, 7g dried yeast, 1 tbsp sugar and 220ml warm milk into a sticky dough and prove 1 hour. Fill 8 balls with 80g brown sugar, 1 tsp cinnamon and 40g chopped walnuts, flatten in an oiled pan and fry 2 minutes a side until crisp.

d.note: Grape juice poured into little bottles labelled vocal tonic
d.how: Chill 1.2L grape juice. Pour into 4 small bottles or pouches, write a label for each that says vocal tonic, and serve very cold. Add a squeeze of lemon and a splash of soda water to each if you want it fizzy.

s.note: Crumbed fish bites with lemon and herby yoghurt.
s.how: Cut 500g white fish fillets into strips. Dip in 50g flour, 2 beaten eggs and 120g panko, and fry at 180C for 3 minutes until golden. Mix 200g Greek yoghurt with lemon and chopped dill and serve with lemon wedges.

s.note: Charred smoked sausages with grainy mustard.
s.how: Cook 600g thick smoked sausages over high heat for 8 minutes, turning, until charred and split. Cut into chunks and serve on a board with 4 tbsp wholegrain mustard for dipping.

m.note: Lamb and barley stew with root vegetables and thyme.
m.how: Brown 1kg diced lamb shoulder, then add 1 onion, 3 carrots and 2 parsnips in chunks, 100g pearl barley, thyme and 1.25L beef stock. Cover and simmer 2 hours until the lamb is tender and the barley is plump. Serve in big bowls with bread.

w.note: Little spiced honey cakes glazed with warm honey.
w.how: Beat 125g butter with 125g honey, add 2 eggs, then fold in 200g self-raising flour, 1 tsp cinnamon and 80ml milk. Spoon into 12 muffin cases and bake at 175C for 18 minutes. Brush with 2 tbsp warm honey while hot.

d.note: Mixed berry and apple juice, blended and strained.
d.how: Blend 300g frozen mixed berries with 1L apple juice for a full minute until completely smooth. Strain through a fine sieve, pressing on the pulp, then chill and serve in 4 glasses over ice.

s.note: Quick-pickled daikon and carrot, cold and crunchy.
s.how: Cut 400g daikon and 2 carrots into thin batons. Warm 250ml rice vinegar with 3 tbsp sugar and 1 tsp salt until dissolved, cool, pour over the vegetables and pickle in the fridge for at least 1 hour before serving cold.

s.note: Fluffy steamed buns filled with sweet red bean.
s.how: Mix 400g flour, 7g dried yeast, 40g sugar and 220ml warm milk into a smooth dough and prove 1 hour. Divide into 12, fill each with a spoon of red bean paste (300g total) and pinch closed. Prove 20 minutes, then steam 12 minutes until puffed.

m.note: Egg noodles in rich chicken broth with greens and a soft egg.
m.how: Simmer 1.5L chicken stock with 150g sliced shiitake for 10 minutes. Boil 4 eggs for 6 minutes, cool and peel. Cook 400g egg noodles and divide into 4 bowls, add 2 halved bok choy blanched in the broth, ladle over the stock and top with halved eggs and sliced spring onion.

w.note: Pink-tipped peach-shaped buns filled with red bean.
w.how: Make a dough of 300g flour, 5g yeast, 30g sugar and 170ml warm water and prove 1 hour. Shape 10 balls around red bean paste (250g total), pinch a point and score a crease like a peach. Steam 12 minutes, then dab the tips with a little red colouring.

d.note: Chilled sweet, sour and smoky Chinese plum drink
d.how: Simmer 6 dried smoked plums, a few dried hawthorn slices and 1 tsp dried osmanthus in 1.5L water for 40 minutes. Strain, sweeten with 100g rock sugar and chill. Serve over ice.

s.note: Lemony sardines on hot buttered toast.
s.how: Drain 2 tins sardines (220g total) and mash with the juice of half a lemon and black pepper. Toast 4 slices white bread, butter them, spread with the sardines and grill for 1 minute until hot. Cut into fingers.

s.note: Iceberg wedges with blue cheese dressing and crispy bacon.
