d.how: Stud 2 oranges with 6 cloves and roast for 20 minutes. Slice into a pan with 750ml port and 3 tbsp sugar and heat for 15 minutes without boiling. Heat apple juice with spices for the kids.

s.note: Crackers, cheddar and pickles from the pantry
s.how: Arrange 200g crackers, 200g sliced cheddar and a bowl of pickles on a board. Add a few candles to the table if you want the power-cut feel.

s.note: Homemade French onion dip with chips
s.how: Cook 2 sliced onions in 30g butter over low heat for 30 minutes until jammy. Cool, chop and stir into 250g sour cream with salt. Serve with 200g potato chips.

m.note: Beef lasagne with a cheesy top
m.how: Brown 600g beef mince, add 700g passata and simmer 20 minutes. Make a white sauce from 40g butter, 40g flour and 500ml milk. Layer with lasagne sheets, top with 150g mozzarella and bake at 180C for 40 minutes.

w.note: Gingerbread men iced with jagged grins
w.how: Melt 100g butter with 100g golden syrup and 80g brown sugar. Mix in 300g flour and 2 tsp ginger, roll out, cut men and bake at 180C for 10 minutes. Pipe on jagged grins with icing.

d.note: Warm spiced apple juice with cinnamon
d.how: Heat 1.2L apple juice with 2 cinnamon sticks and 4 cloves for 15 minutes without boiling. Ladle into mugs and keep the pot warm on the stove for refills.

s.note: Smoked salmon blinis with crème fraîche
s.how: Warm 16 blinis in the oven for 3 minutes. Top each with a spoon of crème fraîche, a curl of smoked salmon and snipped chives and serve on a big platter.

s.note: Buttery Christmas shortbread fingers, the kind of cookie plate Santa works through all night
s.how: Beat 250g butter and 110g sugar until pale, then mix in 360g plain flour. Press into a lined tin, prick all over and bake at 150C for 45 minutes. Cut into fingers while warm.

m.note: Beef rib roast with roast potatoes and gravy
m.how: Roast a 2kg beef rib at 220C for 20 minutes, then 180C for 1 hour for medium rare. Roast 1kg potatoes alongside and make gravy from the pan juices and 300ml stock.

w.note: Sponge, custard, mixed berries and whipped cream layered in a glass bowl
w.how: Tear a sponge cake into a glass bowl and scatter with 250g mixed berries. Pour over 500ml custard, top with 300ml whipped cream and chill for an hour.

d.note: A cold pint of dark ale, lemonade for the kids
d.how: Chill 4 pints of dark ale and pour into cold glasses. Have 1.25L lemonade ready over ice for the kids and anyone not drinking. Make it just before the film starts and keep the jug cold.

s.note: Spiced chicken tacos with salsa and lime
s.how: Toss 600g chicken thighs in taco seasoning and grill for 12 minutes, then slice. Warm 12 tortillas and fill with chicken, shredded lettuce and salsa. Serve with lime wedges.

s.note: White chocolate bark with crushed candy canes
s.how: Melt 300g white chocolate and spread thin on a lined tray. Scatter with 6 crushed candy canes, chill for 30 minutes until set and snap into shards.

m.note: Golden roast chicken with potatoes and carrots
m.how: Rub a whole chicken with 30g butter and salt and roast at 200C for 1 hour 15 minutes. Add 800g potatoes and 3 carrots to the tray for the last 50 minutes and rest before carving.

w.note: Iced sugar cookies in Christmas shapes
w.how: Beat 200g butter and 100g icing sugar, add 1 egg yolk and 300g flour and chill. Roll, cut into shapes and bake at 170C for 12 minutes. Ice with 250g icing sugar and a little water.

d.note: Hot chocolate topped with whipped cream
d.how: Heat 1L milk until steaming and whisk in 150g chopped milk chocolate until smooth. Pour into 4 mugs and top with a swirl of whipped cream.

s.note: Sausages in rolls with fried onions
s.how: Grill 8 beef sausages for 12 minutes, turning. Fry 2 sliced onions in oil until soft and golden. Serve in 8 bread rolls with the onions and English mustard.

s.note: Warm mince pies dusted with icing sugar
s.how: Warm 12 mince pies at 160C for 10 minutes. Dust with icing sugar and serve with 300ml whipped cream on the side. Serve straight away on a big platter in the middle of the table.

m.note: Beef and rice stuffed capsicums in tomato
m.how: Mix 500g beef mince with 150g cooked rice, a diced onion and paprika. Fill 6 hollowed capsicums, stand them in a dish with 700g passata and bake covered at 180C for 50 minutes.

w.note: Gingerbread biscuits with white icing, the kind of thing sold all year in Santa's
w.how: Melt 100g butter with 100g golden syrup and 80g brown sugar. Mix in 300g flour and 2 tsp ginger, roll out, cut shapes and bake at 180C for 10 minutes. Ice once cool.

d.note: Warm spiced red wine with orange
d.how: Heat 750ml red wine with orange slices, 2 cinnamon sticks and 3 tbsp sugar for 15 minutes without boiling. Heat apple juice the same way for anyone not drinking.

s.note: Toasted cheese sandwiches cut in half
s.how: Fill 4 sandwiches with 200g sliced cheddar and butter the outsides. Toast in a frying pan over medium heat for 3 minutes a side until golden and melted, then cut in half.

s.note: Creamy clam chowder with bacon and potato
s.how: Fry 3 chopped rashers of bacon and a diced onion. Add 300g diced potatoes and 500ml fish stock and simmer 15 minutes. Stir in 400g tinned clams and 200ml cream and heat through.

m.note: Roast chicken with herb stuffing and potatoes
m.how: Fill a whole chicken with stuffing made from 150g breadcrumbs, diced onion and chopped sage. Roast at 200C for 1 hour 15 minutes with 800g potatoes around it and rest before carving.

w.note: Flaming brandy cherries over vanilla ice cream
w.how: Simmer 500g pitted cherries with 60g sugar and a splash of water for 5 minutes. Warm 60ml brandy, pour over, light carefully and spoon over 1L vanilla ice cream once the flames die.

d.note: Bourbon over ice, ginger ale for the rest
d.how: Pour 45ml bourbon over ice in 4 short glasses. Have 1.25L ginger ale ready over ice for the students and anyone not drinking. Make it just before the film starts and keep the jug cold.

s.note: Crispy potato skins with cheese and bacon
s.how: Bake 6 potatoes at 200C for 1 hour, halve and scoop out most of the flesh. Fill with 150g grated cheese and 3 chopped bacon rashers and bake 10 minutes. Serve with sour cream.

s.note: Nuts, chocolate buttons and dried cranberries
s.how: Tip 200g mixed nuts, 200g chocolate buttons and 150g dried cranberries into a big bowl and toss. Serve before the opening credits so everyone can grab a handful.

m.note: Grilled rump steak with sweet potato and beans
m.how: Roast 800g sweet potato wedges at 220C for 35 minutes. Grill 4 rump steaks for 3 minutes a side, rest for 5 minutes and serve with the sweet potato and 300g steamed green beans.

w.note: Red and green iced Christmas cookies
w.how: Beat 200g butter and 100g icing sugar, add 1 egg yolk and 300g flour and chill. Roll, cut and bake at 170C for 12 minutes. Ice in red and green.

d.note: Hot chocolate topped with whipped cream
d.how: Heat 1L milk until steaming and whisk in 150g chopped milk chocolate until smooth. Pour into 4 mugs and top with whipped cream. Make it just before the film starts and keep the jug cold.

s.note: Choc chip cookies left out as bait
s.how: Beat 125g butter with 150g brown sugar and 1 egg, then mix in 200g flour and 150g chocolate chips. Roll 16 balls and bake at 180C for 11 minutes.

s.note: Crisp fries with gravy for dipping
s.how: Bake 1kg frozen chips at 220C for 25 minutes, turning once. Whisk gravy powder into 300ml boiling water until smooth and serve on the side for dipping.

m.note: Glazed meatloaf with mash and gravy
m.how: Mix 800g beef mince with a diced onion, 1 egg and 60g breadcrumbs. Press into a loaf tin, brush with tomato sauce and bake at 180C for 1 hour. Serve with mash made from 800g potatoes.

w.note: Iced sugar cookies in stars and reindeer
w.how: Beat 200g butter and 100g icing sugar, add 1 egg yolk and 300g flour and chill. Roll, cut and bake at 170C for 12 minutes, then ice.

d.note: Hot chocolate with marshmallows on top
d.how: Heat 1L milk until steaming and whisk in 150g chopped milk chocolate. Pour into 4 mugs and add a handful of marshmallows to each. Make it just before the film starts and keep the jug cold.

s.note: Ham and cheese toasties in triangles
s.how: Fill 4 sandwiches with 150g ham and 150g cheese, butter the outsides and toast in a pan for 3 minutes a side. Cut into triangles.

s.note: Hot dogs with mustard and sauce
s.how: Simmer 8 frankfurts for 5 minutes and tuck into 8 soft buns. Serve with mustard and tomato sauce so everyone builds their own. Serve straight away on a big platter in the middle of the table.

m.note: Roast beef with potatoes and gravy
m.how: Season a 1.5kg beef topside and roast at 200C for 1 hour with 1kg potatoes. Rest 15 minutes, make gravy with the pan juices and 300ml stock and carve.

w.note: Vanilla cupcakes iced white with coconut
w.how: Beat 125g butter and 150g sugar, add 2 eggs, 200g self-raising flour and 120ml milk. Bake 12 cupcakes at 180C for 18 minutes. Ice with 150g butter beaten with 300g icing sugar and roll in coconut.

d.note: Hot chocolate made with real chocolate
d.how: Heat 1L milk until steaming and whisk in 150g chopped milk chocolate until smooth. Pour into 4 mugs and serve straight away. Make it just before the film starts and keep the jug cold.

s.note: Cheddar, crackers and red and green grapes
s.how: Arrange 200g sliced cheddar, 200g crackers and 500g mixed red and green grapes on a big board. Set it out before the opening credits. Serve straight away on a big platter in the middle of the table.

s.note: Little glazed cocktail meatballs on toothpicks, the classic street party snack
s.how: Mix 500g beef mince with 1 egg and 40g breadcrumbs and roll into small balls. Bake at 200C for 15 minutes, then toss in 250ml warm sweet chilli sauce.

m.note: Roast turkey breast with stuffing and cranberry
m.how: Roast a 1.5kg turkey breast at 180C for 1 hour 20 minutes. Bake stuffing of 150g breadcrumbs, a diced onion, sage and melted butter. Serve with cranberry sauce.

w.note: Sponge, jelly, custard and cream in a bowl
w.how: Make raspberry jelly and let it half set. Tear a sponge cake into a bowl, pour over the jelly and chill. Top with 500ml custard and 300ml whipped cream.

d.note: Chilled eggnog with nutmeg on top
d.how: Whisk 4 egg yolks with 100g sugar. Pour in 800ml hot milk and stir over low heat until it coats a spoon. Chill and serve with grated nutmeg.

s.note: Warm mince pies with a spoon of cream, the staffroom treat every English school
s.how: Warm 12 mince pies at 160C for 10 minutes. Serve with 300ml whipped cream on the side. Serve straight away on a big platter in the middle of the table.

s.note: Golden sausage rolls, the bake sale favourite at every school Christmas fair
s.how: Mix 500g sausage mince with 1 grated onion and roll in 2 sheets puff pastry. Cut into short lengths, brush with milk and bake at 200C for 25 minutes.

m.note: Roast chicken with stuffing and sprouts
m.how: Fill a whole chicken with stuffing from 150g breadcrumbs and herbs and roast at 200C for 1 hour 15 minutes with 800g potatoes. Roast 300g halved sprouts for the last 20 minutes.

w.note: Christmas pudding with warm custard poured over, the dessert after every school nativity
w.how: Heat an 800g Christmas pudding as the pack says. Warm 500ml custard and pour over thick slices at the table. Serve it at the halfway point of the film.

d.note: Warm blackcurrant cordial in mugs, a cosy drink for kids
d.how: Pour 50ml blackcurrant cordial into each of 4 mugs and top with hot water. Stir and let cool a little before handing out. Make it just before the film starts and keep the jug cold.

s.note: Warm cinnamon sugar donuts, a sweet street snack for a cold parade morning in
s.how: Fry 12 frozen donut rings or balls of 500g pizza dough at 175C until golden. Toss while hot in 100g sugar mixed with 2 tsp cinnamon.

s.note: Iced Christmas cookies for the line
s.how: Beat 200g butter and 100g icing sugar, add 1 egg yolk and 300g flour and chill. Roll, cut and bake at 170C for 12 minutes, then ice.

m.note: Roast turkey with mash and gravy
m.how: Roast a 1.5kg turkey breast at 180C for 1 hour 20 minutes. Boil 800g potatoes and mash with butter. Make gravy from the pan juices and powder.

w.note: Spiced pumpkin pie with whipped cream
w.how: Steam and mash 500g pumpkin. Beat with 150g brown sugar, 2 eggs, 200ml evaporated milk and cinnamon. Pour into a pastry case and bake at 180C for 45 minutes. Serve with whipped cream.

d.note: Warm spiced apple juice with cinnamon
d.how: Heat 1.2L apple juice with 2 cinnamon sticks for 15 minutes without boiling. Ladle into mugs. Make it just before the film starts and keep the jug cold.

s.note: Chocolate rocky road loaded with jellybeans and marshmallows, sweet enough for the Easter Bunny's
s.how: Melt 300g milk chocolate. Stir in 100g marshmallows, 100g jellybeans and 80g peanuts, spread in a lined tin, chill 1 hour and cut into squares.

s.note: Crunchy carrot sticks with hummus, the snack every bunny would pick
s.how: Peel 4 carrots and cut into sticks. Serve standing up in a glass with 250g hummus on the side for dipping. Serve straight away on a big platter in the middle of the table.

m.note: Hot dogs with sauce and mustard
m.how: Simmer 8 frankfurts for 5 minutes and tuck into 8 soft buns. Serve with tomato sauce and mustard. Bring it to the middle of the table so everyone helps themselves.

w.note: Chocolate cornflake nests with mini eggs
w.how: Melt 200g milk chocolate and stir in 80g cornflakes. Spoon into 12 patty cases, press a dip in the middle and fill with mini eggs. Chill until set.

d.note: Fresh carrot and orange juice over ice
d.how: Juice 6 carrots and 4 oranges, or blitz and strain. Stir together and pour over ice. Make it just before the film starts and keep the jug cold.

s.note: Radishes with soft butter and sea salt
s.how: Trim 2 bunches of radishes, leaving a little green. Serve with 50g soft butter and a pinch bowl of sea salt for dipping. Serve straight away on a big platter in the middle of the table.

s.note: Garden vegetables with a yoghurt dip
s.how: Cut 3 carrots into sticks, trim 150g snow peas and separate a baby cos into cups. Serve with 200g Greek yoghurt mixed with lemon and salt.

m.note: Vegetables in a cheese sauce under puff pastry, a country pie made from the
m.how: Soften 2 sliced leeks and 3 diced carrots, add 200g peas. Make a cheese sauce with 300ml milk and 150g cheddar, stir in the veg, top with puff pastry and bake at 200C for 25 minutes.

w.note: Warm blackberry crumble with cream, the berries Peter famously used as a weapon
w.how: Tip 750g blackberries into a dish with 2 tbsp sugar. Rub 100g butter into 120g flour and 100g brown sugar, scatter on top and bake at 180C for 35 minutes. Serve with cream.

d.note: Chamomile tea with honey, cold apple juice for kids
d.how: Steep 4 chamomile tea bags in 1L boiling water for 5 minutes and sweeten with honey. Pour apple juice over ice for the kids. Make it just before the film starts and keep the jug cold.

s.note: Sticky barbecue wings with ranch for dipping
s.how: Bake 1.2kg chicken wings at 220C for 40 minutes until crisp. Toss in 150ml barbecue sauce and bake 5 more minutes until sticky. Serve with ranch and celery sticks.

s.note: Toasted bagels with cream cheese, a quick New York bite between tossing sticks and
s.how: Split and toast 4 bagels and spread with 200g cream cheese. Cut each in half and stack on a plate. Serve straight away on a big platter in the middle of the table.

m.note: Big cheeseburgers with whatever toppings each person picks, because in Sonny's house the kid
m.how: Shape 600g beef mince into 4 patties and grill 4 minutes a side, adding cheese at the end. Set out buns, lettuce, tomato, pickles and sauces and let everyone build their own.

w.note: Vanilla sundaes with chocolate sauce and sprinkles
w.how: Scoop 1L vanilla ice cream into 4 bowls. Pour over warm chocolate sauce, scatter with sprinkles and top each with a cherry. Serve it at the halfway point of the film.

d.note: Cold chocolate milk in tall glasses with straws
d.how: Whisk 4 tbsp drinking chocolate into 1L cold milk until dissolved. Pour into tall glasses over ice and add a straw to each. Make it just before the film starts and keep the jug cold.

s.note: Fresh strawberries dipped in dark chocolate
s.how: Melt 150g dark chocolate in short bursts in the microwave. Dip 500g dry strawberries halfway, lay on baking paper and chill for 20 minutes until set.

s.note: Heart toasts with goat's cheese and honey
s.how: Cut 8 slices of bread into hearts and toast until golden. Spread with 150g goat's cheese, drizzle with honey and scatter with thyme leaves. Serve straight away on a big platter in the middle of the table.

m.note: Pan-seared steak with garlic butter and potatoes
m.how: Roast 800g halved potatoes at 220C for 40 minutes. Sear 4 scotch fillets for 3 minutes a side, add 40g butter and crushed garlic and spoon over. Rest and serve with 150g rocket.

w.note: Red velvet cupcakes with cream cheese icing
w.how: Mix 200g self-raising flour, 2 tbsp cocoa, 150g sugar, 2 eggs, 125ml buttermilk, 100ml oil and red colouring. Bake 12 cupcakes at 180C for 20 minutes. Ice with 250g cream cheese beaten with 150g icing sugar.

d.note: Sparkling rosé with pink lemonade alternative
d.how: Chill 750ml sparkling rosé and pour into flutes with a raspberry in each. Have 1.25L pink lemonade over ice for anyone not drinking. Make it just before the film starts and keep the jug cold.

s.note: Warm croissants with butter and jam
s.how: Warm 6 croissants at 160C for 5 minutes. Serve on a tray with 50g butter and a little jar of jam, plus a flower in a glass if you have one.

s.note: Southern pimento cheese with crackers and celery, a proper Georgia party snack
s.how: Mix 200g grated sharp cheddar with 100g mayonnaise, 80g chopped roasted capsicum and a pinch of cayenne. Serve with 200g crackers and celery sticks. Serve straight away on a big platter in the middle of the table.

m.note: Baked ham, spinach and cheese frittata
m.how: Whisk 8 eggs with 150ml milk. Stir in 150g chopped ham, 100g baby spinach and 100g grated cheese. Pour into a greased dish and bake at 180C for 30 minutes until set. Serve with salad.

w.note: Shortcake biscuits with strawberries and cream
w.how: Rub 80g butter into 250g self-raising flour and 2 tbsp sugar, add 150ml milk and pat out. Cut 6 rounds and bake at 220C for 12 minutes. Split and fill with 300ml whipped cream and 250g sliced strawberries.

d.note: Sparkling wine with orange juice, plain orange juice for the kids
d.how: Fill flutes halfway with chilled orange juice and top with sparkling wine. Pour plain orange juice for the kids. Make it just before the film starts and keep the jug cold.

s.note: Smoked salmon blinis and prawn cups
s.how: Top 16 blinis with crème fraîche and smoked salmon. Fill 12 lettuce cups with 300g cooked prawns tossed in mayonnaise and lemon. Serve together on a big platter.

s.note: Spiced chicken skewers with white sauce
s.how: Toss 600g diced chicken thighs in cumin, paprika and oil and thread onto skewers. Grill 10 minutes, turning. Serve with 200g yoghurt mixed with garlic and lemon.

m.note: Garlic butter prawn linguine with lemon
m.how: Cook 400g linguine. Fry 500g green prawns in 50g butter with 4 garlic cloves and chilli for 3 minutes. Toss with the pasta, lemon juice and chopped parsley.

w.note: Warm chocolate fondue with fruit and marshmallows
w.how: Heat 200ml cream until steaming and pour over 200g chopped dark chocolate. Stir smooth and serve warm with 250g strawberries, banana and marshmallows to dip.

d.note: Chilled champagne at midnight, sparkling grape juice for everyone else
d.how: Chill 750ml sparkling wine and 750ml sparkling grape juice. Pour into flutes just before the countdown. Make it just before the film starts and keep the jug cold.

s.note: Greek platter with olives, feta and pita
s.how: Arrange 200g olives, 200g feta drizzled with oil and oregano, sliced cucumber and tomatoes on a platter. Warm 4 pita breads and cut into wedges.

s.note: Crusty bread, cheese and apples, a forest picnic with Robin Hood before the gang
s.how: Slice a crusty loaf and serve with 200g sharp cheddar and 3 sliced apples on a wooden board. Add a dish of pickle on the side.

m.note: Big pot of beef and vegetable stew
m.how: Brown 1kg diced chuck in batches. Add a chopped onion, 2 carrots, 2 potatoes and 750ml beef stock and simmer covered for 2 hours until tender. Serve with crusty bread.

w.note: Small custard tarts dusted with cinnamon
w.how: Line a muffin tin with 12 rounds of puff pastry. Fill with 400ml custard thickened with 2 egg yolks and bake at 220C for 15 minutes. Dust with cinnamon.

d.note: Ginger ale over ice with lemon
d.how: Fill 4 glasses with ice and pour over 1.25L ginger ale. Add a lemon slice to each. Make it just before the film starts and keep the jug cold.

s.note: Egg and cress sandwiches cut into fingers
s.how: Boil 6 eggs for 9 minutes, cool, peel and mash with 4 tbsp mayonnaise and salt. Spread on 8 slices of buttered bread, add cress and cut into fingers.

s.note: Little beef and vegetable pasties with flaky pastry, the classic Cornish snack
s.how: Mix 300g beef mince with finely diced potato, swede and onion. Spoon onto rounds cut from 3 sheets shortcrust pastry, fold and crimp. Bake at 190C for 35 minutes.

m.note: Slow-cooked lamb shanks with mash, the kind of dish you could eat with your
m.how: Brown 4 lamb shanks, add a chopped onion, 2 carrots, 400g diced tomatoes and 500ml stock and braise at 160C for 3 hours. Serve on mash made from 800g potatoes.

w.note: Crushed meringue with strawberries and cream
w.how: Whip 300ml cream to soft peaks. Crush 8 meringue nests and fold through with 500g sliced strawberries. Spoon into glasses just before serving. Serve it at the halfway point of the film.

d.note: Proper English breakfast tea with milk
d.how: Brew 4 tea bags in a warmed pot of boiling water for 4 minutes. Pour into mugs with a splash of milk and sugar to taste.

s.note: Little sausages glazed in honey and mustard, the kind of pub grub served at
s.how: Bake 500g cocktail sausages at 200C for 15 minutes. Toss in 2 tbsp honey and 1 tbsp wholegrain mustard and bake 5 more minutes until sticky.

s.note: Crackers with cheese and pickled onions
s.how: Arrange 200g water crackers, 200g cheddar and a bowl of pickled onions on a board. Serve straight away on a big platter in the middle of the table.

m.note: A hearty fish and potato stew from the galley, the one thing Silver is
m.how: Soften an onion and 2 celery stalks in butter. Add 500g diced potatoes and 750ml fish stock and simmer 15 minutes. Add 600g white fish chunks and 200ml cream and cook 5 minutes.

w.note: Chocolate brownies piled with gold-wrapped chocolate coins, a chest of buried treasure
w.how: Bake brownies from 200g dark chocolate, 180g butter, 300g sugar, 3 eggs and 100g flour at 170C for 28 minutes. Pile gold chocolate coins on top.

d.note: Ginger beer with lime, rum on the side
d.how: Pour 1.25L ginger beer over ice with lime wedges. Have 120ml dark rum on the side for adults. Make it just before the film starts and keep the jug cold.

s.note: Dry-rubbed barbecue wings with a tangy sauce, a taste of Memphis on game day
s.how: Toss 1.2kg wings in 2 tbsp smoked paprika, brown sugar and salt. Bake at 220C for 45 minutes and serve with 150ml barbecue sauce. Serve straight away on a big platter in the middle of the table.

s.note: Southern deviled eggs dusted with paprika, a classic on every Southern table
s.how: Boil 8 eggs for 10 minutes, cool and halve. Mash the yolks with 4 tbsp mayonnaise and 1 tsp mustard, pipe back in and dust with paprika.

m.note: Roast turkey with cornbread stuffing and mash
m.how: Roast a 1.5kg turkey breast at 180C for 1 hour 20 minutes. Bake stuffing from 200g crumbled cornbread, onion and celery. Serve with mash from 800g potatoes and 300g green beans.

w.note: Sticky pecan pie with ice cream
w.how: Whisk 3 eggs, 150g brown sugar, 150ml golden syrup and 50g melted butter. Stir in 200g pecans, pour into a pastry case and bake at 170C for 45 minutes.

d.note: Sweet iced tea with lemon and mint
d.how: Steep 6 tea bags in 1L boiling water with 120g sugar. Add 500ml cold water, chill and serve over ice with lemon and mint. Make it just before the film starts and keep the jug cold.

s.note: Pork and cabbage dumplings with black vinegar
s.how: Mix 400g pork mince with 150g finely chopped wombok, ginger, soy and sesame oil. Fill 30 gow gee wrappers, fold and boil for 5 minutes. Serve with black vinegar and chilli oil.

s.note: Smashed cucumbers with garlic and chilli oil
s.how: Smash 2 cucumbers with a rolling pin and break into chunks. Toss with 2 crushed garlic cloves, 2 tbsp rice vinegar, 1 tbsp soy, sugar and chilli oil.

m.n: Wedding banquet sweet and sour pork
m.note: Crispy sweet and sour pork with pineapple
m.how: Coat 600g diced pork in cornflour and fry until crisp. Toss with capsicum, pineapple and 200ml sweet and sour sauce. Serve with 300g steamed jasmine rice.

w.note: Crisp sesame balls with red bean filling
w.how: Mix 250g glutinous rice flour with 60g sugar and 200ml hot water into a dough. Wrap around teaspoons of red bean paste, roll in sesame seeds and fry at 170C until golden.

d.note: Hot jasmine tea in small cups
d.how: Steep 4 jasmine tea bags in 1L water just off the boil for 3 minutes. Pour into small cups and keep the pot topped up.

s.note: Crisp Filipino spring rolls filled with pork and vegetables, with sweet chilli for dipping
s.how: Mix 500g pork mince with grated carrot, onion, garlic and soy. Roll tightly in 20 spring roll wrappers and fry at 180C until golden. Serve with sweet chilli sauce.

s.note: Stir-fried noodles with chicken and vegetables
s.how: Soak 250g rice vermicelli. Stir-fry 300g sliced chicken with garlic, carrot and cabbage, add 3 tbsp soy and 250ml stock, then toss through the noodles. Serve with lemon wedges.

m.note: Chicken braised in vinegar, soy and garlic
m.how: Brown 1kg chicken thighs. Add 120ml vinegar, 80ml soy, 6 garlic cloves, 3 bay leaves and pepper and simmer covered 35 minutes. Reduce the sauce and serve with 300g jasmine rice.

w.note: Silky caramel custard flan, the Filipino party dessert
w.how: Melt 150g sugar to a caramel and pour into a dish. Whisk 6 egg yolks with 395g condensed milk and 370ml evaporated milk, pour in and bake in a water bath at 160C for 50 minutes. Chill and turn out.

d.note: Lime and lemon cooler over ice
d.how: Mix the juice of 4 limes and 2 lemons with 4 tbsp sugar until dissolved. Top with 1L sparkling water and serve over ice. Make it just before the film starts and keep the jug cold.

s.note: Cheese, crackers and fruit by the fire
s.how: Arrange 150g brie, 150g cheddar, 200g crackers, 500g grapes and a handful of dried apricots on a board. Serve straight away on a big platter in the middle of the table.

s.note: Warm garlic bread to pass around
s.how: Split a baguette, spread with 80g butter mixed with 3 crushed garlic cloves and parsley. Wrap in foil and bake at 200C for 15 minutes.

m.note: Baked egg, bread and ham strata
m.how: Layer 8 slices of torn bread with 150g ham and 150g grated cheese. Pour over 8 eggs whisked with 500ml milk, soak 30 minutes and bake at 180C for 45 minutes. Try not to drop it.

w.note: Warm cinnamon scrolls with cream cheese icing
w.how: Roll 500g pizza dough flat, spread with 60g butter, 80g brown sugar and cinnamon. Roll up, cut 10 scrolls and bake at 190C for 22 minutes. Ice with 100g cream cheese beaten with 100g icing sugar.

d.note: Coffee with cream and hot chocolate
d.how: Brew 1L coffee and serve with warm cream. Make hot chocolate with milk and drinking chocolate for anyone who wants it. Make it just before the film starts and keep the jug cold.

s.note: Little crab cakes with lemon mayonnaise
s.how: Mix 300g crab meat with 60g breadcrumbs, 1 egg, spring onion and lemon zest. Shape 12 cakes, chill, then fry in butter 3 minutes a side. Serve with mayonnaise mixed with lemon juice.

s.note: Mushroom and gruyère tarts, the kind of canapé served in a grand old European
s.how: Fry 250g sliced mushrooms with garlic and thyme. Cut 1 sheet puff pastry into 12 squares, top with mushrooms and 80g gruyère and bake at 200C for 15 minutes.

m.note: Pan-roasted duck breast with orange sauce
m.how: Score 4 duck breasts and cook skin side down for 8 minutes, then roast at 200C for 6 minutes. Make a sauce from 200ml orange juice, 2 tbsp honey and stock. Serve with 800g roast potatoes.

w.note: Chocolate mousse in little glasses with berries
w.how: Melt 200g dark chocolate and cool. Fold through 300ml whipped cream and 2 beaten egg whites. Spoon into 6 glasses, chill 2 hours and top with 125g raspberries.

d.note: Chilled champagne with sparkling apple alternative
d.how: Chill 750ml sparkling wine and 750ml sparkling apple juice. Pour into flutes. Make it just before the film starts and keep the jug cold. Keep a second round ready for the back half of the film.

s.note: Bush damper with butter and golden syrup
s.how: Rub 60g butter into 450g self-raising flour, add 300ml milk and shape a round. Bake at 200C for 30 minutes until it sounds hollow. Serve with butter and golden syrup.

s.note: Pippis with garlic, chilli and parsley
s.how: Soak 1kg pippis in salted water for an hour. Fry 3 garlic cloves and a chilli in olive oil, add the pippis and 100ml white wine, cover and cook until they open. Toss with parsley.

m.note: Pan-fried fish with chips and lemon
m.how: Bake 1kg frozen chips. Dust 4 white fish fillets in seasoned flour and fry in butter and oil for 3 minutes a side. Serve with lemon wedges and tartare sauce.

w.note: Soft dumplings in golden syrup sauce
w.how: Rub 50g butter into 200g self-raising flour, add 1 egg and a little milk. Drop spoonfuls into a simmering sauce of 150g golden syrup, 100g brown sugar and 500ml water and cook covered 20 minutes.

d.note: Strong black tea with milk and sugar
d.how: Boil 1.2L water, add 6 tea bags and let it stew for 5 minutes. Pour into mugs with milk and sugar. Make it just before the film starts and keep the jug cold.

s.note: Hummus, olives, feta and warm flatbread, a meze welcome for a guest a long
s.how: Arrange 250g hummus, 200g olives and 200g feta drizzled with oil on a platter. Warm 4 flatbreads and cut into wedges. Serve straight away on a big platter in the middle of the table.

s.note: Golden oat and golden syrup biscuits
s.how: Mix 100g oats, 150g flour, 80g coconut and 120g brown sugar. Melt 125g butter with 2 tbsp golden syrup, add 1 tsp bicarb in 2 tbsp boiling water and stir through. Roll balls and bake at 170C for 12 minutes.

m.note: Spiced lamb kofte with yoghurt and flatbread
m.how: Mix 600g lamb mince with grated onion, cumin, paprika and parsley and shape onto skewers. Grill 8 minutes, turning. Serve with 200g yoghurt, tomato and onion salad and 4 flatbreads.

w.note: Flaky nut baklava in honey syrup
w.how: Layer 12 sheets filo brushed with 150g melted butter and 250g chopped walnuts and pistachios. Cut diamonds and bake at 170C for 45 minutes. Pour over a syrup of 200g honey, 100g sugar and lemon.

d.note: Strong coffee and sweet apple tea
d.how: Brew strong coffee in a small pot and serve in little cups. Steep apple tea bags in boiling water and sweeten for anyone who prefers tea.

s.note: A big platter of strawberries, apples, melon and grapes, the stalls the gang has
s.how: Hull 250g strawberries, slice 2 apples and cut a rockmelon into wedges. Arrange on a big platter with 500g grapes and squeeze over a little lemon to stop the apple browning.

s.note: Dried fruit and nuts mixed in a big bowl, the loot Barnabas sends the
s.how: Tip 200g dried fruit mix and 200g mixed nuts into a bowl with 100g dried apricots and toss together. Set it out before the opening credits.

m.note: Chicken, leek and carrot pie under golden puff pastry, a proper English city lunch
m.how: Brown 800g diced chicken thighs, add 1 sliced leek and 2 diced carrots, then 300ml stock thickened with 2 tbsp flour. Pour into a dish, top with puff pastry and bake at 200C for 25 minutes.

w.note: Moist carrot cake with cream cheese icing
w.how: Mix 200g self-raising flour, 150g brown sugar, cinnamon, 2 eggs, 150ml oil and 3 grated carrots. Bake at 170C for 45 minutes. Ice with 250g cream cheese beaten with 150g icing sugar.

d.note: Cold apple juice with a slice of apple
d.how: Fill 4 glasses with ice, pour in 1.2L cold apple juice and float a thin slice of apple in each. Make it just before the film starts and keep the jug cold.

s.note: Spiced gingerbread cookies with white icing
s.how: Melt 100g butter with 100g golden syrup and 80g brown sugar. Mix in 300g flour and 2 tsp ginger, roll out, cut shapes and bake at 180C for 10 minutes. Ice once cool.

s.note: Crunchy golden honeycomb broken into chunks, as golden and glittery as the Sandman's dreams
s.how: Heat 200g sugar and 5 tbsp golden syrup until amber. Whisk in 1 tbsp bicarb, pour onto a lined tray and leave to set for an hour. Break into chunks.

m.note: Golden roast chicken with potatoes and carrots
m.how: Rub a whole chicken with butter and salt and roast at 200C for 1 hour 15 minutes. Add 800g potatoes and 3 carrots to the tray for the last 50 minutes and rest before carving.

w.note: Hot cross buns and chocolate eggs
w.how: Split and toast 6 hot cross buns and spread with butter. Hide 200g foil-wrapped chocolate eggs around the room before the film for a quick egg hunt.

d.note: Blue lemonade over crushed ice for movie night, made for four
d.how: Mix 120ml blue cordial with 1L cold lemonade and pour over crushed ice in 4 glasses. Make it just before the film starts and keep the jug cold.

s.note: Egg and cress sandwiches cut into fingers, neat enough for an Easter bonnet crowd
s.how: Boil 6 eggs for 9 minutes, cool, peel and mash with 4 tbsp mayonnaise. Spread on 8 slices of bread, add cress and cut into fingers.

s.note: Warm gruyère choux puffs, a smart little snack for opening night
s.how: Boil 250ml water with 100g butter, beat in 150g flour and cool. Beat in 4 eggs and 120g grated gruyère, pipe small balls and bake at 200C for 25 minutes.

m.note: Roast lamb with garlic, rosemary and mint sauce
m.how: Stud a 2kg lamb leg with garlic slivers and rosemary. Roast at 180C for 1 hour 45 minutes with 1kg potatoes. Rest 15 minutes and serve with mint sauce.

w.note: Toasted hot cross buns with butter
w.how: Split 6 hot cross buns and toast until golden. Spread with 50g butter while hot and serve straight away. Serve it at the halfway point of the film.

d.note: Pink cranberry punch with lemonade for movie night, made for four
d.how: Mix 1L cranberry juice and 1L lemonade in a jug with ice and sliced strawberries. Make it just before the film starts and keep the jug cold.

s.note: Golden oat and golden syrup biscuits
s.how: Mix 100g oats, 150g flour, 80g coconut and 120g brown sugar. Melt 125g butter with 2 tbsp golden syrup, add 1 tsp bicarb in 2 tbsp boiling water and stir through. Roll balls and bake at 170C for 12 minutes.

s.note: Camp damper with butter and golden syrup
s.how: Rub 60g butter into 450g self-raising flour, add 300ml milk and shape a round. Bake at 200C for 30 minutes until it sounds hollow. Serve warm with butter and golden syrup.

m.note: Slow-cooked beef and vegetable stew, the kind cooked in a big pot at camp
m.how: Brown 1kg diced chuck. Add a chopped onion, 2 carrots, 2 potatoes and 750ml beef stock and simmer covered for 2 hours until tender. Serve with damper.

w.note: Soft dumplings in golden syrup sauce
w.how: Rub 50g butter into 200g self-raising flour, add 1 egg and a little milk. Drop spoonfuls into a simmering sauce of 150g golden syrup, 100g brown sugar and 500ml water and cook covered 20 minutes.

d.note: Strong black tea brewed in a billy
d.how: Boil 1.2L water, add 6 tea bags and let it stew for 5 minutes. Pour into mugs with milk and sugar. Make it just before the film starts and keep the jug cold.

s.note: Golden oat and golden syrup biscuits
s.how: Mix 100g oats, 150g flour, 80g coconut and 120g brown sugar. Melt 125g butter with 2 tbsp golden syrup, add 1 tsp bicarb in 2 tbsp boiling water and stir through. Roll balls and bake at 170C for 12 minutes.

s.note: Corned beef and sweet pickle sandwiches
s.how: Spread 8 slices of buttered bread with sweet pickle. Fill with 250g sliced corned beef and cut into triangles. Serve straight away on a big platter in the middle of the table.

m.note: Crisp corned beef hash with fried eggs
m.how: Boil 800g diced potatoes for 8 minutes and drain. Fry with a diced onion and 400g chopped corned beef until crisp. Top with 4 fried eggs.

w.note: Rich fruit cake slices with butter
w.how: Cut an 800g fruit cake into thick slices and serve with soft butter, the way it arrived in parcels for the troops. Serve it at the halfway point of the film.

d.note: Strong black tea with condensed milk
d.how: Brew 6 tea bags in 1.2L boiling water for 5 minutes. Stir a spoon of condensed milk into each mug. Make it just before the film starts and keep the jug cold.

s.note: Salted peanuts and crackers with cheese, the snacks around the base before the concert
s.how: Tip 200g salted peanuts into a bowl and arrange 200g crackers with 150g sliced cheddar on a board. Serve straight away on a big platter in the middle of the table.

s.note: Fresh rice paper rolls with prawns and mint
s.how: Soak 100g vermicelli. Dip 12 rice paper sheets in warm water and fill with prawns, noodles, lettuce and mint. Roll tight and serve with hoisin and peanut sauce.

m.note: Beef and bean stew with tomatoes
m.how: Brown 800g diced chuck with a chopped onion. Add 400g diced tomatoes, 800g drained kidney beans and 500ml stock and simmer 2 hours. Serve with bread.

w.note: Dark chocolate squares with fresh orange segments
w.how: Break 200g dark chocolate into squares and serve with 3 peeled oranges cut into segments. Serve it at the halfway point of the film. Leave it out for anyone who wants seconds.

d.note: Cold lager, lemonade for anyone not drinking
d.how: Chill 8 cans lager and serve in cold glasses. Have 1.25L lemonade over ice for anyone not drinking. Make it just before the film starts and keep the jug cold.

s.note: Sweet corn rolled in butter and salt
s.how: Boil 4 corn cobs in salted water for 6 minutes. Roll in 40g butter, sprinkle with salt and cut each in half. Serve straight away on a big platter in the middle of the table.

s.note: Roasted peanuts and salted sunflower seeds
s.how: Tip 500g roasted peanuts in the shell into a big bowl and 200g salted sunflower seeds into a smaller one. Put out a third bowl for shells.

m.note: Buttermilk fried chicken with mashed potatoes, a Midwest farmhouse dinner
m.how: Soak 1.2kg chicken pieces in 300ml buttermilk for an hour. Dredge in 200g seasoned flour and fry at 170C for 14 minutes. Serve with mash from 800g potatoes.

w.note: Apple pie with vanilla ice cream
w.how: Slice 5 green apples, toss with 100g sugar and cinnamon. Line a dish with 1 pastry sheet, fill, top with another and bake at 190C for 45 minutes. Serve with ice cream.

d.note: Homemade lemonade over ice for movie night, made for four
d.how: Stir the juice of 6 lemons with 150g sugar until dissolved. Top with 1.2L cold water and serve over ice. Make it just before the film starts and keep the jug cold.

s.note: Hot dogs with exactly eight of each
s.how: Simmer 8 frankfurts for 5 minutes and tuck into 8 buns. Exactly 8. Serve with mustard and tomato sauce. Serve straight away on a big platter in the middle of the table.

s.note: Smoked salmon blinis with crème fraîche
s.how: Warm 16 blinis. Top with crème fraîche, smoked salmon and chives. Serve straight away on a big platter in the middle of the table. Put it out before the opening credits so everyone can graze.

m.note: Roast chicken with potatoes and beans
m.how: Roast a whole chicken at 200C for 1 hour 15 minutes with 800g potatoes. Steam 300g green beans and serve together. Bring it to the middle of the table so everyone helps themselves.

w.note: Vanilla butter cake with white icing
w.how: Beat 200g butter and 200g sugar, add 4 eggs and 250g self-raising flour. Bake at 175C for 40 minutes. Ice with 300g icing sugar mixed with butter and milk.

d.note: Cold milk in tall glasses for movie night, made for four
d.how: Chill 1L milk and pour into 4 tall glasses. Make it just before the film starts and keep the jug cold. Keep a second round ready for the back half of the film.

s.note: Ham and cheese sandwiches for camp
s.how: Butter 8 slices of bread and fill with 150g ham and 4 slices of cheddar. Cut in halves and pile on a plate. Serve straight away on a big platter in the middle of the table.

s.note: Hot dogs with mustard and relish
s.how: Simmer 8 frankfurts for 5 minutes and tuck into 8 buns. Serve with mustard and relish. Serve straight away on a big platter in the middle of the table.

m.note: Southern fried chicken with mash and gravy
m.how: Dredge 1.2kg chicken pieces in 200g seasoned flour and fry at 170C for 14 minutes. Serve with mash from 800g potatoes and gravy. Bring it to the middle of the table so everyone helps themselves.

w.note: Warm peach cobbler with cream for movie night, made for four
w.how: Tip 800g drained peaches into a dish. Rub 80g butter into 200g self-raising flour and 100g sugar, add milk, spoon over and bake at 190C for 30 minutes.

d.note: Sweet iced tea with lemon for movie night, made for four
d.how: Steep 6 tea bags in 1L boiling water with 120g sugar. Add 500ml cold water, chill and serve over ice with lemon. Make it just before the film starts and keep the jug cold.

s.note: Meatloaf sandwiches with tomato sauce, packed in a lunch pail for a shift at
s.how: Bake a meatloaf from 400g beef mince, 1 egg and breadcrumbs at 180C for 45 minutes. Cool, slice and make sandwiches on buttered bread with tomato sauce.

s.note: Grilled bratwurst with onions and mustard
s.how: Grill 8 bratwurst for 12 minutes, turning. Fry 2 sliced onions until soft and golden. Serve in 8 rolls with the onions and mustard. Serve straight away on a big platter in the middle of the table.

m.note: Slow pot roast with carrots and potatoes
m.how: Brown a 1.5kg chuck roast, add 750ml stock and braise covered at 160C for 3 hours. Add 3 carrots and 800g potatoes for the last hour.

w.note: Warm apple crumble with cream for movie night, made for four
w.how: Slice 5 green apples into a dish. Rub 100g butter into 120g flour and 100g brown sugar, scatter on top and bake at 180C for 35 minutes. Serve with cream.

d.note: Cold milk with a plate of biscuits
d.how: Chill 1L milk and pour into 4 tall glasses. Serve with 200g plain biscuits on a plate. Make it just before the film starts and keep the jug cold.

s.note: Hot party pies with tomato sauce
s.how: Bake 12 frozen party pies at 200C for 20 minutes. Serve hot with tomato sauce. Serve straight away on a big platter in the middle of the table.

s.note: Apple slices with cheddar, a treat for the horse and the man who loved
s.how: Slice 3 red apples and serve with 200g sliced cheddar on a board. Serve straight away on a big platter in the middle of the table.

m.note: Chicken, lettuce and mayonnaise sandwiches, a classic Cup day picnic
m.how: Mix 300g shredded cooked chicken with 4 tbsp mayonnaise. Fill 6 sandwiches with the chicken and lettuce and cut into triangles. Bring it to the middle of the table so everyone helps themselves.

w.note: Lamingtons dipped in chocolate and coconut
w.how: Cut a sponge cake into squares. Mix 250g icing sugar, 30g cocoa and hot water into a thin icing, dip each square and roll in 150g coconut.

d.note: Sparkling wine, lemonade for the kids
d.how: Chill 750ml sparkling wine and 1.25L lemonade. Pour into flutes. Make it just before the film starts and keep the jug cold. Keep a second round ready for the back half of the film.

s.note: Roasted peanuts in the shell and crackers with cheese, a racetrack crowd snack
s.how: Tip 500g roasted peanuts in the shell into a bowl with a second bowl for shells. Arrange 200g crackers and 150g cheddar on a board beside them.

s.note: Apple and carrot sticks with peanut butter
s.how: Slice 3 apples and cut 3 carrots into sticks. Serve with 200g peanut butter for dipping. Serve straight away on a big platter in the middle of the table.

m.note: Glazed meatloaf with mash, a meal that stretches a little further
m.how: Mix 800g beef mince with a diced onion, 1 egg and breadcrumbs. Press into a tin, glaze with tomato sauce and bake at 180C for 1 hour. Serve with mash from 800g potatoes.

w.note: Apple pie with cream for movie night, made for four
w.how: Slice 5 green apples and toss with sugar and cinnamon. Fill a pastry case, top with pastry and bake at 190C for 45 minutes. Serve with cream.

d.note: Iced tea with lemon for movie night, made for four
d.how: Steep 4 tea bags in 1L boiling water, chill and serve over ice with lemon slices. Make it just before the film starts and keep the jug cold.
